News.title: Andy Burnham ally calling for major shake-up of property taxes – as Labour MP calls for action in PM’s ten-year plan
News.content:
Next

AN ALLY of Andy Burnham is calling for a shake-up of council tax and stamp duty as households face rising bills.

Lord Jim O’Neill insists Britain has a “nonsensical approach” to property taxation which is now outdated and holding back growth.



His remarks come as MPs are due to debate proposals in Westminster today following a petition signed by 100,000 people.

Campaigners are also demanding the issue is addressed in the PM’s ten-year plan that is due to be set out next month.



A coalition of MPs, charities and leading experts have written to Downing Street demanding an independent review into the matter.

Lord Jim O’Neill, a Crossbench peer, said: “There is widespread agreement that we have an utterly nonsensical approach to the taxation of property.

“The owners of higher-value homes can pay far less Council Tax as a proportion of their property’s value than people at the other end of the scale, while Stamp Duty discourages people from moving and holds back economic activity.

“Now is the time for bold action to fix the property tax system once and for all.”

The Peer had been advising Mr Burnham but didn’t take a job in Downing Street.

Meanwhile, Labour MP Jonathan Hinder, said: “Council tax is the most unfair, regressive tax in Britain, and a considered independent review of comprehensive property tax reform is long overdue.



“This debate is an opportunity for MPs to say enough is enough and unite behind real change.”

He added that it should start in the PM’s ten year plan.

The letter warns that without any action over the next ten years, council tax valuations will be nearly fifty years out of date to 1991 levels.

Some low and middle-income households even face a £900 increase in the council tax levy over the next decade without change.

Stamp duty adds thousands of pounds to moving property and often puts off families moving areas for work.



It also puts off older homeowners from downsizing and allowing more suitable families to move into bigger homes.

Neal Lawson, Director of Compass, said: “The Prime Minister has committed to taking on the big challenges where other politicians have failed, and the inequality at the heart of our property tax system should be absolutely central to that.

“We need an independent review to consider the options and deliver for the working people that put their trust in Labour to deliver real change.”

News.title: Burnham’s Brexit fixation puts him in dangerous waters… he’s dragging UK back to 2016 while ignoring small boats & bills
News.content:
Next

EUROCRAT-in-chief Ursula von der Leyen was bang on when she said in ­Brussels last week: “I have many British friends, and they’re very good at ­making up their minds.”

We can only guess what the German supremo’s old pals from her days at the left-wing London School of Economics think about effing Brexit.



And like another famous Ursula, the sea-witch from Disney’s The Little Mermaid, von der Leyen has already entangled hapless Andy Burnham in her tentacles.

Meanwhile, for the rest of us, we are pretty clear as a ­people over what we want our governments to focus on.



If readers were to look at YouGov’s excellent tracker of public priorities, you would see that the economy and immigration are by miles our most pressing concerns.

Cast your eyes further down and you will go past health, crime, defence, welfare . . . and more.

Eventually you will stop and squint and you might just about see the paltry 11 per cent of Brits who see Brexit as a top priority.

These are the Alastair ­Campbells and James O’Briens of the country — Japanese hold-outs in the jungle still fighting a war the rest of us have long since put to bed.

For context, before both the 2016 referendum and 2019 ­general ­election, Brexit WAS the most important issue for ­voters.

But it has since receded drastically and given way to plenty of other priorities that should be keeping Burnham busy.



Yet our new Prime ­Minister has decided to don his steel helmet, fix bayonets and walk back into the jungle.

As a political gambit to unite left-wing progressives, Burnham thinks he is on to a winner.

Nothing brings together Labour luvvies, Lib Dem windbags and Green crusties more than their total, unshakeable hatred of Brexit.

Pinching votes from Ed Davey and Zack Polanski has been the plan since Burnham swept into Downing Street last summer.

Sanctioning Israeli settlements and dangling proportional representation have also helped reel some in.



And all at a time when the Right remains divided.

Nigel Farage has latched on to the new EU battle to attack the Tories just as much as he targets Labour.

Despite the scars the Conservatives still bear from the referendum, Kemi Badenoch has been clear in her opposition to reopening the result.



Having landed decent blows on the economy and welfare, could she now risk being ­distracted by Burnham’s sleight of hand on Brexit?

This is the calculation the PM believes will pay off at the ballot box.

But he is charging into an electoral minefield that could blow up spectacularly.

Potentially his gravest ­mistake is claiming that last week’s EU deal will lead to lower prices for voters.

He even said with a straight face that the agreement will “bring the cost of food down” in supermarkets.



At best this is fancifully ­optimistic and, at worst, it is a deeply disingenuous sale of false hope to millions.

The pennies each person might save from smoother trade ties will be swallowed up by stubbornly high inflation.

Ed Miliband was the latest Cabinet minister hitting the airwaves yesterday, promising people lower prices in the shops.

Remember his similar pledge to knock £300 off energy bills? How’s that one going?

The short-term sugar rush of winning back some middle-class Europhiles in university towns risks backfiring into ­national resentment when Brits realise their milk and eggs are no cheaper.



Maybe the PM is planning that early election after all . . .

Burnham keeps wheeling out polls showing how three-quarters of us back closer ties with Europe, which is innocent enough in itself.

Brexiteers should not fetishise Brexit for Brexit’s sake, and some hardliners do themselves no favours by pretending that everything is fantastic.



But then ask people what they are willing to compromise on to achieve a cosier EU relationship. Ripping up paperwork for producers is great, but at what cost?

Taxpayers footing ­discount tuition fees for ­European students in Britain? Frittering away our fishing waters for the next 12 years?

I laughed over the weekend when a former Labour adviser popped up on telly to cheer Burnham’s deal because it would make life easier for Brits with holiday homes in France.

And sure, now they can take their poodle on the Dover ferry with fewer checks.

That one is for you, ­people of Makerfield!



But if you think the rows of the last few days have been unsettlingly familiar, you ain’t seen nothing yet.

As Farage put it to me in an interview last week, the PM has “let the genie out of the bottle” with his promise to “brainstorm” options for Britain’s longer-term future with the EU.

Ever since our motormouth PM flashed some ankle on rejoining entirely, the Remainiacs in his party have emerged from the woodwork.

Disgracefully, this has even included recent Cabinet ­ministers like David Lammy and Rachel Reeves, who are now saying the opposite of what they did some months ago.

Their shameful hypocrisy is one of the reasons trust in ­politics is so low, and it will plunge even lower as the referendum is gradually unpicked.



Not least because Brexit will now consume ­British politics once again.

Old bands on both sides are being reformed, and old ­arguments are being re-run and re-run.

All while the small boats keep coming, the welfare bill keeps rising and the economy keeps sputtering.

Last week we had the ­Milburn review, tomorrow we have the report into disability benefits.

These are things the British state should be putting its shoulder to fixing, along with our broken asylum ­system, rather than time- travelling back to 2016.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It is ironic that a government that so often hides behind ­consultations is beginning to ignore the biggest consultation in our history.

Governing is about priorities, and the risk is that Burnham has got his so spectacularly wrong that voters end up ­giving him a real piece of their mind.

News.title: Children among 19 rushed to hospital ‘with carbon monoxide poisoning’ as worshippers collapse during church service
News.content:
GAS HORROR Children among 19 rushed to hospital ‘with carbon monoxide poisoning’ as worshippers collapse during church service







Next

CHILDREN are among 19 worshippers rushed to hospital with suspected carbon monoxide poisoning after attending a church service in Germany.

Several people collapsed while visiting a castle chapel in Bavaria’s Allgäu region, with four said to be in a serious condition after the incident.

All 56 attendees were said to be affected by carbon monoxide, which has been blamed on a faulty heater.

Emergency services were called at around 10.50am, with six fire engines carrying approximately 50 firefighters rushing to the scene.





They were joined by paramedics, police and a rescue helicopter, with more than 120 personnel deployed to the Priestly Fraternity of St Peter.

Worshippers began complaining of breathing difficulties and nausea during the service.

Firefighters later detected a “very high concentration of carbon monoxide” inside the chapel.

Police believe that a heater that had been bought recently malfunctioned after being turned on hours before the service.

Kempten Police said: “Based on current information, the heater’s automatic shut-off mechanism did not function properly due to a technical malfunction or an operating error.”

A 70-year-old church official reportedly turned the heater on at around 6am to warm the chapel up ahead of worshippers arriving.

The device was fitted with a safety mechanism that should have shut it down if carbon monoxide levels became too high.

Carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless, and tasteless poisonous gas that stops your blood from carrying enough oxygen to vital organs.



It manifests in flu-like symptoms such as headaches, dizziness, nausea, tiredness, confusion, and breathlessness.

Severe poisoning can cause unconsciousness, permanent damage or death.

It comes after seven people were rushed to hospital with carbon monoxide poisoning after a gas leak in Alzey, Germany.

Around 40 residents had to be evacuated from their homes after a faulty hot water boiler is believed to have caused the leak.

In a more serious incident, around 300 people had to be evacuated from a swingers club in the country in 2019.



Several of the guests reported feeling unwell and had to be taken out of the building mid-party.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Firefighters in the town of Hattingen, between Dortmund and Duesseldorf, said about 300 swingers were brought to safety.

The swingers, many clad just in bathrobes as they left the club, were taken on buses to be examined by medics

News.title: Six former PMs warn Andy Burnham against reigniting Brexit battle with new EU deal
News.content:
Next

SIX ex-PMs have all warned Andy Burnham about creating a new wave of Brexit rows — after he agreed to closer EU links.

The Prime Minister was told to “stop fighting arguments of the past” as his predecessors voiced concerns.



Theresa May, who led the first exit talks with Brussels after the historic 2016 vote, said she was “aghast” at Mr Burnham’s actions.

She said: “I’m afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on.”



She claimed Mr Burnham wants to “pat people on the head” by suggesting: “Remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong didn’t you. So have another go and come out with the right answer.”

Remainer David Cameron, who quit as PM after the 2016 result, said Mr Burnham should avoid a “decade-long debate”.



Boris Johnson, the PM between 2019 and 2022, also said it was “madness” to escalate the Brexit issue as a priority.

Liz Truss, leader in 2022, also slammed it, saying: “The idea that the UK should once again be shackling itself to Brussels rules and regulations is sheer lunacy.”



Rishi Sunak, chief from 2022 to 2024, said he feared the impact of more Brexit debate.

He told Sky News: “It ends up being a huge distraction for Government.”

Ex-Labour PM Tony Blair is also sceptical. He said Britain should only sign up if more innovation on tech is allowed.



He told The Sunday Times: “I was painted as saying Britain should just go back and rejoin — I’m not saying that — it’s heavily conditioned.”

The comments come as Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told the BBC that “all options” will be on the table when it comes to the EU.

But Tory leader Kemi Badenoch ordered Mr Burnham to “come clean” over the deal he struck — as no treaty text had been provided.

She said: “What has Burnham agreed and what is he not telling us?”

News.title: Cops rush to US rapper Don Toliver’s gig as major incident declared & fans evacuated after ‘tear gas released in crowd’
News.content:
Next

FANS were evacuated from US rapper Don Toliver’s concert after tear gas was reportedly released in the crowd during the gig.

Cops rushed to the scene and a major incident was declared following his live performance at Manchester’s Co-op Live arena on Sunday evening.



Pictures show devastated fans heading home early as a cloud of smoke shrouds the venue and staff escort people out.

Cops have declared it a major incident, with emergency rescue teams currently working at the site.





Videos circulating online show police cars and vans circling the venue, with emergency vehicles and officers swarming the arena.

Revellers were reportedly seen rubbing their eyes, spluttering and screaming in panic as they were ushered out of the venue.



Other pictures from the aftermath show hundreds of fans standing in huddles looking confused on the venue floor.

According to the website, ticket-holders were able to enter the venue from 6.30pm onwards.

Don Toliver, whose real name is Caleb Zackery, is a 32-year-old American rapper, singer, and songwriter from Houston, Texas.



He is known for blending hip-hop, trap, psychedelic rap, and R&B, and is signed to Travis Scott‘s Cactus Jack Records together with Atlantic Records.

He is due to go on to the O2 on Monday night as part of his world tour, followed by the OVO Arena Wembley on Tuesday.

Manchester Co-op Live has a capacity of 23,500 people, making it the largest indoor arena in the UK.

Officially opened in 2024, it hosts a variety of events in entertainment, sports and music.

Greater Manchester Police said: “Officers alongside other emergency services personnel are currently in attendance following an incident at Co-op Live this evening.



“It is understood that a substance believed to be tear gas was let off in the crowd towards the end of a concert.

“All attendees are currently being safely evacuated as a precaution.

“Those showing signs of being impacted are being supported by emergency services, with no serious injuries reported.

“Please stay away from the arena whilst emergency services help those that have been at the concert safely make their way to their transport home.

“A major incident has been declared to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response.”

News.title: Blundering Burnham will bend over backwards for Brussels – even if Britain pays the price
News.content:
EU puppet







Next

SO, Prime Minister… deal or no deal?

Andy Burnham claimed a “win-win” EU reset, which will actually cost billions and do nothing to ease the cost of living, was there “in black and white”.



But the Brussels bankers insist the already one-sided agreement is dependent on him also capitulating to demands for us to subsidise EU students coming to UK universities, which could cost us more than £500million.

He inevitably will — to the detriment of our own debt-laden students — because, for people-pleaser Burnham, standing up for Britain’s interests comes a poor second to getting a pat on the head from the Eurocrats.



But now we learn the dodgy agreement may also include plans for Digital ID, despite the PM ditching that idea months ago in virtually the only cost-cutting decision of his reign so far.

Just like the Tories’ Rwanda scheme to tackle illegal immigration, which Labour ditched, it may now be discussed because his EU “friends” support it.

The PM must come clean on the full “reset” details because his dealings in Brussels look about as transparent as the Government’s questionable discussions with Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owners.

And people are only learning the truth about THOSE because of The Sun’s revelations.

Six former Prime Ministers have now expressed either unease or outright dismay over Burnham’s Brexit betrayal.

He won’t listen.



Unless Brussels thinks differently, of course, and then he’ll change his mind soon enough.

Fear we go…

REOPENING the toxic Brexit debate sadly means more deluded Remainers pretending that leaving the EU has been the root cause of all Britain’s ills.

It is as much a lie now as it was during the 2016 referendum, when Project Fear’s doom-mongers predicted economic catastrophe if we left the bloc.

In fact, Britain has recently out-performed Europe and, with the growing AI revolution and Brexit freedoms, it can go further, faster.

A glance at the sluggish economies and social unrest on the Continent dispels any idea that the EU is a utopia.



As Tory leader Kemi Badenoch says, it is an important market but it cannot be our only market.

We need to aim higher and forge stronger links with modern superpowers, not lock ourselves into the trading shackles of the past.

Too many Remainers would rather talk down our country than accept they were wrong about Britain outside the EU.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Politicians need to take off their “gloom-tinted glasses”, to quote CBI boss Rain Newton-Smith.

Then they could unleash the power of our world-beating innovators, thrusting industrialists and aspirational workers currently held back by Labour’s high-tax, low-growth, big-welfare culture.

News.title: Man lured to remote villa in Spain before being tied up and beaten in 15-hour ordeal – as two arrested over ‘kidnapping’
News.content:
'KIDNAP' HORROR Man lured to remote villa in Spain before being tied up and beaten in 15-hour ordeal – as two arrested over ‘kidnapping’







Next

A MAN has been rescued after he was allegedly lured to a remote villa, tied up, beaten and threatened with death in a horror 15-hour ordeal.

A woman he considered a friend tricked him into visiting the isolated property near Montserrat, Spain, before he was ambushed, police said.



When he arrived, the woman and two other male captors allegedly restrained him with ropes and wielded a large machete in his face.

The victim, 54, was then forced inside where he was subjected to hours of physical assaults and denied sleep, according to the Civil Guard.



His accused kidnappers also continued to threaten his life with a range of bladed weapons and batons, seen arranged on a bed in evidence pictures.

They forced the man to record several videos addressed to his family in which he claimed to be doing well.

The hope was that they would stop his relatives from becoming concerned and launching a search for him.

The man was able to briefly make contact with his family asking for help and providing clues as to his location.

After the Civil Guard were contacted, officers were able to find the villa and free the man, who had sustained injuries of varying severity.

Police said that the victim was tricked into picking up the woman he considered a friend near Montserrat in order to drive her home.



When he pulled up to the meeting point, he noticed that the woman was with a man whom he barely knew.

The pair asked him to drive them to the villa, where a third man was lying in wait.

As they arrived, the victim then knew he had been set up.

Two of the alleged perpetrators were arrested at the scene during the rescue mission.

Cops seized several large bladed weapons, along with other items believed to have been used during the kidnapping.



Those arrested – a 41-year-old woman and 54-year-old man – are accused of unlawful detention.

The kidnapping was reportedly linked to a prior conflict between the people involved.

Investigators are still trying to establish a motive behind the kidnapping and whether there were other individuals involved.

News.title: Henry Novak killler Vickrum Digwa befriends black cab rapist John Worboys in jail as monsters play cards & table tennis
News.content:
Next

HENRY Nowak’s killer Vickrum Digwa has befriended black cab rapist John Worboys on a specialist prison unit.

They play table tennis, Scrabble and cards in the Westgate Unit at HMP Frankland, Durham.



The wing is usually for lags with personality disorders — but Digwa, 23, is there mostly to shield him from harm as its inmates are kept apart from other prisoners at the high security Category A jail.

A source said: “Digwa is extremely happy that he has secured a place on the unit.



“Bizarrely, he is getting along really well with Worboys and they chat a lot and watch TV together sometimes.

“But people are pretty disgusted by their friendship and it is the talk of the jail.”

Serial rapist Worboys, 69, is serving life for attacks on 16 women.

Sources say he was moved to the unit as part of a “pathway” to a move from prison to a secure hospital such as Broadmoor.

Digwa is serving a 25-year minimum for murdering Henry, 18, in Southampton last year then falsely claiming to be a victim of racial abuse.

We told how he had previously refused to go on to the prison wing at HMP Frankland where Soham killer was fatally attacked in February.



A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Our thoughts remain with Henry Nowak’s family and friends.

“It’s right his killer received life and remains behind bars for this terrible crime.”

News.title: Preschool workers 'slipped substances' to children during naptime as lawsuit filed
News.content:
Preschool workers 'slipped substances' to children during naptime as lawsuit filed

"You can see the teacher sit down next to our client, pull the blanket up over our client's face, put her hand inside of the blanket where his mouth was, and administer something," an attorney said.

View 3 Images Two mums are suing a day care for allegedly giving their toddlers "sleeping gummies" without parental consent (Image: Andrews & Higgins)

Two mums are suing a day care for allegedly giving their toddlers "sleeping gummies" without their consent, with the incident seemingly being witnessed on a livestream during naptime.

‌



‌



Cassandra Sandoval and Priscilla Ayala said preschool workers Kiddie Academy of Orange, in California, "slipped substances" in children's drinks. They allege that their children were given sleep-inducing gummies between May and September 2026 at according to the lawsuit accessed by The California Post.

‌



The lawsuit filed on November 4 accuses the preschool and three employees of negligence, battery and emotional distress.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images The incident was witnessed on a livestream during naptime (Image: Andrews & Higgins)

Sandoval said her suspicions started when her son's sleep patterns changed. On September 4, her son, 4, allegedly asked her for the "sleeping gummies" he said he got at nap time at school. The lawsuit states she reported his comment to child care licensing authorities three days later.

‌



On September 11, Sandoval says she was watching the school's classroom livestream when she saw a teacher put an unidentified substance into her son's mouth as he lay under a blanket, according to the lawsuit.

"You can see the teacher sit down next to our client, pull the blanket up over our client's face, put her hand inside of the blanket where his mouth was, and administer something," Kimberly DeGonia, the attorney for both families, told KTLA.

‌



Former employees and other parents have also raised similar allegations, some claiming children were given more than one gummy at a time, DeGonia added.

Ayala's lawsuit describes similar concerns about her young, autistic daughter. It said that school employees repeatedly asked her for permission to give her daughter melatonin, which she refused each time. Her daughter later told her that a teacher had given her gummies anyway, the lawsuit alleges.

‌



Ayala said her daughter had nightmares, distress at night and behavioural changes while enrolled at the preschool.

View 3 Images The incident took place at Kiddie Academy of Orange in California (Image: Andrews & Higgins)

‌



The complaint further accuses the assistant director of forcefully restraining the girl during nap time to make her sleep.

A spokesperson for the Kiddie Academy told the news outlet that the company is limited in what it can say publicly as the matter is ongoing and involves children.

Article continues below

"As an independently owned and operated Kiddie Academy franchise, we care deeply about the children, families and community we serve," the spokesperson said.

The accused staff member in this case has been placed on administrative leave while the licensing investigation continues.

News.title: Louise Haigh issues warning over failed status quo on utilities like water and energy
News.content:
Louise Haigh issues warning over failed status quo on utilities like water and energy

First Secretary of State Louise Haigh will bang the drum for greater public control of essentials, which is expected to form a key plank of Andy Burnham's 10-year plan

View 2 Images Louise Haigh will says privatised utilities are failing businesses and consumers (Image: Stefan Rousseau/PA Wire)

The failed status quo on utilities like water and energy is holding Britain back, Louise Haigh will tell business chiefs today.

‌



‌



The First Secretary of State will bang the drum for greater public control of essential services, which is expected to form a key plank of Andy Burnham's 10-year plan next month. The Prime Minister has railed against a "series of wrong turns" taken in the 1980s, when Margaret Thatcher sold off core utilities, arguing it has driven up costs for the public.

‌



Ms Haigh will say privatised utilities are failing business as well as consumers as she seeks to win backing for the agenda in an address to the CBI conference in London. She is expected to say: "This government will put pragmatism and public interest ahead of failed political ideology. Public control is not anti-business - it’s about getting the foundations right, so that private enterprise can do what it does best.”

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has railed against privatisation of essential services (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham vows to unveil 10-year plan to transform Britain before Christmas READ MORE :

Lashing out at politicians for ducking difficult decisions, the she will warn that foreign governments own “significant stakes in our water, electricity and gas networks with returns paid to their taxpayers”. Ms Haigh will say: "The status quo is not the neutral, pragmatic centre ground. It’s the outlier. An exception that no other nation is trying to emulate."

‌



High energy prices, grid connection delays and water pollution are holding back growth, she will say, and point to how effective monopolies have resulted in a lack of genuine competition.

Noting that public control does not have to mean full-scale nationalisation, Ms Haigh will set out the Government’s vision for “a new partnership with private capital built on clear rules, clear expectations and a fair return on investment”.

‌



Mr Burnham has repeatedly discussed greater public control of essentials like water and energy since he came to power. In his Labour conference speech in September, he pledged to drive down energy costs with a new publicly-owned Great British Grid to overhaul the broken energy market.

The ageing grid has suffered from decades of underinvestment, with slow connections and the massive backlog to join the transmission network acting as a blocker for investment.

Article continues below

GB Grid, a new publicly-owned company, aims to speed up grid connections for businesses and drive down costs by increasing competition in the market. The PM argued that energy costs are being dictated by global turbulence, with wars in Ukraine and Iran driving up bills for households and businesses.

The Conservatives accused Labour of treating nationalisation as a “magic wand for every industry and every problem”.

News.title: 'COP31 deal failure is a betrayal of future generations while the world is on fire'
News.content:
'COP31 deal failure is a betrayal of future generations while the world is on fire'

"The UK must keep fighting for a meaningful agreement because history will judge those who put protecting profits ahead of protecting the planet"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

The world is burning, yet the politicians charged with saving it cannot even bring themselves to mention the fuels feeding the flames.

‌



‌



The collapse of a meaningful agreement at the COP31 climate summit is a disgraceful betrayal of future generations. More than 130 countries demanded a commitment to move away from fossil fuels.

‌



Instead, the proposed deal offered weasel words, empty promises, and convenient loopholes for the industries that are poisoning our planet. Thankfully, Britain, the EU and vulnerable nations refused to swallow this shameful surrender.

‌



For countries already suffering devastating floods, droughts and rising seas, these negotiations are a matter of survival. Yet wealthy fossil fuel interests continue to wield extraordinary influence while the world’s poorest pay the heaviest price.

Every year brings fresh warnings, worsening disasters and another summit promising action. And still the political courage falls desperately short. The UK must keep fighting for a meaningful agreement because history will judge those who put protecting profits ahead of protecting the planet.

The King

Tyson Fury conquered the world in the ring, only to find himself fighting a much more terrifying battle outside of it.

‌



The heavyweight champion had achieved everything he dreamed of, yet behind the glory was a man overwhelmed by darkness, hearing voices urging him to take his own life. His heartbreaking account of mental illness reveals how even the strongest among us can be brought to their knees.

And how love, professional help and the courage to speak openly can offer a way back. His wife, Paris, and their seven children have been his greatest source of strength.

‌



Fury has won some extraordinary fights, but his battle to rebuild his life may be his greatest achievement. His message to his children, and to us all, is simple: Never suffer in silence.

It stinks

Britain’s rivers are drowning in sewage while the watchdog paid to protect them is missing in action.

Article continues below

Despite billions in funding, the Environment Agency attends just one in six pollution reports.

The failure of regulation stinks almost as badly as the pollution.

News.title: Andy Burnham accuses Tories of 'letting down the country' over their botched Brexit deals
News.content:
Andy Burnham accuses Tories of 'letting down the country' over their botched Brexit deals

The Prime Minister will face down his Brexiteer critics in Parliament after finalising agreements with Brussels on Friday to ease the impact of the disastrous Tory exit deal

View 2 Images Andy Burnham will sell his Brexit reset deal to MPs on Monday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham will say his new Brexit deal offers change from the "broken status quo" and accuse his Tory predecessors of being unable to admit they "let down the country".

‌



‌



In a statement to MPs, the PM will face down his Brexiteer critics to say agreements made in Brussels on Friday offered hope the next decade can be better than the one before, adding £17bn a year to the economy by 2040.

‌



"The ability to draw a line on a decade of drift and division is in our hands and I believe we should take it," he will say. "This is a choice between a broken status quo or change."

‌



He will add: "Those Tory voices from the past and present trying to close this issue down are doing so because they know they let down the country and can’t face up to that.”

The Prime Minister finalised agreements with Brussels on Friday to ease the paperwork nightmare faced by business following the disastrous Tory exit deal. He will also visit a Morrisons as it gears up for the busy Christmas period, to discuss the impact on food and drink exports as he champions the everyday impact of closer ties with the EU.

Last night, the PM said: “We’re cutting the cost of doing business, backing British companies to grow and taking pressure off the cost of food for families at the checkout. But this is also about something bigger, restoring hope and opportunity to a generation of young people who have too often felt that the odds are stacked against them."

‌

View 2 Images Andy Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel with Mayor of Rotterdam Carola Schouten at a Dutch Eredivisie match between Sparta Rotterdam and AZ Alkmaar on Sunday (Image: ANP/Shutterstock)

‌



Theresa May fires off Brexit warning to Andy Burnham as PM pledges closer EU ties READ MORE :

Rami Baitiéh, Morrisons Chief Executive, said: "Removing these trade barriers will help tackle the cost of living challenge and lighten the load on shoppers."

But Mr Burnham's big ambition is to go further, with a pledge to "brainstorm" ideas with Brussels for closer integration over the coming months. The prospect of the UK rejoining the EU, which the PM has not ruled out, has triggered an avalanche of dire warnings from his predecessors.

‌



Theresa May said she was "aghast" and urged Mr Burnham to abandon thoughts of reversing Brexit. The former Tory Prime Minister, whose premiership was wrecked by rows over the EU divorce, said: "Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on".

Sir Tony Blair also waded into the row, telling the Sunday Times that any return to the bloc should be conditional on reform of the EU. "I was painted as saying Britain should just go back and rejoin - I'm not saying that - it's heavily conditioned," the former Labour PM said.

‌



Boris Johnson and David Cameron have both warned Mr Burnham against trying to undo Brexit in recent weeks.

While there is some nervousness among Labour MPs, including in Cabinet, over the idea of possibly rejoining the bloc, the prospect has been hailed by senior Labour figures, including former Foreign Secretary David Lammy, ex-Chancellor Rachel Reeves and Peter Kyle, the former Business Secretary.

‌



Europe Minister Hamish Falconer suggested on Sunday that there would be a second referendum if going back into the EU was on the table. He said: “Everything will be in the end voted on by the British public.

"We are talking, as the Prime Minister was clear, about the long-term. We will have a general election before then. People will be able to express their views.”

Article continues below

Friday's Brussels summit was dominated by a row over demands for cuts to tuition fees paid by EU students in the UK, which has not yet been agreed. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband insisted it won't scupper the wider deal, which will be brought to Parliament this week under what No10 has dubbed the "cutting costs bill".

The Conservatives and Reform have both vowed to repeal it if they win the next election.

News.title: Don Toliver fans scream 'I can't breathe' and 'it burns' after substance released at Manchester gig
News.content:
Don Toliver fans scream 'I can't breathe' and 'it burns' after substance released at Manchester gig

Witnesses said the standing area of the venue was cleared at around 10pm this evening as Don Toliver was performing on his NITROUS tour, amid claims a smoke canister was thrown

'Major incident' declared as suspected tear gas set off at Manchester concert

This is the horrifying moment fans screamed "I can't breathe" and "it burns" after an unknown substance was released at a concert in Manchester.

‌



‌



Fans were evacuated from the UK's largest indoor music venue on Sunday night after what was thought to be tear gas was let off. Video shows police and other emergency services outside Co-op Live in Manchester.

‌



Witnesses said the standing area was evacuated at 10pm on Sunday (November 22) as Don Toliver performed on the venue's B stage, reports the Manchester Evening News.

‌



Police have confirmed the arena was evacuated after tear gas was released in the crowd during the performance. A video taken from the floor standing area showed the moment fans started coughing and using their t-shirts to cover their face and nose as they make a quick exit when the gas was let off.

The person filming is heard saying: "What the f*** was that smell bro? I can't breathe bro. Bro what was that?!" Someone in the background can be heard adding: "It burns."

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

‌



Another clip, taken from a balcony area, shows a gap in the crowd open up as gig-goers began moving away from the tear gas while Don Toliver continues to perform. The show was stopped shortly afterwards.

Jessica Gannon was at the event. She took to X to say she was "devastated" by the incident. She posted: "[I] w as at Don Toliver tonight in Manchester and I’m devastated that someone ruined the show. At least we are safe but genuinely annoyed at the security at Co-op Live as I got challenged for a portable charge yet you let someone in with tear gas. I want a refund."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

There have not been any reported injuries at this stage, a Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said : "Emergency services are currently in attendance following an incident at Co-op Live this evening. It is understood that a substance believed to be tear gas was let off in the crowd towards the end of a concert.

‌



"All attendees are currently being safely evacuated as a precaution. Those showing signs of being impacted are being supported by emergency services, with thankfully no serious injuries reported.

"Please stay away from the arena whilst emergency services help those that have been at the concert safely make their way to their transport home. A major incident has been declared to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response."

‌



View 2 Images The moment fans start coughing and reach to cover their mouths when tear gas is released at a Don Toliver show (Image: TikTok/TheKidTKR)

They also show more than a dozen emergency service vehicles, including police and ambulance, parked outside the entrance of the arena, and more emergency service vehicles arriving at the scene of the arena as fans stream out of the venue.

‌



Another showed the moment fans were told the show was over. A man, dressed in black, can been seen on-stage holding a microphone while the house lights are on.

View 2 Images Emergency services outside the Co-op Live arena on Sunday after tear gas was released in the crowd (Image: @WillTooley/X)

‌



He tells thousands of fans: "Due to unforeseen circumstances, the show is now finished. In your own time, please make your way to the nearest exit. If you require medical assistance, please speak to a member of staff or visit the level zero concourse."

Article continues below

The 23,500-seat venue is Britain's largest music venue, and has hosted acts like Paul McCartney, Hans Zimmer, and Charli XCX. It has also hosted the Brit Awards, and is due to stage Britain's first NBA basketball game in the coming years.

The Greater Manchester Mayor's office has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Ohio baby shower disaster as three dead and one injured in horror shooting
News.content:
Ohio baby shower disaster as three dead and one injured in horror shooting

Officials have identified two of the victims as 17-year-old Leasia England and 45-year-old Jayson Townsend. Police said Townsend was the father of the woman for whom the baby shower was being held

View Image Parma police officers responding to the scene of a shooting (Image: WEWS/NEWS 5 via AP)

Three people were killed and one was injured at an Ohio baby shower, according to police.

‌



‌



Officers responded to a shooting Saturday evening at Pandora's Magical Events Venue in Parma, about 10 miles south of Cleveland, a police news release said. Authorities said one of the shooters, a 29-year-old man, was taken into custody, but he wasn't immediately charged.

‌



Detectives were trying to determine whether the man was the aggressor or acting in self-defense, police spokesman Scott Traxler said. A second suspected shooter, a 19-year-old man, was one of the people killed, police said.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Officials have identified two of the victims as 17-year-old Leasia England and 45-year-old Jayson Townsend. Police said Townsend was the father of the woman for whom the baby shower was being held; she was not injured.

‌



Officials haven't released the names of the 19-year-old suspected shooter who was killed, or a 39-year-old woman who was shot in the leg.

Preliminary information indicates that the 19-year-old man was the father of the unborn baby, and witnesses told police that he was not invited to the shower, Traxler said. The man in custody appears to be a relative of the expectant mother.

Article continues below

Both firearms involved in the shooting were recovered by police, officials said. Detectives were reviewing surveillance video and witnesses' statements on Sunday to determine what led to the violent confrontation, Traxler said. Ballistics testing might be required to determine which gun shot each victim.

Prosecutors will eventually determine whether the man in custody should be charged with a crime, officials said.

News.title: Iran brutally trolls Donald Trump while boasting about new weapon at underground 'missile city'
News.content:
Iran brutally trolls Donald Trump while boasting about new weapon at underground 'missile city'

Footage released by Tehran shows the new weapon being stored at an 'underground missile city' after Trump claimed Iran's missile programme had been severely weakened

View Image Iran has unveiled its new missile launcher at an 'underground missile city'

Iran has taunted Donald Trump by showing off a new missile launcher hidden inside its vast underground "missile city".

‌



‌



Footage released by Tehran shows the weapon being stored at a subterranean military base, with the system capable of firing two missiles at once. The display appears to be a warning to Trump that Iran still has weapons at its disposal if the US president decided to launch fresh attacks against the country. It also raised questions over his claims that Iran's military has been effectively defeated.

‌



The newly revealed launcher uses liquid-fuel missiles, which can be fired straight upwards and allow operators to control their speed and direction. Iran previously showed off another launcher capable of firing two solid-fuel missiles at once on April 7. However, this is the first time it has publicly revealed the new liquid-fuel system.

‌



The video, posted on X by Iranian news agency Fars, shows senior commanders from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) visiting what Tehran calls an "underground missile city". IRGC chief commander Maj Gen Ahmad Vahidi was briefed on the military's readiness and its recent missile developments during the visit.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



The facility's location has not been revealed, but its underground position could help shield weapons from airstrikes and make them harder for enemy forces to find and destroy. Brig Gen Seyyed Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC's aerospace force, claimed Iran's military capabilities had grown significantly.

"We have integrated 'surprises' and highly effective assets into our combat structure," he said during the unveiling of the new launcher.

‌



Footage showed Mousavi travelling through the tunnels in a Jeep, passing by other weapons, including the newly unveiled double launcher. A message displayed on the clip also appeared to take a swipe at Washington, reading: "At the White House, being [a] b******d isn't an insult, it's a qualification standard."

The footage is likely part of Tehran's efforts to push back against US claims that its missile programme has been severely weakened by the conflict.

‌



Trump has described the war as a "very big victory" and sait it was "effectively over," suggesting more US attacks were unlikely. But he also warned that US forces remain "locked and loaded" if the situation changes.

The president also ordered Vice-President JD Vance to halt negotiations with Iran over its nuclear programme.

Article continues below

Israel has also warned the White House that Iran is making progress with its chemical and biological weapons programmes.

News.title: Psychologist's five-minute technique 'makes you fall asleep faster'
News.content:
Psychologist's five-minute technique 'makes you fall asleep faster'

Roughly one in three people in the UK struggle with sleep or insomnia

Struggling to sleep? A psychologist has shared a simple five-minute technique that she says could help you fall asleep faster.

‌



Dr Ritz Birah, consultant counselling psychologist at Panda London, has explained how a quick bedtime brain dump can help park worries, clear your mind and take the pressure out of falling asleep. Dr Ritz Birah (Ritika Suk Birah) is an HCPC-registered Consultant Counselling Psychologist who serves on the Sleep Expert Panel at Panda London, advising on sleep habits, brain health, and wellbeing.

She says that when people are struggling to sleep, the instinct is often to try harder. But she says that psychologically, that effort can sometimes become part of the problem. To help struggling Brits, Dr Ritz Birah has shared four techniques to take some of the pressure out of sleep, with one taking just five minutes.

1. The 5-minute “park it” technique

Dr Ritz Birah says that one of the most counterintuitive things you can do at bedtime is give yourself permission not to solve anything. She says our brains often use the first quiet moment of the day to surface everything we have not yet processed: tomorrow's tasks, something somebody said, the conversation we need to have, or the thing we are worried we might forget.

She explained: "Try a five-minute bedtime brain dump. Keep a notebook beside the bed and use a simple ‘park it’ technique. Write down the tasks or worries on your mind, then note one next step for tomorrow. You are telling the brain: I have captured this, I know what I am going to do about it, and I do not need to keep rehearsing it tonight.

"Sometimes the best way to quieten a busy brain is not to tell it to stop thinking, but to reassure it that nothing important is being forgotten."

2. Try to stay awake

Dr Ritz explains: "This might seem like the last thing you should do when you’re struggling to sleep, but rather than forcing yourself to fall asleep, deliberately allow yourself to stay awake instead. This is the principle behind a psychological technique known as paradoxical intention."

She added: "When we start thinking, ‘I have to sleep now’, sleep can begin to feel like a task we have to perform. That pressure creates frustration and alertness, which are exactly the opposite of what we need."

Instead, allow yourself to lie quietly without trying to make sleep happen, she recommends. Don’t check the clock or calculate how much sleep you have left.

"If sleepiness arrives, let it," she said. "The aim isn’t to stay awake all night, it is to remove some of the performance anxiety around falling asleep."
