View Image About 1 in 3 people in the UK experience trouble getting to sleep or staying asleep

3. Give your brain something random to think about

If your mind becomes busy at bedtime, cognitive shuffle offers an alternative to trying to empty it completely. The technique involves moving your attention between unrelated, neutral objects or images, such as picturing a book, then a banana, then a bicycle.

She said: "Trying to force the mind to go blank can become another form of effort. Instead, cognitive shuffling gives the brain just enough to focus on without creating a storyline, problem to solve or emotionally loaded train of thought. I particularly like this technique for people whose minds immediately jump into planning mode when their head hits the pillow."

4. Get out of bed when you can't sleep

When you’re struggling to sleep, getting out of a warm bed can feel completely counterproductive, but lying there becoming increasingly frustrated can teach the brain that bed is somewhere we stay awake and worry, Dr Ritz Birah said.

"This is why stimulus control is used within CBT for insomnia," she said. "If you have been awake for a while and feel yourself becoming frustrated or increasingly alert, get up and do something quiet in low light, such as reading a few pages of a book or listening to something calming.

"Then return to bed when you notice yourself becoming sleepy again. You are helping to rebuild the association between getting into bed and actually sleeping."

News.title: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
News.content:
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.

The deal is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.

He will also call it "the single biggest growth measure to be delivered in this parliament" - repeating his claim it could add Â£17bn to the British economy.

The PM described it on Friday as a "win-win" deal with the EU on British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. But since then a host of politicians have criticised the plan, with one former prime minister urging him to "move on" from Brexit.

Burnham believes the agreement reached in Brussels "holds out the very real prospect that the next decade can be a much better one for Britain than the one we have just lived through".

"The ability to draw a line on a decade of drift and division is in our hands and I believe we should take it," he will say in his speech.

He will also paint the move as a choice "between easing pressure on the cost of living or allowing food prices to rise further" and "creating opportunities for young people or denying them".

He believes polling suggests the UK public "want closer ties" with the EU and the deal "delivers that".

But his announcement on Friday was greeted with a chorus of criticism from a number of opposing political figures.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said the deal was unfair because UK farmers would now have to follow rules made by Brussels.

She questioned the Treasury's analysis, which Burnham said suggested the deal "will add up to 0.5%" to UK gross domestic product and he described it as a "Â£17bn boost to the British economy".

Badenoch accused him of having "plucked that figure out of the air" before saying "the only modelling I've seen that even talks about that figure says it's actually 0.0%".

Meanwhile Reform UK leader Farage called the deal a "very good day for the EU", before adding: "A good day to try and humiliate the one member state that actually had the courage to say, 'We don't need to be part of you, we can govern our own country'."

Farage, who was a leading figure in the 2016 campaign to get Britain out of the EU, added in a social media post: "Like every prime minister before him, Burnham is a total fraud. Only Reform will stop the endless betrayal of the British people."

Over the weekend former prime ministers including Theresa May, Sir Tony Blair and Rishi Sunak also criticised the EU-UK deal.

May, who presided over three years of Brexit negotiations during her premiership, said she was "aghast" by the deal and warned Andy Burnham should "move on".

Sir Tony, who was a prominent opponent of leaving the EU, told The Sunday Times Britain should only rejoin the EU if it reforms, and allows more innovation on technology.

Badenoch will use her speech at the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) annual conference on Monday to criticise Burnham's EU deal.

She will accuse the prime minister of securing a "terrible" deal and will say he should be "aiming a lot higher" in terms of driving growth.

Farage will tell the same conference that establishing closer ties with the EU would be a "disaster" for British businesses.

Rejoining the EU will hit the small firms that do not even trade with Europe with more red tape, more compliance costs, more Brussels rules they never asked for, he is expected to say.

On Friday, the PM said that over the coming months both sides will "seek to conduct an informal brainstorming process" to look at the options for the UK's "long-term relationship" with the EU.

He was also clear that the deal he struck was "probably the limit of what we can achieve in this Parliament, given what needs to be done to implement it".

He added: "But we want to inform the Parliament after this one, so that decisions can be taken about that long-term relationship."

News.title: Can AI spot breast cancer earlier? NHS launches world's largest trial to find out
News.content:
Nearly 700,000 women across the UK are to be invited to join the world's largest trial of how artificial intelligence can help in breast cancer screening.

AI will be used to review mammograms to see if it can improve early cancer detection and ease the workload of clinical staff, while not over-diagnosing women unnecessarily.

Recruitment to the EDITH trial , externalhas already begun at Cambridge University Hospitals, the first of 30 sites across the UK.

Women aged 50 to 71 are invited for routine breast screening every three years in the UK, and more than two million attend annually.

At present two NHS experts look at each breast X-ray, known as a mammogram, but in the trial, one of the human readers will be replaced by AI.

Several smaller studies have already shown that AI can improve breast cancer detection rates, but researchers running this trial say they need to be sure it won't cause harm by leading to women being recalled unnecessarily for further tests.

Sian Taylor-Phillips, professor of population health at the University of Warwick, and co-chief investigator said: "AI-assisted technology could help improve early cancer detection but we want to avoid the overdiagnosis of milder disease that would never have caused symptoms."

Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in the UK, with around 59,000 cases diagnosed each year.

About a third of these are picked up by routine mammograms, usually at an early stage when they can be more easily treated.

It's estimated the screening programme helps prevent around 1,300 deaths a year.

News.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer after 14 hours, in overnight Russian strikes on Dymer, in the Kyiv region, that killed nine people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.

Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.

Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.

Response teams including police, explosive technicians, dog handlers and medics are continuing with rescue efforts.

In a telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.

Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

News.title: Will it snow this week? Mild Atlantic air collides with cold air across the UK
News.content:
The UK is in the grip of the coldest spell of autumn so far, but will it result in snow?

Mild Atlantic air that arrived in the south-west of the UK over the weekend is pushing eastwards, coming up against colder Arctic air.

In this setup, the meteorological ingredients for snow are in place; however, there remains uncertainty in where the boundary between the cold and mild air will sit.

Even small shifts in temperature could make a significant difference to what falls from the sky and, crucially, the chances of snow.

News.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
News.content:
Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.

A string of black and white photos shared by the Flowers singer on Instagram showed the pair kissing while surrounded by white roses.

Her mother, Trisha Cyrus, and sister, Noah Cyrus, could be seen in the background of one image. Her father Billy Ray Cyrus was not in the picture but was at the ceremony with his partner, actress Liz Hurley.

Grammy-winning Cyrus, 33, wore a white silk dress designed by Anthony Vaccarello for Saint Laurent, while 28-year-old drummer Morando said "I do" in a black suit from the same fashion house.

In one of the photographs, which was the first in a series of images shared by the singer in an Instagram post, the newly weds posed next to a golden retriever.

The post was captioned with "M+M" followed by a white heart and the ceremony date, 21 November.

Miley's sister Brandi Cyrus, singer Doechii and fashion designer Donatella Versace were among those to congratulate the couple in the comments.

The ceremony reportedly took place at a resort formerly owned by Fly Me To The Moon singer Frank Sinatra.

Guests stuck to an all-black dress code, according to reports.

News.title: Russell Brand's wife says she'll honour prison rules after message row
News.content:
The wife of disgraced comedian Russell Brand says she will "honour" the rules of his prison, a week after she read a message from her husband proclaiming his innocence.

Laura Brand, 39, drew criticism from ministers after reading out the message from inside HMP Littlehey last week, prompting the government to seek to have the episode removed from social media platforms.

She said on Sunday that she would continue to defend her family and herself over her portrayal in the media during the couple's weekly podcast, which she now presents alone.

Russell Brand, 51, is currently serving a 10-and-half-year prison sentence after being convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

"Last week's episode drew a considerable amount of attention," Laura Brand said during this week's episode of Sunday Service.

"Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that."

In the relayed message last week, Russell Brand had said he was "not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for".

Laura Brand said she had spoken to him at the Cambridgeshire prison and said he was "OK".

Russell Brand was found guilty of raping a woman at his home in 2009, as well as three counts of sexual assault against three other women.

Further allegations have since been reported about him and some have called for consent laws to be revised.

His conviction has renewed conversation about safeguarding in the media industry, and whether some celebrities are still able to use their fame to prey on women and then silence them.

Ministers have pointed out that inmates are prohibited from making statements that are likely to cause their victims distress and have said Brand's message was being investigated.

A woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16, but who was not among the women whose accusations led to his conviction, said his prison message was "upsetting" and "really shocking".

The government attempted to have the podcast removed from YouTube, but this was refused by its owner Google. Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged social media companies to "show some decency and take these videos down".

On Sunday, Laura Brand also said that Sunday Service would be a place where she would "continue to be proud to be a wife, a mother and a woman defending her family at a time when the media's image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny".

She expressed feeling a mixture of "grief", "absence", "desolation" and "loneliness" since her husband's imprisonment.

News.title: Manchester Co-op Live evacuated after suspected tear gas incident
News.content:
Thousands of people were evacuated from a concert in Manchester on Sunday night after tear gas was believed to have been let off in the crowd.

The incident happened towards the end of US rapper Don Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena at about 22:00.

Greater Manchester Police said no serious injuries were reported and those affected were treated by emergency services.

The force said a major incident had been declared "to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response".

Footage on social media showed emergency services converge on the 23,500-capacity arena, while some concertgoers were seen coughing as they streamed out of the venue.

Police said the substance let off was believed to be tear gas.

News.title: Energy bills will soar - here's how you can ease the pain
News.content:
Moving to a fixed energy tariff means the price you are charged per unit of gas or electricity does not change every three months, although the total bill will still vary depending on how much energy you use.

The trouble is that it is very difficult to work out whether a fixed deal is a good deal at the moment, for those renewing fixed deals or looking for one for the first time.

Some fixed deals are available at unit prices below the next forecast price cap level. But should energy prices fall sharply then a longer-term fix might not seem such good value compared with the price cap.

So consumer group Which? also recommends paying close attention to any exit fees when picking a fixed deal. If variable prices fall below your fixed rate and you want to get out of it before the end of your agreement period, you may have to pay a hefty sum.

Before you fix, consumer website MoneySavingExpert advises you look at all the deals available, not just what your own supplier is offering.

News.title: Boss of British Gas owners Centrica 'hugely concerned' over impact of soaring energy bills
News.content:
The boss of British Gas owner Centrica says he is "hugely concerned" about the impact the expected jump in energy bills in January will have on consumers.

Chris O'Shea told the BBC he thought the number of people unable or unwilling to pay their energy bills would rise when prices go up in the new year.

The new energy price cap to take effect from January will be announced on Wednesday and consultancy Cornwall Insight has forecast it will jump by Â£443 a year for a typical household.

The government has said some households will get Â£100 to help with energy bills, but Citizens Advice said it was a "drop in the ocean" while one pressure group called for action on "inflated energy firm profits".

Speaking to the Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, O'Shea said the predictions for a "substantial increase" in bills from January were "materially correct", adding that the first quarter of the year was the time when most energy was consumed.

"That's right at the point where people will be paying for Christmas and the like. So I am hugely concerned," he said.

O'Shea added there was a "massive problem" with people not paying their bills in the UK, with some not able to pay their bills and an "increasing number of people that are choosing not to pay their bills".

He said the collective impact of that was that "every single electricity consumer, is paying about Â£1.50, Â£1.60 a week to cover the cost of people that are not paying their bills, and it's just going to get worse when bills go up".

The amount owed to energy suppliers by households hit Â£5bn in the April to June period, according to energy regulator Ofgem.

News.title: Theresa May 'aghast' at Burnham's EU plans and says 'Brexit is done'
News.content:
Former Prime Minister Theresa May has warned Andy Burnham he should "move on" from Brexit, telling the BBC she is "aghast" the prime minister could be considering rejoining the EU.

At the Brussels summit this week the PM said he wanted to "brainstorm" options for the future relationship between Britain and the trading bloc.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Baroness May, who spent three years negotiating an EU exit deal, said: "Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."

May claimed Burnham "wants to pat people on the head" by suggesting: "Remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you. So have another go and come out with the right answer."

May, who was prime minister between 2016 and 2019 urged Burnham to "just get on with" today's challenges rather than re-opening the conversation around being in the European Union.

Before becoming PM she had campaigned to stay in the EU, but when in No 10 she presided over three years of tortuous negotiations.

The deal she concluded was rejected by MPs. She was forced to quit and was replaced by Boris Johnson in 2019.

Telling Burnham to "move on", she said: "What I saw was that the extent of those negotiations, the hours that have to be put in - it's across the whole of government.

"It's not just prime ministerial time, cabinet ministers' time, officials' time, to-ing and fro-ing on those negotiations. Because you have to negotiate hard in order to make sure that you're getting out what you want.

"And that's one of the reasons why I look slightly aghast at what Andy Burnham is talking about, further negotiations of going into the EU. And also we, as a country, we voted for Brexit.

"When I was prime minister I was very clear, we should deliver on that vote. So I'm afraid my message to him really is, you know, people voted for Brexit. Brexit is done. Just accept Brexit and move on."

Warning against another vote, May told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg: "I almost think this is what Andy Burnham is saying to the British people, sort of patting them on the head.

"He wants to pat them on their head and say, you know what, remember that vote? Well, you got it wrong, didn't you? So have another go and come out with the right answer.

"Or what he thinks is the right answer. But as I say, let's just get on with making sure the UK is as strong economically, in security terms, and in terms of opportunities for people as it can be."

Speaking to the BBC back in 2023, she said the UK "would have been better off if MPs had backed her deal to leave the European Union".

Her deal had included the prospect of a vote on holding a second referendum, and a vote on a temporary customs union, as well as promises on workers' rights and environmental protection.

May claimed her plan was thwarted by "hardline" Brexit-supporting MPs and those who wanted to remain in the EU.

News.title: Tories would scrap Burnham's deal with EU, deputy leader says
News.content:
Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart has said his party would scrap the deal agreed between the UK and the European Union on Friday, if the Tories win the next general election.

The agreement signed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham covers a youth travel scheme, emissions trading and British food exports.

The government has argued scrapping most checks on British food exports will cut costs for businesses and could bring down prices for shoppers.

Burghart told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme the deal was "a dog's dinner", which would not lead to lower prices in the shops and would mean the UK "gives up our ability to set our own rules".

Under the agreement, the UK will also have to follow some EU regulations.

Burghart acknowledged the deal would reduce some trade "friction" but he said it would put a "massive additional burden on the 90% of farmers that don't do any trade with the EU".

Pressed over whether the Conservatives were committed to scrapping the deal if the party wins the next general election, Burghart said: "I don't think that there will be positive outcomes, and yes, we would scrap it."

He added: "I also don't think it is a good idea for a country like Britain to hand over control of its rules to another power and have no say over how those rules are created right into the future."

Food retailers have welcomed the deal, saying it will cut costs, reduce bureaucracy and remove barriers to trade.

However, they have not committed to cutting prices as a direct result of the changes.

The British Retail Consortium has said it does not expect prices on supermarket shelves to fall in response to the deal.

It has said upward pressures on prices remain and will not be alleviated by the agreement.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband insisted the deal "reduces pressure on trading costs", adding: "They're the things that go into prices."

"It will reduce the costs that the retailers face, all of that Brexit red tape, millions of forms that they were having to fill in, frankly pointlessly, as a result of the bad deal that we had," he told the BBC.

Challenged that the UK was also giving up some powers to set regulations itself, Miliband argued businesses were already "rule takers" from Brussels if they wanted to sell into the European market.

"So they have to abide by the rules of the European Union. But at the same time, because we are not integrated into that market for food and agricultural products, they have to fill in a whole bunch of forms... to confirm that they're observing the right standards, which is frankly crackers," he said.

Under the deal, he said the UK would "be able to shape decisions" for the first time.

News.title: RAF's next fighter jet could be last crewed combat plane, air chief says
News.content:
Britain's next-generation fighter jet could be the last crewed combat aircraft the UK builds, the head of the RAF has said.

Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth, said Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled, uncrewed aircraft would "transform military aviation".

His comments refer to the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a partnership between the UK, Italy and Japan to develop a sixth-generation fighter jet, expected to enter service by 2035.

The aircraft, commonly known as Tempest, is expected to provide speed stealth, use advanced sensors and even AI to assist the human pilot when they are overwhelmed, or under extreme stress.

Writing in the Telegraph, external, Sir Harv said the GCAP aircraft was "perhaps the last crewed fighter we will ever build", not because people would become less important, but because advances in technology were changing the nature of air combat.

He said AI and machines would take on "the most dangerous tasks instead of humans", while stressing that technology should enhance human judgement and "not replace accountability". He added: "Uncrewed fighter jets will start flying in UK airspace next year. This is exciting and necessary in equal measure."

Sir Harv also said the RAF of the future would combine Typhoons and F-35s with autonomous systems.

The programme was announced in 2022 by the UK, Italy and Japan, which are jointly developing the aircraft. In July, the three countries signed a Â£4.6bn contract covering the next phase of its design through industry joint venture Edgewing.

According to GCAP, the aircraft will be powered by advanced data processing and artificial intelligence, while also featuring enhanced stealth technology. The UK government says the project already supports 3,500 jobs and 1,000 apprenticeships.

Canada was granted "observer nation" status in July, giving it privileged access to the programme without a decision-making role.

In October, Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, said the UK government would "seek to progress" Germany joining GCAP. He said the partnership could also support cooperation on issues including "countering hybrid attacks" and "countering interference in our democratic processes".

News.title: BBC apologises for 'any offence caused' by Strictly noise disruption
News.content:
The BBC has apologised "for any offence caused" after lewd audio was heard during the live broadcast of Strictly Come Dancing.

A recording of sex noises appeared to be playing from the audience in Blackpool's Tower Ballroom as judge Motsi Mabuse gave feedback early in Saturday's episode. She paused before joking: "It's not me."

At the end of the programme, presenter Emma Willis apologised to viewers "if you heard any audio disruptions". A BBC spokesperson also issued an apology and said it was "investigating how this happened".

Lancashire police said it was assessing whether any criminal offences may have taken place, after receiving a formal complaint and a mobile phone being seized.

The moment was streamed on social media by content creator Daniel Jarvis, whose videos include pranks. He appeared to place a phone call before the audio began playing in the ballroom, and suggested he was trying to target judge Craig Revel Horwood for his "bullying".

Jarvis has previously claimed he was responsible for sex noises disrupting Match of the Day in 2023.

Willis told viewers: "Before we see the judges' leaderboard, we'd like to apologise if you heard any audio disruptions earlier in tonight's show and for any offence caused."

News.title: Widow fears losing home built by husband after support payments end
News.content:
Every room in Lauren's family home reminds her of her late husband.

A self-employed builder, Andy carried out much of the work on the property himself, helping create the house where the couple raised their four children.

Now, more than two years after his death from cancer, Lauren fears she may struggle to keep it.

The financial support that helped her cover mortgage payments and household bills has ended, leaving her facing uncertainty as she prepares to remortgage the property.

"I don't want to uproot my children," she said. "They've already been through too much the last two and a half years."

News.title: Village vote 'sent powerful message', say politicians
News.content:
No-one was surprised by the outcome of the poll which saw 257 people vote for the village ''to become an independent self-governing Crown dependency'' and just 16 vote against the idea. One ballot was spoiled.

The result has no legal basis, but there were warnings from local politicians for ministers not to ignore the result.

"It sends a powerful message that it is a completely unsuitable site.

"I hope just for once that the government will actually listen to local people," said Tim Passmore the Conservative Police and Crime Commissioner for Suffolk.

"That is what Andy Burnham said he would do, now it's time for action."

Terry Jermy is the Labour MP for Thetford, which is just two miles away from the base.

He said: "The people of Barnham have done a really good job in raising awareness of the issue and demonstrating the strength of feeling against these plans.

"The message to the government is that this MoD site is not suitable."

While Michael Hadwen, the Reform UK leader of Suffolk County council, said: "This is a clear demonstration of democracy at work.

"Barnham has said loud and clear that that the government cannot impose this base upon them and the government should start to listen because when things like this start to get ignored that's when society starts to collapse."

The estimated turnout of around 70% was lower than campaigners had been hoping for.

When a similar referendum was held in the Oxfordshire village of Piddington 89% of locals took part.

The chair of the residents association in Barnham said some people had decided not to vote after seeing the government ignore the result in Piddington and give planning permission for a nearby military base to be used for asylum seekers.

News.title: Joanna Page says she nearly messed up Gavin and Stacey audition
News.content:
Joanna Page has said she nearly messed up her Gavin And Stacey audition after failing to do a Cardiff accent.

The 49-year-old rose to fame after starring as Stacey in the BBC comedy opposite creators James Corden and Ruth Jones.

Page, from Swansea, told campmates on ITV's I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! that she had initially read some scenes for Jones using her actual accent.

She recounted that she was then asked to do it in a Cardiff accent, as that was where her character was supposed to be from, but Jones told her it sounded "awful" and to "just be you".

Speaking about her preparations for the life-changing audition, she said: "I remember reading the script, Ruth and James had written it and I remember thinking, 'This is me, she is me, I can do this'."

Page said she got the offer for the part in the Bafta-winning sitcom two weeks after being rejected from a West End show.

She said: "I was working in a shoe shop in East Dulwich and I'd just missed out on getting the part in Dirty Dancing The Musical.

"And so if I'd have got that, I never, ever would have done it."

Page also recalled her first impression of Mathew Horne - who played Gavin in the series - during their chemistry read and said "he seemed really cool, and I thought I'm not cool and I'm just a nerd".

The hit series aired for three seasons from 2007 until 2009 followed by Christmas specials including the series finale in 2024.

News.title: Miley Cyrus marries rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate Palm Springs wedding
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Pop culture icon Miley Cyrus married rock drummer Maxx Morando in an intimate weekend wedding in Palm Springs, California, according to a post on the singer’s Instagram account.

The post said Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, were wed on Saturday. Photographs show the couple embracing in front of a white backdrop with a palm tree characteristic of the Palm Springs desert in the background, a large dog lying at their feet. In one photo, the couple kisses standing in an aisle of white roses.

The “Party in the U.S.A.” singer wore a long-sleeve silk Saint Laurent gown by Anthony Vaccarello and elegant white silk kitten heels, according to a statement from Saint Laurent. The dress had a low back, and she wore flowers in her hair, which was pulled back into an updo.

Morando wore dark, square shades. His single-breasted tuxedo was also made by the French luxury fashion brand.

The pair have been together since 2021, meeting after they were set up on a blind date, according to an interview Cyrus gave Vogue in 2023. Morando proposed to her while the couple were in Japan late last year, he said in a separate interview with Wonderland Magazine.

“I could feel my heart pounding” before popping the question, Morando said for a profile in the magazine.

Morando is the drummer of the rock band Liily.

News.title: 15 best deals in the Space NK Black Friday sale: Up to 30% off YSL, Ouai and more
News.content:
Space NK Black Friday deals are officially here, and with them comes good news for anyone who usually struggles to justify the price of their favourite luxury beauty products. Running from 23 to 30 November (Cyber Monday), the retailer's sale includes up to 30 per cent off brands including Color Wow, Elemis, Phlur and Drunk Elephant, with further reductions on everything from Medik8 skincare to Byredo fragrances.

As IndyBest's senior shopping writer, I've tried more beauty products than I care to count, and I've learnt that a discount is only worth celebrating if the product itself delivers. With some of my favourite brands included in this year's promotion, I've been particularly interested in the savings on products I'd happily recommend at full price.

So, with that in mind, every item featured below has been tried and tested by yours truly. And, if you're shopping beyond beauty, the IndyBest team is tracking the best Black Friday deals across every category, from tech to home appliances. Let’s get saving.



Deals picked by Lucy Smith

( )

Beauty is my specialist subject and after six years in the industry, reviewing skincare, make-up, fragrance and haircare, I've developed a fairly good idea of which products I can justify spending my own money on. I've tried everything from £5 cleansers to £300 face creams, and I've found that a luxury price tag doesn't always mean better results (and, in some cases, it does!) For Space NK's Black Friday sale, I'm drawing on that experience to pick out the products that have impressed me during testing, checking their prices against competing retailers and looking beyond the percentage discounts to see where the savings actually lie.

When will the Space NK Black Friday deals start?

Space NK's Black Friday sale began today, Monday 23 November, which means us beauty obsessives have four extra days to make the most of the discounts before Black Friday itself (27 November) kicks in. The retailer is offering up to 30 per cent off a sizeable selection of brands, with some particularly lucrative reductions on products – ahem, perfumes – that rarely come cheap.

Among those receiving the full 30 per cent discount are Nars, Summer Fridays, Tom Ford, Kiehl’s and YSL – the latter of which is new to Space NK. Meanwhile, the likes of Charlotte Tilbury, K18 and Hourglass have been reduced by 25 per cent, with 20 per cent off selected luxury fragrance houses, including Creed and Parfums de Marly.

Though, as any savvy saver knows, Christmas beauty gift sets often boast a bundle saving before you even take Black Friday reductions into account. Therefore, you’ll likely be able to score a stacked reduction exceeding Space NK’s 30 per cent ceiling.

Will there be Cyber Monday 2026 Space NK deals?

Yes, Space NK's Black Friday promotion runs until Monday 30 November, meaning the discounts will still be available for Cyber Monday 2026.

Unlike some retailers, who launch a separate set of offers once Black Friday weekend is over, Space NK has announced a one week-long promotion, running from Monday 23 November through until to Cyber Monday 30 November. There's no indication of additional reductions being introduced specifically for the final day, so I wouldn't necessarily recommend waiting until Monday to make a purchase.

With popular brands such as Augustinus Bader, Saltair and Refy included in the sale, there's plenty to choose from, but I'd be mindful of stock levels on particularly sought-after products. And, while the promotion is scheduled to finish on 30 November, it's worth checking individual offers rather than assuming everything will remain available until the last minute. Lucky for you, I’ll be updating this guide as items go in and out of stock – so consider your job done.



Why you can trust IndyBest’s coverage of Space NK Black Friday deals

Lucy Smith has been The Independent’s senior shopping writer since July 2024 and in that in time she’s reviewed all manner of beauty products, from luxury skincare and make-up to budget fragrance and haircare. With six years of product reviewing under her belt, she knows that a hefty price tag doesn't necessarily mean better quality. She's also covered Black Friday since 2022, giving her plenty of experience comparing retailers' offers and spotting when a discount isn't all it's cracked up to be.

For this guide, Lucy has drawn on her own testing of Space NK favourites, including Westman Atelier's baby cheeks blush, Tatcha's water cream and Living Proof's advanced clean dry shampoo. She's assessed everything from how the make-up products wear throughout the day to whether the expensive skincare picks delivered noticeable results, using that experience to select deals on products she'd recommend buying, rather than those with the most eye-catching reductions.

News.title: Manchester Co-op Live arena evacuated after ‘tear gas let off’ during US rapper’s show as police declare major incident
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Manchester’s Co-op Live arena has been evacuated tonight after tear gas was reportedly let off during US rapper Don Toliver’s show.

The incident is reported to have taken place while the 32-year-old rapper, whose real name is Caleb Zackery Toliver, was performing on stage and is understood to have occurred towards the end of the gig.

Emergency services including ambulance and police officers are currently at the scene following the incident with those affected being supported by authorities.

A major incident has been declared as thousands have been evacuated. No serious injuries have been reported so far.

In a statement on Sunday night (22 November), a Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “Emergency services are currently in attendance following an incident at Co-op Live this evening.

open image in gallery Rapper Don Toliver was reportedly performing when the incident occurred ( Getty )

“It is understood that a substance believed to be tear gas was let off in the crowd towards the end of a concert. All attendees are currently being safely evacuated as a precaution.

“Those showing signs of being impacted are being supported by emergency services, with thankfully no serious injuries reported.”

Police advised members of the public to “please stay away from the arena whilst emergency services help those that have been at the concert safely make their way to their transport home.”

The spokesperson added: “A major incident has been declared to ensure emergency services and partner agencies can work together quickly and effectively to coordinate a safe response.”

Footage circulating on social media appears to show crowds of concert-goers appearing to look distressed while coughing.

open image in gallery The Co-op Live arena can hold up to 23,500 people ( AFP/Getty )

Other images show groups of fans in the crowded arena while the issue was being investigated.

An organiser is reported to have addressed the crowd and explained that the gig would have to be cut short to which many fans booed before it was confirmed what had taken place.

The arena is a relatively new venue, having opened in 2024 has the capacity to hold 23,500 people.

Fans told the Manchester Evening News that they saw what appeared to be smoke canisters thrown into the crowd.

The rapper is one of the world’s biggest musicians with over 45 million listeners per month, according to Spotify and ranks as the 86th most popular artist in the world. His top song on the streaming service, “No Pole”, has over 1 billion plays.

He is set to continue his tour with a performance at both the O2 Arena and OVO Arena in Wembley in London.

News.title: Union warns strike action could hit nuclear and defence response capabilities
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Strike action set to start at the Royal Naval Armaments Depot in western Scotland could affect the UK’s nuclear and defence response capabilities, a union has warned.

Unite members at the depot at Coulport in Argyll and Bute will begin strike action on Monday in a dispute over pay.

The union said about 70 members, employed by companies which form the ABL Alliance, are taking action after rejecting unacceptable pay offers.

The ABL Alliance is a joint venture company which was awarded a contract by the Ministry of Defence (MoD) to provide services for the UK’s Trident nuclear weapons system at Coulport.

It is formed of AWE plc, Babcock Marine, and Lockheed Martin.

Unite said that AWE plc workers will take strike action on November 23 followed by Lockheed Martin members on November 24 and Babcock Marine Marine members on November 26.

The union said that a continuous overtime ban and work to contracted hours has been in place since November 9.

James O’Connell, Unite regional co-ordinator, said: “Unite has tried to resolve this pay dispute through talks but the ABL Alliance has continued to table low ball offers to our members.

“It wouldn’t even dent the profit margins of these extremely wealthy companies to resolve this dispute.”

“Strikes will hit the UK’s nuclear and defence response capabilities.”

Unite general secretary Sharon Graham said: “Our members have Unite’s complete support until a fair offer is made.”

The union said that action will escalate at the end of the month and in December.

An MoD spokesperson said: “We are disappointed that negotiations have not reached an agreement and we strongly encourage ABL Alliance and the Unite trade union to continue to work together to reach a resolution.

“We deeply value the staff who work in this area, and our focus remains on maintaining the safe, secure and effective delivery of the important work at Coulport.”

Babcock Marine, and Lockheed Martin have been asked for comment.

AWE said it is a matter for the MoD.

News.title: Rents forecast to rise faster than house prices over next three years
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The rate of rental price growth for newly-let properties is expected to be around double the pace of house price growth over the next three years, according to a property firm.

Across Britain, Hamptons expects private rents paid on newly-let properties to increase by 14.2% on average between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the fourth quarter of 2029.

Over the same period, it forecasts that house prices will increase by 7.2%.

Private rents paid on rental homes generally – both newly-let properties and ones where there is a tenant already in place – are expected by Hamptons rise by 10.9% over the next three years.

Hamptons pointed to a tight supply of rental homes and affordability pressures for aspiring first-time buyers.

Growth in rents on newly-agreed lets is expected to ease somewhat in 2028 and 2029, alongside expected falls in mortgage rates, Hamptons said.

But it added that many of the longer-term pressures on the rental market are likely to remain.

Aneisha Beveridge, head of research at Hamptons, said: “With fewer homes entering the rental market, competition between tenants is likely to keep rents rising faster than house prices over the next few years.

“For landlords, that creates a delicate balancing act because higher costs do not automatically translate into higher rents.

“Historically, landlords have had limited scope to pass those costs on, with rents set by wider market conditions rather than their individual bills.

“But as costs have risen across the sector and rental supply has fallen, the bar has shifted, allowing more of those increases to feed through into higher rents.

“There is, however, a silver lining for investors. With rents rising faster than house prices, yields are improving, particularly across parts of southern England.

“In London, that has already started to tempt some landlords back into the market.

“For tenants, though, a smaller rental market means more competition and continued pressure on affordability.

“Existing tenants may initially be more insulated from rising rents, but the new-let and existing-tenancy markets do not operate independently.

“Over time, stronger new-let rental growth is likely to filter through to the wider market.”

A separate report, from Lloyds, analysed the average cost of buying a home versus renting in 12 major UK cities.

Lloyds, which used Office for National Statistics (ONS) research, estimated that monthly mortgage costs could potentially be cheaper than monthly rents typically in seven out of the 12 cities.

The research made several assumptions, including a 5% buyer deposit, and people’s individual circumstances, such as the house price paid, mortgage rates, deposit sizes and mortgage term lengths, will vary.

Lloyds analysis of the 12 cities indicated that Glasgow could potentially lead the way for buying versus renting, with a potential monthly saving of £288.

It was followed by Newcastle, with a potential saving of £187 per month compared with renting.

Bristol was third, with buyers potentially saving £139 a month compared with renting.

Andrew Asaam, mortgages Director at Lloyds, said: “Higher mortgage rates have seen the cost of borrowing increase this year, making that affordability calculation even more important.

“But in many cities across the UK, buyers could still pay less for their mortgage than they would typically be charged in rent – giving them an immediate saving as well as a place of their own.”

Meanwhile, Knight Frank has downgraded its UK house price forecasts, with price growth now expected to be 1% in 2027, down from 3% forecast in April.

Cumulative UK house price growth over the five years to 2031 is forecast to reach 14.2%, revised down from 20.4%, Knight Frank said, with a more uncertain political backdrop, higher borrowing costs and ongoing geopolitical instability weighing on buyer demand and market confidence.

News.title: Bereaved families should not have to battle with paperwork, says FCA
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Investment firms must do more to help people dealing with the death of a loved one, the City regulator has said.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) said a review had found some confusing communications, delays and gaps in support.

It looked at how financial advisers, wealth managers and investment platforms support bereaved families and those handling someone’s estate.

Some firms provided thoughtful, personal support, but others had processes that risked adding to people’s distress and financial pressure, the FCA said.

The regulator added that some also left people unclear about what to do next or offered limited ways to get in touch.

It also said that in some cases, advice fees were still being taken until an original death certificate was provided.

Kate Tuckley, head of department, consumer investments at the FCA, said: “Dealing with someone’s finances after a death should not mean a battle with paperwork. Firms should ease the burden, not add to it.

“Families need clear information and help without needless delays, not fees for advice they no longer receive.

“Some firms get this right and do it really well, now others must follow their lead.”

The review identified steps firms can take, such as explaining what happens next in plain language and giving people options about how they can report a death to suit their needs.

Firms should keep paperwork requirements proportionate and avoid unreasonable delays in access to money, the FCA said.

They should also explain which charges stop or continue and stop ongoing advice fees where the related service is no longer being provided, it said.

The regulator said firms should check whether people are getting the support they need, rather than relying on low complaint numbers as an indicator that everything is working.

The review said in some cases, firms relied only on unsolicited customer comments and complaints to check whether their information was clear and helpful.

It said: “Firms should consider other ways to measure the effectiveness of their communications, as people who are grieving may not feel able to explain what went wrong.”

Previous research by the FCA indicated that less than half of bereaved customers (47%) felt they had received the support they needed from financial firms.

Liz Field, chief executive, Pimfa (Personal Investment Management and Financial Advice Association) said: “Improving the bereavement journey means looking at both the support firms provide and the wider processes that can create additional stress for families.

“Pimfa is committed to working with the FCA and our members to build on good practice, improve consistency and reduce avoidable burdens on bereaved customers.”

Lisa Lund, director of bereavement services at Octopus Legacy said: “The best firms design bereavement around people, not paperwork.”

A spokesperson for Step, a professional body for trust and estate practitioners, said: “Dealing with the financial affairs of a loved one can be complex, time-consuming and emotionally challenging.

“Unnecessary delays, confusing processes and disproportionate paperwork can add significantly to that burden.

“Our members regularly support families through the estate administration process and understand how important it is to them that financial institutions communicate clearly, provide information promptly and take a compassionate, proportionate approach.”

Rob Hillock, head of personal financial planning at financial services consultancy Broadstone, said: “The last thing anyone needs when grieving the loss of a loved one is the added stress of sorting out their finances.”

Tom Selby, director of public policy, AJ Bell, said: “Grieving families should not face unnecessary delays, repeated requests for the same information or be left chasing different departments simply to establish what someone owned and whether there is any tax to pay.”

News.title: Smart buoys that let wind farm support vessels charge at sea trialled
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A smart buoy that vessels can use to charge while at sea is being trialled off the coast of Scotland.

It is hoped the device, developed by Aberdeenshire-based engineering firm Oasis Marine, could ultimately help cut emissions from shipping.

Oasis Marine is initially targeting the buoys at maintenance ships servicing offshore wind farms, saying it will enable them to charge safely away from wind turbines.

The Oasis Power Buoys will be connected to wind turbine generators by subsea cables, allowing boats to recharge with low-cost clean energy.

All aspects of offshore performance, including vessel approach, mooring, power connection and safety, are now being tested by a prototype which has been deployed in the Cromarty Firth.

Oasis Marine said vessels using the mooring buoys will be able to pull up, plug in and replenish their power supplies.

George Smith, Oasis Marine founder and chief technical officer, said: “Offshore wind has revolutionised energy production and now we’re doing the same for the vessels that keep those wind farms running.

“But this is about more than just one buoy. We’re building the infrastructure that can help global shipping decarbonise on a vast scale.

“We’ve developed technology that’s elegantly simple by applying hard-won lessons from the oil and gas industry.

open image in gallery The device is being targeted at vessels servicing offshore windfarms (Oasis Marine/PA)

“We know from experience that anything going offshore has to be reliable – and simplicity is a cornerstone of reliability.”The prototype is expected to remain in the water until early summer next year so its performance can be assessed.

The company said feasibility studies have shown offshore charging of hybrid and electric support vessels is technically and operationally viable with the device.

It said vessels with diesel or marine gas oil engines can also use the Oasis Power Buoy as it can be used to power on-board systems such as electrics, heating and air conditioning.

Oasis Marine said the device can be retrofitted to existing wind turbine generators or incorporated into new designs.

While the buoy is being targeted at maintenance ships servicing offshore windfarms, it is hoped it could in future help reduce pollution from other vessels such as merchant ships, cruise liners and service vessels for oil and gas platforms.

Trials in the Cromarty Firth are being backed by a Scottish Enterprise Grant and a crowdfunding initiative which launched this month.

News.title: Any regrets, Mauricio? Man Utd are deep in relegation battle after Anfield farce
News.content:
Bruno Fernandes says he has shelved talks over a new contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but said all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

“We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

“We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

“The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”

Fernandes said claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the issue he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

“The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he said.

“There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

“I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

“Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

“The thing is, I’ve always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

“I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”

United chief executive Omar Berrada said of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his new contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

Fernandes said the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

“He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

“He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

“Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”

News.title: Verstappen mocks ‘absolute joke’ Russell after thrilling Las Vegas win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, coming to you from very early on a Sunday morning (if you are in the eastern hemisphere) and very late on a Sunday night (if you are in the western hemisphere).

It is a strange race in a strange place, but this is now the fourth edition of the race and it looks to be here to stay for all its strangeness. It does present the teams with problems and problems are there to be solved or negotiated as well as can be in F1. That is the name of the game.

In qualifying yesterday the world champion, Kimi Antonelli, did that expertly, sneaking in at the end to finish fastest. He does, however, take a five-place grid penalty, so will be starting in sixth. Taking first place on the grid will be the in-form Max Verstappen, followed by George Russell, who could do with a strong finish to the season.

Russell seemed miffed about missing out on pole position, particularly with how Mercedes managed the qualifying situation, particularly with how the tow was managed. Antonelli was always going to take a grid penalty, so why give him the tow, was Russell’s reasoning.

In any case, Russell has a good chance to take his third victory this season. At least on paper. Russell’s qualifying has probably been his strongest suit this season, but race days have let him down. Let us not forget that Lando Norris, who won last time out in Brazil, starts third.

There could be a bit of aggro on the first lap, given Russell and Verstappen’s “disagreement” yesterday, but let’s see. It may end up being a clean race.

It all starts in about an hour and we will be here for all the updates and reaction from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

News.title: Wales ‘frustrated’ after being brought back down to earth by Wallabies
News.content:
Wales have a spring in their step coming into their game tonight as they host Australia at the Principality Stadium. Wales pulled off one of their best wins in recent memory last weekend, ending an over 70-year with for a victory over New Zealand. Despite pulling off that shock victory, Wales sit down in fifth in the northern hemisphere standings coming into this final round of fixtures. In all likelihood, they can only improve one spot. They have made four changes from the historic win over the All Blacks, with the likes of Josh Adams and Aaron Wainwright coming in.

“We were all immensely proud to make history last week,” Wales head coach Steve Tandy said. “There is a new opportunity and challenge for us against Australia and we are looking to back up our performance this weekend. It is our last home game of this competition. The support that fans give to the players and staff has been incredible and we cannot wait to get back out at Principality Stadium.

“We made nearly 350 tackles, the ball in play time was one of the highest in Test rugby in the last three years and we have got competition. The plan was always to freshen up and we are likely to do similar for the week after, because we need to find out about players. We have fresh and hungry players coming in, which will add the energy that we need at the weekend. The training environment is getting more competitive in certain positions we have the ability to put people in and feel confident about performance.”

News.title: Whiff of arrogance as Arsenal unexpectedly implode
News.content:
Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. I think we were exceptional in the first half. At every level. Our intensity, the clarity that we have, how to attack the jumps of Newcastle every time they wanted to go man-to-man, the composure that we have, the way we use our relationship to break their press. And it should have been 2-0, 3-0 or 4-0 up, clear.

“But it wasn’t. And when it wasn’t, then we expected in the second half that we have to again raise the level because the opponent is going to have a reaction. And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. And then we gave them belief.

“And I say we give them belief because we give them a goal, we give them a throw-in that we just give them the ball. We have no structure to control the opposite winger. We concede a goal and it’s game on. And from that it became a very chaotic game. Every set-piece, we know that they are exceptional at it and we concede from a set piece.

“And then you have to react. And then we went back to the team that the exceptional team that we were in the first half again for another 25 minutes and we scored a great goal. We create infinity of openings to create and score the third goal, but we lack some time or to be precise, to make that count.”

News.title: ‘Remarkable’ Ireland deliver perfect riposte to Erasmus mind games
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Ireland vs South Africa from the Nations Championship in Dublin, with both teams harbouring hopes of finishing the day at the top of their respective tables.

Ireland and South Africa have both won four of their five games in the group phase of this year’s inaugural Nations Championship, and come into their last match before next weekend’s finals still in contention for the overall title.

Andy Farrell’s men begin the afternoon in third in the Northern Hemisphere table, but level on points with second-placed England, who are currently hosting New Zealand, and just one point behind leaders France, who take on Argentina this evening.

The reigning world champions, meanwhile, are guaranteed to at least remain in second in the Southern Hemisphere table, but are just one point behind the All Blacks at the top of the group, so will be hoping for a favour from Steve Borthwick’s men at Twickenham.

The Springboks will be without head coach Rassie Erasmus for today’s contest in the Irish capital, with the 54-year-old facing a six-match ban because of his criticism of officials following his team’s narrow defeat by France last weekend, including asking whether they were “match-fixing”.

“He’s been hands-on with our team, and we’re in a good space,” assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus on Friday. “Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure.”

In the same press conference, Erasmus predicted that Sam Prendergast would be cleared to play after being cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji. The Ireland fly-half escaped punishment from the independent panel and starts for Farrell’s side this afternoon.

News.title: Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

“(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

“It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

“We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his new-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a big shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

“It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

News.title: England obliterate All Blacks in record win
News.content:
A nearly perfect half for England was ruined just two minutes before half-time when Ben Earl gave up a penalty from the restart, immediately after scoring the home side’s third try. New Zealand kicked to the corner and Ethan de Groot plunged over to give the All Blacks a lifeline they scarcely deserve.

Until that point, this was as dominant a half against top-tier opposition that we have ever seen from Steve Borthwick’s team. Much like they did against Australia, England have strangled the life out of New Zealand and have enjoyed a preposterous 78 per cent territory.

They have also repeatedly cut New Zealand open in midfield. The interplay between Fin Smith, Seb Atkinson and the regal George Furbank has been sumptuous to watch. England have struggled to break New Zealand down in the red zone but still have three tries to show for their efforts. Smith’s cute little poke through was grounded by Henry Slade after five minutes and then scrum half Jack van Poortvliet did his best Superman impression by diving over the top of a ruck for England’s second try.

Earl also went route one, picking off the back of a scrum and through Cam Roigard’s tackle to put England in dreamland. Not every department has functioned perfectly. New Zealand have been on top of the scrum and have stopped the English maul in its tracks, but the All Blacks have been dominated physically. When was the last time we said that about an England team?

The De Groot try has taken the wind out of England’s sails a little but a similar setback took place in the Australia game just before half-time and Borthwick’s team responded with an emphatic second-half performance.

England need to see this out too, otherwise they’ll be kicking themselves all the way through to the World Cup.

The winger, his partner Paige Milian, and their children were present at the time of the burglary – but were not harmed.

PETER SCHMEICHEL revealed hard truths following Manchester United’s tragic 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

The Red Devils legend watched on as his former side went down to ten men in the eighth minute after Leny Yoro was sent off before conceding four goals.



Dominik Szoboszlai struck first from the resulting free-kick before Florian Wirtz doubled their lead.

Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz put the icing on the cake for the Reds in the second half.



And, speaking on Viaplay, club legend Schmeichel was left fearing United could actually go down.

The former keeper said: “Realistically, can Man United just finish 10th or 12th? It would be okay.



“I know it’s silly to say, but we are in the relegation zone.”

The catastrophic defeat left United in 19th and marked Mauricio Pochettino‘s first game in the new dugout as one to forget.

There are already 20 points between the struggling side and league leaders Arsenal, but they have 27 games remaining in the Prem season to avoid the drop.

Schmeichel added: “This team looks like a team that could get relegated. So now the target should be to avoid relegation.”

“We’ve all played in the Premier League, so we know we’re in November, approaching December. It’s not really now, it’s when we get to March.

“But I think, at least, I have faith that he can correct those things. He’s never going to make a championship-winning team, not with these guys.”

But when the new United boss spoke with Viaplay, he said: “Relegation battle? That is our reality, no…? We are there.

After the game, other ex-United stars gave their two pence on the state of the team.

Sports.title: 'I don't see this in League Two' - Gary Neville and Roy Keane tear into Man Utd defending v Liverpool
Sports.content:
'I don't see this in League Two' - Gary Neville and Roy Keane tear into Man Utd defending v Liverpool

Manchester United's disastrous start to the season continued as they were thumped 4-0 at Anfield by arch-rivals Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach

View 2 Images Gary Neville gave a bleak assessment of Manchester United's defending against Liverpool (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville suggested that the defensive chaos on show from Manchester United in their chastening 4-0 loss against Liverpool wouldn't even be seen in League Two.

‌



‌



The Red Devils were thrashed at Anfield as Mauricio Pochettino's tenure got off to the worst possible start at the hands of United's arch-rivals, who inflicted maximum punishment on their beleaguered visitors following Leny Yoro's eighth minute red card.

‌



Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz scored twice in the five minutes after Yoro's dismissal with Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz adding to the scoreline in the second half.

‌



United now have the worst defensive record in any of Europe's top five leagues after shipping 34 goals in all competitions this term.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Neville, the co-owner of Salford City, claimed that the standard of defending was below what he watches week in week out in League Two as he follows the club's progress after Roy Keane tore into United's defensive structure.

‌



"My worry for United's defenders [is] they're not getting great help," said Keane on Sky Sports post-match.

"I don't think they're great individually the defenders and they're certainly not great as a group. It's not as if you're going, 'Lads, we're not all great. But the four of us together, we can do a good job'."

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United fell to their latest heavy defeat of the season at Anfield (Image: Carl Recine)

As Sky Sports showed footage of Liverpool's third goal, which was scored by Ngumoha after unselfish work from Bradley Barcola, Keane pointed out the positioning of Lisandro Martinez.

‌



Neville then said: "Do you know something. You watch a lot of League Two football, Roy. I watch League Two every single week; I don't see a lack of order like this in League Two like I do in the Premier League sometimes. Chelsea [in their 4-1 loss vs Leeds on Saturday] were the same."

Manchester United finish the weekend moored in the relegation zone after collecting just eight points from their 11 games this term.

Captain Bruno Fernandes admitted it was hurting everybody at the club for them to be sat 19th in the Premier League, telling BBC Sport: "Very painful, it hurts a lot. It's a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation."

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim takes dig at clubs sacking managers after latest Ineos dismissal
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim takes dig at clubs sacking managers after latest Ineos dismissal

Former Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim has questioned how some big clubs operate on a weekend where Mauricio Pochettino prepares to oversee his first Red Devils game

View 2 Images Ruben Amorim has hit out at the strategy of some big clubs (Image: Claudio Villa/AC Milan via Getty Images)

Ruben Amorim, the former Manchester United manager, has bemoaned the lack of long-term strategy at "big clubs" on the eve of his previous employers' first game under Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



‌



Amorim, 41, arrived at Old Trafford as one of Europe's most exciting young coaches following a fine spell in charge of Sporting Lisbon. However, the Portuguese lasted just 14 months at United after failing to live up to the hype in the Premier League.

‌



With Amorim now embracing a new challenge in Italy with AC Milan, United are about to start life under another new manager after Michael Carrick paid the price for a disastrous start to the season.

‌



Milan are fourth in Serie A, with Amorim losing just one of his first 11 league games in the Italian capital - and he has shared some interesting thoughts around strategy.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"That is the biggest mistakes of the big clubs," said Amorim in a press conference. "Is thinking that I look at the table: If we are near, let's invest. Crazy invest. If we are not near, let's not invest.

‌



"I think the key point is - have a long term plan. If you lose, all the games, sack the manager. That is normal. I'm not talking about that [laughs]. But what I'm saying is that stick with your plan.

"We have a plan. What kind of player we want. Whether he's able to make all the runs that we want. He has the character that we want. Not a big star, like a guy that is composed and come here to be one of the part of the team."

‌



He continued: "If we have a clear plan, don't look at the table. Look at the table only to evaluate the process. But to buy, to spend money, only consider things for the next 5 years. Don't spend money by constantly looking at the table at the end of November or December. And I think that is the biggest mistake of the clubs."

View 2 Images Amorim's time in charge of Manchester United was unsuccessful (Image: Getty)

‌



Although Amorim arrived in the Premier League with a burgeoning reputation, his period in charge of Manchester United failed to yield much in the way of success. He won 25 of his 63 games in charge of the Red Devils, who paid £9.25million to trigger Amorim's release clause at Sporting Lisbon.

His 14-month reign came to an explosive end when Amorim took aim at the club hierarchy. Confirmation that he had left his post came the following day.

‌



"I just want to say I came here to be the manager, not to be the coach," Amorim said in press conference. "In every department - the scouting department, the sporting director – [they] need to do their job. I will do mine for 18 months and then we move on.

"I just want to say that I'm going to be the manager of this team, not just the coach. I was really clear on that. That is going to finish in 18 months and then everyone is going to move on. That was the deal. That is my job. Not to be a coach."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino fumes over two decisions in Man Utd's trashing by Liverpool
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino fumes over two decisions in Man Utd's trashing by Liverpool

New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start to his new job as the Red Devils were thumped by Liverpool at Anfield

View 2 Images Man Utd manager Mauricio Pochettino after defeat to Liverpool

Mauricio Pochettino was left fuming after Leny Yoro’s red card condemned Manchester United to a “painful” humiliation at Anfield.

‌



Pochettino suffered the biggest defeat of any new United manager’s first game in charge in 100 years which left them rooted in the relegation zone.

But Pochettino said United should have had a penalty for Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet’s challenge on Bryan Mbeumo a minute before Yoro got his marching orders for pulling back Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick.

United boss Pochettino said: “It is painful we lose 4-0 but we play more than 80 minutes with 10 men but also it was a penalty to Mbeumo. We can make a mistake, and we were punished and they were not.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“We need to be critical of ourselves but also at the same time we need to put some situations that happened during the game that we are not happy.

“The ball was going to the keeper. I think in that situation if you review the VAR you can see, like we see on the cameras now, that Yoro never had the intention to connect with Isak. The striker saw that the ball was going to the keeper and he delayed a little bit of his run and goes down.

“But if you go two minutes before. Sixth minute. Jacquet on Mbeumo, they are similar, no? When you compare the actions, that's a penalty, no. And if we score after six minutes for sure we are talking in a different way.”

But Pochettino admitted they have to “accept the reality” of the situation they are in but insisted they showed fight after going down to ten men.

View 2 Images United were thrashed by Liverpool at Anfield (Image: Getty Images)

Pochettino added: “So, so painful. So disappointed. It's not in your head to start here in the Premier League in this situation. We need to accept the reality and we need to be united and all together and we feel disappointed because it is clear what happened.

“The plan was in the bin but what I learned from my players is that they like to fight, they are committed to the team and to the club and they want to win games and today we made an effort. Today was a test that for me is very positive.”

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola celebrated after the final whistle with fist pumps in front of the Kop and was adamant that it was a foul on Isak.

Iraola said: “It is clearly the last man, clearly a foul, Alex on the keeper, will he score, we never know, but for us it is a good moment because we are going to play a lot of time against ten men.

“I always enjoy the moment with the fans and I think we owe them because we have had much better results and we want to solve this and give them a big win and more to celebrate.”
