Sports.title: New manager, same old chaos - Man Utd are in a relegation scrap under Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
New manager, same old chaos - Man Utd are in a relegation scrap under Mauricio Pochettino

LIVERPOOL 4-0 MANCHESTER UNITED: Mauricio Pochettino's tenure as the Red Devils boss got off to a nightmare start as they were thrashed by their rivals at Anfield

View 3 Images Mauricio Pochettino watches on as Man Utd are thrashed by Liverpool

New manager, same old chaos for Manchester United.

‌



‌



Mauricio Pochettino’s brave new world lasted all of 13 minutes before they found themselves 2-0 down and reduced to ten men.

‌



As starts go, it was hard to imagine it could have gone much worse for Pochettino. There was no new manager bounce and instead just a reminder that far too many of this United squad are not fit to wear the shirt.

‌



You have to go all the way back to 1926 and Lal Hilditch to find a United manager who suffered such a big defeat in his first game in charge.

After the fourth goal went in, the away end was half empty. Even the loyal United fans had seen enough. Liverpool supporters sang a chorus of: “You’re getting sacked in the morning.”

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The only saving grace for Pochettino was that the scoreline was not more embarrassing. It could and should have been. That was down to Liverpool’s wasteful finishing as much as any United defiance.

‌



United now find themselves second from bottom and, on this evidence, they are stuck in a relegation scrap. United have managed one win all season and only bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace have conceded more goals.

Last season, Tottenham had 18 points after 11 games. United have eight points after 11 games. And Tottenham only survived on the final day of last season.

‌



United looked a mess, a ramshackle bunch of misfits who were torn apart. Former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson, watching on from the directors’ box at Anfield, said recently that “Anfield is like a trip to the dentist without the benefit of painkillers or earplugs.”

View 3 Images United were thrashed at Anfield

‌



Well, this was more painful than pulling teeth for United. Liverpool feasted on United’s failings and frailties - and there were far too many to make it an even contest.

But let’s start with Matthijs De Ligt who was given his first Premier League start in 12 months and that will surely go down as Pochettino’s biggest mistake of all. Diogo Dalot was also tormented by Rio Ngumoha.

‌



It was De Ligt who was badly at fault in the build-up to Liverpool’s first goal as it was his misjudgement which left Leny Yoro exposed and led to him being sent off.

Ronald Araujo’s long ball over the top sent Alexander Isak away, De Ligt misjudged it and Yoro pulled back the Liverpool forward. Isak’s touch looked heavy and he might not have got the ball but referee Sam Barrott still sent Yoro off for the foul on the edge of the box.

‌



Dominik Szoboszlai drilled a low free kick from the edge of the box and into the far corner. United 1-0 down and down to ten men within ten minutes at Anfield.

View 3 Images It was a different story for Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola

‌



The TV cameras panned across to the directors’ box. There was United’s director of football Jason Wilcox sinking deeper into his coat as he nearly buried his face underneath his collar.

It soon got even worse. Ngumoha tore Dalot apart yet again, cut the ball back for Florian Wirtz and the Liverpool midfielder hooked home off the crossbar. Only 13 minutes had gone.

‌



Liverpool wasted chances as Bradley Barcola was the worst offender. United switched to five at the back and Harry Maguire came on to tighten them up at the back as he also made a goal-saving block to deny Isak.

United offered nothing going forward. Finally, a third goal came after 66 minutes. Barcola burst forward, his delicious cross set up Ngumoha who slammed home past United keeper Senne Lammens.

‌



De Ligt gave the ball away again in the build-up to the fourth. Wirtz found substitute Victor Munoz and he fired home to compound United’s misery.

At the end, Pochettino went over to applaud the few remaining United fans. In contrast, Andoni Iraola was fist-pumping in front of the Kop in true Jurgen Klopp style. Liverpool fans are firmly onboard with their manager.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes fires thinly veiled dig in pointed message to Man Utd teammates
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes fires thinly veiled dig in pointed message to Man Utd teammates

Bruno Fernandes has entered the final year of his contract with Manchester United and has rejected two offers to extend his stay, putting him on course to leave as a free agent in June 2027

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes doesn't want to leave under a cloud (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes insists that he won't down tools and see out his contract at Manchester United - like he's seen some of his teammates do.

‌



‌



Fernandes, 32, recently turned down a second offer of a new deal with the Red Devils, with his current terms expiring at the end of this season.

‌



But the United captain says that he'll make a decision on his future before then or accept being sold in January. Fernandes has played with multiple big names who've opted to run down their contracts at Old Trafford before leaving on a free transfer, meaning that the club have missed out on a fee.

‌



Some players have left much more amicably at the end of their deals and Fernandes wants to be in the latter camp if this proves to his final campaign in Manchester. "I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on," the Portugal international told Sky Sports.

"I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door."

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Fernandes' comments could be referencing a host of ex-team-mates such as Paul Pogba or Jesse Lingard, who left the club in 2022 without much of a farewell, while they serve as a message to current players who've also entered the last year of their contracts, including Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw.

‌



There remains the possibility that Fernandes could extend his stay with United, having joined them in January 2020 and been captain for the last four seasons. However, talks are on hold.

"No, there's no negotiations ongoing," the former Sporting Lisbon star confirmed. "But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years.

‌



"If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

Should Bruno Fernandes stay at Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is one of several players out of contract next summer (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club."

‌



Fernandes added: "Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

Sports.content:
Argentina World Cup villain who was hit with huge ban collapses during live TV interview

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed after Boca Juniors' Copa Sudamericana final win over Clube Atletico Mineiro

View Image World Cup winner Leandro Paredes collapsed (Image: DSports)

Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live TV interview on Saturday evening following Boca Juniors' Copa Sudamericana win. The Argentine caused a stir at World Cup 2026 for his rough post-final antics and was given a 10-game ban.

‌



‌



Paredes, 32, had just played in Boca's 2-0 victory over Clube Atletico Mineiro at Estadio Metropolitano Roberto Melendez in tropical conditions. Temperatures reached high levels in the Colombian city of Barranquilla and the captain was taken off in the second half.

‌



Speaking to DSports reporter Marcelo Benedetto after the victory, Paredes soon became faint and collapsed to the floor. Broadcasters cut away immediately as medical staff rushed in to assist the World Cup 2022 winner.

‌



The player was able to regain his footing and walked into the dressing room under his own power to celebrate with his team-mates. He was taken to hospital by ambulance to undergo routine checks roughly two hours after the final whistle. Paredes later posted on social media to let fans know he was okay, stating: "Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just dizziness."

The win marked the first time Boca had won the Sudamericana in over two decades. Paredes issued an emotional statement in the wake of the success.

‌



He said: "I fulfilled a dream. I always dreamed of being able to win a title. I only have words of gratitude for the club. Thanks to my children, my family and my friends.

"Since I was little, I've been taught to compete and win everything possible. I love winning and competing. I'm lucky to achieve important things."

‌



Paredes was at the centre of some ugly scenes following the World Cup 2026 final this summer. Argentina fell 1-0 to Spain in a cagey match after extra time and following the final whistle, there were some altercations.

Sports.title: Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting Worlds glory
Sports.content:
Gerwyn Price won the Grand Slam of Darts with a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen; the last four winners of the Grand Slam have gone on to win the World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace; Price is hoping to continue the trend

Gerwyn Price looking to continue trend of Grand Slam victors tasting World Darts Championship glory

Gerwyn Price reflects on winning his first major for four years after beating Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

An interesting trend has occurred over the last four years: The winner of the Grand Slam has gone on to win the World Darts Championship.

It started with Michael Smith back in 2022, with Luke Humphries continuing it in 2023.

Of course, Luke Littler's back-to-back triumphs in Wolverhampton in 2024 and 2025 were then followed by him lifting the Sid Waddell Trophy.

Gerwyn Price wants to continue that in 2026.

Price roared to a 16-11 victory over Gian van Veen in the final of the Grand Slam, hitting five massive ton-plus checkouts in a confident display.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Grand Slam of Darts final between Price and Van Veen

The win moves Price up to world No 3 ahead of Humphries and marks his first major title in four years.

Alexandra Palace was immediately on Price's mind following his victory and he hopes to extend the trend into a fifth year and become a two-time world champion.

"The sweet thing about this is the last couple of years, whoever won has gone on to win the World [Championship], so....," Price said after beating Van Veen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the moment Price ended his wait for another major title as he won the Grand Slam of Darts

"If that happens, then I'll take six months out!"

"I am superstitious and I believe in stuff like that," he later added.

"I hope I am not the one to break the trend."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price closed in on victory against Gian van Veen with a tops-tops checkout

Price has been in some form in 2026, the Grand Slam marking his fourth major final of the year but his first victory.

The Welshman has maintained he is the most consistent player across 2026 and puts part of that down to the love he now gets from the crowd.

It is a very different story from when he last won a Grand Slam title five years ago.

"How different it is, the crowd right behind me and cheering me all the way. How things can change." Price added.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at all five of Gerwyn Price's ton-plus checkouts during his sensational win over Van Veen

"I thought these days would happen, I just didn't know when. I am glad it happened sooner rather than later.

"It definitely helps and spurs you on to come out to a crowd who is right behind you rather than against you.

"I have had that for the last two-and-a-half years and hopefully it continues.

"People have just realised I am who I am, I wear my heart on my sleeve, and I don't do things to put people off which people think I did.

"I am the most consistent. I am not saying I am the best player.

"I am full of confidence, I am in some great form. I am the most consistent across this season."

'I have now got the media off my back, not the monkey'

Now, the narrative changes.

"You guys [the media] were putting pressure on me and reminding me I hadn't won a tournament in a long time," Price said.

Sports.title: Gary Neville on De Ligt selection and 'negligent' Man Utd
Sports.content:
Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their back line as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe.

Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure.

United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.

"It's negligent," said Sky Sports pundit Neville.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the game between Liverpool and Man Utd

"The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years."

Pochettino made the decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield but the Netherlands international was partly at fault for the opening goal and endured a torrid evening along with the rest of United's defenders.

Watching back the opener, when De Ligt misjudged a high ball, Neville said: "The minute that De Ligt makes that run in that channel, Yoro has to come across within 10 metres of him, and [Diogo] Dalot has to come across. This is so bad from Yoro and Dalot.

"De Lift makes a right mess of it. He can't believe it though, De Ligt. He's played centre-half before. He can't believe Yoro's not there. Then Yoro makes contact and it's clumsy.

"Honestly. You can't get worse that that.

"You've got a back four who are looking after their own jobs, they're in fear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane shares his thoughts on Manchester United after their 4-0 loss to Liverpool and his disbelief at their 'lack of fight'

"De Ligt and [Lisandro] Martinez have dropped off, Dalot's not coming quickly enough.

"It's a mess because of the fact they've got no confidence and haven't got the ability to play out there at Anfield in a game against Liverpool."

Neville 'very surprised' by De Ligt call

Neville was baffled by Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt, who was similarly poor when returning from injury in last month's 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher give their verdict on the result at Anfield

"We were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," added Neville.

"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes.

"Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville react to Leny Yoro's early red card

"Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.

"I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como, he was all over the place in Como.

"It's almost like you don't know what's happening.

"I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well.

"I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either."

'That back four will get you relegated'

United's total of eight points after 11 games is their lowest at this stage of a season since the 1972/73 campaign.

"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," added Neville.

"A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville makes a passionate plea to Man Utd's defenders

"At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact.

"The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly."

He added: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Martinez.

"Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.

"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.

"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact."

Keane: Why were Man Utd fans applauding?

Roy Keane, meanwhile, was amazed to see some travelling fans at Anfield give the players a positive reception after the game.

"Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done," he said on Sky Sports.

"Are you telling me Man Utd couldn't have done better and everyone is saying it's not bad?

"At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality, I can't believe what I'm hearing.

"Fans are applauding the players. Applauding what? Applauding rubbish. When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision-making? Liverpool should have scored eight or nine.

"I feel like swearing. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad?"

Sports.title: Thitikul completes three-peat at LPGA Tour finale and breaks money record
Sports.content:
Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida.

Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.

She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the first 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

Image: Aki Iwai finished her round with five consecutive pars

Thitikul becomes the first player to win an LPGA Tour event three years running since Inbee Park at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship from 2013-2015, with her latest a fifth of another memorable season.

A $4m (£3.06m) first prize also sees her end Annika Sorenstam's 25-year stint at the top of the LPGA Tour's career money list, moving ahead of the Swede with a total of $24,292,858 (£20.3m).
