Sports.title: Scott McTominay and girlfriend Cam Reading announce pregnancy: Ex-Man United star celebrates 'precious gift' months after having heart surgery
Sports.content:
Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together. The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself. They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino. The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours. It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news. It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece. Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift' Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000. According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano. There, McTominay can be by the seaside quickly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre. The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan. This season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health. Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat. The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training. But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday. McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights. The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly. 'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'

Sports.title: Big Ten tumbles out of AP top 5 for first time since '21; Georgia, Utah remain 1-2
Sports.content:
How far could Indiana fall in CFP rankings after Week 12 loss? (1:42)

Open Extended Reactions

A weekend of Big Ten upsets battered its teams in The Associated Press Top 25, with Sunday's poll absent a single program from the conference among the top five for the first time since 2021.

Georgia, Utah and Notre Dame all won to hold steady as the top three teams in the survey of the 69-person media voting panel with one week left in the regular season. The Bulldogs earned 56 first-place votes, Utah received 12 (two more than last week), and the Fighting Irish got one.

Associated Press Top 25 School (1st) Record LW 1. Georgia (56) 10-1 1 2. Utah (12) 11-0 2 3. Notre Dame (1) 10-1 3 4. Miami 10-1 5 5. Texas 9-2 8 6. Alabama 9-2 7 7. Tennessee 9-2 9 8. Wake Forest 10-1 10 9. Texas Tech 10-1 11 10. UCLA 10-1 4 11. BYU 9-2 12 12. Indiana 9-2 6 13. Iowa 9-2 13 14. Oregon 8-3 14 15. USC 8-3 18 16. Arizona 8-3 19 17. Houston 8-3 20 18. Louisville 8-3 21 19. Oklahoma 7-4 NR 20. Florida 7-4 23 21. Liberty 10-1 22 22. Boise State 9-2 15 23. Ole Miss 7-4 25 24. Missouri 7-4 NR 25. Ohio State 7-4 16

From there, changes were everywhere, starting with UCLA dropping six spots to No. 10 -- the best of the six Big Ten teams in the poll -- after an 18-16 loss in triple-overtime at Michigan. Indiana also fell -- from No. 6 to No. 12 -- after its 27-24 overtime loss at Washington.

It is the first time since Nov. 7, 2021, that the Big Ten hasn't had a team ranked in the top five.

Ohio State's briefly resurgent playoff hopes took a fatal blow after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska. The Buckeyes fell nine spots to No. 25, with something similar expected Tuesday night in the College Football Playoff rankings, where they had climbed to 14th last week.

Despite convincing wins over the weekend, two-loss Iowa and three-loss Oregon stayed put in the poll, at Nos. 13 and 14 -- another less-than-encouraging sign for the conference that has produced the past three national champions. Even so, they remain in the hunt for a CFP spot, with the Ducks having an inside track (along with UCLA) for a spot in the Big Ten title game.

There was a significant 100-point gap in poll voting between No. 3 Notre Dame and fourth-ranked Miami, a sign that the AP voters have made up their minds who the best teams are. Notre Dame was ranked sixth by the CFP last week.

Rounding out the AP top 10 were No. 5. Texas, followed by Alabama, Tennessee, Wake Forest, Texas Tech and UCLA. Texas leapfrogged Alabama after a 45-3 win over old rival Arkansas, while the Crimson Tide beat FCS team Chattanooga 47-0.

At No. 8, Wake Forest has its highest ranking in program history.

Another key upset Saturday -- the first week in three years without a matchup between AP Top 25 teams -- was San Diego State's 22-20 win over Boise State in the Pac-12.

The loss dropped the Broncos seven spots to No. 22. Boise State, which was the only Group of Six team in last week's CFP rankings (but one of three in the AP poll), is now a spot behind Conference USA leader Liberty in the AP rankings.

WHO'S IN; WHO'S OUT

Oklahoma climbed back into the poll for the first time since Week 3 at No. 19 after a 28-7 victory over Texas A&M.

Missouri, which beat Kentucky 28-14, is back in the poll at No. 24 after a three-week absence. The Wildcats, meanwhile, are no longer ranked after their second straight loss.

Memphis also dropped out after a 38-34 loss to Navy.

CONFERENCE CALL

SEC (8 ranked teams): No. 1 Georgia, No. 5 Texas, No. 6 Alabama, No. 7 Tennessee, No. 19 Oklahoma, No. 20 Florida, No. 23 Ole Miss, No. 24 Missouri.

Big Ten (6): No. 10 UCLA, No. 12 Indiana, No. 13 Iowa, No. 14 Oregon, No. 15 USC, No. 25 Ohio State.

Big 12 (5): No. 2 Utah, No. 9 Texas Tech, No. 11 BYU, No. 16 Arizona, No. 17 Houston.

ACC (3): No. 4 Miami, No. 8 Wake Forest, No. 18 Louisville.

Independent (1): No. 3 Notre Dame.

Conference USA (1): No. 21 Liberty.

Pac-12 (1): No. 22 Boise State.

RANKED VS. RANKED

No. 15 USC at No. 10 UCLA: It was only four years ago that they met in this classic rivalry while both were ranked, but this game is far more meaningful because of both teams' positions in regard to the 12-team playoff. UCLA needs the win to improve its résumé and grab a spot in the Big Ten title game. USC needs a convincing win to improve a playoff résumé that is teetering on the edge of extinction.

No. 24 Missouri at No. 19 Oklahoma: Where's Barry Switzer when you need him? This once-classic Big Eight matchup is now a meeting of two good-but-not-great SEC teams. The winner probably has the inside track to a trip to the Citrus Bowl.

Sports.title: Steelers Metcalf ejected for trying to poke Eagles' DeJean in eye
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

PHILADELPHIA -- Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles for attempting to poke cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye.

DeJean said afterward that Metcalf "just missed."

"We were just competing," DeJean said. "Things like that happen in football. It wasn't anything crazy. No one was really saying anything, it was just two guys going at it. He was trying block me, I was trying to get him off of me, things like that. Obviously, it carries over to whatever that was when he got thrown out."

Metcalf left the locker room without speaking to the media after the loss.

DK Metcalf is held back by Steelers teammate Pat Freiermuth in the third quarter Sunday. Metcalf was ejected from the game. Emilee Chinn/Getty Images

The 28-year-old receiver initiated the altercation with DeJean away from the third-quarter play, and then he appeared to also jaw with Eagles safety Marcus Epps. A scrum around the two quickly broke out as teammates moved to separate Metcalf from the Eagles defenders.

Officials threw an unsportsmanlike conduct flag for Metcalf's taunting as the incensed receiver continued talking on his way to the Steelers sideline, escorted by a team staffer. Upon hearing the announcement of his ejection, Metcalf nodded his head and headed for the locker room.

"He knows that's unacceptable," said tight end Pat Freiermuth, who was part of the group trying to separate Metcalf from the situation. "He'll be fine. He's one of my closest [friends] on the team. And so he knows that I have his back in those situations, but it just can't happen."

Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said the Steelers "need" Metcalf so his ejection was disappointing.

"We need him in those games, and that's not acceptable to be thrown out of a game," McCarthy said.

The third-quarter altercation was Metcalf's second of the day. He was also flagged for unnecessary roughness in the first half when he held his block of DeJean well after the play finished. Already deep in their own territory, the Steelers were backed up to their own five-yard line as a result of Metcalf's penalty.

"That was disappointing," quarterback Aaron Rodgers said. "Obviously we love DK, and I don't know what was going on out there, what was happening, but yeah, we can't have two of those."

The ejection marked Metcalf's third career disqualification since his debut in 2019. It's tied with Dre Greenlaw for the most disqualifications in the NFL during that time span, per ESPN Research. DeJean said the Eagles weren't aware of Metcalf's history of ejections and weren't specifically trying to get under the receiver's skin.

"I didn't know how many ejections he had or whatever before going into it," DeJean said. "But he wasn't getting the ball a whole lot during that game, and some receivers could let that get to them. He obviously tried to take it out on me."

As is standard with any ejection, the NFL will review Metcalf's actions for possible additional punishment, including suspension. That means the Steelers could be short-handed as they host the Denver Broncos on Friday afternoon.

McCarthy also said the team will gather all information before determining any additional internal punishment.

"It's emotional on a number of fronts," McCarthy said. "We lost a game, a tough game. You take all that in, and everything will be addressed -- and definitely. We can't have players getting ejected from games."

Acquired in a blockbuster trade that included a second-round pick on the eve of free agency in 2025, Metcalf has hardly lived up to the $132 million contract extension given to him by the Steelers immediately following the acquisition.

Though the deals weren't done concurrently, Metcalf essentially took over the Steelers' No. 1 receiver role for George Pickens, whom the team traded to the Dallas Cowboys two months after landing Metcalf. Pickens, in part, was dealt because of behavior concerns and locker room fit.

While Metcalf led the Steelers with 850 receiving yards last season, he was suspended for the two final regular-season games after an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan during the Steelers' Week 16 win. This season, Metcalf is catching just 48% of his targets, making him the only qualified wide receiver in the NFL catching fewer than 50% of his targets this season.

Metcalf has been flagged for eight accepted penalties through 10 games this season, matching his total number of accepted penalties from last season. Meanwhile, he's on pace for a career low in receiving yards with just 434 on 36 catches with two touchdowns.

By comparison, Pickens has been flagged just three times this season, including once for taunting in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and he has 780 receiving yards and six touchdowns on 57 catches.

At the time of Metcalf's ejection Sunday, he had just one catch for 2 yards on four targets.

Metcalf's ejection, though, gave wide receiver Max Hurleman, a practice squad member elevated for the game, an expanded role in his NFL debut. Hurleman, who played three seasons at FCS program Colgate and one season at Notre Dame, led the Steelers with six catches on seven targets for 61 yards, and he hauled in a 20-yard touchdown reception to pull the game within a field goal with less than two minutes to go.

ESPN's Tim McManus contributed to this report.

Sports.title: Red Wings deal star forward Larkin to Canadiens, ending stalemate
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Former Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin was moved to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal Sunday, a move that ends a drawn-out process of Detroit honoring a trade request Larkin submitted to the team in June.

Larkin along with a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 third-round selection head to Montreal in exchange for forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Samuel Montembeault, prospect Michael Hage, a first-round pick in 2027, a first-round pick in 2029, a second-round pick in 2027 and a fourth-round pick in 2028.

Larkin's contract -- an eight-year, $69.6 million pact he signed in March 2023 -- held a full no-move clause. Originally, the top center was open to being traded only to Florida, Minnesota or Vegas. When a move failed to materialize, Larkin widened the scope to include several other teams, although Montreal wasn't reported to be on even that expanded roster.

Larkin was clearly frustrated, though, by the lack of movement; he has been sitting out, by choice, since October 29, collecting two goals and 10 points in six games before benching himself until a trade came to fruition. In the end, getting back on the ice somewhere else took precedence over landing in his most desired location. Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff wasn't willing to send Larkin just anywhere, showing patience in waiting for a mutually beneficial transaction to materialize.

Dylan Larkin, 30, has 278 goals and 649 points in 818 NHL games, all with Detroit after the Red Wings drafted him with 15th pick in 2014. Brett Holmes/Getty Images

Montreal had been after Larkin with an eye on improving its center depth behind Selke Trophy winner Nick Suzuki. The Canadiens knew Detroit was looking for a hefty return that would include Hage -- Montreal's first-round pick at No. 21 in 2024 -- and they eventually decided it was worth parting with the University of Michigan product before his NHL debut.

Larkin, 30, has 278 goals and 649 points in 818 NHL games to date, all with Detroit after they drafted him 15th overall in 2014. The lack of playoff experience for Larkin since -- with just one appearance in his rookie season and no return opportunities since -- is one of the factors souring him on remaining in the Motor City.

Now Larkin gets a fresh start with the rising Canadiens, who are building off their showing in the Eastern Conference Final last year. In return for Larkin, Detroit gets Dach -- a third-overall selection by Chicago in 2019 hampered by injuries -- and Montembeault -- driven down the depth chart by the emergence of Jacob Fowler and Jakub Dobes - to slot in immediately, with a handful of picks and Hage in the wings to make them better for the future.

Montreal is currently sitting third in the Atlantic Division. Detroit is 13th overall in the Eastern Conference.

Sports.title: Frustrated Saleh calls Titans' effort 'disgusting, embarrassing football'
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

ARLINGTON, Texas -- Tennessee Titans coach Robert Saleh couldn't hide his frustration when he stepped behind the lectern after Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Titans' defense had no answer for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' offense. Dallas scored touchdowns on its first six drives and came away with points on every drive except for their final one, which concluded with victory formation to end the game.

Saleh didn't pull any punches when he was asked about the loss.

"It was disgusting, embarrassing football," Saleh said. "That starts with me. I got to figure it out."

The Cowboys racked up 480 yards of total offense, and Prescott finished with 325 passing yards. Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb led Dallas with 132 receiving yards. This marked the fourth consecutive time an opposing team gained 400 yards of total offense, had a passer with at least 300 yards and a receiver with at least 100 yards against the Titans. Tennessee is 0-4 in that stretch.

Given how well both offenses have played recently, Saleh said he expected the game to be a high-scoring one, but not as high as it was.

"Giving up 50 is unacceptable," linebacker Cedric Gray said. "We got to stop the bleeding."

Opposing offenses have now scored 40-plus points in three consecutive games against Tennessee, joining the 1975 Cleveland Browns, 1981 Baltimore Colts, and 2004 Titans as the only teams to do so since the 1970 NFL merger.

Saleh said that failed execution led to losing too many one-on-one matchups. Cornerback Josh Williams agreed.

"It's a team sport, but somewhere on a play you're going to have a one-on-one matchup," Williams said. "Our job as a professional is to win them."

Saleh said he hoped the players "feel pissed" about the results and called the defense stuck in the mud. He said it's the most frustrating football experience he has had since 2021, when as the Jets' coach his defense gave up 504 points, at an NFL-worst average of 29. This season's Titans are on pace to give up a franchise-record 493 points, also an average of 29.

"We have no choice but to get better," Saleh said. "I mean, s---, it can't get any worse."

Sports.title: NFL draft risers, notes off Saturday's college games: An elite CB class? Two WRs in the top five?
Sports.content:
Open Extended Reactions

Week 12 of the 2026 college football season saw Georgia rout South Carolina, Michigan edge UCLA, Washington take down Indiana, BYU survive against Kansas and Nebraska shock Ohio State.

What about the top 2027 NFL draft prospects? Who stood out? Yes, the draft is still about five months away, but our analysts are always looking down the road, taking early notes on top players and starting to stack their rankings for an exciting class.

With that in mind, Mel Kiper Jr. and Jordan Reid will size up college football action through a draft-centric lens on Sundays all season long. They are answering lingering questions on the best 2027 prospects, sharing insights from scouts, picking out risers to watch and pulling back the curtain on their evaluation process. Here is what they saw and heard through Week 12.

Jump to:

Week 12 | Week 11 | Week 10 | Week 9

Week 8 | Week 7 | Week 6 | Week 5

Week 4 | Week 3 | Week 2

Nov. 22

How would you grade the cornerback class?

Reid: I would say it's a solid nine out of 10. The only reason it's not a perfect score is because of the lack of great depth after the early rounds. We still have a long way to go until April, but as of today, I believe there's a possibility that we could see three corners drafted in the top 10 for the first time since 2005.

Atop my CB board, Notre Dame's Leonard Moore has been consistent and proven as a shutdown corner. He keeps showing his excellent length, speed, physicality and technique, and the 6-foot-2, 197-pound cover man had two pass breakups Saturday against SMU. But the next two CBs in the class matched that, as Clemson's Ashton Hampton and Georgia's Ellis Robinson IV each had two pass breakups of their own in Week 12. Hampton is the linchpin of the Tigers' defense, and it has been a rare occurrence to see him allow a catch this season. And Robinson has transformed from a raw athlete who primarily relied on his tools into being a true technician.

We haven't seen two WRs go in the top five since 2003. Could it happen in 2027?

Reid: I think it's certainly a possibility. In my latest mock draft, I had Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith going No. 1 to the Titans and Indiana's Charlie Becker going No. 4 to the Chargers (after having L.A. trade down from No. 2). And both of those receivers put on shows in Week 12. Smith had 165 yards and two touchdowns against Nebraska, while Becker went for 167 yards and a score against Washington.

Smith remains in a tier of his own. I saw him up close this weekend, and while his 68-yard touchdown grab was great, his most impressive play came when he raced past double coverage to haul in a 31-yard touchdown in the back of the end zone, somehow managing to get his feet in bounds. He is sure-handed and can glide past defenders with ease. And Becker just has easy vertical speed to stride past matchups and win vertically.

What else are you hearing this week?

Kiper: Houston left guard Shadre Hurst was very impressive against West Virginia. At 6-foot-2 and 304 pounds, he is a drive blocker who just gets after it every weekend. Hurst can pull, he sustains well, and he shows the ability to anchor as a pass blocker. He lands a strong punch, too. And I see good lateral quickness along the line. Amazingly, Hurst has not allowed a single sack over 55 career games. He looks like he could go in the early-Day 3 area, and I think he could start somewhere in the NFL.

Reid: At 6-foot-2 and 315 pounds, Nebraska's Justin Evans isn't as tall as some of his counterparts in this center class, but his grit and strength at the point of attack keep popping on tape. He was great in the win over the Buckeyes. I have Evans graded as a mid-Day 3 prospect, but he's a major stock-up candidate who could find his way into the middle rounds.

Kiper: I love his experience and versatility. Evans has 42 career starts, and he was a starter at left guard earlier in his career before becoming one at center. His high school wrestling background shows on tape -- he's strong and agile. Evans should compete for a job in the NFL as either a late-Day 2 or early-Day 3 pick.

Kiper: All I can say on Kansas edge rusher Leroy Harris III is "wow." He had a really impressive performance against BYU, with nine tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a pass breakup. He now has five sacks over his past three games. Harris is 6-foot-5 and 270 pounds, but he's still quick. He's good on lateral pursuit, can drop into coverage, plays fast off the edge and wastes no time disengaging against the run. And he makes plays on the ball with six pass breakups and four forced fumbles over 11 games this season. He has also blocked two kicks, showing some special teams value.

The only time he didn't Saturday -- and really the only blemish on his outstanding day -- was on a touchdown pass where he had the WR blanketed but just didn't locate the pass. Sharpe is looking like a second-round pick.

He has the speed to get to the second level or bounce outside to the perimeter. But at 5-foot-11 and 205 pounds, Lacy is also really tough inside. He runs hard and can be creative between the tackles with subtle moves, nimble feet and physicality. I love his running style -- he just finds yards. Plus, Lacy displayed some solid pass-blocking ability (especially in the first half) and can line up out wide as a pass catcher. I have a third-round grade on him.

At 6-foot, 206 pounds, he is a sudden receiving threat who can make defenders look silly when trying to bring him down in the open field. With six touchdowns this season, Thomas is a game breaker who can change games in an instant. He got grades in the range of early-to-mid Day 3 coming into the year, but scouts that I've talked to have him graded as a top-100 prospect now.

Georgia's Chris Cole is the clear top linebacker in the class, but there are mixed opinions among evaluators on who's next after that. And Omosigho's effort, speed and playmaking ability make him a huge stock-up candidate with a strong Day 2 grade.

Kiper: I love's Omosigho's versatility, too. UCLA uses him both off-ball inside and off the edge outside. He can get off blocks, and he sheds and diagnoses very effectively. Omosigho is very consistent game to game.

Oct. 11

Is Arch Manning sliding a bit in the class? Is he still an early-Round 1 prospect?

Reid: Manning has two or three plays per game that explain why some scouts still view him as a potential top-10 pick. But those plays are surrounded by too much inconsistency, which is why I have him graded as a Day 2 prospect right now on my QB Hot Board.

Manning has a curious way of making routine throws look difficult ... and difficult throws look routine. Against Oklahoma, he had a beautiful 41-yard touchdown pass to Cam Coleman in the first quarter, evading pressure and keeping his eyes downfield. But then he had two egregious fourth-quarter interceptions, one a pick-six to help the Sooners take the lead. He ultimately went 19-for-31 for 260 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions.

At 6-foot-4 and 222 pounds, Manning has scattershot accuracy throughout games, which is a result of his footwork and mechanics being out of whack. The inconsistencies, turnovers and lack of accuracy is reminiscent of what he showed during the first half of the 2025 season.

Could LaNorris Sellers get back into the early-round mix?

Reid: Sellers entered this season as one of the most polarizing signal-callers in the class among NFL scouts and evaluators. But the past two weeks -- a combined 505 passing yards and seven total touchdowns (six passing, one rushing) against Kentucky and Florida -- have definitely been encouraging for him. On Saturday against the Gators, Sellers went 23-of-35 for 279 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions. He also added 20 rushing yards and a fifth score on 14 carries.

After early-season struggles with field vision and chemistry with his perimeter playmakers, Sellers has been able to piece together exciting flashes with his A-level traits. At 6-foot-3 and 238 pounds, his arm power and mobility are two of his greatest assets. Scouts whom I've spoken with view Sellers as a middle-to-late-round option. But if this current trend continues, yes, he certainly has the potential to climb back into the early-round picture. The NFL is a traits-driven league, and Sellers' arm talent could push a team to take a swing as early as near the end of Day 2.

He finished with 222 rushing yards and two scores against Texas A&M, displaying his vision and tackle-breaking ability. At 6-foot and 216 pounds, he is a tough, rugged and grind-it-out type of runner who is challenging for defenses to bring down over the course of a game. Roberts came into the season with early-to-mid-Day 3 grades, but I think he's now a potential late-Day 2 selection.

On the Wildcats' first play from scrimmage against LSU, Price paved a beautiful run lane for CJ Baxter (who turned it into a 77-yard run), showing off his powerful hands and ability to sustain at the point of attack. Price was seen as a late-round hopeful coming into the season. Now? He has a case as one of the top three players at the position. Kiper: I think Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone could enter the Round 1 discussion. He's a pure powerhouse, and he pushed the pocket against Texas. Stewart will still have to answer questions about what transpired prior to his suspension -- including throwing a punch at an Alabama player and arguing with his coaches -- but his talent and overall ceiling arguably tops all defenders in the 2027 class.

At 6-foot-6 and 265 pounds, he is a physical specimen with good hands, an impressive catch radius, some downfield ability, strong route running and after-the-catch traits. Plus, he can block, making two key ones in this game. Clarke is out of the NFL Academy in London, and he's still learning the game. He's just scratching the surface of what he can be, and I expect him to be an intriguing Day 3 pick.

Oct. 4

Is there any chance Jeremiah Smith goes No. 1 in April?

Reid: Smith will be mentioned in the same breath as some of the best receiver prospects we've ever seen, and we saw why Saturday when he caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns against Iowa. But even elite receivers like Calvin Johnson (No. 2) and Larry Fitzgerald (No. 3) weren't selected at the top of the draft. And while I believe Smith is the unquestioned best player in the 2027 class, it's just really rare to see a wideout drafted with the top pick. That has historically been a quarterback, offensive tackle or edge rusher. And Keyshawn Johnson was the last receiver to go No. 1 -- in 1996.

There are a lot of things to consider here, though. What happens if a team that doesn't need a quarterback earns the first pick, like the Buccaneers, Chargers or Giants? Could that team trade back for a haul of selections ... or could it simply select the best player in the draft? I'll say there's a 10% chance just because Smith is that good, but I'd still project a quarterback ends up going first (even though none of the signal-callers have truly emerged quite yet).

Sept. 27

Is Colin Simmons the runaway top edge rusher in this class?

Reid: The scouting trail continued for me this week in Knoxville, Tennessee, where I had a front-row seat for Simmons' five-sack performance against the Vols. It tied the Texas single-game record set in 1990. Outside of an excessive sack celebration from Simmons, it was one of the best defensive performances that I've ever seen. At 6-foot-3 and 246 pounds, his combination of upfield burst and closing speed make it challenging for blockers to keep pace with him. Most impressive was how many different spots he got pressure from. Simmons not only rushed from both edges but also reduced down inside on late downs and wreaked havoc from there, as well.

I got to see South Carolina's Dylan Stewart last week against Mississippi State, and he should be a top pick, too. It's likely going to be a "traits against production" debate between the two; Stewart is the more explosive athlete with better size (6-foot-5, 250 pounds), but Simmons continues to produce at an elite level (seven sacks this season). But yes ... Simmons is the clear top player at the position at this point in the season.

What's the earliest Jadan Baugh could come off the board if he keeps this up?

Reid: A tough and rugged runner at 6-foot-1 and 225 pounds, Baugh has the makings of a top-20 pick. I think the Florida standout could go in the teens, as there are a lot of NFL teams that need a true RB1.

How good has Baugh been? Per ESPN Research, he became only the second player in the past 20 seasons with at least 100 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in each of the first four games of a season, joining Leonard Fournette (2015). After 142 yards and three touchdowns against Ole Miss, he now has 600 rushing yards and 11 TDs on the season -- both top-two numbers in the FBS. The clear RB1 in the class so far, Baugh has terrific contact balance and lower-body quickness. With back-to-back games with at least 25 carries, he has proved that he's capable of taking on a heavy workload.

Trinidad Chambliss and Darian Mensah are the current Heisman Trophy favorites. Has either QB played his way into the first round?

Reid: I do have Chambliss in Round 1 now, but I'm taking a wait-and-see approach with Mensah; Miami just hasn't played anyone yet.

Let's start with the 6-foot-3, 205-pound Mensah, whom I saw in person Friday when Miami faced Wake Forest. He started the game with an impressive 24 straight completions and finished 30-of-34 for 220 passing yards and three touchdowns. I would classify his arm strength as slightly above average, as he has displayed beautiful touch down the field and enough velocity to drive the ball. The fourth quarter was the first time we saw him pressured and knocked off schedule this season, and the Hurricane's modest schedule so far brings curiosity. How will Mensah look against a higher quality opponent? Scouts already have Nov. 7 circled -- that's when Miami travels to Notre Dame. Mensah is certainly in the first-round conversation, but I want to see him against better competition.

Chambliss, meanwhile, went 33-of-48 for 363 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and one interception against LSU. Oregon's Dante Moore lost. Texas' Arch Manning pulled off a comeback. Is there any movement at the top of the QB class?

Reid: We are only two weeks into the season and there's still plenty of evaluation time left, but Week 2 spoke loudly for the top of the 2027 quarterback class. Through two weeks, Moore -- and Oregon as a whole -- has looked extremely inconsistent. He got off to a woeful start in the surprising 39-31 loss to Oklahoma State, going 1-of-6 for 9 yards in the first quarter. I saw three overthrows, and Moore didn't seem able to get comfortable. He was my top passer entering the season, but the QB1 race seems to have opened up a bit.

In fact, Manning is now my top-ranked quarterback. He led the Longhorns to 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter in an epic 24-23 comeback win over Ohio State. He made two impressive throws in the first half that weren't even completions. He placed the ball nicely on both the bizarre interception off Cam Coleman and the clear drop by Ryan Wingo near the end zone. In the second half, Manning was 16-of-23 for 136 yards and one touchdown, and he was much more poised as he executed the offense.

Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker made a statement. In his very first game against a Power 4 opponent, he finished with 317 passing yards and two touchdowns while adding another 109 yards and a score on the ground. Mestemaker -- along with Miami's Darian Mensah -- are certainly staking their own claims in the QB1 race. But I have Manning at the moment.

Kiper: I don't know that there even is a true QB1 right now. Remember when Moore looked like Superman against Penn State last season? I keep waiting for him to show that again, but he just hasn't taken over a game since then. And while Manning led the Longhorns back, I want to see consistency across the whole game.

Mestemaker was definitely the better quarterback in that Oregon-Oklahoma State game, but he still has 17 career starts (and threw two interceptions for the second straight game). Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Miami's Mensah have looked awesome, but neither QB plays anyone of significance until they face each other ... in November (though Carr does get BYU next month). Sam Leavitt threw three interceptions for LSU against Louisiana Tech on Saturday, and NC State's CJ Bailey has had uneven play.

So far, this quarterback class -- one that was widely expected to be amazing -- has underwhelmed. There's still a lot of time. We're only through Week 2. But I want to see the group level up and play with more consistency. This is the reason I don't do rankings until October -- we have to let these guys play a bit.

Even in the loss, it was a huge game for Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith. What has impressed you most about his start to the season?

Reid: There aren't enough words to describe how special Smith is as a prospect. The most impressive part about his start is that everyone knows that the Buckeyes are going to target No. 4, and yet nobody has managed to stop him. He finished with eight catches for 164 yards and a touchdown Saturday, meaning Smith has now surpassed 150-plus receiving yards in three consecutive games dating back to last season (he had 151, plus two touchdowns, last weekend vs. Ball State). That's the longest streak for an Ohio State receiver in at least the past 30 seasons, per ESPN Research.

Smith is capable of winning with speed or power, and he's a true mismatch for any coverage that secondaries attempt to play against him. He entered the season as the top prospect overall on my board and could end up with the highest grade that I've ever given out to a receiver.

Kiper: Smith has worked on becoming more dominant after the catch, and it's showing. He can power through with his physicality, but adding that YAC fear factor could make him even more of a problem for opponents. And Smith looks quicker and more dynamic once the ball is in his hands right now.

What else are you hearing this week?

Kiper: LSU edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen had three sacks and four tackles for loss against Louisiana Tech. At 6-foot-4 and 244 pounds, he shows impressive speed off the edge and just explodes out of the blocks. But he also shows a really good inside move to beat offensive tackles and even makes plays in pursuit. I think Umanmielen could still add weight to his frame -- he gets swallowed up at times -- but he has a track record of being disruptive. He could be a good rotational pass rusher in the NFL, and I'd slot him into the second-round range right now (though he could play his way into Round 1 if he keeps this up).

Reid: The scouting trail continued for me this weekend, as I made a stop in Minnesota to see the Gophers against Mississippi State. One prospect that I wanted to pay close attention to was Bulldogs cornerback Kelley Jones. At 6-foot-4 and 205 pounds, he checks a ton of boxes for pro secondaries. His length, technique and ball skills all carried over into the game; he had a pass breakup and caused plenty of trouble for wideouts at the line of scrimmage. Jones is viewed as a potential top-40 pick, and I believe that he can end up at the back end of Round 1.

Reid: Arizona State receiver Reed Harris keeps catching my eye. The Boston College transfer finished with nine catches for 189 yards and two touchdowns against Texas A&M. At 6-foot-5 and 220 pounds, he has an outstanding frame and showcased his long speed on a 58-yard touchdown. Harris is viewed as a middle-round prospect, but with continued production, he could find himself squarely in the Day 2 mix.

Kiper: I was impressed with Harris, too. He has length and big hands, and he tracks the ball really well. He has averaged 20.7 yards per catch over his career; big plays are his calling card. And while he's being used mainly outside, I think he could be a big slot receiver at the next level. I have a similar grade on Harris at the moment, Jordan -- he's probably in that late-Day 2, early-Day 3 range.

play 0:35 Cutter Boley finds Reed Harris for a 58-yard ASU TD

Kiper: We weren't even sure Texas offensive tackle Trevor Goosby would be playing early in the season, with the bone bruise in his knee after an August injury in practice. But he's out there, and he played solid on Saturday night against the Buckeyes. Goosby anchors well, making him tough to beat in pass protection. But despite not being the most athletic OT prospect, he also made a nice block in space. The 6-foot-7, 325-pounder remains very consistent, and he's a clear early-to-mid Round 1 guy.

Reid: Michigan edge rusher John Henry Daley was a major addition in the transfer portal for the Wolverines, and he showed why in the 17-10 upset victory over Oklahoma. At 6-foot-5 and 252 pounds, he finished with a sack and three tackles for loss, as his tenacious effort and deep repertoire of pass-rush moves were on full display. Daley suffered a torn Achilles last November while at Utah, and there were question marks about his overall explosiveness post-injury, but he has shown why many scouts believe he's a top-100 prospect with the potential to climb even higher.

Kiper: Alabama's Devan Thompkins is going to have a lot of NFL eyes on him this fall if he keeps playing this way. At 6-foot-5 and 300 pounds, he is probably a 3-4 defensive end in the pros. He can win off the edge, he can win with a rip move, and he can win with his bull rush. Despite his size, he can even drop into coverage, and he made a nice play there against Kentucky. Thompkins brings scheme versatility, and you'll see him move inside at times. But no matter where he lines up, he brings imposing size at the point of attack and plays with high intensity. Thompkins had two sacks Saturday. He's a second-round player with the potential to rise.

Kiper: I think Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons might be a 2028 guy because he has started only four games, but he has looked good so far this season. The Ole Miss transfer can spin it with the best of them, and the ball jumps out of the lefty's hand. He throws with accuracy and touch -- he's a pure passer. After three TD passes against Kansas on Friday night, he has a spotless 7-0 touchdown-to-interception ratio on the season.
