Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr in talks to fight Kell Brook in first bout since Conor Benn loss - with 'Special K' to come out of retirement
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr is in talks to fight Kell Brook in his return to the ring.

Brook, 40, has not fought since beating Amir Khan in 2022, but has emerged as a potential option to fight Eubank in his first fight since losing to Conor Benn late last year.

According to Elliott Amoakoh, the executive director of Eubank Jr's management team, Nova Sport LLC, any agreement is still a way away.

He told Sky Sports: 'Talks are ongoing but the date, purse and location are yet to be confirmed.'

Ben Shalom, however, who has represented both fighters in the past, told talkSPORT: 'It's a fight that we have been trying to make for a couple of months.

'They have pretty much agreed terms on both sides, there is just some final bits to go. It is one of the biggest fights in British boxing. I think you are right on February and in Manchester.'

Chris Eubank Jr (pictured) is in talks with Kell Brook to face off in his return to the ring

Brook (pictured) hasn't fought since 2022 and retired after beating long-term rival Amir Khan

Brook retired after beating long-time rival Khan in Manchester, having been linked with a fight with Eubank in the aftermath.

Brook has seemed almost certain to return to the ring, having revealed his return fight would be 'announced soon'.

He retired with 40 wins from 43 fights, and is a former International Boxing Federation welterweight champion.

Having debuted as a professional in 2004, he didn't lose until September 2016, when he was stopped in the fifth round by Gennady Golovkin.

Eubank Jr, meanwhile, had faced questions over retirement following his defeat by Benn but has refused to call it quits on his 15-year career.

He had claimed to have major fights scheduled for 2026, but has taken a whole year out of action.

Sports.title: English boxer, 18, banned from World Championships after extraordinary sex test mix-up: 'Broken' teenager reveals how his dream was shattered after team forgot to prove he was a man
Sports.content:
A teenage English boxer has said they have been left 'broken' after being denied the chance to compete at the World Championships due to officials failing to organise a sex verification test to prove he is male.

George Francis, 18, had been due to represent England at the Under-19 World Championships in Budva, Montenegro last month.

Francis was withdrawn from competition on the eve of the event after an administration error by England Boxing, with the governing body having failed to arrange the necessary sex verification test.

'They got me in a room and told me that I couldn't box because they didn't know if I was a boy or a girl, basically,' Francis told the BBC.

'The explanation was that they couldn't provide a blood sample for me in time. Everyone else was able to provide a blood sample, but they just forgot me.

'Somehow I wasn't on the system.

George Francis, 18, missed out on competing at the Under-19 World Championships after England Boxing failed to arrange a necessary sex verification test. Source: Instagram/georgefrancis_07

'It was the worst news I've ever had in my life.

'I wouldn't wish it on anyone, to be honest. I was just broken. They were speaking to me and I couldn't even really hear. I was devastated.

'I couldn't really talk. I literally couldn't feel anything. There was a hole left there.'

Francis's situation, first reported by The Times, followed the mandatory introduction of sex verification tests by the sport's governing body World Boxing.

World Boxing announced the move last year, with genetic sex testing initially introduced for female competitors aged 18 and above. The governing body stated the move was due to a 'duty of care to deliver safety and competitiveness fairness'.

It followed controversy at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, where boxers Imane Khelif and Lin Yu-ting won gold.

Khelif and Lin had been disqualified from the previous year's World Championships, with boxing's former governing body – the International Boxing Association – claiming the pair had failed sex eligibility tests.

Earlier this year, Lin was cleared to compete in women's events following a review of her sex eligibility.

World Boxing's mandatory tests were extended to include male boxers earlier this year.

Francis had been required to undergo a test due to turning 18 four days before travelling to the World Championships.

Francis, a multiple national champion, had been required to undergo a mandatory test after turning 18 days before the World Championships. Source: Instagram/georgefrancis_07

World Boxing introduced sex testing last year amid the controversy surrounding Algerian boxer Imane Khelif's participation at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games

The multiple national and GB champion has claimed he is considering turning professional following the mix-up.

England Boxing reportedly contacted Francis's father to apologise for the 'administrative oversight', with the governing body stressing it will 'strengthen processes' to avoid a repeat incident.

'We maintained open communication with George and his family throughout, despite this, a resolution was not possible,' an England Boxing statement read.

'George remained a valued member of the England team, including representing the squad as flag bearer.

'England Boxing has no greater priority than the health and wellbeing of athletes on its performance pathway and are committed to learning from this experience and strengthening our processes to prevent a recurrence.'

World Boxing's policy requires boxers to undergo a once-in-a-lifetime PCR (polymerase chain reaction) test to determine their sex and their eligibility to compete in either the male or female category.

The PCR test is a laboratory technique used to detect specific genetic material, in this case the SRY gene, which reveals the presence of the Y chromosome that is an indicator of male biological sex.

A dozen boxers, representing five nations, were last year blocked from competing at the World Championships in Liverpool because deadlines for their sex tests were missed.

Under World Boxing rules, national federations are responsible for testing and will be required to confirm the sex of their athletes when entering them into World Boxing competitions

Sports.title: Viddal Riley opens up on why he stuck with his dad instead of moving to Las Vegas to train with a Mayweather as he eyes fighting Oleksandr Usyk
Sports.content:
Viddal Riley opens up on why he stuck with his dad instead of moving to Las Vegas to train with a Mayweather as he eyes fighting Oleksandr Usyk

Derrick Riley almost never speaks publicly. Ahead of his son's European title defence against Seydi Coupe at Wembley on Saturday, father and son sat down together to talk about trust, tough love, Joe and Enzo Calzaghe, and why Oleksandr Usyk returning to cruiserweight is 'a little bit greedy'.

But to understand where Viddal is going, you first have to understand the man in his corner.

Derrick Riley has been watching his son get punched since he was a little boy. He still can't put into words what it does to him.

'It's strange,' he exclusively tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I've been doing it for a long time. But you have to try and separate it. You have to shut off the emotion and the sentiment. If you let that sentiment in, I think that's a bad thing. That's your boy in there. He's getting hit and he's getting hurt. I would say it's not easy, and some people can't separate it.'

It's rare to hear Derrick say anything at all. He stays out of the spotlight, and he leaves the talking to his son. Sitting beside Viddal days before the biggest night of his career, when the unbeaten Londoner headlines OVO Arena Wembley against Frenchman Coupe, you quickly see how their relationship works.

'Only my dad would be able to speak to me the way he does,' Viddal says. 'But it comes from a place of genuine care. It's not a job. Someone can only care so much when it's a job. It's like being an employee at a company and having your own business. It's a completely different mentality. This is my business, so he cares and I care.'

WATCH THE EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW ON THE DAILY MAIL BOXING YOUTUBE CHANNEL

Derrick Riley (R), the father and trainer of son Viddal Riley (L), almost never speaks publicly

Viddal is set to take on Seydi Coupe at Wembley on Saturday evening, headlining the event

Derrick added: 'Part of caring too is the fact it's the same brain you've got now that you're going to need after boxing. You can't go to the shop and buy a new one, so you need to protect it. That's why it's difficult to separate the two.'

Viddal grins and says: 'It's the same brain I need for the grandkids.'

The partnership was not always a given. At 21, Viddal went looking for something of his own.

'I was at a stage where I was trying to find some independence. That's the truth,' he says. 'I was presented with the opportunity to go to Vegas, train with a Mayweather and work with Jeff Mayweather. I was thinking, "Yeah, I'm doing this my way. I'm doing things differently."

'But the truth is, I knew my ceiling was getting lower. And I knew the only person who could push that ceiling higher, and continue to do so, was my dad.

'So when I came back to the UK, I said, "Dad, can you train me?" He was like, "Nah, I'm alright. I'm not doing it." And I was like, "Nah, I need you to do it, because that's the only way this dream we've been talking about is going to be fulfilled."

Derrick's refusal was not stubbornness. It was self-preservation.

When asked why he initially said no, Derrick admitted: 'I know what the game is about. I know what boxing involves, and I thought to myself, do I want that in my life? It's a good question when you're in your 50s. I've lived life. There are no rose-coloured glasses. I know what boxing is. But I had to think about it.'

Derrick Riley has been watching his son get punched since Viddal was a little boy

The irony was that he was already qualified for the job. 'By this point I already had a British Boxing Board of Control licence, because I was in the corner with Viddal in Dubai,' he laughs. 'So, funnily enough, I already had the licence.

'He looked at me with those puppy-dog eyes, and I thought, you know what? We've got to do this. But I did say to him, "It's not going to be easy, son. We're going to have to do this properly. You're going to get no ranking belts, no intercontinental belt, nothing like that. You're going to have to do it the old-school way, with the British, Commonwealth, European, and it's going to be hard." And we've done it, man.'

The record backs him up. Viddal is 14-0 with seven knockouts. He won the European title in April with a wide points win over the vastly experienced Pole Mateusz Masternak at The O2, a fight that also served as an IBF world title eliminator. Saturday is his first defence, and it's a mandatory one against a challenger who is also unbeaten in 14.

For a template of what father and son can achieve together, Derrick points to Wales.

'I appreciate Enzo [Calzaghe] more now than I did before,' he says. 'I've always appreciated him, but I appreciate him even more now because I'm doing it myself. People have no idea what it takes, and for him to do what he did with Joe was absolutely amazing. I take my hat off to him.

'Don't get me wrong, I had a boxing background. I wasn't great, I wasn't pulling up trees, but I had a boxing background. Enzo had no boxing background whatsoever, yet he managed to do what he did with Joe. That is amazing.

'It's funny. During the fight with Bernard Hopkins, I think Enzo was saying something to Joe, and Joe gave Enzo a look. I know that look. I give Viddal that same look.'

Viddal and his father have become a force to be reckoned with but they've faced criticism

Joe Calzaghe has described his own brief split from his father, and how he came back because he realised he wanted those highs to be shared with Enzo. Viddal sees the same story in his own.

'We relate to that story because we were severely doubted,' he says. 'It wasn't celebrated. The partnership is only now starting to get some recognition, with people acknowledging that it works. It wasn't like that at the beginning.

'It's been suggested to me that my dad shouldn't train me and that there are people better suited to the job. That's what we walked into. It wasn't accepted as, "Oh yeah, this is a nice family dynamic, let's get it going." It was challenged. The aim was to separate us.

'When we're up against it, we just keep proving ourselves, time and time again. That's what I take from Enzo and Joe. It wasn't celebrated either. They had to keep doing what they were doing, and he turned his son into a 46-0 fighter and one of the best to have ever done it.'

Fathers who train their sons are often accused of living through them. John Fury, so often more visible than Tyson, is the obvious example. Derrick, a former boxer himself, rejects the comparison.

'I don't live vicariously through Viddal. I don't want that,' he says. 'I'm not hogging the camera. It's not about me. It's about Viddal. He asked me to help him, and I'll help him.'

Viddal is just as clear about who he fights for. 'I do it primarily, first and foremost, for me,' he says. 'And very quickly after that, it's for everyone around me that's put work into me achieving it, because it couldn't be done by myself.

Derrick has said he resonates with Enzo (pictured right) and Joe Calzaghe (pictured left)

'When I became British champion, it made me give my dad the belt. We sat down at home for years watching people pick up the Lonsdale belt and hold the Lonsdale belt. So I heard the announcement, "British champion", and I'm like, "Dad, hold this." That's something he's always deserved.'

By rights, Viddal should already have fought for a world title. When Jai Opetaia was stripped of the IBF belt after signing with Zuffa Boxing, the Masternak win put Viddal in line for a shot at the vacant title against New Zealand's David Nyika. Then Opetaia sued the IBF, the governing body held off sanctioning the fight, and Viddal was left waiting.

At the same time, the division has been turned upside down. Opetaia is moving up to heavyweight to face Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua card in Cardiff on December 11. David Benavidez holds the WBA and WBO belts and faces WBC champion Michal Cieslak next month. And now Oleksandr Usyk wants to come back down.

'As I have been saying, it's messy, but I'm trying to get in the mess,' Viddal says. 'I don't want to be on the outskirts of that mess. I'm trying to be in it.

'Right now, I'm just on the outside of the door. I can hear the music in the club, I can hear the bassline. I know there's a vibe in there. I've been seeing the people getting in the door, walking past me. I want to get in there. And Coupe this weekend is another step towards that.'

The most famous person trying to get through that door is Usyk. The Ukrainian became undisputed at cruiserweight, moved up to become undisputed twice at heavyweight, and his team says he now plans to return to 200lbs to chase Benavidez and become undisputed at cruiserweight again. He hasn't fought at the weight since knocking out Tony Bellew in November 2018, and he turns 40 in January.

Viddal admires him. But he isn't convinced.

'It's a bit greedy. It's a little bit greedy,' he says. 'He's completed the level here. He's gone up, he's completed it there, and I think he's just needing that challenge. He's a guy you can tell lives for challenge. All he does is take challenges. "If I'm fighting for a world title, I'm going to go to your country and I'll beat you there." He's that character. That's what makes him a GOAT. That's what makes him a legend.

Viddal has said Oleksandr Usyk is 'greedy' for returning to the cruiserweight division

'But it's dangerous too. Forty years old, dropping all that weight. He hasn't been a cruiserweight since 2018. If I'm in his circle, I'm saying, "Bro, you ain't got to do this. Why? There's no need to." It's not going to be financial. It's just that craving for a challenge.'

Regardless, Viddal is happy with where he is at.

'What I like is that if I'd done this interview four or five years ago, everyone would have asked me, "Do you want to fight Tommy Fury or Jake Paul?" he says. 'Now people ask me, "Would I fight Usyk?"

'Clearly, I'm doing something right.'

Sports.title: F1 plans two-team engine supply limit under 2030 V8 rules
Sports.content:
F1 is planning a shift to just two power unit supplies per manufacturer in 2030, Autosport has learned, raising questions over the status of Mercedes' three current customers.

Over the Las Vegas weekend the FIA announced there was unanimous support to bring the next generation of power unit regulations forward to 2030. That includes a move to 2.1-litre V8 engines, including a turbocharger, a maximum of 200 kilowatts of electric power and the use of sustainable fuels.

That move satisfies the demand for cheaper and less complex engines, which FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 chief Stefano Domenicali had been pursuing in unison. Meanwhile, adding a turbo was a key requirement for the likes of Audi and also ensures engine noise remains at a suitable level for some of F1's urban venues.

What was also part of a wide-ranging document the FIA produced on the 2030 framework, but wasn't part of the public announcement, is an agreement between the six 2030 power unit manufacturers to supply just two teams each. This also includes their works team, leaving just one single engine supply available for external customer teams.

Autosport understands that one aim of the move is to reduce the political influence of manufacturers supplying a large share of the grid, in this case Mercedes and Ferrari, while the manufacturers in question had also been willing to downsize as supplying F1 engines is a loss-making operation, with supplies capped at just $18m per season.

Ferrari is currently supplying the works team, Haas and Cadillac, but the latter will be moving to in-house engines from 2030, meaning the question of Ferrari's supply is solving itself. Red Bull Powertrains will also be taking care of two teams, Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, while at present Audi, Aston Martin partner Honda and Cadillac's shareholder General Motors will all have their own works teams as their one and only confirmed customer.

Photo by: Manuel Eletto

The Mercedes question

That leaves the question of what will happen to Mercedes and the customers of Mercedes High Performance Powertrains. Alongside the works team in Brackley, the Brixworth operation is currently supplying McLaren, Williams as well as Alpine, whose parent company Renault recently abandoned and sold its in-house engine operation.

Per the 2030 framework, two of those three teams would be looking for a new engine supply if the FIA World Motor Sport Council approves the proposal in Shanghai next month. That seismic shift will set up months of political intrigue in the F1 paddock as teams scramble to secure what has been F1's most reliable and performant power unit supplier ever since F1 moved to hybrid engines in 2014, or conclude deals with currently less desirable options.

Autosport.com understands that both McLaren and Williams are fancying their chances of remaining with Mercedes. And while McLaren at least explored the idea of becoming its own power unit manufacturer when a move to a cheaper formula would make that more feasible than it is now, CEO Zak Brown indicated that ship has sailed for 2030 as he aims to remain a Mercedes customer.

"It's something we've looked at in the past, but we're very happy with HPP," Brown said in Las Vegas on Thursday. "I think we've proven that we can win championships with them, so we don't have any intention to have anything in the back of our car other than a Mercedes."

Zak Brown on the idea of McLaren building its own engines: "It's something we've looked at in the past, but we're very happy with HPP. I think we've proven that we can win championships with them, so we don't have any intention to have anything in the back of our car other than a Mercedes." Photo by: Alex Pantling / Getty Images

Mercedes' intentions about what its ideal customer team would look like are less clear right now. Having been beaten by McLaren in 2024 and 2025, CEO Toto Wolff maintained that a win for a customer is still a feather in the cap for HPP and the Mercedes brand as a whole, while a strong customer team also provides a valuable chassis benchmark for the works operation.

And while Brown hailed HPP as an "awesome partner", it's no secret that the relationship between HPP and McLaren has at least come under some strain at the start of this year amid a knowledge gap between the works team and its customer over how to exploit and deploy the complex new power units.

Whether Mercedes will continue to lease engines to its most formidable rival or whether a deal with a midfield team is the preferred option will likely become the subject of plenty of intrigue in the coming months.

Why FIA engine is dead

What is certain is that the FIA's proposed third-party engine plan is now dead in the water. With F1 power units becoming less complex and expensive in 2030, FIA president Ben Sulayem had floated the idea of sourcing a supply of off-the-shelf, white-label engines to further alleviate concerns over team independence.

However, that plan never seemed economically viable for any prospective engine builder, and with all six PUMs at the table now unanimously agreeing to 2030's key infrastructure, a cap of two supplies would mean there are at least 12 power unit supplies available for 11 teams.

The FIA did include a safety net in case one of the six manufacturers decides to drop out, adding a clause under which a departing manufacturer’s F1 power unit intellectual property would transfer to the FIA, which could then assign it to a new manufacturer coming in.

As is the case today, there will also be an "obligation to supply", meaning the FIA could force one of the manufacturers to supply an additional, third team with an engine if that outfit can't arrange a deal to find one, which may well end up becoming a key clause.

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali have long been in agreement over the future direction of F1's power units. Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

What has also been agreed is the basis for the power unit cost cap for the 2030-2034 period. The cap will remain at today's figure of $190m for 2030 before falling by $7.5m per year, ending at $160m for the 2034 season.

That sliding scale helps manufacturers with the initial development cost of the new power units. A development freeze of the current engines from 2028, as well as a ban on V8 dyno testing until the summer of that year, is expected to help F1's current manufacturers manage their resources between the two projects. Existing manufacturers will also receive more cost-cap headroom than newcomer General Motors, which can now abandon its V6 plans and just focus on the V8 program in Charlotte. GM is understood to be signing up to a budget cap of $170m for the first couple of years.

Why early deal is so crucial for F1

There are still several important topics to be fleshed out further by the manufacturers, such as the exact nature of the electric push-to-pass system as it would need to work in conjunction with the chassis design to promote close racing.

But by defining the overarching framework and key engine architecture, which will be rubber-stamped by the FIA World Motor Sport Council, both the manufacturers and the FIA can now get to work on the next rules cycle on a reasonable timeline.

That should help the governing body come up with chassis regulations which are tuned to work well with the new power units and deliver a more pure and exciting set of rules, without facing the prospect of having to adapt to late U-turns by OEMs, which led to 2026's compromised and criticised formula to begin with.

Sports.title: Camara to finish F1 season with Haas, ending F2 title bid
Sports.content:
Haas rookie Rafael Camara will see out the season with Haas in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, effectively ending his F2 championship challenge.

Camara was confirmed in October as a full-time replacement for Esteban Ocon in 2027, and was fast-tracked into the seat after Ocon's relationship with the US-owned team deteriorated.

After test driver Ryo Hirakawa took over Ocon's car midway through the Mexico Grand Prix weekend, Camara made his F1 debut on home soil in Brazil and was also in the VF-26 at this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The final two rounds presented a bigger decision to make, though, because the 21-year-old is leading the F2 championship by seven points over Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov. Drivers are unable to take part in both F1 and F2 on the same weekend.

Haas has now decided to keep the Brazilian in the seat to finish the season, rather than bringing back Hirakawa, to give Camara as much experience as possible ahead of his 2027 rookie campaign.

"We’re excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and build on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America," said Haas F1 Team boss Ayao Komatsu.

"I’m delighted that Rafa’s embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team. We now get to finish the season together which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get underway."

Rafael Camara, Haas Photo by: Lars Baron / LAT Images via Getty Images

Camara finished 20th after a difficult maiden race in Interlagos in the wet, and took 16th in Las Vegas.

While Tsolov now just needs seven points to match Camara, Camara’s absence also boosts third-placed Alex Dunne’s title chances, who trails the Brazilian by 18 points.

Sports.title: Hadjar penalised after backing up Russell in Las Vegas GP, Perez given grid drop for Qatar GP
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar has received a 10-second penalty for driving unnecessarily slowly in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix – the result of his actions under the safety car.

The race was neutralised on lap 19 when Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara collided; Max Verstappen was leading team-mate Hadjar but the Red Bulls and Mercedes cars lay within just over a second; the double-stack meant Hadjar risked losing track position to Russell and other drivers.

The Frenchman therefore slowed down, to the extent that he was 4.288s slower than his team-mate on that lap. This mitigated the effect of the double-stack, though he still couldn’t retain second position.

Hadjar has now landed a 10-second penalty, whose impact actually is marginal, dropping him from 14th to 15th after his front wing broke at the restart.

“While driving on the straight between Turns 13 and 14 under Safety Car conditions, the driver of Car 6 received repeated instructions from his team stating ‘five seconds, five seconds, five seconds’,” the stewards’ report read.

“Following these instructions, Car 6 significantly reduced its speed, at one point travelling approximately 100km/h slower than Car 3, which was ahead of it. The Stewards determined that this significant reduction in speed was deliberate and intended to create a gap to the car ahead and was not made for safety reasons, thereby allowing the team to perform a double-stack pitstop without Car 6 losing time waiting behind its team-mate in the pitlane.

Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Furthermore, this manoeuvre directly impacted the cars following Car 6, which were forced to reduce their speed accordingly and could not overtake Car 6 due to the restrictions applicable under Safety Car conditions.

“The Stewards considered that Car 6 was driving unnecessarily slowly for tactical reasons and that such conduct constituted a breach of the applicable regulations. In reaching their decision, the Stewards also took into account the precedent involving Car 4 (Norris) at the 2023 Canadian Grand Prix, where a penalty was imposed for similar conduct.”

The aforementioned clash, with Perez spinning Camara around and breaking his Cadillac’s suspension, earned the Mexican a five-place grid penalty for the Qatar round.

“Car 11 (PER) attempted to overtake Car 51 (CAM) on the inside, on the left-hand side, approaching Turn 14,” the stewards wrote.

“The Stewards noted that at no point during the manoeuvre was the front axle of Car 11 at least alongside the mirror of Car 51. The two cars collided at the entry to Turn 14, resulting in Car 11 retiring from the Race.

“Applying the Driving Standards Guidelines, the Stewards determined that Car 11 had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame for the collision.”

Sports.title: Vasseur furious with "unprofessional" Ferrari clash and demands fresh talks after Las Vegas GP
Sports.content:
Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur says Charles Leclerc's contact with Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "unacceptable" and showed "lack of respect for the team", with the Formula 1 team set for fresh crisis talks just three weeks after their spat in Mexico.

Vasseur had to hold talks with both Leclerc and Hamilton for their costly Mexico skirmish and will do so again after his two cars tangled on the streets of Las Vegas on lap 38, with Leclerc to blame for leaving his front wing dangling on the inside of Hamilton, sending the Briton into a spin.

Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for the collision, while Hamilton dropped to 10th and eventually crossed the line in eighth. Leclerc was classified in 10th place after the penalty had been added to his race time.

Coming so soon after Mexico, the thought of his drivers tangling again and the prospect of fresh talks to clear the air had worn thin on Vasseur.

"Charles, I want to see you at the end of the race, before anything else," Vasseur said on the team radio during the cooldown lap.

When asked what that discussion was like, Vasseur tellingly replied: "It was not a discussion. I spoke.

"I think he apologised, he understood, but the result is there. You make a mistake, you say: 'My mistake, I'm sorry'. But you [still] made a mistake."

Frederic Vasseur, Ferrari Photo by: Alex Pantling / LAT Images via Getty Images

He added: "It's unacceptable. It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn't professional. I think it's probably the escalation of tension."

Following complaints from Hamilton, Ferrari had already been in touch with Leclerc about the aggressive way he was squeezing the Briton. Las Vegas' oval-like slipstreaming race required a degree of trust and teamwork for drivers to move through the pack of cars, as not racing each other was not an option either. The race became a painful reminder that trust between Leclerc and Hamilton is absent.

"We passed the message to Charles during the race to think about the team when he was fighting in the right way, but you can't freeze the position on this kind of race, because you are in the slipstream," Vasseur explained. "If you slow down, the guy who is behind you is overtaking you. And all the other teams were able to overtake each other 20 times during the race. You can't imagine the frustration for me, but more important for all the guys at home."

When asked if it's now time for tougher guidelines or rules, he said: "It's not a matter of rules. What can you do differently, except that you have to respect your team-mates. In this kind of race, you have to overtake the car in front of you. You can't stay behind. It's completely unmanageable. You just have to do it with respect when it's your team-mate, to take less risks. They just have to act in a professional way."

Having just had this very talk between Mexico and Brazil, it is not entirely clear what Vasseur can now do differently, a thought which has left the Frenchman feeling powerless.

"That's why I want to once again have a discussion tomorrow," he added. "And also, to try to digest the situation. I think it's not the right place to discuss with them two minutes after the race. I saw Charles a bit down. And I told him what I have to say. I've got to discuss it with him tomorrow."

Sports.title: Verstappen hits back after Russell criticism: “He’s so far below my level”
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen has hit back at George Russell’s Friday comments by winning Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix – and delivering scathing remarks afterwards.

The pair were involved in an incident in Free Practice 3, with Verstappen breaching what Russell deemed to be a gentlemen’s agreement by overtaking him ahead of a flying lap. The Briton moved to get back ahead but Verstappen unsuccessfully attempted to close the door and the duo eventually had a small collision.

The shenanigans led stewards to officially warn Verstappen for moving under braking, while Russell unabashedly blamed his rival on Sky Sport Italy: “He does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it, and I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy.”

Twenty-four hours later, Verstappen held off both Mercedes for victory in an eventful race as they traded the lead throughout the contest. Russell crashed as he locked up when diving down the inside of team-mate Kimi Antonelli for second place on lap 48 of 50, ending up ninth – and in Verstappen’s eyes, this speaks volumes.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Jordan McKean / Formula 1 / Getty Images

Asked if Russell’s words had been on his mind when they were racing one another for the lead, Verstappen retorted: “It's not like it's a success today.

“I mean, the thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn't really matter because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway, to try and challenge that, so it doesn't bother me.

“And today karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening. So I was like, ‘Fantastic! My day is only getting better.’

“And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete.”

Verstappen may not care about the runner-up spot in the championship, but his victory and Russell’s downfall mean he now has a 40-point advantage over the Mercedes driver, with just two rounds remaining – only Lewis Hamilton is closer, albeit still 37 points adrift.

Sports.title: “My mistake was to lift” – Why Antonelli lost power in Las Vegas GP victory battle
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has explained the quirky “mistake” that cost him a shot at Formula 1 victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The fastest driver in qualifying, Antonelli was sixth on the grid owing to a five-place drop for an engine change and was the only top-10 starter on mediums rather than softs, which contributed to a further two-position drop on lap one.

The new world champion recovered to fourth by lap 17 and went on to challenge polesitter Max Verstappen and Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the second half of the race, emerging as the Red Bull’s main rival late on.

Antonelli and Verstappen traded the lead repeatedly as ‘yo-yo’ racing returned, with the Italian 0.001s ahead on the finish line on lap 43 of 50, which was a major concern for his rival.

Attempting to be in the optimal position to overtake the Red Bull on the final lap, Antonelli refrained from attacking Verstappen at the end of the penultimate tour, but ended up losing out to both McLarens and finishing just fourth.

“Basically I lifted off before Turn 14 to keep overtake [mode] and stay behind Max to give myself the best shot for the win,” the Mercedes driver explained. “However, the lift triggered something in the system so I exited the corner at zero battery. So I lost it all.”

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Manuel Eletto

Pressed on the issue by Autosport, he added: “My mistake was to lift, actually. That triggered the issue, so I couldn't charge any energy. So already by the end of the straight you're quite low on energy. So because I couldn't harvest anything, then I see that I'm zero.

“Basically the system wasn't ready for that and my mistake was to lift off, reapply a bit of throttle to keep a little bit of speed, and that triggered the system, and that meant that in the straight I lost almost two seconds.”

When it was suggested to him that Mercedes was losing out to Red Bull on straights – despite the W17’s top speed in the race being 320.6km/h, compared to the RB22’s 314.3km/h – Antonelli clarified: “No no, we were able to keep up.

“Obviously, we had a lower downforce level this weekend and it was a bit more difficult in the corners, but definitely it was helping us in all the straights. It was clear where Red Bull was deploying more, but we had something in the pocket for that last lap, but I couldn't even try.”

As for the ‘yo-yo’ style of racing, unlike some of his peers, Antonelli appreciated it.

“I mean, it was a bit stressful at times because it was impossible to pull away and there were so many different speeds in all kinds of straights so you had to be very strategic,” the Italian admitted. “But other than that, I think it was a fun race, and it was a shame not to be able to fight all the way to the end [because of] something out of my control.”

Sports.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Verstappen wins thriller as Russell hits the wall late on
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen won a wild Las Vegas Grand Prix, holding off both Mercedes drivers as Formula 1’s ‘yo-yo’ racing returned – with no Silver Arrow on the eventual podium.

With qualifying pacesetter Andrea Kimi Antonelli taking a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation, Max Verstappen inherited pole position and retained the lead from George Russell at the start with an unchanged top five: Lando Norris, Isack Hadjar and Arvid Lindblad followed – though Hadjar swiftly found a way past the McLaren on lap one.

The only top-10 driver starting on mediums, Antonelli lost two spots to the Alpines at lights out, finding himself eighth ahead of the Ferraris, who were out in Q2 – though Franco Colapinto would soon collapse from seventh to 10th, then out of the points-paying positions.

Verstappen couldn’t break away from Russell, and the Briton briefly snatched the lead away on lap two before the Dutchman immediately responded. Russell couldn’t attack the leader again and was instead overtaken by the sister Red Bull car. Further back, Lindblad overtook Norris and Russell in quick succession, even though he could not hold the Mercedes off.

Meanwhile, Hadjar was pressuring Verstappen for the lead but had to deal with Russell’s attacks. “We need to not lose time as a team,” the Frenchman was told. “Can he stop defending?” he inquired as to his team-mate’s driving. Hadjar briefly took the lead soon after, though he dropped to third moments later.

On lap 10, the top 10 cars still lay within four seconds. Russell momentarily retook the lead again as Pierre Gasly fought to third, though he couldn’t hold off Hadjar for long. There were no changes among the top four for a moment, but Norris’ collapse continued as he ended up outside the top 10.

Russell took the lead back on laps 14 and 18, but this was again Turn 14 moves with Verstappen sweeping back past on the start/finish straight. The second time, Hadjar snuck by in second.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Jim Watson / AFP via Getty Images

New world champion Antonelli climbed to fourth on lap 17, recovering from eighth on lap one. Meanwhile, the Ferraris were battling both their rivals and among themselves for seventh place. Charles Leclerc called on his team-mate to “be careful with this squeezing”, Lewis Hamilton said the sister car should “back the fuck off” – and copped a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage after a move on Norris.

The safety car was called into action on lap 19 as Sergio Perez spun Rafael Camara around and broke his front suspension; nearly all cars pitted straightaway – Red Bull’s double-stack allowing Russell to sneak back into second – but not Hamilton, due to the seven-time world champion’s track position ahead of his team-mate and his 10-second penalty. In order not to delay the sister car in the pits, he changed tyres on the following lap and emerged back out in 14th.

Meanwhile, sixth-placed Lindblad had an odd spin in safety-car conditions and retired from the race, promoting Norris back to sixth ahead of Leclerc and Gabriel Bortoleto.

The green flag was waved on lap 26, and Hadjar’s front wing broke on its own. The Red Bull driver pitted, with Gasly inheriting third before losing out to a resurgent Norris on lap 31. Meanwhile, Hamilton needed just one lap to fight his way back into the top 10.

Russell retook the lead then – again ever so briefly – but his incessant attempts to surpass Verstappen brought Norris into play, with the Briton now challenging – and temporarily overtaking – the leader.

Russell recovered second place, and finally found a way past Verstappen into Turn 1 on lap 37, rather than Turn 14, but he still couldn’t hold on to the lead. Antonelli, the only driver on soft tyres in the top 10, even took second place away from his team-mate on lap 38 and briefly passed Verstappen for the lead one lap later.

At the same time, further down the field, Leclerc and Hamilton clashed as they battled each other for sixth, with the latter being spun around and ending up down to 10th. Leclerc dropped down to himself eighth and copped a 10-second penalty.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Manuel Eletto

So far, Verstappen had proved to be only temporarily assailable, but the Red Bull driver was worrying about the end of the race. “You guys have to look at the deployment of the final lap because they’ve figured it out, that they can stay ahead of me until the line, so we need to see what we need to do for the final lap only,” he said on team radio.

Antonelli and Verstappen traded the lead again and again, with Antonelli 0.001s ahead on the finish line on lap 43, vindicating the Dutchman’s aforementioned concern. However, Red Bull let its driver know that there was no better deployment strategy available for the final lap.

On lap 48, Russell attempted to overtake Antonelli for second place but locked up and hit the wall, collapsing down to ninth, seemingly letting the top two drivers fight it out for the win… but Antonelli lost ground at the end of lap 49 and dropped behind the McLarens.

Verstappen therefore triumphed from pole ahead of Norris, who had started third but dropped to 11th before driving to the runner-up spot, and Piastri, who was 15th on the grid and fought to a podium finish.

Antonelli saved fourth ahead of Alpine duo Gasly and Colapinto, while the Ferraris of Hamilton and Leclerc were a disappointing seventh and 10th respectively, separated by Carlos Sainz and Russell.

Hadjar couldn’t do better than 14th after his front wing broke, right ahead of Lawson, who was supposed to be seventh on the grid but had to start from the pitlane due to a fuel leak and never recovered.

Alex Albon, who was supposed to start from 14th, encountered a brake overheating issue despite 12C weather and couldn’t take part in the race.

Sports.title: Antonelli and Russell set for Mercedes talks over Las Vegas GP qualifying mix-up
Sports.content:
George Russell and Kimi Antonelli will discuss the fallout from Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying “offline” following confusion over team orders and track position.

Traffic played a significant role in qualifying on Friday night with drivers reluctant to go first, considering the advantage of a tow is huge around the low-downforce street circuit.

There was the added complexity of five drivers taking a grid penalty, so their primary role was to help their team-mate like Haas’ Oliver Bearman giving Rafael Camara a tow in Q1.

Antonelli was another one of those, taking a five-place drop for a new engine, so the plan was to give Russell the slipstream in the fight for pole but it quickly unravelled.

That was because the Mercedes duo got caught in a pack with both Alpine and Racing Bulls cars ahead of the final lap, at times going three-wide despite trying to find space.

Antonelli eventually backed off at Turn 5 while Russell reluctantly went first of the pack and the 2026 world champion was fastest in qualifying with his team-mate 0.331s off in third.

So when asked afterwards if he was hoping for assistance from Antonelli, Russell replied: “It's still important, if you've got a grid penalty, to start as high up the order as possible.

“But we'll take it offline and we can talk about it. I think tomorrow is going to be very close between everybody, similar to Monza - it'll be very challenging to pull away from the pack.

“I would have liked to have been on pole, but I think anywhere in the top seven positions and you're in the fight.”

The situation caused Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to express disbelief at how Antonelli was quickest, particularly because Russell didn’t receive his request of leaving the pits second.

“It's very high risk,” added Russell, who will share the front row with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen due to Antonelli’s penalty.

“Kimi got the pole, but if he started the lap a second later, he wouldn't have got the lap in.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images

“It's very difficult to orchestrate because everybody's going for it, and also the fact that half the cars were doing prep laps and half the cars were not also made it difficult.

“If you could choose, you would be at the back of a pack of nine cars with around a three-second gap, if you could perfectly choose.

“But that's what everyone's chasing, so it's kind of like Monza 2019."

Although Antonelli eventually backing off gave him the space needed to set his fastest lap, a 1m33.893s, it could have cost him as he only just crossed the line in time to start his final tour.

“As George said, we will talk about it because we've been sent out at the front in qualifying always,” said Antonelli.

“About Turn 5, it was fully on me. Like I said, we were three-wide, first of all, and I just said, "You know what? I'm just going to back off’."

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“It was tricky because, first of all, I almost missed the flag. Yes, I did get a big tow, but I was also so close that getting around the corner was actually difficult with the dirty air and so on.

“We're already on a lower-downforce package, so you do feel even more the loss when following.

“But overall, it was just one of those times where you think you're screwed, but actually it works out.

“On Turn 5, I just decided to back off. I didn't really know how tight I was with the timing. I probably would have done it differently, but in hindsight, it still worked out.”

Sports.title: Jermell Charlo Out Of December 5 Vergil Ortiz Fight
Sports.content:
Jermell Charlo will not replace Keith Thurman against Vergil Ortiz Jr. on December 5, according to Mike Coppinger. Good. Bringing a 36-year-old fighter out of mothballs with no tune-up after more than three years away would have been terrible optics. Charlo has not won a fight since May 2022, over four years ago. Is this really what Ortiz wants for his career at 28?

“Charlo indeed is not in the mix to fight Vergil Ortiz,” Coppinger wrote on X. Chris Mannix reported that Brian Mendoza and Eric Priest are the expected options after Thurman withdrew injured. Charlo is already set to face Brock Jarvis at 160 pounds on December 12 in Australia.

Poor Replacement Options For PPV

What about DAZN? They are charging fans $79.99 in the United States and £24.99 in the UK for the December 5 pay-per-view headlined by David Benavidez and Michal Cieslak. Ortiz was brought into the co-feature slot to liven things up, yet there is nothing sporting about feeding him either of these replacements.

Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) is no upgrade after dropping three of his last four fights. He caught lightning in a bottle with his seventh-round knockout of Sebastian Fundora in April 2023, though it has been all downhill since then with clear decision losses to Tim Tszyu, Serhii Bohachuk, and Yoenis Tellez.

Priest has spent six years fighting on small club cards without beating a single ranked contender, and Esneiker Correa even held him to a draw last November. Expecting fans to shell out $79.99 to watch Ortiz face a faded Mendoza or a club-level opponent like Priest makes zero sense for a pay-per-view show.

What Charlo Has Left At 160

Charlo has not stepped through the ropes since September 2023, when he jumped up two weight classes and lost a lopsided decision to Canelo Alvarez. Canelo dropped him in the seventh round and swept the cards by scores of 119-109 and 118-109 twice. Moving to 168 pounds was never going to be easy, yet Charlo spent the whole night in survival mode and gave Canelo zero reason to take his foot off the gas.

Coppinger noted that an Ortiz versus Charlo fight at 160 could happen in the first half of 2027 if both win next month. Beating Jarvis in Australia gets Charlo active again, though it still proves nothing against top middleweights.

Ortiz has already burned roughly 13 months since stopping Erickson Lubin in two rounds. His promotional dispute with Golden Boy helped kill talks for a fight against Jaron “Boots” Ennis, which would have answered every question about where Ortiz stands. Ortiz cannot afford to keep wasting his prime against short-notice fill-ins.

Sports.title: WBC Mandatory Challenger Souleymane Cissokho Wants To Face Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
The WBC world welterweight champion Ryan Garcia has mentioned the possibility of a fight with either Floyd “Money” Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez, but the WBC mandatory challenger is wondering when he will receive his shot at the title.

In some cases, a fighter can enter the sport of boxing and gradually build his pro career brick by brick. Once that fighter has earned the right to walk through the door of opportunity, a boxer with name recognition cuts the line.

Back in May 2025, Souleymane Cissokho was set to defend his WBC Silver welterweight title against Egidijus Kavaliauskas. In addition to being a fight for the Silver belt, this matchup also served as a world title eliminator bout.

In a very competitive 12-round contest, Cissokho defeated Kavaliauskas by way of unanimous decision. With the victory, Souleymane Cissokho officially became the WBC number one ranked welterweight contender.

Eleven days later, the then 46-year-old Manny Pacquiao announced he was ending his four-year retirement to fight for the WBC world welterweight title. In a match that ended up being a draw, the champion Mario Barrios held on to the belt.

Seven months after the Pacquiao fight, Ryan Garcia leaped over Souleymane Cissokho, and he was locked in to challenge Barrios for the title. At the time, Garcia was coming off a loss he suffered against Rolando “Rolly” Romero.

On February 21, 2026, Ryan Garcia defeated Mario Barrios via unanimous decision. After Garcia became the new world champion, it seemed like the path was cleared for Cissokho to finally receive his shot at the world title.

Unfortunately for Cissokho, another named person cut in front of him as Conor Benn was penciled in to challenge Ryan Garcia. In their world title fight, Garcia stopped Benn in the 2nd round.

Once again, Souleymane Cissokho is at the front of the line as it relates to the opportunity to fight for the world title. Now it appears Cissokho will get skipped for a fourth time.

The WBC welterweight world champion Ryan Garcia and his promotional company CEO Oscar De La Hoya have been very vocal regarding the next title defense being against Floyd “Money” Mayweather or Teofimo Lopez.

The current No.1 contender Souleymane Cissokho was born in Dakar, Senegal, but moved to France when he was 4 years old. He started boxing at the age of 14 and would go on to represent France and win a Bronze medal in the 2016 Olympics.

Now the undefeated Souleymane Cissokho (18-0, 9 KOs) is waiting to receive the world title bout he rightfully earned. Unfortunately for him, Mauricio Sulaiman and the WBC are known for having number one contenders who don’t receive title shots.

Mauricio Sulaiman has the authority to order a mandatory world title fight. Hopefully, in 2027, Sulaiman will step up and make the proper decision in favor of the number one-ranked WBC welterweight contender Souleymane Cissokho.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Plans To Retire After Ennis And Fundora
Sports.content:
IBF junior middleweight champion Josh Kelly has come up with one of boxing’s unlikeliest exit plans. He wants to beat Jaron “Boots” Ennis, take the last belt off Sebastian Fundora, and walk away as undisputed champion.

“Yeah. No, it’s Boots, Fundora, and then sail into the sunset,” said Kelly to Fight Hub TV. Asked if he would call it a career after that, he said, “Yeah, bro. Yeah, I don’t need to do much after that.”

Running Will Not Beat Boots

What Kelly never answered is whether he plans to retire if he loses to Ennis. The interviewer dropped the ball by skipping the most obvious follow-up question on the board. Getting carved up by Boots the way Kelly was in his sixth round stoppage loss to David Avanesyan in 2021, when his corner threw in the towel with him a bloody mess, would leave his career in rough shape.

Ennis is up first on February 27 in Atlanta. Anyone who watched Kelly win the IBF belt off Bakhram Murtazaliev saw a twelve round track meet, and he used the same running routine to get past his last opponent. Kelly thinks he can read Ennis’s style because he uses similar moves in the ring. He also claimed he saw a few habits from the Xander Zayas fight that he is keeping quiet until the opening bell.

“It’s whoever can adjust first is going to get the better of the fight,” said Kelly. He expects the fight to shift from round to round and even within a round.

Kelly liked being the underdog against Murtazaliev and says he fights looser when people expect him to lose. Atlanta is a totally different problem. Boots cuts off the ring, switches stances effortlessly, and punishes fighters who try to survive on their bicycle. A counter Kelly lands in the third round could easily turn into a trap Ennis springs in the fourth.

At this point, Fundora is not even worth discussing yet. Kelly said he has enough left to fight until 36 or 37 if he wants. “Why spoil that? Why come back after something like that?” said Kelly.

He will not have to worry about retiring early. His whole exit plan ends in Atlanta against Boots, so the Fundora fight will never happen.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Wants Unification After Facing Nelson Hysa
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel could not get the heavyweights he wanted for his first WBC title defense. Instead, he gets 42-year-old Nelson Hysa on November 28 in Düsseldorf. He is already looking past Saturday. Kabayel wants another belt next, though one possible opponent has to get through a fighter Kabayel already stopped.

“I want only the big fights, but none of the big guys are available. Now I will teach him respect,” said Kabayel in an interview with Queensberry Promotions. The unbeaten champion meets Hysa at Merkur Spiel-Arena, with DAZN streaming the main card from 1 p.m. ET.

Hrgovic Has Mandatory Ahead Of Unification

IBF champion Filip Hrgovic is one option, except Sky Sports reported he is headed toward a mandatory defense against Frank Sanchez in Croatia in early 2027. Hrgovic also wants WBO champion Daniel Dubois. The two faced off after Dubois defended his belt against Fabio Wardley in October.

Sanchez gives Kabayel plenty of reason to watch that IBF fight. Kabayel stopped Sanchez in seven rounds in 2024 on the Oleksandr Usyk vs. Tyson Fury undercard. If Sanchez beats Hrgovic, Kabayel could land a rematch with a second belt on the line. If Hrgovic wins, both Kabayel and Dubois will be chasing him.

Dubois holds the WBO title. He also shares promoter Frank Warren with Kabayel. That gives Warren a clean path to put two belts together while Hrgovic deals with Sanchez, provided both fighters want it. Dubois has also talked about a third fight with Usyk, so Kabayel is not the only name on his list.

What Kabayel Faces In Hysa

Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) sat ringside when Hrgovic stopped Moses Itauma for the vacant IBF belt in August. Hysa stopped Thomas Narmo in two rounds on that same undercard, then called out Kabayel and promised a knockout. Now Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) gets his shot in Germany on Albanian Independence Day.

Hysa carries a streak of 19 straight knockouts into the ring, though he did not turn pro until age 37 and has spent four years beating regional club fighters and aging journeymen like Danny Williams and Patrick Korte. Kabayel stopped Arslanbek Makhmudov, Sanchez, Zhilei Zhang, and Damian Knyba in consecutive fights. He took the interim belt against Zhang before being elevated to full champion in June after Usyk vacated the WBC title.

“Nelson is my focus now. But after this fight, it’s a unification fight,” said Kabayel. Getting past Hysa is the easy part on paper, though a 42-year-old puncher who has never gone past six rounds still has to be put away before Warren can start calling Dubois.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua Eyes Retirement Ahead Of Tyson Fury Fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua says he expects to retire “pretty soon,” and beating Tyson Fury in Cardiff might give him an easier exit than another loss. At 37, Joshua gets his shot at settling an old score on December 11 at Principality Stadium. Netflix will stream the card.

“When am I going to retire? Pretty soon. I’m getting old now. From an athlete’s point of view, I’m getting old,” said Joshua in an interview with The Sun. He said he had few years left in boxing and brought up investing in longtime sponsor Under Armour once his career ends. He did not set a date.

Through much of his career, Joshua has been at the top of the heavyweight division since winning Olympic gold in 2012.

What A Fury Win Does For Joshua

Joshua stopped Wladimir Klitschko in 2017, outpointed Joseph Parker to pick up the WBO belt in 2018, then avenged his 2019 stoppage loss to Andy Ruiz Jr. six months later by boxing behind his jab for 12 rounds. He proved in that rematch he could stick to a disciplined game plan instead of trading hooks in the pocket.

Fury ended Klitschko’s title run in 2015 and built his reputation on two wins over Deontay Wilder. Both British heavyweights later lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk. Beating Fury settles who owns the head-to-head edge after years of stalled negotiations.

It is tempting to say age is catching up to Joshua, though his problems started back in 2017 when a 40-year-old Wladimir Klitschko put him on the canvas and nearly finished him. Two years later, fringe contender Andy Ruiz Jr. knocked him out in 2019. Then came two losses to Oleksandr Usyk and the fifth-round knockout against Daniel Dubois in 2024.

Joshua’s stamina and punch resistance flaws were there from the beginning, even if Eddie Hearn’s careful matchmaking hid them for years after Joshua’s disputed 2012 Olympic gold medal. Usyk and Dubois simply stripped away the cover. At 37, putting Joshua in with Filip Hrgovic, Agit Kabayel, Moses Itauma, or Frank Sanchez would go badly.

What Joshua Faces In Cardiff

Joshua’s exit would cost British promoters their biggest stadium draw, though that is their problem after December 11. Joshua’s problem is surviving 12 rounds against a 6-foot-9 heavyweight who still knows how to lean on smaller men and spoil their rhythm. He cannot afford to leave his chin up in the pocket the way he did against Dubois. If Joshua wins, he gets to walk away on his own terms. If Fury beats him, retirement stops being a choice he gets to time himself.

Sports.title: Aaron Pryor Overwhelms Gaetan Hart In Six Rounds
Sports.content:
Aaron Pryor never gave Gaétan Hart a chance to settle into their November 22, 1980 title fight at Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati. Pryor dropped the Canadian challenger three times and stopped him in the sixth round, keeping his WBA and The Ring junior welterweight belts.

Understandably, referee Roberto Ramírez Sr. stepped in at 2:09 to stop the contest. Hart was pinned in a corner, bleeding, and taking clean shots with nothing coming back.

At 25, Pryor was already a nightmare matchup for anyone at 140 pounds. He came into the fight with an unbeaten record, fresh off flattening Antonio Cervantes in four rounds in the same arena three months earlier.

Hart, a 27-year-old lightweight champion from Buckingham, Quebec, brought legitimate fight-ending power into his first world title shot. It didn’t matter. Pryor forced a pace that kept Hart in a constant state of defense, taking away his leverage before he could ever set his feet to throw heavy shots.

What Followed Hart To Cincinnati

Hart carried dark history into Ohio after two brutal fights in Canada earlier that year. In May, he stopped Ralph Racine in the 12th round of a Canadian lightweight title bout, putting Racine into a coma that ended his career. One month later in Montreal, Hart stopped Cleveland Denny in the 10th round. Denny died 16 days later.

Opponents in Canada made the mistake of letting Hart plant his feet and unload. Pryor never gave him the chance. He backed Hart up in the first round and dropped him 20 seconds into the second. Hart beat the count, then went down again before the bell. He was gassed out before the fight even got started.

Hart Couldn’t Survive Pryor’s Pace

Hart absorbed heavy shots in the third without going down and had a brief spell of offense in the fourth before Pryor took back control and knocked out his mouthpiece. Early in the fifth, a punch buckled Hart’s knees. He steadied himself and landed two crisp lefts that snapped Pryor’s head back, the exact kind of heavy shots that had ruined opponents in Canada. Pryor walked straight through them without getting hurt.

Hart landed first in the sixth, too. Pryor answered with a right hook that sent him down for an eight count, then chased him into the corner until Ramírez waved it off. Pryor was already running away on the cards, leading 50 to 45 on two and 50 to 43 on the third.

Pryor went to 27 and 0 and knocked out his next four challengers before stopping Alexis Argüello twice. He finished 39 and 1 with 35 knockouts and made the Hall of Fame in 1996. Hart never fought for a world title again and later turned up in the documentary The Steak. Nobody at 140 pounds could take Pryor’s punches or survive that pace in 1980.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Sets 24-Hour VADA Deadline For Devin Haney
Sports.content:
IBF welterweight champion Liam Paro has given WBO champion Devin Haney 24 hours to enroll in VADA testing, or he will walk away from their December 20 unification fight in San Francisco. That is a pretty bold ultimatum from a guy entering the biggest payday of his career, especially when Haney is the A-side drawing the crowd at the Chase Center.

No Limit promoter Matt Rose confirmed the deadline on Sunday morning after Paro called Haney out on social media over the delay.

“We’re very disappointed they [Team Haney] have failed to enroll in VADA testing,” Rose told Fox Sports Australia. “One of the first things we agreed to when negotiating this fight was that VADA testing would take place. So now we’re giving them 24 hours …”

Paro already went after Haney on X over the weekend, questioning why the three-division titleholder hadn’t signed the paperwork yet despite preaching about clean boxing for the past two years.

“@realdevinhaney you preach serious boxing and speak out against PEDS, yet we’re still waiting for you to agree to VADA testing to begin. What’s the hold up???” wrote Paro.

Haney fired back quickly, reminding everyone about his testing track record and taking another shot at Ryan Garcia, who tested positive for ostarine after their April 2024 bout.

“This is will be my 14th consecutive fight using VADA testing,” Haney wrote. “Over 65 clean tests. Thanks for tagging the cheater.. the one that got popped for PEDS.”

The Problem With The Paperwork

If Haney has already gone through more than 65 VADA tests without a single issue, what is taking so long to get the forms signed for December 20? You can understand why Paro (25-1, 15 KOs) is suspicious. Haney spent all of 2024 and 2025 demanding 24/7 year-round testing, filing lawsuits against Garcia, and lecturing everyone about drug cheats. Now that he is moving up to 147 pounds to face a tough Australian southpaw, the enrollment is suddenly dragging out less than a month before fight night.

Paro already got under Haney’s skin at their launch press conference when Team Haney showed up nearly half an hour late.

“I don’t want any excuses or lawyers,” Paro said across the stage. “That’s what happened last time, isn’t it?”

Team Haney has until Monday to get the paperwork submitted. If they miss that deadline, Paro can pack his bags in Las Vegas and leave Haney scrambling for a replacement on December 20.

Sports.title: David Morrell Stops Julio Rodriguez in First Round
Sports.content:
David Morrell (13-2, 10 KOs) stopped Julio de Jesus Rodriguez (27-11, 24 KOs) by first-round TKO on Saturday night, November 21, at the Coliseo Carlos “Teo” Cruz in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

The Cuban southpaw hurt Rodriguez with clean power shots and staggered him before the referee stepped in. Their light heavyweight bout was scheduled for 10 rounds on the Shuan Boxing card, though Morrell needed less than one in his first fight in over six months, getting his first win since edging Imam Khataev by split decision in July 2025.

The fight lasted less than a round, yet Morrell immediately fell into the same pattern. Rodriguez walked forward, and Morrell froze behind his shell guard rather than letting his hands go.

Rodriguez simply lacked the quality to make him pay for it. Once Morrell opened up, he clipped Rodriguez with a right hand to the back of the head that sent the 44-year-old backing toward a corner. Sensing Rodriguez was hurt, Morrell unloaded several hard punches until the referee stepped in and waved it off.

Rodriguez brought six straight defeats into Saturday’s fight, five of them inside the distance. The Dominican veteran had 24 knockouts on his record, but his recent form gave little reason to believe he could test Morrell or take him into the later rounds.

Morrell badly needed this victory after getting stopped in the tenth round by late replacement Zak Chelli in Manchester. That loss came on the heels of a unanimous decision defeat to David Benavidez in February 2025, plus a rough night five months later when Imam Khataev dropped him.

At 28, Morrell looks like he hasn’t improved or changed his fighting style at all. Whenever an opponent attacks, he still covers up behind a static shell and waits for them to stop throwing, the exact habit that caused him major trouble against Radivoje Kalajdzic, David Benavidez, and Imam Khataev before Chelli treated him like a heavy bag and stopped him.

Getting past an aging club fighter in Santo Domingo hides the flaw for one night, though against any durable light heavyweight who refuses to stop punching, Morrell will be right back in the same trouble.

Ghana News.title: External debt servicing will create depreciatory pressure on cedi in 2027
Ghana News.content:
Fitch Solutions is warning that external debt service will generate depreciatory pressure on the cedi in 2027.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects external debt-service payments of roughly US$5.05 billion, up from US$4.7 billion in 2026.

Meanwhile, the government’s 2027 Fiscal Strategy rules out Eurobond issuance until 2030 and caps project-loan disbursements, while Ghana’s Extended Credit Facility ended in July 2026.

The UK-based firm said that although the reactivated Dollar Sinking Fund will likely cover around US$1.2 billion in Eurobond repayments, the remaining US$3.9 billion owed to multilateral, bilateral and commercial creditors will thus directly weigh on foreign exchange reserves.

“This will drive the BoG [Bank of Ghana] to rebuild its reserves towards its Ghana Accelerated National Reserve Accumulation Policy (GANRAP) targets, limiting its willingness to supply dollars to the market and creating a further headwind for the cedi”, it explained.

Risks To Outlook

Fitch Solutions said the risks are mixed but skewed to a weaker cedi in 2027.

“Dollar supply depends closely on gold, so a sharper fall in prices than our US$4,200/oz [per ounce] forecast, or disruptions to GoldBod’s exports, would quickly reduce flows to the FX [foreign exchange] market”, it stressed.

Furthermore, it said a renewed flare-up in the US-Iran conflict would raise the oil import bill.

In addition, the February 2027 redemption of domestic bonds could also see more cedi liquidity switched into dollars than expected as a result of low domestic Treasury yields.

On the upside, Fitch Solutions said a further lift in gold prices towards US$5,000 per ounce, or BoG action to drain excess liquidity and lift market rates, would ease pressure on the cedi.

Ghana News.title: Melania Trump gives a peek inside her marriage, motherhood and more in new series
Ghana News.content:
Melania Trump is back on screens on Friday with another behind-the-scenes look at her life before and after she became first lady, discussing her marriage to President Donald Trump, her relationship with son Barron and the healing power of a day at the spa.

“Melania: The Series” is a two-part follow-up to a documentary released in January covering her life in the two weeks before Donald Trump returned to the presidency in 2025.

The first lady is known for being private. In this series, set for release on Prime Video, she spends a lot of onscreen time answering probing questions from director Brett Ratner.

She talks at length about Barron Trump, her only child with the president. Her father, Viktor Knavs, who is rarely seen in public, makes a cameo and explains why she is a good daughter. Melania Trump also talks about her relationship with the president — and he answers a few questions about his wife, too.

“She’s very strong. She’s not easy to get to the peace table,” the president says in the series.

The first lady, now 56, was executive producer of what she calls a “unique story” — her humble beginnings in small-town Slovenia in Eastern Europe, a career as a fashion model and a marriage to an ambitious New York businessperson who was elected president and made her first lady of the United States.

“People are interested, and I think they like to see what is going on behind the scene, what you need to do and what is it when you’re becoming first lady,” she said Thursday night at a glitzy event before an audience of several hundred people at Lincoln Center who got an advance look at the series.

President Trump did not attend because he was flying home after spending several days in Asia. Her father was there along with some current and former Trump administration officials, including Frank Bisignano, head of the Social Security Administration, former Attorney General Pam Bondi, and Kellyanne Conway, a senior adviser to Trump in his first term.

Here are some takeaways from the series:

Barron is his mother’s priority

Asked who came up with their son’s name, she says, “Donald.”

She describes their now 20-year-old son, a business major at New York University, as “very strong” because “he grew up very fast” in the spotlight. “His life is not the same as other children,” she acknowledges.

The first lady describes the role a then-teenaged Barron played in the 2024 presidential campaign, encouraging his father to do interviews with social media influencers to reach new segments of the electorate.

Her father and her late mother, Amalija Knavs, were “influential” in his upbringing, and that helped him become “an incredible young man,” she says.

She says she tries not to be “controlling over him” and wants him to do what “makes him happy.”

“I’m a very cool mom to Barron, and I remind him all the time,” she says, laughing. “He’s my priority, and he will always be my priority.”

Melania is funny in ways she often isn’t in public

She usually wears a poker face in public. But beyond the “cool mom” joke, Melania Trump jokes around with Herve Pierre, her stylist, as he helps accessorize her black and white inaugural gown.

She pokes fun at the way her husband dances, or shakes his hips while moving his arms back and forth, to end some campaign rallies and other appearances, saying she’s told him he doesn’t have to do it every time.

In one scene, she is tasting dessert samples prepared by the White House executive pastry chef, including an assortment of cookies.

“My husband loves Oreos,” she says. “I’m not a cookie person. I’m an ice cream person, by the way.”

She says she reads a lot. When asked to name her favorite book, she laughingly says, “Of course it’s ‘Melania.’” That’s her memoir, published in October 2024.

She discusses their marriage, but not the hiccups

Melania talks about meeting Donald in 1998 in New York and marrying him in 2005 in Florida.

But she and Ratner avoid any mention of what may have been the darker moments in the couple’s relationship, such as the extramarital affairs the president has denied he had or the reports that she renegotiated their prenuptial agreement after he was elected.

Ratner asks and the first lady notes that her parents were married for 56 years. She offers not trying to change your spouse as a key piece of marital advice.

“You need to let them be who they are,” she says. “I let him be who he is, and he supports me and let me be who I am.”

For her, she says solitude is “very important,” and it is well known that she doesn’t spend as much time at the White House as other first ladies. She says in the series that “my home is in three cities.” The couple has homes in New York City, New Jersey and Florida.

The film attempts to counter speculation about the state of their marriage by showing the Trumps together smiling, laughing, holding hands and her kissing him on the cheek as they go their separate ways after a trip to Los Angeles. She says they aren’t into public displays of affection beyond that.

Melania prioritizes her privacy

“I don’t need to be all the time with people,” she says. “I’m very happy in my own company. I always was.”

At another point, she denies that she is shy. “I’m selective,” she says.

She says she is “very comfortable” in the first lady spotlight because she was at the center of attention long before Donald Trump jumped into national politics.

“When I need my privacy, I have my private moments,” she says.

Asked how she takes care of her mental health, Melania Trump says she tries to get enough sleep, though she didn’t say how many winks she gets on average. She’s also big on self-care.

“The spa brings me calmness,” she says as a jeans-and-sweatshirt-clad first lady is seen entering the spa at the Trumps’ Mar-a-Lago home and resort in Palm Beach, Florida.

Melania’s takeaway

Asked what she would like people to get out of watching the series, she says it would be a better understanding of who she is.

“Everybody will have different opinions, and that’s OK,” Melania Trump says. “This is me. This is my life.”

Ghana News.title: Government’s key test in managing debt lies in 2027 – KPMG UNDP report
Ghana News.content:
The KPMG UNDP 2027 Budget Highlights says the government's key test in managing Ghana’s public debt lies in 2027, when about GH¢53 billion of Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP) obligations and US$1.17 billion of Eurobond payments fall due.

The Cedi Sinking Fund held GH¢29 billion as at 11 November 2026, enough to cover the February 2027 principal (now offered for early redemption), while the US Dollar Sinking Fund is projected to reach about US$600 million by December 2026.

According to the highlights, sustaining monthly Sinking Fund transfers (7% of non-oil tax revenue), lengthening the domestic maturity profile and keeping debt near the 45% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) anchor will be critical as the deficit widens to 2.9% of GDP in 2027.

Ghana’s 2027 Budget shows that the country’s debt position remains stable, although the KPMG/UNDP report warned that significant repayment obligations for 2027 will test the durability of the debt management framework, anchored on the fiscal consolidation achieved in 2025 and sustained through 2026.

As of end-October 2026, provisional total public debt stood at GH¢759.3 billion (US$65.3 billion), up from GH¢641.1 billion (US$61.3 billion) at end-2025.

“Although the debt-to-GDP ratio rose to 47.5% from 44.7% at the end of 2025, it remains well below the 61.6% recorded at the end of 2024 and the ECOWAS convergence ceiling of 70%. The 18.4% increase in the debt stock was driven mainly by domestic debt, which rose by 28.2% to GH¢427.9 billion, while external debt increased by 7.8% to GH¢331.4 billion. Domestic debt now accounts for 56.4% of total public debt (external: 43.6%), consistent with the government’s strategy to reduce external exposure and limit exchange rate valuation effects”, the report said.

Similarly, lower Treasury bill rates kept interest payments in October 2026 at GH¢38.8 billion, 24.7% below target, it mentioned

The 2026 Debt Sustainability Analysis rates Ghana’s risk of external and overall debt distress as moderate, supporting rating upgrades by Fitch (‘B’) and Moody’s (‘B3’) in 2026.

The report added that the government has remained current on its restructured obligations, paying GH¢10.8 billion to DDEP bondholders in August 2026 (GH¢41.36 billion since 2025) and US$700 million to Eurobond holders in July 2026 (US$2.1 billion since 2025).

Bilateral restructuring agreements have been signed with 16 of 24 official creditor countries, with four more expected by the end of December 2026, alongside four commercial debt agreements.

But the report stated that the actual test lies in 2027.
