World.title: WHO chief calls for peace amid heavy fighting in Ebola-hit DR Congo region
World.content:
Fighting near DRC hospital disrupts Ebola efforts, putting patients and workers at ‘grave risk’, WHO warns.

Share WHO chief calls for peace amid heavy fighting in Ebola-hit DR Congo region on social media

The World ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Health Organization (WHO) chief has urged peace following heavy fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) northeastern province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠on ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Sunday that fighting near a hospital in the DRC’s Ituri ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠province disrupted Ebola response efforts and forced health workers and aid partners to shelter ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠inside a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.

“Heavy fighting has been ongoing since yesterday in the vicinity of a hospital in Ituri – in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged,” Tedros said on X.

“The situation has disrupted the work of the hospital and the wider Ebola response, putting patients, families and health workers at grave risk.”

Medical staff have been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward in the facility for more than 24 hours, and the WHO is working to arrange a safe exit for the team and “for the hospital facilities, staff and patients to be protected,” Tedros also said.

“The best medicine is peace,” he added.

‘High-level transmission continues’

As of November 17, the WHO reported a total of 5,678 deaths out of 11,613 cases in the DRC, the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country.

The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that “while some areas had seen a slight decline in cases, sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the country.”

Ituri and North Kivu, in the eastern part of the DRC, remain the most affected provinces.



The virus, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids, has spread across swaths of the DRC’s east and northeast, which have been plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

Earlier in November, armed men thought to be linked to an ISIL (ISIS)-affiliated group raided villages and killed dozens of people in North Kivu, forcing ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠patients with confirmed and suspected Ebola infections to flee.

The outbreak is also occurring amid ongoing fighting between government forces and the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, which has seized key cities in eastern DRC, making transport of healthcare resources to remote regions difficult.

World.title: Asian stock markets tumble as AI bubble fears mount
World.content:
Asian stock markets have opened to sharp losses amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom.

Key indexes in South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and mainland China fell on Monday, continuing Friday’s tech-led sell-off on both sides of the Pacific.

The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi) in Seoul slid as much as 4.5 percent in morning trading, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index dipped 1.8 percent.

The CSI 300 Index in Shanghai dropped more than 1.3 percent, while the Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Stock Index (Taiex) swung between losses and gains after falling more than 1 percent at opening.

Japan’s stock markets were closed for Labour Thanksgiving Day.

On Friday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 closed 3.7 percent lower for its seventh straight loss, while the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3 percent to erase all of its gains for 2026, following a rout in Asia.

The Kospi, Nikkei 225, and the Taiex entered the weekend between 5.1 percent and 6.2 percent lower, while the Hang Seng Index finished down 1.9 percent.

Wall Street appeared on track for a rebound on Monday, with S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures up 2 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.

Investors have long been concerned that tech firms may not be able to sustain the multi-trillion-dollar investments they have poured into the infrastructure needed to train and run AI.

Global AI-related investment, much of it fuelled by debt, is expected to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.



Concerns that the AI boom may be running out of steam have been exacerbated by growing calls for greater oversight of the sector.

The Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the US midterm elections is expected to slow data centre construction in US states, while the alleged espionage scandal embroiling chip giant Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang has led to a push for tighter restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips.

World.title: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
World.content:
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.

Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.

But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.

The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed".

He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he said were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

"That is the reality," he said on Monday.

After two weeks of negotiations, exhausted delegates were presented with a new, draft deal in the early hours of Sunday to try to break the deadlock.

But the words "fossil fuels" did not appear anywhere in the text. The only indirect reference to coal, oil and gas was a nod to a deal agreed at COP28 in 2023, when countries agreed to "transition away" from fossil fuels in energy systems.

The EU's representative, Irish Minister Darragh O'Brien, made it clear that the EU "strongly" objected, saying that the "decisions go nowhere near the level of ambition needed to tackle climate change".

"It is unconscionable that we would have a climate pact that makes no mention of fossil fuels," he said.

Other countries, such as Panama and the Marshall Islands, also criticised the deal for doing nowhere near enough to tackle the pace of climate change.

A first draft of the deal on Monday mentioned "fossil fuel" or "fossil fuels" six times, but that was unacceptable to oil-producing nations.

Saudi Arabia's delegate Mohammad Ayoub said that Arab countries "continued to engage in good faith" but argued that they only accounted for a small proportion of historical greenhouse gas emissions.

Russia warned not to "turn to slogans" over coal, oil and gas, claiming that if countries moved away from fossil fuels too quickly it would lead to "fuel poverty".

World.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
World.content:
The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially come to an end after countries failed to come to a consensus on a new deal.

The European Union and some other countries rejected a fourth draft agreement over its failure to mention a need to phase out fossil fuels, the largest driver of global climate change.

An EU representative accuses some oil states of hijacking talks, as Russia defends opposing the inclusion of such a commitment and levels direct criticism at the EU in its speech.

The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.

BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard reports from Antalya, in Turkey.

World.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
World.content:
An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.

The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government.

The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.

Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said.

The UN mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, calling for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation".

"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the UNSMIL wrote on X., external

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.

World.title: 'Danger seems greater all the time': Ukrainians search for missing after Russian strikes
World.content:
Several bodies have been recovered from the site of a residential building that was hit by a Russian strike in the Kyiv region, Ukraine's State Emergency Services said.

The attack early on Sunday morning in the village of Dymer killed six people, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said. Six people were injured, while others are still missing.

Continued warnings of further drone threats near the site have hampered efforts, the service added, but some people were successfully evacuated earlier in the day.

"We are living a nightmare... only God knows when it will end," one woman told the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, who's reporting from Ukraine's Kyiv region.

World.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
World.content:
A Russian cargo vessel that was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland is being towed away, authorities have said.

The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, sparking a fire aboard.

It then drifted into Finnish waters and its crew were evacuated to Russia. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday afternoon that fire was no longer visible from the outside but thermal cameras showed that some containers on the ship were still warm.

The Sparta II was "slightly listing", Finnish authorities added, but the "situation is stable" and no fuel or other "hazardous substance leaks" had been detected.

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones appeared to have been used in the strike and that there was "no threat" to his territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

While Besprozvannykh initially said the crew of the Sparta II intended to repair the ship and carry on their journey, the Finnish Border Guard later said they had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was en route to Russia.

Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, director of maritime operations at the Finnish Border Guard, said during a news conference on Sunday that one Sparta II crew member had suffered minor injuries.

The Russian rescue vessel Murman is leading towing operations with the support of a Finnish guard ship and a Estonian naval patrol vessel.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

World.title: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
World.content:
"As the minister in charge, I believe I cannot escape criticism that we failed to prepare in advance," Choi was quoted as saying on Sunday by South Korea's Yonhap's news agency.

"Now that the exam has concluded, I feel a deep sense of responsibility and am offering my resignation," the minister added.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung - who has been calling for an overhaul of the current exam system - later accepted Choi's resignation.

The education ministry earlier said 111 candidates had been found with unauthorised smart devices during this year's Suneung, which was taken by about 500,000 students.

Concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam had been brewing in recent weeks, after reports of candidates cheating with the help of AI devices.

These fears came to a boil last weekend, when Han Won-seok, the top tax accountancy exam scorer in April, admitted to cheating.

His confession came amid speculation over his unusually high score, with just one out of 160 questions wrong.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI, then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating," the 34-year-old said in a video message.

This prompted the authorities to introduce urgent measures, with just days ahead of the Suneung.

This included sending nationwide emergency alerts on the exam day.

Three alerts were sent between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, causing phones across the country to blare out in unison - even if they were on silent mode, and even if they belonged to tourists using data roaming.

The phones did not ring out if they were switched off or on airplane mode.

It was the first time that South Korea used its national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters.

Candidates also had to cover up the buttons on their shirts and jackets to block any hidden cameras, and authorities conducted inspections of eyewear.

All this made even honest test takers paranoid.

Ahead of the Suneung, one high school senior told the Korea Times he was worried his horn-rimmed spectacles would be mistaken for smart glasses.

Another told Yonhap he usually wore glasses but made an effort to put on contact lenses for the Suneung to avoid raising suspicions.

World.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
World.content:
At least three people have been killed after a fire at a confectionery factory in western Java on Saturday, with the death toll expected to rise.

Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for around 36 missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.

Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency said on Sunday 15 survivors had been located, and four others taken to hospital and a local clinic with undisclosed injuries.

Rescuers recovered 24 body bags from the fire as of Sunday evening, as search operations continue to locate missing people.

Banten Governor, Andra Soni, told media about 60 people were believed to be inside the factory when it caught fire on Saturday evening.

The factory is in Serang district, Banten province, about 50km (31km) west of Jakarta. Authorities have not yet determined the fire's cause.

Photos and footage of the scene showed the large factory taken over by flames during the night, firefighters battling the flames, and first responders retrieving at least one body from the wreckage on Sunday morning.

Local media reported that the search had been called off for the night late on Sunday, and would resume on Monday.

World.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
World.content:
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.

Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

Sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.

"I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change," Hubbard told the BBC News Channel after his victory. He pledged to work alongside his fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Earlier, he wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

Hubbard added: "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District."

Foxx, meanwhile, said in a statement: "After running a campaign focused on my track record of commonsense solutions and conservative values, I'm humbled and grateful that so many North Carolina voters responded by supporting my candidacy, even if we came up just a few votes short."

World.title: TotalEnergies deepens support for vulnerable Nigerians
World.content:
TotalEnergies has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting organisations that provide care and rehabilitation for vulnerable people in Nigeria.

The Country Chair of TotalEnergies Companies in Nigeria, Matthieu Bouyer, gave the assurance at the 2026 TotalEnergies Charity Golf Tournament in Port Harcourt on Sunday.

Mr Bouyer said the company’s continued investment in charitable organisations reflected its commitment to supporting communities and improving lives.

He also said the tournament aimed to raise funds for two organisations whose activities focused on vulnerable people.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the beneficiaries include the Little Sisters of the Poor Home for the Elderly in Enugu and Rosaline Home Rehabilitation Centre in Ogale, Eleme, Rivers State.

Mr Bouyer said the Little Sisters of the Poor had cared for elderly people in difficult circumstances for more than five decades, irrespective of their backgrounds or religious affiliations.

“The home provides accommodation, meals, medical attention and daily assistance to its residents,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He described Rosalie Home Rehabilitation Centre, run by the Daughters of Charity of St. Vincent de Paul, as another important beneficiary.

He said the centre provides care and rehabilitation for women living with mental health conditions who have experienced homelessness or abandonment.

“One tournament cannot meet every need. But a well-directed donation makes a real difference,” he said.

Mr Bouyer said TotalEnergies would supplement the proceeds from the tournament to support the two charities, urging participants and well-wishers to contribute towards their agreed priorities.

“The impact of the competition will be measured not only by sporting achievements but also by improvements in the lives of vulnerable people and communities,” he said.

NAN reports that TotalEnergies donated N5 million each to the two charitable organisations to support vulnerable persons in their care.

Appeal for further assistance for elderly people’s home

Receiving the donation, Mary Jacinta, mother superior of the Little Sisters of the Poor Home for the Elderly, Enugu, commended TotalEnergies for its support.

She appealed for further assistance to improve the facilities and care provided for the home’s more than 46 residents.

She said the home, established in 1975, catered for elderly people, many of whom were physically challenged and battling age-related illnesses.

Ms Jacinta, a reverend sister, also said that most of the residents depended on others for their personal needs and required constant attention and assistance.

She said the home relied entirely on public charity, adding that the sisters dedicated their lives to caring for the elderly without receiving salaries.

“We stay in the same house with the old people. We share everything with them and are available day and night to provide care.

“Our aim is always to make the old people happy,” she said.

Ms Jacinta described TotalEnergies’ support as a welcome surprise, saying it would help the home address some of its pressing needs.

She added that beyond providing food, clothing, medical attention and daily care, the home was seeking funds to renovate residents’ rooms and improve their comfort.

The reverend sister explained that the home needed adjustable medical beds to help caregivers position residents’ heads and legs according to their medical and personal needs.

She identified unreliable electricity and inadequate water supply as challenges, adding that the home planned to install solar power and construct a borehole.

She appealed to individuals, organisations and well-wishers to support the home in improving the welfare of its elderly residents.

World.title: NPFL Roundup: Rivers, Barau record big wins as Rangers maintain lead
World.content:
Rivers United produced the biggest result of Matchday 14 of the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL), thrashing Niger Tornadoes 6-0 on Sunday, as Rangers International maintained their position at the top of the table.

Samson Olasupo scored a second-half hat-trick at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt to cap Rivers United’s dominant display, while Barau FC also recorded a convincing 5-0 victory over Inter Lagos.

Rivers United took an early lead in the 13th minute through an own goal by Moses Obioma before Temple ThankGod doubled the advantage in the 29th minute. Shola Oladunjoye added a third three minutes later to leave the visitors facing a difficult afternoon.

Olasupo then took centre stage, scoring in the 63rd, 87th and 90+4th minutes to complete his hat-trick and hand Tornadoes their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

The victory moved Rivers United to fifth place with 22 points from 13 matches, keeping them within six points of leaders Rangers, who have played the same number of games.

Barau FC were equally ruthless against Inter Lagos, securing a 5-0 win with Joseph Atule scoring three times. Atule found the net in the 34th, 66th and 87th minutes, while Ayoola Ibrahim scored before half-time and Adamu Hussain added another in the 79th minute.

The result lifted Barau to third place with 23 points, level with Nasarawa United but ahead on goal difference.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rangers maintained their lead with a 2-0 home victory over Shooting Stars in Awka. James Emo opened the scoring in the 14th minute before Chidiebere Nwobodo sealed the win in the 74th minute, taking Rangers to 28 points from 13 matches.

Nasarawa United also moved into the top four after beating Warri Wolves 2-0 in Lafia. Kelechi Ogbodo headed home in the 25th minute before Jofrank Joshua converted an 83rd-minute penalty to secure the points for the hosts.

In Aba, the Oriental derby between Abia Warriors and Enyimba ended goalless, leaving both sides on 12 points and deep in the relegation battle.

READ ALSO: Former NFF Vice President Uchegbulam loses wife

Kun Khalifat FC edged Katsina United 1-0 through Innocent Arigu’s 17th-minute own goal, while Saturday’s fixtures saw Kano Pillars beat Ikorodu City and Doma United defeat Bendel Insurance by identical 1-0 margins.

Ranchers Bees drew 1-1 with Plateau United, while Sporting Lagos and Kwara United also shared the points.

Rangers remain top of the standings with 28 points from 13 games, followed by Kano Pillars on 25 points. Barau FC and Nasarawa United occupy third and fourth positions respectively with 23 points, while Rivers United are fifth on 22 points, with a game in hand. Bendel Insurance are sixth on 21 points.

Plateau United, Doma United and Katsina United are seventh, eighth and ninth respectively, all on 20 points, while Ikorodu City and Shooting Stars occupy 10th and 11th positions with 18 points apiece. Niger Tornadoes are 12th on 17 points.

Sporting Lagos, Ranchers Bees and Kun Khalifat are 13th, 14th and 15th respectively with 16 points, although Sporting Lagos have played only 12 matches. Kwara United and Warri Wolves sit 16th and 17th on 14 points, while Enyimba and Abia Warriors occupy the bottom two positions with 12 points each. Inter Lagos remain bottom with seven points after a three-point deduction, while Warri Wolves have also been docked three points for infractions.

World.title: Police in Akwa Ibom honour Gov Eno, Akpabio, 254 officers
World.content:
The Nigeria Police Force, Akwa Ibom State Command, has honoured the Governor of Akwa Ibom State Umo Eno, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and 254 police officers at an award ceremony in Uyo, recognising their contributions to security and policing in the state.

The awards were presented at the Command’s Award and Dinner Night held at Ibom Hall, Uyo, on Saturday, according to a statement issued on Sunday by the police spokesperson, Timfon John, a deputy superintendent of police.

The ceremony also recognised 22 other security stakeholders, including commanders of four sister security agencies, for their contributions to security operations and collaboration with the police.

The Commissioner of Police, Baba Azare, said the awards were intended to recognise officers whose dedication and sacrifices often go unnoticed despite their role in protecting lives and property.

He said the 254 recipients were drawn from different ranks, divisions and formations across the command, adding that the initiative was designed to promote merit, discipline and operational excellence.

Mr Azare also recognised 22 individuals and stakeholders for supporting police operations, particularly those who accompanied security personnel during operations in difficult terrains, including creeks and waterways.

The four commanders of sister security agencies were honoured for their contributions to inter-agency collaboration and operational coordination.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Eno, Akpabio receive awards

Mr Akpabio received an award in recognition of his contributions and support to the security sector, while Mr Eno was recognised for his leadership and support for security agencies in the state.

In an unusual recognition, the command also honoured Ezra Obareki, the governor’s grandson, for his affection and positive disposition towards the police.

The governor’s chief security officer, aide-de-camp, principal security officer and Government House camp commandant were also recognised for their services.

Police seek public cooperation

Mr Azare reaffirmed the command’s commitment to intelligence-led policing, professionalism, respect for human rights and community partnership.

READ ALSO: 10 police vans deployed as Jimmy Odukoya attends service

He said the relative peace in the state was a product of cooperation among the government, security agencies, community stakeholders and residents.

The development comes amid continuing public concerns about security and policing across Nigeria, where police authorities have repeatedly emphasised the importance of community cooperation in tackling crime.

PREMIUM TIMES has reported on security operations and policing challenges in Akwa Ibom, including the police’s crackdown on the proscribed Ibom Youth Council in December 2024.

The police commissioner called on residents to continue providing useful information to security agencies and supporting efforts to maintain peace in the state.

World.title: COP31: Nigeria absent at closing plenary
World.content:
The Nigerian government delegation was conspicuously absent at the closing plenary of the controversial United Nations climate summit (COP31) in Türkiye, where countries expressed frustration over the failure to reach consensus on key climate issues.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that parties at the United Nations climate change talks in Türkiye failed to reach consensus amid deep divisions over fossil fuel phase-out, just transition, climate finance and other contentious issues.

COP31 President Murat Kurum confirmed during the closing plenary on Sunday that the final draft agreement, the Antalya Pact, would not be approved, despite negotiations being extended by nearly 48 hours beyond the officially scheduled closing date of 20 November.

The development made COP31 the longest climate summit in the convention’s history and arguably one of the most criticised in recent years.

Amid the disappointment, parties and negotiating blocs took turns expressing their positions to the COP president. The frustration and dissatisfaction with the outcome of more than two weeks of negotiations were evident in the tone of representatives who addressed the plenary.

However, despite the controversy surrounding the COP31 outcome, Nigeria’s head of delegation, ministers, and other representatives were absent, even as a few African countries spoke, despite Nigeria having one of the largest delegations at this year’s COP.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Nigeria ranked third among countries with the highest number of registered participants at this year’s COP, with 1,506 delegates, according to provisional figures released for the summit.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Of this number, 573 participants were registered under the “Party” badge category, while 933 received “Party Overflow” badges.

Nigeria’s delegation to UNFCCC COP31 is usually led by the Director-General of the Nigeria Climate Change Council (NCCC), Teniola Majekodunmi. This year, however, it remains unclear how many of the registered participants were sponsored by the Nigerian government. The council has yet to provide a comprehensive breakdown of participants whose trips were funded with public resources.

At the conference venue, PREMIUM TIMES gathered from some associates of the NCCC director-general that she had left the COP venue midweek.

The lack of disclosure raises concerns about transparency and accountability in the management of Nigeria’s participation in international climate negotiations.

It also limits public understanding of who represents the country in various negotiating groups and technical sessions, as well as who is responsible for advancing Nigeria’s positions on critical climate issues.

Some observers have also expressed concerns that Nigeria’s participation in these conferences sometimes goes beyond diplomatic engagement, with some registered participants allegedly treating the meetings as opportunities for international travel rather than meaningful negotiations.

They argue that inadequate technical knowledge, negotiating experience and understanding of diplomatic processes among some participants could undermine Nigeria’s ability to secure favourable outcomes from the annual climate negotiations.

One of Nigeria’s notable appearances at the summit was the delivery of its national statement by Environment Minister Balarabe Lawal. PREMIUM TIMES reported that the government reaffirmed its commitment to advancing climate action, calling for stronger international cooperation and increased climate financing to accelerate the global response to climate change.

Nigeria reacts after deadlock

In a brief statement issued after the COP plenary ended on Sunday, Ms Majekodunmi said COP31’s failure to reach consensus on an overarching political outcome was disappointing and underscored the continuing challenges facing international climate cooperation.

She noted that the absence of a new political agreement did not diminish the urgency of climate action or invalidate the commitments already undertaken under the Paris Agreement.

“For Nigeria, our focus remains firmly on implementation. We will continue advancing our NDC 3.0, strengthening climate governance, mobilising investment and pursuing an orderly, just and nationally determined energy transition,” she said.

Ms Majekodunmi said the discussions in Antalya reinforced an important lesson: climate ambition must be matched by credible financing, practical implementation pathways and recognition of different national circumstances.

She added that Nigeria remained firmly committed to multilateralism and would continue working constructively with African partners and the wider international community to advance consensus and accelerate climate action.

“Ultimately, Nigeria’s climate progress will be measured not only by emissions reduced, but by jobs created, businesses developed, energy access expanded and livelihoods improved,” she said.

PREMIUM TIMES contacted the DG on Sunday to inquire why she was absent from the closing plenary, why Nigeria had no representative who spoke at the session, and why she left the conference midweek. In what has become her usual practice, she asked a third party to contact our reporter with a response.

A representative of the council, who identified herself as Jummai Vandu, said she had been directed to clarify Nigeria’s position regarding the COP31 closing plenary in Antalya.

She said Nigeria’s national position was fully presented through the African Group of Negotiators (AGN), which serves as Africa’s unified negotiating voice.

According to her, under UNFCCC plenary procedures, countries are welcome to speak in their national capacity, but doing so is entirely optional and not mandatory. In practice, she said, member states routinely align themselves with the AGN.

“Chair’s statement during overtime closing sessions to manage tight time constraints, avoid repetition, and project a unified continental front that maximises collective leverage on key issues. Those African nations that took the floor individually simply chose to add specific national emphasis to the shared regional position already delivered by the AGN,” she said.

She explained that the DG actively championed Nigeria’s core priorities across high-level sessions and bilateral engagements, ensuring the country’s interests were firmly embedded in the final African position.

However, she did not explain why the DG left the conference venue midweek.

READ ALSO: UN chief blames fossil fuel interests for climate inaction as COP31 ends without consensus

COP31 priorities

COP31 was expected to offer countries an important opportunity to advance negotiations on practical measures to address gaps in climate action implementation.

Alongside formal negotiations, the Global Climate Action Agenda was expected to provide opportunities to boost electrification, improve access to climate finance, and cut waste and emissions of super-pollutants such as methane.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the African Group of Negotiators (AGN), which includes Nigeria, said it would push for increased climate finance, including an ambitious replenishment of the Green Climate Fund (GCF), among other priorities.

The group said securing adequate and predictable climate finance, particularly grant-based and concessional funding, would be central to Africa’s negotiating priorities at the conference.

But the group was not satisfied with the COP outcome. It made its position clear at the closing plenary.

World.title: Bayelsa Boat Mishap: Death toll rises, Tinubu approves N250mn for victims’ families
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has approved N250 million in financial assistance to families of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Bayelsa State, where the death toll has risen to 29.

Vice-President Kashim Shettima announced the presidential intervention on Sunday during a condolence visit to the state, following the tragedy near Oweikorogha community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

The boat was conveying passengers to Ukubie community for a burial ceremony when it capsized on 20 November.

According to a post on the Bayelsa Government New Media Facebook page, Mr Shettima, who visited survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital in Yenagoa, said Mr Tinubu had directed relevant federal agencies to support the state government’s search and rescue efforts and provide assistance to affected families.

He also disclosed that the president had directed the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) to procure boats to improve water transportation in the riverine communities.

Mr Shettima described the incident as a national tragedy, saying the victims were people with families, relationships and responsibilities who had left home for a funeral but never returned.

He acknowledged the importance of waterways to Bayelsa communities, noting that the state’s geographical peculiarities make water transport essential for access to schools, hospitals, markets and other services.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Death toll rises

Bayelsa Governor Douye Diri said 29 people had been confirmed dead, while more than 51 survivors had been recorded.

He said search and recovery operations were continuing, adding that the capsized boat had yet to be recovered. Some bodies could still be trapped inside the vessel, he said.

The governor said preliminary findings suggested that the accident might have been avoided if established safety regulations had been observed.

According to him, the boat was neither seaworthy nor suitable for river transportation, while the location where passengers boarded was not an approved government loading point.

“From what we have gathered so far, the boat was not seaworthy or river-worthy. The loading point was not an approved government loading point, and that is why all the necessary government requirements were not found in this incident,” Mr Diri said.

The governor said the state government was coordinating the rescue operation with federal agencies, security services and other relevant authorities.

He added that the government was paying the medical bills and providing feeding for survivors receiving treatment in hospitals across the state.

Mr Diri also commended the president’s intervention, recalling that Mr Shettima, the president’s chief of staff, and the minister of marine and blue economy were among the first senior federal officials to contact him after the incident.

He described the tragedy as particularly painful because many of the victims were young people with promising futures.

Diri seeks federal intervention

Beyond the boat accident, the governor used the visit to appeal for federal intervention over infrastructure challenges facing the state.

He specifically called for accelerated work on the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road project, saying the difficult riverine terrain makes road construction in Bayelsa expensive and challenging.

He also appealed to the federal government to collaborate with the state government towards completing the three senatorial roads.

Mr Shettima commended the governor’s response to the tragedy, particularly the establishment of a commission of inquiry.

He stressed the need for the panel’s recommendations to be implemented to prevent similar accidents.

The vice-president also met with families of the victims and presented cash assistance to them.

The condolence visit was attended by several government officials, including the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Heineken Lokpobiri; the NDDC Managing Director, Samuel Ogbuku; and the Director-General of the National Emergency Management Agency, Zubaida Umar.

World.title: Go reconcile with Katsina governor, Tinubu tells Masari
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Sunday in Lagos underscored the virtue of forgiveness at a prayer session organised in his honour by his extended family, urging APC leaders to forgive one another and seek reconciliation.

His message was specifically directed at his Special Adviser on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, and former Defence Minister, Abubakar Badaru, both of whom were in the audience at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club, where the president spoke.

Apparently reacting to reports of a quarrel between Governor Dikko Radda and Mr Masari in Katsina State, President Tinubu urged Mr Masari to go back home to reconcile with his governor.

“Alhaji Kabiru Masari, go back home and reconcile with everybody. That is the president’s order. When you finish that, you move to Jigawa. You move to other places and reconcile them, beg them, because we have to reconcile and every anger must dissipate and evaporate,” the president said.

The president also gave the same order to Mr Badaru, the former governor of Jigawa State.

President Tinubu appealed to all APC leaders to set aside personal differences, strengthen internal cohesion, and work collectively to consolidate his administration’s gains ahead of the 2027 elections.

The president thanked the organisers of the Islamic prayer session and clerics who prayed for him, his administration, and Nigeria.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He thanked God for his victory in the 2023 presidential election, despite formidable obstacles.

“People cried. People suffered. People died. People had no five naira in their pockets because their money was in the bank and they couldn’t get it out. There was also no fuel.

“We invoked the spirit of Almighty Allah and said, ‘Kun faya kun (‘Be, and it becomes’). It got us there, and we have the presidency. Allah gives power to whom he wants, and he takes it from whoever he wants,” the president said.

The prayer session was attended by Muslim and Christian clerics as well as Governors of Lagos, Kaduna, Kwara, Ogun, and Imo states.

Other dignitaries in attendance included National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, and Lagos Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat.

Also present were the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; Speaker of Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Abou-Nolla; the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Coalition of Northern Groups (CNG), Nasturah Sharriff; the Tinubu family members and party faithful.

The president recalled that he invoked “Emilokan’s spirit (it is my turn) in 2022. It is now your turn (Eyinlokan) to make the re-election possible.”

He appealed to Lagosians to come out en masse on Election Day to exercise their right to vote.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday, but we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door, tell them to collect their PVC. If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6th, and that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” the President said.

“We must generate enough votes to overwhelm the opponents,” he emphasised.

He reaffirmed his commitment to providing purposeful leadership, strengthening national unity and justice, and building a prosperous country for all Nigerians.

Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State described the president as an epitome of justice, fairness, equity, and inclusive governance, calling these virtues essential pillars for building a united, peaceful, and prosperous Nigeria.

Former Governor of Jigawa, Badaru Abubakar, said Northerners appreciated President Tinubu’s support for the late former President Muhammadu Buhari in his 2015 and 2019 election victories.

Mr Badaru urged Northern voters to reciprocate the gesture and help the president consolidate the administration’s achievements so far.

The Chairman of the occasion and elder statesman, 94-year-old Lateef Okunnu, promised to canvass and vote for the president on 16 January 2027.

He said the president has done a lot to be re-elected.

The elder statesman also emphasised the need to uphold justice, saying that the Tinubu administration is focusing on the economy and infrastructure, especially the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, as well as strengthening the naira and foreign reserves.

In their vote of thanks, representatives of the Tinubu family, Rafiu Tinubu and Bintu Tinubu, thanked God for the family’s blessings and urged Nigerians to support the President in his determination to deliver the dividends of democracy to the people.

Honsu Oluremi, chairman of Lagos State Government House Chapel, referenced the Bible and urged the people to always pray for leaders’ success.

The Coordinator of the Prayer session and the Grand Chief Imam of Lagos, Sheikh Sulaimon Abou-Nolla, while reading from the holy Qur’an, asked Allah to grant the president success in his affairs and good health.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

November 22, 2026

World.title: Nigeria signs MoU with World’s largest pivot irrigation manufacturer to drive ‘Irrigate Nigeria Programme’
World.content:
The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) has formally signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Valmont Industries, Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, marking a major step in the Federal Government’s flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme under the present administration.

The signing of the MoU at the weekend, according to the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the full implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, officially brings Valmont — through its Valley Irrigation brand, the global leader in mechanised irrigation — on board as a major partner in the development of irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria.

Under the agreement, Valmont will not only partner in building world-class irrigation infrastructure in Nigeria but has also agreed to partner with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI) to establish an irrigation equipment production plant in the country.

The partnership comes with a firm commitment for transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, positioning the country to domesticate mechanized irrigation technology rather than rely solely on imports.

Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed who signed the agreement with the Regional Vice President, Middle East and Africa, Valmont, Mr. Kalle Autto, said “This MOU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.”

“Valmont will not only partner with us in building irrigation infrastructure — they have also agreed to partner with NASENI to build an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria. Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” Dr Muhammed added.

The agreement sets the stage for a pilot programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State, to be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). PICTT will lead the full implementation of the programme, while NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

There are also promising opportunities to collaborate with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management. Dr Muhammed added that key stakeholders had already shown interest in scaling irrigation infrastructure using the partnership, a development he described as a strong vote of confidence in the direction of the programme.

Valley Irrigation’s global footprint underscores the scale of the partnership: more than 40 percent of center pivots in service worldwide are Valley machines, with over 250,000 Valley pivots operating across 120-plus countries and approximately 12 million hectares under irrigation. The company also operates more than 146,000 connected irrigation devices worldwide.

Valmont Industries itself brings 80 years of industrial expertise, net sales of $4.1 billion in 2025, 83 manufacturing facilities, operations in over 100 countries, roughly 11,000 employees, and 31 distinct brands.

Officials noted that the partnership marks an important step toward enhancing agricultural productivity, strengthening national food security, and promoting the sustainable use of water resources in line with the administration’s agricultural transformation agenda.

World.title: Makinde: Bride or side-chick?, By Wole Olaoye
World.content:
Of course, you very well know that a bride is a woman on her wedding day, while a side chick is a mistress or sidekick. Forty-seven years ago, during the 1979 elections in which Alhaji Shehu Shagari of the National Party of Nigeria (NPN) came first, beating Chief Obafemi Awolowo of the Unity Party of Nigeria to second place, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe (the great Zik) branded himself the beautiful bride of the moment because both front-runners needed his support to control the legislature.

Zik eventually said yes to the nuptial proposal of the NPN. A power-sharing formula was then worked out in which both NPN and NPP shared power in the executive and legislative arms of government.

Ongoing Talks

The ongoing alliance talks between Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde (running on the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, platform) and former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar (the African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential flag-bearer) remind me of Zik’s beautiful bride manoeuvre—except that Makinde is poised to wear the bridal garment before the first ballot is cast.

In a pragmatic effort to forge a unified opposition front against incumbent President Bola Tinubu ahead of the January 2027 general election, both Makinde and Atiku are currently engaged in high-level bilateral negotiations alongside broader opposition consultations (such as those facilitated by the G-100 pressure group).

The cooperation is driven by cold electoral arithmetic rather than personal sentiment, as Makinde himself has emphasised that any decision will be data-driven.

Presently, opposition votes are fragmented. Major opposition figures are scattered across different platforms — Atiku in the ADC (with Rotimi Amaechi as running mate), Peter Obi in the NDC (with Rabiu Kwankwaso), and Makinde in the APM—contesting independently. The Atiku and Makinde camps recognise that pooling resources is essential if they want to overcome the ruling party’s incumbency advantage.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

This is a time for cold calculations. Atiku has always been weak in the Southwest, Tinubu’s backyard. As the most politically entrenched opposition governor in the region, Makinde gives Atiku an institutional foothold, grassroots mobilisation machinery, and a credible Yoruba voice in the team.

Makinde has publicly ruled out working with President Tinubu, citing a past “broken agreement” from the 2023 electoral cycle. The Oyo State governor is like the proverbial leper who may not be able to collect cow milk but is quite capable of spilling a basin of the product.

Bargaining Power

By holding parallel talks with both Atiku and Peter Obi while maintaining his own presidential candidacy, Makinde maximises his bargaining power—positioning himself either as the consensus Southern candidate or as a decisive kingmaker deserving major post-election concessions.

If you prime your nose to pick up the aroma, you’ll smell the coffee being brewed by the opposition. Strategists working for Tinubu’s opponents are weighing whether to rally behind a Southern candidate to satisfy zoning sentiments or bank on Atiku’s established northern vote reservoir.

Hypothetically, in the kind of politics played in these climes, the fact that Atiku and Obi command demonstrably larger bases would not make Makinde a pushover in any negotiation. He appears to hold that tiny fraction that could make a difference between 24.5 per cent and the required 25 per cent that a presidential candidate needs from two-thirds of Nigeria’s 36 states. So far, everything considered, it appears that only the incumbent President Tinubu can muster that spread for now.

In this kind of calculation, the question must be asked: who is stepping down for whom? Is Makinde’s fortune better guaranteed under Atiku or in collaboration with Obi?

In my view, Makinde has two options:

Makinde/Atiku (APM/ADC) Alliance

In this scenario, the Oyo State governor collapses his APM structure into Atiku’s African Democratic Congress (ADC) or negotiates a joint front. It will have to be a gentlemen’s agreement because the electoral law and INEC guidelines have foreclosed the issue of mergers and substitution of candidates.

Atiku’s stronghold is in the North (particularly the Northeast), whereas Makinde is the only sitting opposition governor in the South-West. Together, they create a classic North–South bridge.

In addition, Atiku commands decades of nationwide elite networks, party machinery, and campaign financing touted as capable of matching the APC state for state, Naira for Naira.

If you think Makinde is a small fry, consider the fact that Atiku desperately needs a credible South-West general to challenge Tinubu in his backyard. Because of this unique position, Makinde can demand maximum post-election influence from Atiku.

However, backing a Northern candidate (Atiku) after only four years of a Southern presidency risks alienating Yoruba voters who believe the South should complete the unwritten eight-year rotation. Also, having famously opposed Atiku in 2023 on principles of power rotation and fairness, a sudden U-turn could be framed by APC opponents as opportunistic.

Makinde/Obi (APM/NDC) Alliance

If Makinde aligns with the “OK Movement” (Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso) under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), the alliance keeps power in the South for 2027–2031 (before rotating north to Kwankwaso under the NDC pact), making it far easier for Makinde to sell the ticket to South-West voters.

Research conducted in mid-2026 indicates that the Obi–Kwankwaso ticket enjoys the highest favourability traction among opposition blocs, while the South-West shows a high share of undecided voters (around 23%) whom Makinde is uniquely positioned to sway.

The Oyo State governor has painstakingly marketed himself as a reformer determined to reset and reposition Nigeria, not a professional politician. He makes it known to whoever may listen that he has an alternative address and another day job outside the public office. His technocratic reputation in Oyo State meshes naturally with Obi’s anti-establishment, cost-of-governance message, avoiding the baggage associated with traditional political heavyweights.

Nonetheless, realistically speaking, considering that the NDC already features two heavyweight principals (Obi and Kwankwaso) with a pre-negotiated power-sharing deal, Makinde enters as a third partner rather than a co-equal architect. Two is romance; three is a crowd!

Obi’s electoral math relies heavily on high voter turnout—especially among younger and urban demographics. In low-turnout scenarios or heavily monetised grassroots contests, NDC’s structure is more vulnerable to APC state machinery than Atiku’s entrenched network. Nobody knows this better than NDC’s strategists.

If Makinde backs Obi while Atiku remains in the race on the ADC ticket, the Northern opposition vote remains split between Atiku (North-East) and Kwankwaso (North-West), potentially allowing Tinubu to win a plurality. No one can discount the fact that incumbent Vice President Kashim Shettima is a much more formidable politician in 2026 than he was as candidate Shettima in 2023.

Getting down to brass tacks, Makinde’s fortunes are best enhanced by an alliance with Peter Obi, which gives the NDC a realistic shot at sweeping the undecided voters in the southwest —provided the coalition can overcome Atiku’s parallel candidacy in the North and Tinubu’s indubitable dominance in the southwest.

In that eventuality, Makinde will be the OK ticket’s bride.

On the other hand, if he decides to go with Atiku, he can only end up as ADC’s mistress or side-chick, not legally wedded but positioned to enjoy the perks of political conjugation.

Wole Olaoye is a Public Relations consultant and veteran journalist. He can be reached on [email protected], Twitter: @wole_olaoye; Instagram: woleola2021

World.title: Climate talks collapse in chaotic end to COP31
World.content:
COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (left) speaks with Ghanaian Environment Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings after a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. Photo by Yasin AKGUL / AFP.

Climate advocates reacted with indignation on Monday to the COP31 summit ending in failure, with contentious talks collapsing over fossil fuels after the meeting in Turkey stretched into record overtime.

The final agreement was rejected on Sunday in a chaotic finale to the UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay.

“I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement.

COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”.

“Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters.

More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks.

Calls for reform

Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the summit with Turkey, attributed the failure of the talks to “difficult geopolitical times”.

Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis.

But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas.

The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal.

“We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.

“And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.”

Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record.

Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”.

The COP process is “in need of significant reform”, Gore said on X, as most countries sought “to move forward in good faith.”

Falling short

The outcome revived memories of the failed Copenhagen summit of 2009 and raised fresh doubts about the effectiveness of climate diplomacy.

“It certainly fell short today,” said UN climate chief Simon Stiell.

“The world cannot afford a repeat.”

Frustrated by the inertia, countries are pushing ahead outside the COP process.

Around 60 countries joined a first-of-its-kind conference in April on phasing out fossil fuels while several nations at COP31 unveiled their own plans to exit coal, oil and gas.

In a last-ditch bid for compromise, COP31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia could only muster a veiled reference to fossil fuels in the final text.

But the pact also took fire for retaining a call to expand carbon capture — a costly technology championed by the fossil fuel industry.

“We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table,” said Mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator for oil giant Saudi Arabia.

Facing blowback over the fossil fuels omission, the co-host nations tried to rally support behind a global goal to electrify the world economy.

They said “electrification” could cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security but the target was ultimately torpedoed, along with the rest of the doomed Antalya Pact.

‘Profoundly disappointed’

Countries lamented a missed opportunity to reinforce the Paris agreement’s 1.5C target, which scientists expect the world to overshoot in a few years as carbon-cutting goals fall short.

The summit also widened fault lines over science, with a fight over the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) spilling into the negotiations.

“We are profoundly disappointed by the substance of the cover decision,” said UK climate negotiator Kate Hughes.

“It moves us backwards on the science… It is a lowest common denominator where it should have been, instead, presenting bold collective ambition on climate action.”

As always, the summit laid bare the divide between major polluters driving climate change and smaller nations bearing the brunt of its impact.

Developing nations pushed for a $120 billion target climate goal which disappeared from the failed deal.
