World.title: 2027: Lagos is a big deal to me – Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has urged residents of Lagos State to mobilise eligible voters and collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the state remains a major political priority for him.

Tinubu made the call on Sunday while addressing guests at the Yoruba Tennis Club in Onikan, Lagos, during a special prayer session organised by members of his family ahead of the elections.

The President urged residents to encourage their neighbours to collect their PVCs, stressing that voter participation in Lagos should reflect the state’s large voting population.

“The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock your neighbour’s door. Tell them to go and collect their PVCs,” he said.

He jokingly told those without voter cards that they had little business attending the political gathering.

“If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are here for Amala,” he said.

Tinubu urged eligible voters to turn out on the scheduled election dates and exercise their franchise.

“If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16 and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise,” he said.

Emphasising the political importance of Lagos to him, the President declared: “To me, Lagos is the big deal.”

The appeal comes as political parties and their candidates intensify preparations for the 2027 general elections, with voter mobilisation and PVC collection expected to feature prominently in their campaigns.

World.title: Gombe awards seven road contracts covering 97km
World.content:
…Projects to open up rural communities, boost economic activities in four LGAs

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The Gombe State Government has signed contract agreements with construction companies for the execution of seven road projects covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas.

The projects, which span Balanga, Kaltungo, Shongom and Yamaltu-Deba Local Government Areas, are aimed at improving rural connectivity, facilitating the transportation of agricultural produce, enhancing access to markets and stimulating economic activities.

The contract agreements were signed at a ceremony organised by the Ministry of Works and Infrastructure, attended by government officials and representatives of the construction companies.

Speaking at the ceremony, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Hon. Shehu Yerima Abdullahi, said the projects were part of the infrastructure development agenda of Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya’s administration to connect underserved communities and promote socioeconomic growth.

He said the road projects demonstrated the government’s commitment to extending infrastructure development beyond urban centres and improving the living conditions of rural residents.

Abdullahi charged the contractors to justify the confidence reposed in them by adhering strictly to approved engineering specifications, quality standards and contractual obligations.

He stressed that timely completion and quality workmanship were non-negotiable, adding that the ministry would sustain monitoring and supervision to ensure the projects were delivered within the agreed timelines and required standards.

Earlier, the Permanent Secretary of the ministry, Danladi Adamu, said the contract-signing exercise was an important step towards ensuring effective implementation, supervision and delivery of the projects.

In their separate remarks, the Branch Manager of EEC International Limited, Mr Dong Jian; representative of the Managing Director of SWAS GRADE Limited, Engr. Christina Daniel; and Managing Director of DATUM Construction Nigeria Limited, Engr. Daher Kaworma, thanked the state government for awarding the contracts to their companies.

They pledged to deliver quality infrastructure in line with approved specifications and contractual provisions, assuring that the projects would be completed within the agreed periods.

The seven road projects were approved by the State Executive Council at its last meeting presided over by Governor Yahaya.

They include the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, with a spur to Dalawaja, and Phase One of the four-kilometre Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road.

Others are the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak; the 15-kilometre Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road; and the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road.

The remaining projects are the 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road and the 1.5-kilometre Kunuwal Road Network.

The latest contracts add to the administration’s ongoing efforts to expand the state’s road network, improve connectivity between rural and urban communities and enhance access to economic opportunities.

The projects are expected to ease transportation challenges, facilitate the movement of farm produce to markets, reduce travel difficulties and improve economic activities across the benefiting communities upon completion.

World.title: COP31: Onuigbo tasks legislators on climate laws, funding
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

The President of GLOBE Legislators International, Rt. Hon. Sir Sam Ifeanyi Onuigbo, has urged parliamentarians across the world to translate international climate agreements into enforceable national laws, backed by adequate funding and effective oversight.

Onuigbo said international climate agreements would achieve little unless national parliaments incorporated decisions reached at United Nations climate conferences into domestic legislation and ensured their implementation.

He made the call at the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) COP31 Parliamentary Meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, where he highlighted the role of legislators in ensuring that commitments reached at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conferences of the Parties (COPs) produced tangible results at the national level.

In a statement made available to journalists in Gombe on Saturday, the former member of the House of Representatives said parliamentarians must deploy their constitutional powers of lawmaking, budgetary appropriation and oversight to ensure governments implement international climate commitments.

Drawing on his legislative experience, Onuigbo recalled that his participation in the GLOBE COP21 Legislators Summit in Paris influenced his decision to sponsor Nigeria’s Climate Change Act.

He argued that without the necessary legislative backing, negotiations and agreements reached at international climate conferences could fail to translate into practical outcomes.

“After all the contributions here, if they are not brought down into laws for implementation, it becomes an exercise in futility,” he said.

Onuigbo described parliamentary action as central to bridging the gap between international climate negotiations and domestic implementation.

He stressed that legislators must ensure that agreements reached at COP meetings were reflected in national laws, budgetary allocations and effective government oversight.

Describing the deliberations at the Antalya meeting as detailed and incisive, he said their impact would ultimately depend on the ability of parliamentarians to translate the discussions into actionable legislation.

The GLOBE Legislators president also commended the National Council on Climate Change, its leadership under Dr Majekodunmi, researchers and other stakeholders for their contributions to the development of the Host Country Approval Criteria for Carbon Market Activities in Nigeria and the country’s broader climate change efforts.

He also acknowledged President Bola Tinubu’s role in Nigeria’s climate change efforts.

“Above all, I want to thank President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who has exercised admirable leadership in ensuring that the climate journey remains steady and very successful,” he said.

Onuigbo was inaugurated as President of GLOBE Legislators at the United Kingdom Parliament on June 24, 2026.

Established in 1991, GLOBE Legislators works to strengthen parliamentary engagement and international cooperation on environmental governance and climate change.

World.title: Tinubu’s reforms may be difficult to sustain without re-election — Wike
World.content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said it would be difficult to sustain and stabilise President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms if he fails to secure re-election in 2027.

Wike said the initial challenges associated with the removal of petrol subsidy were temporary, arguing that Tinubu should be allowed to complete the foundation he had laid for Nigeria’s economic recovery and prosperity.

The minister spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving service at St Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State.

He said Nigeria had been facing the threat of economic collapse before Tinubu assumed office, describing the president as courageous for taking difficult decisions.

“This country was on the verge of collapse. But by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” Wike said.

“And that is why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. He has laid his foundation; now it’s time for prosperity. If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done.”

Wike cited what he described as improved stability in the university system, noting that strikes by lecturers over unpaid entitlements, which frequently disrupted academic calendars in the past, were no longer a recurring feature under the Tinubu administration.

He also recalled the difficulties pensioners previously encountered in accessing their entitlements, arguing that decisions taken by the president had helped address some of the country’s longstanding challenges.

The FCT minister urged Nigerians across religious divides to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, insisting that the president’s campaign would accommodate Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers.

“I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters. The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes,” he said.

Wike also dismissed claims of religious imbalance in appointments under the Tinubu administration, insisting that Christians had enjoyed greater representation in the current government than in previous administrations.

“Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” he said.

The minister, during the service, announced a donation of N100 million to the church on behalf of the Rainbow Coalition, his friends and associates.

World.title: NELFUND considers increase in ₦20,000 student upkeep
World.content:
…Sawyer says allowance under review, hints at possible changes

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) is considering an increase in its ₦20,000 monthly upkeep allowance for students amid concerns that rising living costs have reduced its purchasing power.

The Managing Director of NELFUND, Akintunde Sawyer, disclosed this during an interview on TVC’s Beyond the Headlines, saying the allowance was under constant review.

Although he did not announce a new amount or timeline for any adjustment, Sawyer confirmed that the possibility of an increase was being considered.

“Are we considering it? Yes, of course. It’s under constant review,” he said.

The proposed review comes amid complaints by students that the current allowance is inadequate to meet the rising costs of feeding, transportation, accommodation and other basic needs.

Sawyer, however, said any increase would have to take into account the fund’s financial capacity and the need to sustain support for all eligible beneficiaries.

“What we need to do is plan it in such a way that it doesn’t put us in a situation where we can’t cater for the totality of the people that we need to cater for,” he said.

Beyond the proposed review, the NELFUND chief disclosed that President Bola Tinubu was considering an intervention to provide students with more substantial financial support to help them complete their academic programmes.

He did not provide details of the proposed intervention, including its scope, funding or implementation timeline.

“I know the President certainly is looking at intervening in a way that helps the students have more meaningful sustenance so that they can get through their courses,” Sawyer said.

He also hinted that changes could be introduced in the future, although he gave no definite commitment on when the review would be concluded.

“I suspect that if you watch this space, you’ll see some changes coming up in the future,” he added.

NELFUND’s proposed review comes as the Federal Government’s student loan scheme continues to expand, with millions of applications received from students seeking financial assistance for tertiary education.

According to figures provided by the fund, it has disbursed ₦180.5 billion in upkeep allowances since the scheme commenced in May 2024, while another ₦194.7 billion has been paid to tertiary institutions to cover tuition fees.

The combined disbursement of approximately ₦375.2 billion underscores the scale of the programme, which is intended to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education and help students remain in school.

The fund has also recorded more than 2.5 million applications and about 1.6 million loan transactions across 320 beneficiary institutions.

Despite the programme’s expansion, the adequacy of the monthly upkeep allowance remains a concern for beneficiaries who depend on it to meet their daily expenses.

For now, the ₦20,000 monthly allowance remains unchanged, pending any formal announcement by NELFUND or the Federal Government on a possible increase or additional intervention.

World.title: Atletico Madrid beat Getafe 3-0 to keep pressure on Barcelona, Real Madrid
World.content:
Atletico Madrid’s Spanish defender #22 Alejandro Grimaldo celebrates with teammates scoring his team’s third goal from the penalty spot during the Spanish league football match between Getafe CF and Club Atletico de Madrid at Coliseum Stadium in Getafe on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP)

Atletico Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe in La Liga on Sunday.

Diego Simeone’s side, third, are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off second-place Real Madrid, who both won earlier this weekend.

Alex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julian Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Alex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sorloth.

“I think the team had a very good, serious game, in defence and attack,” Atletico playmaker Baena told Movistar.

“We are focused on our own work, not looking at what Barcelona and Madrid are doing, and that suits us best.”

The Rojiblancos moved ahead after 10 minutes, with Alvarez teeing up Baena on the edge of the box to drill home low and hard at the near post.

Getafe goalkeeper David Soria saved well from Alvarez and David Hancko but was at fault for Atletico’s second goal.

Soria missed his punch from Alvarez’s corner and United States international Cardoso turned home with his knee from point-blank range.

Baena smashed over a fine chance for the third after Pablo Barrios played him in behind.

Soria denied Baena in the second half and Lee Kang-in fired over as Atletico continued to control the game and defended solidly to keep Getafe, 17th, at bay.

Atletico substitute Sorloth should have scored with a few minutes remaining but powered an effort straight at Soria.

The Norwegian striker won a penalty when Djene pushed him over as he ran through on goal and Grimaldo dispatched it with the minimum of fuss to close things ou

World.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
World.content:
Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz poses with the trophy after victory against Germany’s Alexander Zverev during the final of the ATP Finals tennis tournament, in Turin on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP)

Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.

After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament.

Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

With his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998.

“It’s been an amazing week. I couldn’t finish the week in a better way, so I’m really proud,” Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year.

“I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I’m playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I’ve been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me,” he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament.

A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles.

But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals.

He lost in the season-ender’s final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one.

Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings.

– Topsy-turvy –

The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three.

The first set of Alcaraz’s semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week.

Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold.

Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand.

Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1.

Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native’s serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob.

A netted backhand by Zverev — his 19th unforced error of the match — on Alcaraz’s first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame.

Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance.

The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points.

But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve.

The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand.

World.title: Tinubu to Nigerians: I Guarantee You Improvement in Electricity Supply If Re-elected
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

•Mocks supporters of Makinde’s APM, says they have nowhere to go

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, yesterday in Ibadan, the Oyo State capital, assured Nigerians of improvement in power supply across the country if elected for a second term, and called on the people of the state and the South-west to sustain their support for the All Progressives Congress (APC) by voting massively for him and other candidates of the party in the 2027 general election.

Tinubu gave the assurance during the APC presidential campaign rally for the South-west, held at the historic Mapo Hall, where he said his administration was doing everything possible to ensure improved electricity.



The president mocked the supporters of the Allied People’s Movement (APM), the party under which Oyo State Governor, Mr. Seyi Makinde, is pursuing his 2027 presidential ambition, saying the party’s supporters have nowhere to go.

But in a swift reaction, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) described the APC presidential campaign rally as a disgraceful flop and a loud signal to President Tinubu and the APC that he has also been rejected in his home South-west zone.

Tinubu also revealed an agreement between the federal government and a Chinese firm to revive Leyland Motors, a former automobile manufacturing company that left Nigeria several years ago.



According to him, the proposed revival would help restore industrial activity, create jobs and renew hope for Nigerians, particularly young people.

“We have just signed an agreement with Yutong of China to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan,” Tinubu said.

“We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plants there.”

The president said his administration would continue to attract industries to the country, adding that he was committed to improving electricity supply.



“We will continue to bring industries. You will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Joseph Tegbe (Minister of Power) is working really hard with his team,” he said.

Tinubu urged Oyo residents and the South-west to remain with the APC, recalling their support for the party in the previous election.

“APC is our party. It’s your party. Is it clear? You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course,” he said.

He said government policies aimed to secure a better future for Nigerians, particularly younger generations, adding that education and agriculture were imperative for national development.



“For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for your children and our great-grandchildren, we must give them the right education and invest in agriculture,” Tinubu said.

The president called for the observance of a minute of silence in honour of those who lost their lives in a boat mishap that occurred in Bayelsa State on Friday.

Tinubu also announced that Vice President Kashim Shettima would proceed to Bayelsa State after the campaign rally to commiserate with the bereaved families and the people of the state.

Tinubu Mocks Supporters of Makinde’s APM, Says They Have Nowhere to Go

Tinubu also mocked Makinde’s APM, saying that the party’s supporters have nowhere to go.

However, he did not name the APM or Makinde.

“We heard there is a certain group/faction called the ‘palemo’ (pack up) group. Don’t mind them; they are only waiting in vain; there is nowhere they are going,” the president said.

The remark appeared to be a veiled reference to the APM, which has adopted Makinde as its presidential candidate ahead of the 2027 election.



Makinde had promised to reset Nigeria if elected president in 2027.

Earlier, in separate goodwill messages, the governor of Ekiti State, Mr. Biodun Oyebanji, on behalf of the 31 progressive governors, and the governors of Anambra and Osun states, urged Yoruba voters not to trade their votes.

Also, the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, said that splitting votes for different parties across different political offices in Oyo State would not benefit the party.

South-west Monarchs Hail Tinubu, Demand Constitutional Role by 2031

Meanwhile, traditional rulers across the South-west geopolitical zone have praised Tinubu’s administration’s interventions in infrastructure and security reforms while renewing calls for a defined constitutional role for royal fathers before 2031.

Speaking on behalf of South-west monarchs at a brief reception at Ibadan Airport shortly before the APC presidential campaign rally, the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, said the president’s three-and-a-half-year track record speaks for itself.



“If it had been possible for the President to contest as an independent candidate, you would get 95 per cent of the votes,” Olubadan said, adding that other candidates running on the APC platform were largely benefiting from the president’s goodwill.

“What he did is what is standing in for him. All other people that are contesting on the platform of APC are just riding on his back,” he said.

According to Ladoja, the monarchs gathered not to present new local demands, noting that the president had already granted Ibadan’s earlier request to create Ibadan State. Instead, the royal father attributed the zone’s enthusiasm directly to the president’s personal performance rather than party affiliation.



Oba Ladoja announced that traditional rulers from the region would formally present a charter of demands on January 17, centred on securing formal recognition in the 1999 Constitution.

“There is no role that has been assigned to the traditional rulers in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” the monarch told the president.

“So, we want you to look at it carefully, so that by the time we are finishing in 2031, we will have said ‘yes, our president has done it.’ We are watching very, very carefully.”

Oshiomhole Urges Oyo Residents to Reject Makinde’s ‘Reset Nigeria’

Speaking at the rally, former Edo State governor Senator Adams Oshiomhole, who attempted to address the crowd in Yoruba to connect with the people, urged them to reject what he described as Makinde’s attempts to reset Nigeria.

Oshiomhole challenged Makinde to explain what he intended to change about the policies and programmes of the Tinubu administration, particularly in education, infrastructure, and economic development.



Tinubu is giving loans to poor students in tertiary institutions. Is that what Governor Makinde wants to reset?” Oshiomhole asked.

Oshiomhole, who repeatedly challenged Makinde’s call for a reset, urged the governor to reconsider his position and align himself with the aspirations of the electorate ahead of the 2027 elections.

“The governor needs to reset his own mind before the election,” Oshiomhole said.

Makinde: Poor Attendance Confirms South-west Has Rejected Tinubu

Meanwhile, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has described the APC presidential campaign rally in Ibadan as a disgraceful flop and a loud signal to President Tinubu and the APC that he has also been rejected in his home South-west zone.

MDPCO said in a statement last night that it was not surprised that the people of Oyo State and, of course, the South-West largely shunned President Tinubu’s re-election rally, given their reputation for political intelligence, sophistry and independent-mindedness to make informed choices despite the propaganda, deceit and lies of the APC.



The Director of Strategic Communications of the campaign, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, said in a statement that ”The fact that the people of Oyo State who turned out in their millions to grace Seyi Makinde’s May 14, 2026 presidential declaration on the platform of the APM, spurned President Tinubu’s rally today, validates our position that Nigerians and particularly the South-west region prefer Makinde as a viable replacement for Tinubu to complete the remaining four years’ tenure of the region in the current zoning arrangement.”

MDCO stated that President Tinubu’s veiled attack on the APM was an indication that Tinubu had “become jittery and unable to stand Makinde’s towering acceptance, leading to the scanty attendance at the APC rally despite the huge financial resources deployed for mobilisation



”It was a pathetic sight as the deflated President Tinubu lost his bearings in the face of Engr. Makinde’s intimidating popularity, to the extent that Mr. President resorted to insults, mudslinging, incoherencies, repetitions and bogus promises.”

Ihediuwa further said that ”Burdened by failure and rejection, President Tinubu could not articulate any meaningful message to the people of Oyo State but ironically accepted an empty score card by saying “I will not be able to speak much to you. I just want to greet you”.



”Instead of presenting his stewardship in government, President Tinubu is making another list of fake promises, including the provision of electricity, the same promise he made three and a half years ago, apparently forgetting that he had asked Nigerians not to vote for him in 2027 if he fails to deliver,” he added.

World.title: Skystone Awards N53m Grants to 20 Nigerian SMEs
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Esther Oluku

Skystone Finance Company Limited has awarded grants totalling N53 million to 20 small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria as part of an initiative to support business growth and development.

The grant presentation, held in Lagos, followed a five-day SME boot camp organised by Skystone Finance in partnership with Capstone Advisory and Fate Foundation. The event also featured a gala and awards ceremony.

Speaking at the event, the Chief Executive Officer of Skystone Finance, Olasunkanmi Olabinjo, said the initiative was designed to address funding and capacity gaps affecting small businesses.

He said many SMEs faced challenges beyond access to finance, including limited technology, human resource capacity, business structures and corporate governance.

Olabinjo said the company introduced the programme to equip selected entrepreneurs with the knowledge and resources required to expand their businesses and develop into larger enterprises.

According to him, the 20 beneficiaries were selected from across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones and participated in an intensive business training programme designed and delivered by Skystone Finance and Fate Foundation.

He said the grants would be complemented by one year of business mentorship and human resource support to help the beneficiaries implement their growth plans.

Olabinjo described the initiative as the first grant cycle in the company’s nine-year history, adding that Skystone had previously supported businesses in strengthening their operations and accessing capital.

Also speaking, Skystone’s Head of Corporate Services, Oladoyin Elegbe, said the programme was part of the company’s ambition to expand its presence in the SME financing sector.

She said the organisers received more than 100 prequalified applications, with social media platforms, including TikTok and Instagram, used to publicise the programme and reach small business owners.

Elegbe said the 20 successful applicants were divided into two groups of 10 for the boot camp, which focused on improving participants’ business management and operational capabilities.

She said the company hoped to make the grant programme a regular initiative, potentially holding it once or twice a year.

One of the beneficiaries, Prince Kayode Oguntayo, founder of F&F Fruits and Veg, said his business received a N2.5 million grant, which he planned to reinvest in its operations.

Describing the training as intensive, Oguntayo said the sessions covered key business disciplines and provided practical knowledge that could support the growth of participating enterprises.

Under the grant allocation, the top three participants received N5 million each, while the bottom three received N1 million each. The remaining 14 beneficiaries received N2.5 million apiece.

World.title: Boosted by Customer‑driven Business Activities, 12 Banks Record N253tn Assets
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Kayode Tokede

Following growth in lending, transaction volumes and customer deposits, a total of 12 deposit money banks recorded N253 trillion total assets in nine months ended September 2026.

This represents about 7 per cent increase from N237.42 trillion reported in the corresponding period of 2025.

The banks are: United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA), Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc (GTCO), Access Holdings Plc, Zenith Bank Plc (FUGAZ), First Holdco Plc and Ecobank Transnational Incorporated.

Others are: FCMB Group Plc, Stanbic IBTC Holdings Plc, Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc, Jaiz Bank Plc, Wema Bank Plc, and Abbey Bank Plc.

Analysis of the banks unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, showed that Tier 2/3 banks are growing 10 times faster than the, Nigerian fintechs and mid-tier banks are outpacing the FUGAZ banks (First HoldCo, UBA, GTCO, Access Holdings, and Zenith Bank) with expectations of Ecobank that declared decline in total assets in the period under review.

Tier 2 banks in Nigeria are mid‑sized commercial banks that operate below Tier 1 institutions in terms of capital base, market share, and overall financial strength.

A breakdown of the results revealed that the 12 banks posted N180.11 trillion deposits from customers as of September 30, 2026, about nine per cent growth from N165.06 reported in the 2025 financial year.

Access Holdings led the chart as the largest financial institutions in terms of total assets and deposit from customers.

Access Holdings declared N52.6 trillion total assets during the period, representing an increase of 1.7 per cent when compared to N51.71 trillion reported in 2025.

The unaudited result and accounts revealed that customer deposits of Access Holdings moved to N36.85 trillion trillion as of September 2026, up by 6.6 per cent from N34.56 trillion in 2025, a major indicator that contributed to total assets.

The group also declared that loans and advances to customers increased by 7.4 per cent to N14.3 trillion while shareholders’ funds remained broadly stable at N4.5 trillion, compared with N4.5 trillion in 2025. The size of the balance sheet gives meaning to the strategic language the group has adopted.

Ecobank Transnational Incorporated in the period declared N47.92 trillion total assets, a decline of 3.5 per cent from N49.66 trillion reported in 2025. UBA recorded N34.96 trillion total assets, a 5.4 per cent growth from N33.17 trillion reported in 2025.

Zenith Bank declared N34.4 trillion total assets, a growth of 10.24 per cent from N31.18 trillion reported in 2025 while First Holdco posted N32.2 trillion total assets, a growth of 18.1 per cent from N27.25 trillion in 2025.

Zenith Bank in a statement said, “Our performance during the first nine months of 2026 reflects the increasing contribution of customer‑driven business activities across the Group. Growth in lending, transaction volumes and customer deposits continued to support the business during the period, while lower funding and credit costs contributed to profitability and improved earnings quality.

“We are seeing growing momentum as more customers continue to choose Zenith Bank as a trusted partner for their banking needs. This is translating into deeper customer relationships, greater business volumes and a more balanced earnings profile across the Group. Our focus is not only on growing the business, but on ensuring that growth translates into greater value for our customers, shareholders and the communities we serve. We believe the progress we have made positions us well to capture future opportunities while maintaining the financial strength and disciplined execution that have long defined the Zenith brand.”

Further analysis showed that GTCO recorded N18.37 trillion total assets, representing 3.45 per cent increase over the N17.76 trillion announced in 2025. Stanbic IBTC Holdings recorded 11.35 per cent increase in total assets to N9.6 trillion; FCMB Group reported 9.7 per cent growth in total assets to N8.3 trillion; Wema Bank declared 46.4 per cent appreciation in total assets to N7.43 trillion; Sterling Financial Holdings Company saw its total assets up by 30.4 per cent to N5.1 trillion; Jaiz Bank announced 31.6 per cent increase in total assets to N1.69 trillion and Abbey Bank declared127 per cent growth in total assets to N375.7 billion.

Commenting, Investment Banker & Stockbroker, Tajudeen Olayinka said, “The nine per cent growth in the combined total asset base of these 12 banks to N253 trillion is a positive indicator of balance-sheet expansion.

“However, there is a difference between growth in asset size and improvement in asset quality or earnings capacity. Growth appears to have been driven partly by increased holdings of investment securities, reflecting banks’ preference for government securities amid elevated interest rates,” he said.

He added that Tier 2 banks have shown massive increase in assets on improved deposits from customers.

On his part, the Managing Director, Globalview Capital Limited, Mr. Aruna Kebira, said, “For the banks, the balance sheet is growing, but slowly. You can also see that Access Holdings and Zenith Bank contributed most of this growth, which reflects their size and market share.”

World.title: Nasarawa Attracts $2.3bn Investments in Seven Years, Implements 21 Reforms
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Nasarawa State Government has has said that it attracted investments worth more than $2.3 billion over the past seven years, implemented 21 economic reforms and executed 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at approximately N93 billion as part of efforts to transform the state into one of Nigeria’s most competitive investment destinations.

The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this while outlining the economic transformation agenda of Governor Abdullahi Sule’s administration at the just concluded World Public Relations Forum.

Abdullahi, who described the achievements as the outcome of deliberate institutional reforms and sustained efforts to create an investor-friendly environment, said the state had prioritised building a credible economic foundation before embarking on aggressive investment promotion.

He explained that when he joined the state government seven years ago as Economic Adviser to the governor, his mandate was to develop a compelling investment proposition for Nasarawa and position it as an attractive destination for local and international investors.

According to him, the administration recognised from the outset that investment promotion could not succeed without first putting the necessary structures, policies and institutions in place.

He said, “The first lesson from that very daunting task was to realise that you cannot give what you don’t have. We could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. You cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build.”

Abdullahi explained that the administration subsequently developed the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, anchored on the vision of making the state one of Nigeria’s most competitive economies through accelerated growth and improved living conditions for its citizens.

He said the 21 reforms implemented by the government focused largely on improving the business environment, strengthening public financial management, digitising revenue administration and establishing institutions capable of sustaining economic reforms.

He added that the reforms were also designed to provide credible feedback channels between investors, citizens and government institutions, thereby strengthening transparency, accountability and confidence in the state’s investment climate.

The N93 billion PPP projects, he said, complemented the reforms, while the investments attracted across various sectors reflected growing confidence in the state’s economic prospects.

He listed agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commerce, manufacturing, agro-processing and education among the sectors that had benefited from the investment drive.

Beyond the economic achievements, Abdullahi challenged public relations practitioners and communication professionals to recognise the responsibility that comes with shaping public narratives, stressing that effective communication must be anchored on purpose, credibility and integrity.

He said communication professionals must constantly examine the intentions behind their messages, particularly whether their interventions were designed to build institutions and strengthen society or undermine them.

“Do I want to communicate to build or destroy? Once you have that conviction and a sense of purpose, it guides how you communicate your message,” he said.

He also emphasised the importance of reputation management, noting that credibility was not automatically acquired but deliberately developed through consistent actions and responsible conduct.

He urged young communication professionals to demonstrate courage, determination and a spirit of collaboration, arguing that groundbreaking ideas and achievements required considerable commitment to translate them into reality.

Meanwhile, the President of the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, Professor Justin Green, described the organisation’s decision to host its major international conference in Africa, particularly Nigeria, as a remarkable achievement.

Green said the successful hosting of the conference had surpassed expectations, despite initial doubts and discouragement from some quarters about the possibility of bringing the global gathering to the African continent.

He particularly commended the President of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), Dr Ike Neliaku, and members of the institute for the enormous commitment and organisational work that went into making the event successful.

According to him, preparations for the conference spanned two years and required extensive collaboration among stakeholders.

“It has been a huge journey for Global Alliance. When we first said we wanted to bring it to the African continent, we got knocked down. People didn’t think it would ever take place. I was told there was no way it would ever happen. But we made it happen,” he said.

Green described the gathering as the biggest, brightest and boldest conference ever organised by the Global Alliance, attributing its success to collective leadership, teamwork and international cooperation.

He stressed that the achievement was not the accomplishment of one individual but the product of shared responsibility and the contributions of several people and institutions.

World.title: WHY NIGERIANS MUST ASK FOR CREDIBLE ELECTIONS
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

How long will Nigerians continue to watch helplessly while political leaders treat them as though their voices and interests do not matter? Another election season is approaching, bringing with it fresh promises, political manifestos, campaign slogans and bags of propaganda. Yet, the average Nigerian continues to hope for a better tomorrow while struggling with insecurity, unemployment, economic hardship and declining living standards.

The question remains: who will rescue Nigeria from these persistent challenges? Perhaps the answer begins with the people themselves. The time to demand accountability, responsible leadership and electoral credibility is now, not after another disappointing political cycle.

However, while demanding free, fair and credible elections, Nigerians must understand that this is not a call for political violence. The recent slogan, “Rig and Die,” reportedly gaining attention in public discourse, raises serious concerns about the direction of political engagement in the country. Such expressions deserve careful reflection because political frustration should never become an excuse for threatening human lives.

We must embrace a paradigm shift in our political thinking. Disagreement is part of democracy, and every citizen has the right to defend their political choice. Nevertheless, political differences should not turn polling units into battlefields or election officials into targets of public anger.

It is important to remember that the people responsible for conducting elections at various polling units are human beings like everyone else. They have families, friends and loved ones waiting for them to return home safely after performing their national duties. While electoral officials must be held accountable for any proven misconduct, it is equally important not to assume that every electoral failure or unexpected result is necessarily the fault of polling-unit officials.

This is why voter education, political awareness and responsible civic participation must begin before election day. Citizens must understand the electoral process, know their rights, follow lawful procedures for reporting irregularities and use the appropriate channels to challenge electoral misconduct.

Beyond voting, citizens must also understand their responsibility in protecting the credibility of their votes. Political participation should not end at the ballot box; it must continue through lawful demands for transparency, accountability and respect for the people’s mandate.

The victory or defeat of a political candidate should never be worth the destruction of another person’s life. Democracy must be built on the strength of our convictions, not the violence of our reactions.

As another election season approaches, Nigerians must wake up to their civic responsibilities. We must demand credible elections, reject political intimidation, resist misinformation and refuse to become instruments of violence in the hands of desperate political interests.

The time to be informed is before election day. To be forewarned is to be forearmed. Vote wisely, protect your rights, respect human life and demand accountability through lawful means. Nigeria belongs to all of us, and its future must never be sacrificed on the altar of political ambition.

Idris Rufai,

idrisrufai744@gmail.com

World.title: 22 STATES AND THEIR PENSIONERS
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

States should perform promptly their obligations to pensioners

Following the passage of a motion of urgent national importance last week, the House of Representatives called on the federal government to prevail on 22 state governments to pay outstanding pension arrears to retired civil servants. This came on the heels of a recent disclosure by the National Pension Commission (Pencom) Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran, that only 14 of Nigeria’s 36 states are paying pensions on a regular basis. The member representing Apapa federal constituency of Lagos State, Adesola Adebayo had expressed concern that thousands of pensioners were dying of hunger and poverty because of unpaid retirement benefits after 30 to 35 years of faithful service to their fatherland.

Even though it is not a discretionary obligation, a PenCom publication noted last August that states implementing and remitting contributory pension included Edo, Lagos, Kaduna, Ogun, Osun, Ekiti, Ondo, Delta, and Anambra. Another report also stated that as of October 2026, only eight states had cleared inherited pension liabilities, with six others paying over 80 per cent. Yet Section 210 of the 1999 Constitution guarantees pension and gratuity entitlements for persons who have served in the public service of a state, while Section 173 provides similar protection for federal public servants.

Ironically, one major attraction in public service, despite its poor remuneration package, is the benefit of receiving pension after retirement. But as we have repeatedly stated, such a prospect has become problematic and uncertain over the years. The failure of government to meet the pension expectation of retirees ends up shattering the plans of many. And this has worsened the woes of pensioners, particularly those without other sources of income. In the prevailing economic circumstances, many are driven to the wall. There have been several unpleasant stories about how many of them die without dignity while on the queue for what is ordinarily their entitlement.



Meanwhile, as it is often pointed out, there are issues that are yet to be resolved regarding pension. Complications in meeting up with some obligations had arisen fundamentally with the failure to link those in the old scheme with those in the new scheme. It was in a bid to address this that the Pension Reforms Act of 2004 was enacted. The act covers both public and private sector employees. The Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) was introduced to replace the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS). Under the new regime, both the government/companies and the workers themselves are to save a given amount of their earnings towards building an accumulated funds reserve which they could fall back on after retirement.

But even after it seems to have been done, the federal and many state governments have serially failed in remitting deducted sums from workers’ salaries to the Pension Fund Administrators. The result is that neither government contribution nor workers’ deducted sums are credited to the accounts of the workers with the Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs). The problem is more prevalent in the private sector where many companies do not remit their counterpart deductions to the PFAs as required by the Pension Act.

The provisions of the act had demanded that the government issues bonds in favour of retired workers, which will be redeemed to the PFAs who will credit same to the accounts of the individual staff. Therefore, the non-remittance of the deductions of staff is a clear breach of the provisions of the Pension Reforms Act, and that perhaps explains why pension liabilities run into hundreds of billions of naira. While we urge the federal and state governments to keep faith with their obligations to pensioners, we also hail the new Presidential Pension Security Initiative, seeking to lift thousands of vulnerable retirees struggling with rising costs of living. No pensioner should die in need

World.title: Tinubu’s Agricultural Reset: ₦1.5 Trillion BoA Recapitalisation, ₦450 Billion Committed, 500,000 Farmers Reached
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Gloria Adebajo-Fraser

Nigeria’s food security ambitions depend on turning its vast agricultural resources into productive farms, dependable harvests and affordable food. President Bola Tinubu’s administration is committing substantial financing to that task, combining a N1.5 trillion Bank of Agriculture recapitalisation with N450 billion in programmes supporting production and commodity markets.



In a statement issued on Sunday, November 22, 2026, Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, said interventions through the bank had reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers, with particular attention to Northern Nigeria.

The measures bring together credit, improved inputs, mechanisation, irrigation, storage and market access—essential foundations for strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to feed its people.



The approach reflects the President’s commitment to domestic production:

“We will continue to drive local production and ensure that we produce what we eat and use locally.” — President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, in remarks delivered on his behalf by Vice President Kashim Shettima at the public presentation of Chief Olusegun Osoba’s My Life in the Public Eye, Lagos, July 13, 2024.

N250 BILLION SMALLHOLDER FUND

According to Alake’s statement, the N250 billion Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund finances farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies coordinating registration, input distribution, extension services and market connections.

The programme has reached over 500,000 smallholders across 16 states, including more than 70,000 women. Approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds have been distributed.

Its wider target is to reach two million farmers and distribute more than 10 million bags of fertiliser.

Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi were identified among states receiving attention. The council emphasised the significance of these interventions in Northern Nigeria, where agriculture remains a major source of livelihood and economic activity.

N200 BILLION TO SUPPORT COMMODITY MARKETS

The second component of the N450 billion commitment is the Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme, valued at N200 billion.

Under this initiative, the Bank of Agriculture has procured approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava, the statement said.

The programme is designed to strengthen commodity markets and protect farmers against distress sales. It addresses the pressure producers face when immediate financial needs or inadequate storage force them to sell cheaply after harvest.

Connecting production support with dependable market opportunities can help farmers recover their investment and prepare for subsequent planting seasons.

ONION FINANCING AND STORAGE

The bank has developed an Onion Financing Programme with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria, representing over 11,800 onion farmers.

The scheme provides for improved seeds and fertiliser, commodity purchase financing for processors, and the development of storage and solar-powered cooling facilities to reduce post-harvest losses.

Cooperatives will contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, while the bank finances the remaining 70 per cent.

According to the council, this arrangement will strengthen production, improve farmers’ incomes and expand market access, particularly in Northern Nigeria.

N1.5 TRILLION TO EXPAND AGRICULTURAL LENDING

The approved recapitalisation is intended to strengthen the Bank of Agriculture’s capacity to provide affordable and accessible funding to farmers, cooperatives, processors, aggregators and other agricultural businesses.

Alake’s statement described the measure as a major step towards fulfilling the President’s campaign commitment to strengthen agricultural financing.

A better-capitalised bank would be positioned to support larger investments, expand services to underserved farming communities and mobilise additional resources for domestic production.

The council also linked the administration’s agricultural agenda to support for cultivation across 500,000 hectares, reinforcing the connection between institutional financing and expanded productive activity.

NIGERIA’S LAND RESOURCES

Nigeria has approximately 70.8 million hectares of agricultural land, including about 34 million hectares of arable land, according to the Federal Ministry of Agriculture’s National Agri-Food Systems Investment Plan, citing the Food and Agriculture Organization.

These resources provide a substantial foundation for increased cultivation, rural employment and agro-processing. Developing that potential requires investment in farmers, water management, equipment, storage and transport.

The importance of harnessing these agricultural resources is also explored in Nigeria’s Great Reset: Rebuilding today for a prosperous tomorrow, which examines agriculture’s contribution to economic renewal and national food security.

SPIN: STRENGTHENING IRRIGATION

Complementing agricultural financing is the $500 million World Bank-assisted Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria project, known as SPIN.

Approved in September 2024, it targets improved irrigation and drainage services across 40,000 hectares. Up to 950,000 people, including farmers, households and livestock breeders, are expected to benefit from more reliable water services and increased agricultural productivity. The project also supports dam safety and water management.

Reliable irrigation supports cultivation beyond seasonal rainfall, giving farmers greater confidence to plan production and strengthening resilience to drought.

DRY-SEASON FARMING, GINGER AND WOMEN

The PCC statement said the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria on a dry-season financing pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.

This includes 120,000 hectares of wheat and another 300,000 hectares for rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava and soybeans.

The Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds. More than 9,000 bags have been recovered for multiplication, with expansion planned across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.

At least 50,000 women are also being targeted through insured cooperative production financing at nine per cent, in partnership with the Federal Ministries of Women Affairs and Agriculture.

MECHANISATION AND SOLAR SUPPORT

Under the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme, 1,571 tractors have been deployed across 23 states, according to the council.

They are expected to serve 1.2 million hectares through qualified Mechanisation Service Providers.

Separately, a N385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme provides for 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps, targeting 500,000 farming families. Youth participation and commercial poultry production feature among other interventions.

These programmes reflect a wider development principle: productive agriculture sustains livelihoods, supplies industry and supports national stability.

“If agriculture fails, everything else will fail.” — Professor M. S. Swaminathan, agricultural scientist and father of India’s Green Revolution.

His warning places agricultural investment in its proper national context. Financing farmers, improving irrigation and protecting harvests strengthen the foundations on which food security and economic resilience depend.

NATIONAL PATRIOTS POSITION

National Patriots commends the administration’s substantial commitments to domestic production and rural livelihoods.

“Food security begins with empowering those who feed the nation. President Tinubu’s interventions recognise that farmers need affordable finance, reliable inputs, modern equipment and dependable markets. Stronger lending, irrigation and storage can turn Nigeria’s enormous agricultural resources into productive opportunities, better incomes and affordable food for families.” — National Patriots

Nigeria’s agricultural strength must be felt in the farmer’s income, the trader’s supply and the family’s food basket. The financing commitments and production programmes outlined by the administration provide a substantial platform for that progress including a strong case for continuity and re-election.

National Patriots urges sustained delivery across farming communities so that investment becomes harvest, harvest becomes prosperity, and food security becomes a dependable foundation of national strength.

•Princess Gloria Adebajo-Fraser, MFR, MBA, MIoD, FIPMD

President, National Patriots

Member, APC-PCC Strategic Communications Committee 2027

World.title: TINUBU AND THE PRESIDENCY
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Has he fixed the problems he was elected to solve? asks TONY ELUEMUNOR

Why this “giantification” and “colossalization” of a minuscule and miniature presidency? Instead of listing President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s achievements and the campaign promises he has fulfilled, and allow the citizens to rate him based on his verifiable record, some of his incensed (yes, as in furious) supporters are making him out to be superhuman.

The national insecurity of terrorism and kidnapping was Nigeria’s biggest challenge in 2023 when Tinubu became President. Almost four years later on Friday November 16, 2026, Mr. Dele Alake, Spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress – Presidential Campaign Council, said that over 15, 000 terrorists have been killed and 130,000 others have surrendered in three years, as though the terrorists did not kill our gallant soldiers and policemen and sundry civilians they kidnapped. Instead of saying how many states or Local Government Areas have been liberated from terrorists, he announced a NEW five-year plan to wipe out terrorism, that would end with Tinubu’s second tenure. But in a September 30, 2023 speech at the Nigerian Defence Academy passing-out parade Tinubu vowed to eliminate terrorism, criminality and poverty – because military action must be paired with social measures.

Claims apart, has kidnapping rate been reduced if not eliminated – as Tinubu had promised? Unfortunately, Security monitors, SBM intelligence reports cited by the BBC and International Centre for Investigative Reporting (ICIR) said that kidnapping upped from 3,620 incidents in 2023 to 7,825 people kidnapped in 1,713 incidents between July 2025 and June 2026 – in just a year. 20,115 people were snatched across the country between July 2023 and June 2026 – a 66% increase in the last 12 months. Yearly ransom payments rose more than seven-fold from N1.05 billion in 2023/2024 to N7.78 billion in 2025/2026 when group kidnappings became the new method.

Election is around and Team-Tinubu should be reelected or rejected based on his national security and economic records as happened to Goodluck Jonathan, against Muhammadu Buhari, and the Peoples Democratic Party lost power to All Progressives Congress.

In how many Local Government Areas or states have Tinubu erased terrorists and normalized citizens’ lives. Promises are fine but an egg can’t go on being good forever; it must either hatch or go bad.

Second, what has been the result of Tinubu’s economic salvation efforts in 2026, three years plus a few months (almost a full tenure) in office and power – and the appraisal of his administration (it is also called an election) is less than 60 days away? Instead of stout results and achievements we are being given more promises, promises, promises.

Sad to say, even Tinubu’s greatest supporters still grant that multi-faceted hunger still stalks the land in 2026 and worse still, they accept that his removal of petrol subsidy worsened the peoples’ sufferings. Still, they stoutly state that Tinubu had to take harsh measures to stop the economy from collapsing but advance no timelines for succour to come. Surprisingly, though they justify the President’s petrol subsidy removal because importers were hoodwinking Nigeria through over-invoicing and other sundry acts of corruption, none of them has wondered why Tinubu did not even bother to straighten the crooked petrol subsidy ways and punish the criminals. Also, they have over-looked the option open to Tinubu to make Nigeria’s refineries productive and corrupt-free. Worst of all, the petrol that comes into Nigeria now has been said to originate, not directly from any identifiable country or refineries but is blended offshore near Malta.

On July 22, 2024, the Cable online newspaper published this: “The businessman, Aliko Dangote, said at the House of Representatives that “Some of the NNPC people and some traders have opened a blending plant somewhere off Malta. The diesel produced locally at 650 parts per million (ppm) and 700 ppm is of better quality than imported fuel. Many vehicle issues can be traced back to the “substandard” imported fuel.

The House of Representatives joint committee on petroleum resources (downstream and midstream) had launched a probe into claims that local refineries, including the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, produced inferior products and investigating the allegations that the international oil companies (IOCs) in Nigeria are frustrating the survival of the Dangote refinery. Actually, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) and Dangote refinery had been embroiled in a dispute and on July 18, Farouk Ahmed, NMDPRA’s chief executive officer had said local refineries, including the Dangote refinery, were producing inferior products compared to the ones imported. The oil regulator also accused Dangote of monopoly”.

PUNCH newspaper reported on July 26, 2024 that Nigeria actually imported fuel from Malta; $59.98m in 2014, $117.01m in 2015 and $13.32 in 2016 and the importations stopped from 2017 to 2022 resumed in 2023 with a “geometric leap in 2023 when the country imported fuel worth $2.08bn”. Jonathan was President in 2013 when the Malta magic started but stopped for some six years that fell under Buhari but resumed and increased exponentially in 2023. Please draw your conclusions!

So, how did the poor petrol quality issue end? According to the Cable, “Heineken Lokpobiri, minister of state petroleum resources (oil), intervened in the ‘ongoing issues’ after having a meeting with Aliko Dangote, chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of Dangote Group and Farouk Ahmed, CEO of Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). Gbenga Komolafe, CEO of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), and Mele Kyari, group CEO of the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) Limited were also at the meeting”. That was the last Nigeria heard about the drastic disclosures. Nobody was punished…the truth didn’t emerge, despite the lawmakers stand in July 2024 that product test results would be publicized.

The Cable online explained: “An oil blending plant has no refining capability but can be used to blend re-refined oil (a used motor oil that has been treated to remove dirt, fuel, and water) with additives to create finished lubricant products”. A real expert in the field, Isoil Impianti which developed from Isothermic Swiss which Carlo Blumer and Pierluigi Guazzoni founded in 1958 holds that:

“Traders ship intermediate petroleum products and off-spec fuels to Malta from major refining hubs. Common inputs include straight-run gasoline, reformate, heavy naphtha (which make up roughly 35% of shipments into the area), and high-sulfur or off-spec distillates. (The) blending is purely mechanical. Components are mixed either inside onshore tank terminals (such as the facilities at Marsaxlokk) or directly at sea through ship-to-ship (STS) transfers, where tankers pump different grades of hydrocarbons into a single receiving vessel.

• Adjusting fuel specifications. Operators use precise flow meters and chemical additives (such as oxygenates, octane boosters, or ethanol) to alter the properties of the base liquid. By adjusting the ratios, blenders control key metrics like the octane rating, vapor pressure, and sulfur content.

Different regions enforce different environmental and engine standards. While European markets require ultra-low sulfur and strict emissions compliance, traders in Malta frequently blend lower-cost components like naphtha into gasoline to create “African Spec” fuel. This lower-grade blend meets the more lenient import thresholds of West African markets—such as Nigeria—before being loaded onto vessels for export”.

This serious allegation should have bothered the National Assembly and the law authorities and President Tinubu for two reasons; corruption as Nigerians pay high petrol prices for low quality petrol. Second, low quality petrol destroys engines. Now, who knows which petrol stations sell Sulphur-saturated Malta-blended petrol, though Nigeria’s Bonny Light is of the “sweet” Sulphur – free variant? Nobody! And how much do importers buy the sulphuric blend they sell to us at premium price? That Malta-blend controversy has been swept under the carpet. Corruption was a major problem Tinubu was elected to combat in 2023…but the Malta-blend petrol controversy outcome is not the way to end corruption.

Simply because America’s President Roosevelt championed and introduced large-scale projects to stimulate nation-wide employment after the Great Depression of the 1930s, some applaud Tinubu as Nigeria’s Roosevelt because he started the Coastal Road and the Apapa Port rehabilitation and upgrade. By the way, the popular Roosevelt served more than two terms of four years; he won four presidential elections, serving 12 years from 1933 – 1945 when he died in office, so some people may be campaigning for Tinubu’s life-presidency. Who will tell such people that they are only advertising their ignorance of developmental issues? First, instead of two mega projects costing colossal sums, smaller but numerous labour-intensive ones dotted across the federation would better spread employment and income nationally. David Umahi, minister of works said on Arise TV, a standard carriageway on the 750-Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway costs $5.5 million or N7, 468, 489, 105.00 (N7.4 billion) per kilometer which equals N5.55 trillion for the entire road. If that contract was awarded in 2025, it would have swallowed 10% of the budgeted N54.99 trillion. But the Federal Government under President Bola Tinubu first announced the award of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway contract to Hitech Construction Company Ltd in September 2023, before the Federal Executive Council (FEC) approval of the first phase in early 2024. Umahi defended the contract award to Hitech Construction through direct procurement rather than open competitive bidding, saying it broke no law. He didn’t call it a noble transparency example, though.

That quantum of fund would have been better spent in constructing or repairing both urban and rural roads in the 36 states plus Abuja FCT and the ripple effects of pumping that gargantuan amount into the economy would spread nationally. Earmark that money to repair two roads in each state plus Abuja and that would have sent in N743.11 billion into each state.

As 25 states had 2025 budgets less than N743.11 billion, starting with Kano’s N719.7bn to the least, Yobe’s N320, each state should have been able to construct or repair from five to 10 roads with N74311 billion and the Federal Government could even have controlled the contract rollout and the payment. So, the money being poured into the Coastal Road would have been able to fund up to 370 road repairs if not constructions across the country at 10 roads multiplied by 37. As the money would never have been released at once, the projects across the country would have been gradual but continuous. And it would have spread job creation voluminously and evenly especially if labour-intensive projects as manual construction of gutters were focused on in the rural roads.

It is unfortunate that because Chief James Onanefe Ibori, 1999 – 2007 Delta State Governor, gave little attention to bull-horn governance, many don’t know that he also jumpstarted his state’s economy. He didn’t publicize his projects maximally (read; inducing journalists to report them and also paying to be given newspaper awards) and so far not a single book has been written about the trails he blazed. To fight unemployment at the local level, he started the walling of primary and secondary schools across Delta state on assumption of office. Such contracts went to local companies and they employed local labour and thus money seeped into the remote villages as well as the cities. The contractors requisitioned cement, iron rods, planks and other materials from the villages while the labourers bought sundry necessities and victuals and kept transporters and sectorial operators busy. That was the first money that reached Delta state grassroots as dividends of democracy.

PS, I deliberately didn’t write the promised “Wrong, Magnus Onyibe: Roosevelt’s Subsidy Ended USA’s Great Depression (2)” because nobody disputed any of my theses. If any antithesis appears, I will revisit that topic.

Eluemunor, a Ford Foundation scholar and 1991 Fellow of the Nieman Foundation for Journalism at Harvard University (where he focused on Development and Population studies), is an authority on the Nigerian Presidency.

World.title: Rassie sets his sights on France with bold social media move
World.content:
Rassie has followed the France rugby team on X. Images via X

He may not be able to set foot in the stadium on match day, or give his opponents a stare-down during a training session, but Rassie Erasmus is still laser-focused on the Springboks’ next opponents – France.

South Africa will play their final test at Twickenham next weekend in the inaugural Nations Championship tournament.

RASSIE FOLLOWS FRANCE ON X

Hours after SA’s 20-17 defeat to Ireland, and subsequent advancement to the Nations Championship finals, Springbok coach clicked “follow” on the official X account for the French rugby team.



The countries will clash again – two weeks after playing in Paris – as the Northern and Southern Hemisphere contenders.

The match will take place at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, England, on Sunday, 29 November.

As Rassie has been sanctioned by World Rugby over comments questioning the efficiency of match officials, he will be watching from the sidelines, and not the coaches’ box.

Rassie is prohibited from entering the stadium on match day, communicating with players or coaching staff, issuing instructions, influencing tactical decisions or performing match-day media duties.

However, he can continue to perform his general head coaching duties in the build-up to match day, provided he does not breach the conditions of his suspension.

He is likely to be formulating his master plan, which could possibly rely on monitoring France’s social media activity for new information.



HOW TO WATCH SPRINGBOKS FINAL TEST MATCH

South Africa’s face-off against France in the Nations Championships will be broadcast on Sunday, 29 November at 18:40 SA time.

The match will be broadcast on DStv’s SuperSport Rugby channels on the premium package, open to all DStv subscribers under its OpenTime promotion, which runs from 25 November to 25 December.

This means that irrespective of package, subscribers will have access to every live channel at no extra cost.

World.title: Former Pirates superstar says Mofokeng is always five steps ahead
World.content:
The former Orlando Pirates and Bafana Bafana ace has been particularly impressed by the way Relebohile Mofokeng reads matches and anticipates situations before they develop.

The 22-year-old has enjoyed a productive start to the 2026/27 campaign. He has delivered 10 goals and four assists in 20 appearances for club and country.

RELEBOHILE MOFOKENG FLYING IN EUROPE

His move to Belgian side Royale Union Saint-Gilloise has also provided another opportunity to test himself outside South Africa after establishing his reputation at Orlando Pirates.



Modise believes the midfielder’s understanding of the game is what separates him from many other players.

Speaking on the CARWASH podcast, the former Bafana international suggested that Mofokeng still has another level to reach.

“He is a different player. If South Africans think they have seen the best of Rele, they haven’t,” Modise said.



“I honestly believe that. You can see that he is five steps ahead in everything that he does. You can see his movements. It’s amazing to see.”

The assessment goes beyond his technical ability. Modise is particularly impressed by the youngster’s movement and his ability to influence matches without necessarily being involved in every attacking action.

Mofokeng initially attracted attention as an attacking midfielder, but his development has shown that he can contribute in different areas of the pitch.



Modise believes there is no need to place unnecessary restrictions on his game. “So we are not saying we need to protect Rele anymore; we need to let Rele fly! Rele is football,” he added.

BRIGHTON MHLONGO HIGHLIGHTS ANOTHER IMPORTANT FACTOR

Former Pirates goalkeeper Brighton Mhlongo has also praised the youngster, although his attention was directed towards the mentality that has helped him reach this level.

For Mhlongo, the support Mofokeng received from his family during his development deserves recognition.



He believes the player’s willingness to learn and remain grounded could become just as important as his footballing qualities.

“Credit must go to his parents for supporting him and being there for him as a child, not as a superstar. What we are seeing is someone who is enjoying his football and someone who is willing to learn,” he said.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs prepare to promote two new youngsters
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs duo Neo Bohloko and Steven Mendes have emerged as candidates for promotion, with the club’s technical team monitoring their progress under reserve coach Vela Khumalo.

The possibility of integrating the pair into the first team comes during a season in which Chiefs’ reserve side has established itself at the top of the DDC standings.

BOHLOKO LEADS KAIZER CHIEFS’ GOALSCORING CHARGE

Bohloko has scored 11 goals in nine appearances, including a penalty in Chiefs’ 2-1 victory over Milford FC.



His scoring record has made him one of the leading attacking performers in the competition.

The 18-year-old Mendes has also contributed to the team’s attacking output. The attacking midfielder previously won the Golden Boot at the COSAFA Under-20 Championship with Amajita.

He has continued his involvement in the final third at club level, providing assists and scoring goals for Khumalo’s side.

According to a report by KickOff, Chiefs are considering gradually introducing both players to senior training, with possible first-team opportunities towards the end of the season.

A source told the publication:

“The boys have shown that they are simply outgrowing the reserve level. The technical team is very impressed with their maturity and consistency.



“The plan being discussed is to gradually integrate them into first-team training and potentially give them their senior debuts maybe at the end of the season.”

AMAKHOSI RESERVE SIDE SETS THE PACE

Under Khumalo, Chiefs had won their opening nine DDC matches, collecting 27 points to occupy first position in the standings.

That run included the 2-1 victory over Milford, in which Bohloko converted from the penalty spot.

Mendes’ international achievements have also added to his profile. His Golden Boot at the COSAFA U20 Championship came while representing South Africa’s junior national team.

HAVE YOU SEEN ANY OF THEM IN ACTION?
