World.title: Former player warns of a dangerous future for Kaizer Chiefs winger
World.content:
The 21-year-old Kaizer Chiefs attacker has found himself in an uncomfortable situation at Naturena. He failed to return to training following the recent international break.

His absence also meant missing Amakhosi’s preparations in Polokwane ahead of their Carling Knockout semi-final against Mamelodi Sundowns.

KAIZER CHIEFS STAR FAIZ ABRAHAMS GOES AWOL

Abrahams joined Amakhosi on a season-long loan from Stellenbosch FC in August, having previously played for Cape Town Spurs.



His situation has attracted attention, particularly following reports that he is considering walking away from professional football altogether.

Khanye believes the youngster needs to understand the significance of the opportunity he has been given.

The former Chiefs attacker knows what it means to represent one of the country’s biggest football institutions. He also knows how quickly things can change when a player’s conduct becomes an issue.

“For a boy of his age to be given a chance to play for an institution as massive as Kaizer Chiefs and decide to misuse it like he is doing currently, he must be from a very wealthy family,” says Khanye, in conversation with KickOff.

“Do you know how many players across South Africa would give everything just to train at Naturena for one day? When you get to Chiefs, you have arrived at the biggest stage in local football, yet he is treating it like it is nothing.”

Khanye’s concern is not only about the current situation but also how other clubs might view Abrahams when he eventually looks for another opportunity.



A reputation can be difficult to rebuild in professional football, especially when a young player is still trying to establish himself.

THE WARNING FROM JUNIOR KHANYE’S OWN EXPERIENCE

Khanye’s comments carry an additional dimension because his own career at Chiefs was affected by off-field controversies.

He believes Abrahams could be making a decision that becomes difficult to reverse once the immediate emotions surrounding his situation have passed.

“What the boy is doing right now is going to haunt him for the rest of his life,” Khanye added.

“Knowing South African teams, they will always judge him on this even if he is done serving his sentence. To everyone, he will always appear as a Bad Boy from now on.

“Chiefs are very professional. Where is Dumisani Zuma? We were also favourites of Bra K [Kaizer Motaung] and Bobby Motaung, but nevertheless we were released because of our bad behavior, even though we were from the club’s development.

Khanye concluded to say Abrahams doesn’t know what he is doing. He may end up in the bush.

World.title: Former Pirates and Sundowns star says footballers need more than money
World.content:
Formerly a defender/midfielder for Orlando Pirates and Mamelodi Sundowns, Mhlongo feels the proposed pension fund for footballers is overdue but not enough. He is calling for a more serious issue.

For Mhlongo, the pressures experienced by players during their careers deserve equal attention, with Faiz Abrahams being the latest case.

BENSON MHLONGO CALLS FOR PYSCHOLOGISTS

Footballers are often expected to perform at the highest level while dealing with personal responsibilities that extend well beyond their professional commitments.



Some become the main providers for their families before they have developed the experience needed to manage the demands that come with financial responsibility.

Mhlongo believes clubs and football authorities should recognise that reality rather than treating players purely as sporting assets.

“That’s not even a question, we must have (psychologists), we’re dealing with human beings here. Human beings from different backgrounds, some of them are carrying huge responsibilities that are overwhelming and we’re not talking about people who are from the university,” Mhlongo told Kick Off.

His argument is that a player’s age does not necessarily reflect their ability to deal with the pressures of professional football.

Many young players enter the game having spent most of their childhood concentrating on training, matches and developing their abilities.

Suddenly, a professional contract can change their circumstances and those of the people around them.



The responsibility of supporting an entire family can become overwhelming, particularly when a young footballer is still learning how to navigate life outside the game.

Mhlongo believes this is where psychologists can make a meaningful difference.

Rather than waiting until a player experiences serious difficulties, clubs should have professionals who can help them understand and manage their challenges.

The former Cape Town Spurs assistant coach also highlighted the difference between entering a profession later in life and becoming financially responsible while still young.

“Where you start your career at the age of 28 or 30 and you are knowledgeable. We’re talking about young boys, who, the only thing they have been focusing on is playing football and when they become bread-winners at a young age there is a lot they encounter in family dynamics,” Mhlongo continued.

“So we need such people to help how to navigate around our challenges,” the Bafana Bafana legend added.

World.title: Sundowns coach says a different Chiefs player was the real Man of the Match
World.content:
Miguel Cardoso believes Mamelodi Sundowns had enough opportunities to change the outcome against Kaizer Chiefs, but their failure to take them proved costly in the Carling Knockout semi-final.

The Portuguese coach was particularly unhappy with the way his team handled possession in dangerous areas, arguing that unnecessary mistakes allowed Amakhosi to exploit spaces during transitions.

CARLING KNOCKOUT: MAMELODI SUNDOWNS 1-2 KAIZER CHIEFS

Kaizer Chiefs eventually secured a 2-1 extra-time victory at Loftus Versfeld, with Elias Mokwana playing a decisive role after coming off the bench.



But while Mfundo Vilakazi received the Man of the Match award, Cardoso had another player in mind.

The Sundowns coach singled out Brandon Petersen, whose performance between the posts helped Chiefs survive several difficult moments during the encounter.

“Just score our moments, I hope the fans at home understand that today the man of the match is Petersen, a goalkeeper today that showed himself in a level that we have…he is a wonderful goalkeeper but today he was extraordinary,” Cardoso told SuperSport.



The Carling Knockout award is determined through fan voting, meaning Cardoso’s preferred choice did not necessarily reflect the outcome of the supporters’ selection.

Petersen’s contribution was particularly important because Chiefs had to withstand pressure from a Sundowns side that struggled to turn its possession into goals.

Cardoso, however, felt the result was more about his team’s mistakes than anything else.



WHY MIGUEL CARDOSO BELIEVES SUNDOWNS LOST

The former Sporting CP coach pointed to the midfield as an area where Sundowns repeatedly gave away possession.

He believes those errors allowed Chiefs to attack quickly, something that played into Da Cruz’s tactical approach.

“That’s the story of this match, I told before details will define it, we didn’t score our moments, they profited two mistakes from us, we made a few of those mistakes wrong passes in the middle, allowing transitions and that’s what their game, it’s the game they play.



“The intention is to use the mistakes to profit from spaces, you need to be accurate, you cannot make those mistakes it’s so clear, the boys tried, but the story of the game is definition, definition, definition.”

Sundowns will now have to put the cup disappointment behind them as they return to Betway Premiership action. Cardoso’s immediate task is to get his players ready for their next league assignment against Kruger United.

With another trophy opportunity gone, the pressure will be on the Brazilians to respond positively in the league.

World.title: Tatjana Smith claps back at ‘running away’ criticism
World.content:
Tatjana Schoenmaker has reflected on representing South Africa as a professional swimmer. Images via IG

Tatjana Smith has responded to critics who’ve accused her of “running away” after she announced her decision to switch sporting nationalities from South Africa to the Netherlands.

Earlier this month, the Olympic swimmer revealed that she would be representing the European country, to which she has dual citizenship.

This follows her sharing her grievances with Swimming South Africa (SSA).



TATJANA SMITH RESPONDS TO CRITICISM OF SPORTING NATIONALITY

In a social media post, Tatjana Smith reflected on representing South Africa as a professional swimmer. She also responded to her critics who questioned her new allegiance to the Netherlands, of which she holds dual citizenship.

Posting a montage of her career highlights, Tatjana shared: “11 years being part of Team SA.

One flag. Countless sacrifices. Four Olympic medals. World Championship medals. Commonwealth medals. African Championship medals.



“Years of dedication, commitment and pride in wearing the green and gold”

She continued: “Giving up when things get difficult doesn’t produce a journey like this. And running away when things get tough? I think 11 years tells a different story”.

Tatjana – whose gold and silver Olympic medals will remain SA accolades – added: “Forever grateful for the privilege of representing South Africa”.



‘I CAN ALREADY FEEL THE DIFFERENCE’

In an interview with SwimSwam earlier this month, Tatjana Smith set the record straight on why she chose to switch sporting nationalities.

The 29-year-old explained that she held dual citizenship because her father was a Dutch citizen.

“The reality is that it was always an option”, she said.



Because she hadn’t competed for her country since announcing her retirement at the 2024 Paris Olympics, she was now eligible to represent the Netherlands.

Despite her “love and pride”, Tatjana Smith detailed the financial, practical, and emotional “burdens” she faced in the South.

Since switching nationalities, the Olympic gold medallist stated that she was impressed by how the Dutch prioritised their athletes’ well-being.



She said: “Off the bat, I can already feel the difference and changes. I don’t have to self-fund my way to get to World Championships”

In a clip announcing her decision to switch nationalities, the 29-year-old revealed that she had based her decision on financial stability, support, and sustainability.

World.title: ‘I can do taxes but too old for companies’: Pensioner hits back at age barrier
World.content:
An older man wearing eyeglasses is reading documents next to a laptop at home. Image: Pexels

A South African pensioner has called on employers to give older people a chance at work, saying age should not cancel out years of experience.

Ria Cordier shared the plea on The South African’s Facebook page, where grant recipients discussed returning to work to supplement their SASSA payments.

“They must hire pensioners; we will work, unlike the youngsters who think the world owes them everything. We have skills; I can do taxes, but I’m too old for companies,” Cordier wrote.



‘We will work’

Cordier’s comment speaks to a frustration shared by many older South Africans who still want to earn an income but say the door is closed to them.

According to Cordier, the issue is not ability or willingness. The skills are there, including tax work, but companies see age first.

The comment also aims at younger job seekers, suggesting that older workers bring a stronger work ethic to the table. It is a view likely to spark debate in a country where youth unemployment remains a major challenge.



Still job hunting after retirement

Cordier is not alone in looking for work later in life.

Esaiah Scavity Padi shared a brief update on his own situation in the same thread.

“Still looking for a job as pensioner now,” Padi wrote.



The short comment shows how retirement no longer means the end of the job search for many South Africans. With the grant under pressure from rising prices, some pensioners say part-time or contract work is the only way to keep up with monthly expenses.

For older job seekers, the search often means competing against younger candidates for limited positions, while facing assumptions about their health, energy or ability to adapt to new technology.

Can pensioners work and keep their grant?

Pensioners who find work should be aware that the Older Persons Grant is means tested. The test determines the amount of the grant a person can receive based on their financial situation, and for married applicants, both spouses’ income and assets are taken into account.



This means income from a job could affect the grant amount. Pensioners considering work should check with SASSA before taking on employment so they understand how their earnings could affect their payments.

The Older Persons Grant increased by R80 to R2 400 from April 2026, an amount many grant recipients say does not stretch far enough

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.



Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Overberg fire contained - Municipality
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - A fire that had engulfed parts of the Overberg has been contained.

According to the Overberg District Municipality, there is no immediate threat to the surrounding communities.

Firefighters managed to bring the De Hoop-Potberg blaze under control overnight. The fire threatened residential areas in Malgas and Reverine.

Despite the fires being brought under control, the devastation is significant.

Over 25,000 hectares and 22 homes were destroyed.

Firefighting teams are still working to prevent the blaze from spreading towards Infanta and Sandhoogte.

Residents are being urged to remain vigilant.

World.title: Surveyed teenagers confident they can refuse alcohol
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - About 75% of teenagers say they are confident refusing alcohol.

This is according to Aware.org's alcohol awareness program targeted at high school students.

They are working on ways to curb alcohol-related harm through education and prevention programs

With the academic year winding down, a lot of teenagers will be looking for different ways to keep themselves entertained.

In the organisation's latest study, over 100,000 students were questioned in 2025 broadly.

In their targeted groups 10,000 were reviewed and 75% of those said that they were confident to not engage in underage drinking.

World.title: Ferrari chief furious after Leclerc, Hamilton clash again
World.content:
Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur lambasted Charles Leclerc for a "lack of respect" after the Monegasque driver's latest clash with team-mate Lewis Hamilton torpedoed the Italian team's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Vasseur was left furious after Leclerc collided with Hamilton on lap 38 in Las Vegas -- just weeks after the drivers had been told that the team must come first after clashing at the Mexico Grand Prix.

Leclerc was subsequently hit with a 10-second penalty after an FIA Stewards inquiry and finished in 10th, while Hamilton finished seventh.

"Honestly, my position is that once again it's more than unacceptable," Vasseur said of the latest incident.

"I had exactly the same word after Mexico -- but it's a lack of respect. It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsor, but mainly for the people at home.

"Charles clearly made a mistake, and it has cost the team dearly."

The signs of lingering tension between Hamilton and Leclerc had been brewing during the early stages of Saturday's race.

A frustrated Hamilton at one point used an expletive as he told the team over the radio to get Leclerc to "back off" while he chased the leaders.

Vasseur said he had given Leclerc a warning shortly before he collided with Hamilton.

"I think I was quite harsh, we passed the message to Charles five corners before, and for me it's a professional mistake," Vasseur said.

"I know that he apologized. I know that he was sorry. But once again we destroyed the race today that we could have done much better... we can't lose points like this.

"More than points, it's the motivation of everybody -- the reward of the job done, the reward of the effort, and this it's a huge frustration for me."

Asked if he felt both drivers bore some of the responsibility for the latest controversy, Vasseur replied: "No, I think the decision of the FIA was quite clear."

Hamilton meanwhile would not answer when asked if he felt Ferrari should issue clear team rules to its drivers.

"That is for Ferrari to decide," the seven-time world champion told Sky Sports.

"I've done all I can and I've said everything and more. It has been difficult.

"All I can do is show up and give it everything I can, and hopefully in the background they eventually figure it out."

World.title: Prayer service held in honour of Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka
World.content:
She became a deputy minister of trade and industry from 1996 until 1999. Thereafter she became minister of Minerals and Energy from 1999 until 2005.

Mlambo-Ngcuka served as deputy president under former president Thabo Mbeki from 2005 until 2007. At the time of her death, she served as Chancellor at the University of Johannesburg since 2022.

She is survived by her husband, former head of the National Prosecuting Authority, Adv Bulelani Ngcuka and her five children.

She has been granted a state funeral and will be buried on Saturday at eXesi in the Eastern Cape.

World.title: Family searching for Mathibestad granny who went missing on Durban trip
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The family of an elderly woman are in desperate search after she went missing in Durban on Monday.

Selinah Boiyane Peete (84) from Mathibestad near Hammanskraal was part of a group of elderly women who regularly play soccer together.

The group, that had been visiting Durban, went to the beach before checking into the Albany Hotel.

Peete is said to have disappeared between getting off the bus and reaching the hotel.

A missing person's case has been opened with the Durban Central Police. However, there has been no breakthrough as yet.

Her grandson and a councillor from Moretele Local Municipality have since travelled to Durban, to join the search party.

World.title: Summer rains temporary relief as SA farmers brace themselves for drought
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa has over the past few weeks been experiencing rainy weather that is bringing much needed relief to the country's farmers.

According to Agbiz Chief economist, Wandile Sihlobo, despite this, there is still a risk of a drought.

Improved soil moisture and grazing conditions do not necessarily mean the drought threat has passed.

Sihlobo says while some areas might have experience flooding, which might many farmers think the country is out of the woods. The data shows that South Africa will experience a delayed drought.

World.title: DA, ActionSA failing to find each other
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Democratic Alliance leader Geordin Hill-Lewis has accused ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba of trying to justify his U-turn on working with the ANC.

The DA has made what it has called its full and final offer to ActionSA. The offer includes offering Tshwane in exchange for Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.

This will mean that Nasiphi Moya remains mayor of the Tshwane if elected by council.

Mashaba, however, has rejected the proposal, saying it does not deserve a response.

Hill-Lewis insists that compromises are necessary, describing the offer as reasonable.

"He has to find a way to justify his betrayal to the voters wishes," Hill-Lewis says about Mashaba.

World.title: Fossil fuels still missing from latest COP31 draft deal
World.content:
The COP31 presidency proposed an eleventh-hour deal Sunday that again fails to mention fossil fuels -- an omission that deepened a tense standoff at the UN climate talks.

The latest offering by summit co-hosts Turkey and Australia published deep into overtime leaves unresolved tensions over planet-heating fossil fuels but retains a much-sought goal to electrify the global economy.

The proposal needs consensus approval from nearly 200 nations at a closing session Sunday but they have struggled to bridge differences during two weeks of grinding negotiations.

The European Union and other nations have pushed for strong language on transitioning away from fossil fuels, a call that has faced resistance from oil-rich Saudi Arabia.

An EU official told AFP the latest proposal was a "backwards" step, warning there was a "very real possibility" that COP31 ends with no deal.

"I am more pessimistic today than I was yesterday," the official said on condition of anonymity.

"The situation is difficult, and the outcome is uncertain. The oil-producing countries are putting up a fierce fight," a German official said.

A Saudi official declined to comment when approached by AFP.

Fossil fuels are a flashpoint at the climate talks and the summit comes against a difficult backdrop of soaring energy prices and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran.

A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase out of fossil fuels but a second, pared-down version released Thursday stripped away all mentions of coal, oil and gas.

Threats of a walkout prompted Turkey and Australia to convene a hurried meeting between the European Union and Saudi Arabia in a bid to broker a compromise.

The latest text introduces a reference to a previous global deal in 2023 to shift the world away from fossil fuels -- but stops short of naming them explicitly.

And it retains a contentious push to expand carbon capture and storage, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised as costly and ineffective in cutting emissions.

"We are very disappointed with how the text looks," the environment minister of Antigua and Barbuda, Michael Joseph, told AFP after leaving the COP31 presidency's offices.

"I can't honestly say that I'm okay with it passing" in its current state, Joseph said, adding that the draft was "quite silent" on fossil fuels.

- Goal to electrify -

The draft also calls for global efforts to boost the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035 and the expansion of "clean energy".

The summit had been under pressure to show progress in tackling soaring greenhouse gas emissions in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia.

Facing blowback over fossil fuels, Turkey and Australia pointed to "electrification" as a way to cut heat-trapping emissions and bolster energy security.

This works by replacing technologies that burn fossil fuels directly -- like diesel cars and gas heating -- with electric alternatives.

But some nations had demanded an explicitly "clean" target to ensure the electrification push was powered by renewable energy and not fossil fuels.

Around one-third of global electricity is produced using coal and another fifth using fossil gas.

Attempts by Saudi Arabia, India and Kenya meanwhile to delay the next set of reports by the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) have been another major source of friction at the talks.

The draft text "highlights the importance" of these reports for an upcoming stocktake of global carbon-cutting efforts in 2028.

Dozens of countries across Europe, Africa and the Pacific want these assessments by the global scientific authority on climate change published in time for that crucial stocktake.

Countries have also disagreed at COP31 over how to respond to the looming breach of the 1.5C warming target set under the Paris climate accord.

The latest draft expressed "deep concern" that global warming would cross 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the next few years.

The talks also jammed over long-running complaints that rich nations are shirking their obligations to help developing nations confront climate change.

The removal of a $120 billion target for climate adaptation angered developing nations.

By Laurent Thomet, Nick Perry And Fulya Ozerkan

World.title: Ruto seeks way out of isolation as regional leaders lose trust in him
World.content:
President William Ruto arrives in Congo Brazzaville for a high level meeting on November 21, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto arrived in the northern Congolese town of Oyo on Saturday evening aboard a military aircraft from Kisumu, stepping into a four-way summit convened by Congolese President Denis Sassou Nguesso with the explicit hope of arresting a diplomatic free fall that has left Kenya increasingly isolated in its own neighborhood.

On Sunday, Ruto came face to face with Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi for the first time since relations between Nairobi and Kinshasa soured nearly three years ago.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.

Omollo warned that anyone suspected of destroying property would be taken to court in accordance with the law, where the judiciary would determine their cases.

He maintained that political differences should not be used to justify vandalism, endanger lives or disrupt public services.

“The Constitution protects the right to express ourselves peacefully and unarmed. Political differences cannot be an excuse to vandalise property, endanger lives or disrupt the services our communities depend on,” he said.

Those present included Public Service, Human Capital Development and Special Programmes Cabinet Secretary Geoffrey Ruku, Embu Governor Cecily Mbarire, Senator Alexander Munyi and Deputy Governor Kinyua Mugo, among others.

World.title: Narok Senator under fire after threatening to shoot auctioneers in Sh1.2m dispute
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama ole Kina is at the centre of a national uproar after a viral video captured him threatening to shoot individuals during a volatile confrontation involving auctioneers and a former Senate office employee.

The dramatic standoff erupted when court-backed agents attempted to seize a milk delivery truck over an unresolved legal dispute and has since ignited intense public debate regarding political accountability and the rule of law.

The controversy surrounds long court battle after Zakayo Rotiken, who served sacked as Narok North Constituency Coordinator between 2017 and 2020, was sacked.

According to records, the claimant was illegally dismissed amidst unpaid salary arrears.

On October 31, 2023, the Employment and Labour Relations Court ruled in Rotiken's favour , a decision that was subsequently upheld when the Senator lost his appeal.

With accrued interest, the court decree now stands at Sh 1.2 million.

Consequently, when the debt remained unsatisfied, licensed auctioneers moved in to execute lawful warrants which in turn provoked a furious reaction from Senator Ole Kina, who fiercely framed the entire episode as a political witch-hunt.

The lawmaker argued that Rotiken was hired by the Narok Senate office rather than his personal capacity, maintaining that any resultant liabilities ought to be handled by the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) rather than attaching his private property.

Defending his harsh words in the widely circulated footage, the senator dismissed the agents as trespassers and asserted action against them.

"Anybody who trespasses will get a bullet in their head or leg because that is trespass," said Ole Kina.

“Nitakupiga Risasi!” Senator Ledama Ole Kina embroiled in confrontation with alleged auctioneers over unpaid car loan https://t.co/k4OSXpNsdi November 21, 2026

The claimant's legal team condemned the threats made against statutory court officers emphasizing that a court judgment is an enforceable command rather than a mere suggestion, calling upon the Inspector General of Police of Police and the Director of Criminal Investigatons to urgently investigate the alleged death threats.

Rotiken noted that he merely sought justice through proper judicial channels and should not be penalized or intimidated for pursuing his lawful entitlements.

"When I was illegally dismissed with unpaid salary arrears, I did not resort to violence or politics—I went to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Nobody is above the law, and I appeal to the police to protect the officers doing their job so that justice can finally be served," he said.

Ultimately, as pressure mounts on security agencies to look into the firearm threats, the unfolding saga highlights a tense intersection between public office obligations and the absolute sanctity of judicial decrees.

While the senator maintains that his assets were unjustly targeted by political rivals, legal experts and the public continue to demand that the rule of law must prevail without exception.

World.title: Ruto defends IEBC, challenges rivals to present alternative policies
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has launched a scathing attack on opposition leaders over their demands on the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), accusing them of attempting to interfere with the electoral agency because they fear losing the 2027 General Election.

The President challenged opposition leaders to allow IEBC to prepare independently for next year's elections, saying they should instead focus on identifying their presidential candidate, developing a manifesto and presenting alternative policies to Kenyans.

Ruto accused his competitors of attempting to play the roles of both contestants and referees by seeking to influence decisions on the procurement of election materials and equipment.

He spoke a day after opposition leaders walked out of a meeting convened by IEBC, alleging bias by the commission.

“Please give IEBC a chance to arrange the elections next year. The people of Kenya will decide. You go and first look for your candidate, find your policies, agenda and plans and sell them to the wananchi. We shall meet at the ballot,” said Ruto.

Speaking during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto questioned why opposition politicians were concentrating on determining how IEBC should procure election materials instead of preparing to face voters.

“How can somebody who is in a competition want to decide where the pitch will be, who the referee will be and where the ball will be placed? Leave IEBC alone. Those who will vote are the citizens, and they are the ones who will decide,” he said.

The President accused his opponents of lacking a clear political agenda and capacity to deliver, claiming their campaigns were centred on slogans and personal attacks against him.

He challenged them to explain what they would do differently in agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure and employment rather than mobilising Kenyans around the slogan 'Kasongo Must Go'.

“The reason why my competitors cannot develop a plan is that they have no capacity. The reason why they have no agenda is that they have no knowledge. The reason why they cannot develop anything is that they know they have no capacity to deliver on anything that they will say,” he said.

His remarks were echoed by Kakamega Governor Fernandes Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, who rallied Western Kenya leaders behind his re-election bid and defended IEBC against what they termed unnecessary political pressure. President William Ruto during his tour of the Western region. [ Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

Speaking in Butere, Barasa said the region's political leadership, including Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya, Wetang'ula and trade unionist Francis Atwoli, was united behind Ruto's development agenda.

“IEBC will conduct the elections according to the law. Opposition leaders should leave IEBC alone and allow it to do its work,” he said.

Wetang'ula maintained that IEBC was independent of both the government and the opposition and should be allowed to conduct its work without interference.

“IEBC is independent of the government and independent of the Opposition. You stand there to do your work fairly, truthfully and equally,” he said.

He added: “Just as Arsenal supporters cannot dictate what uniform the referee should wear, the referee's responsibility is to ensure the game is played fairly and the winner emerges through a legitimate process.”

The exchanges underline the growing political contest over the management of the 2027 elections, with the government side accusing the opposition of undermining the electoral agency before campaigns gather momentum.

Beyond the political exchanges, Ruto used his Western Kenya tour to highlight development projects, saying his administration was committed to correcting years of neglect and unequal distribution of national resources.

He also announced plans for a second phase of the Nyota programme targeting an additional 200,000 young people, each expected to receive Sh50,000 to establish or expand businesses.

The government is also targeting 100,000 college graduates for internships from January, with each expected to receive a monthly stipend of Sh20,000.

Ruto's tour comes amid growing competition for Western Kenya's support ahead of the 2027 General Election, with emerging opposition alliances seeking to challenge his influence.

World.title: Ruto sustains attacks on Gachagua, dares Opposition to name 2027 flagbearer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto launches Matisi-Bokoli-Milani-Teremi road in Webuye West on November 19, 2026. [Benjamin Sakwa, Standard]

President William Ruto has challenged Opposition leaders to name their presidential candidate and unveil a clear political agenda, accusing them of wasting time hopping from one hotel to another and holding meetings in private residences in search of a flagbearer and campaign manifesto.

The President said the Opposition was yet to settle on a flagbearer or agree on a common agenda despite the clock ticking towards the 2027 General Election.

He dismissed the rival camps' political engagements as endless consultations and manoeuvres, arguing that their leaders were more preoccupied with political meetings than developing policies to convince Kenyans.

Speaking in Bungoma during his development tour of Western Kenya, Ruto challenged his opponents to stop what he termed political confusion and present an alternative development agenda, insisting he was ready to face them in the 2027 contest.

"These people do not have a candidate. They are struggling, moving from one hotel to another and from one person's house to another, trying to find an agenda and a manifesto before they can start campaigning. Time is running out, yet they are still struggling to agree on an agenda," he said.

Ruto also launched a fresh attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, accusing him of promoting tribalism and hatred while questioning his remarks about relocating to Texas, United States.

The President mockingly referred to Gachagua as "Mr Chuki wa Texas", questioning why he would allegedly acquire a house in the US while engaging in politics that could divide Kenyans and fuel hostility.

"Mr Chuki wa Texas has gone to buy a house in Texas. He wants to know whether he will flee our country after spreading tribalism and hatred, dividing people and turning them against each other, before boarding a plane to Texas and leaving others to deal with the consequences," Ruto said.

He accused the former Deputy President of attempting to turn communities against one another for political gain, warning that he would not allow anyone to undermine national unity through ethnic mobilisation.

Ruto said he was ready to confront his political opponents directly but insisted that political competition should not become an avenue for spreading hatred and inciting Kenyans against one another.

The President also questioned Gachagua's allies over their reported visit to the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) offices in Kizirani, accusing the Opposition of picking unnecessary fights with the electoral agency ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He suggested that politicians who begin questioning the electoral commission before elections could be preparing grounds to reject the results should they lose.

"Whenever you see someone picking a fight with IEBC, that person is already looking for an excuse to fail. Now they are coming up with all sorts of excuses, asking whether it is IEBC that votes. Is IEBC responsible for the votes?" He posed.

Ruto urged politicians to stop harassing the electoral agency, maintaining that the power to elect leaders rests with Kenyans and not the commission.

"I want to tell Kenyans to stop harassing IEBC. IEBC does not have votes. The votes belong to the people of Kenya," he said.

The President maintained that his administration was focused on delivering development, challenging the Opposition to explain its alternative plans on electricity connectivity, education, healthcare and infrastructure.

He questioned what the Opposition considered its development agenda, dismissing what he described as recycled political slogans and simplistic promises.

The President particularly took issue with promises centred on providing porridge to Kenyans, questioning whether such pledges could constitute a credible national development agenda.

He urged voters to interrogate the policies and development track records of politicians seeking their support instead of being swayed by political rhetoric and personal attacks.

The latest attack marks an escalation in political exchanges between Ruto and his rivals as competing camps intensify mobilisation ahead of the 2027 General Election.

It also comes amid efforts by Gachagua and other Opposition figures to consolidate their political formations and build a formidable challenge to Ruto's re-election bid, with Western Kenya emerging as a key battleground.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.

The birth marks a remarkable new beginning for the Langat family after 22 years of waiting for a child.

World.title: TSC picks Cheptumo Ayabei as new Chief Executive Officer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Teachers Service Commission headquarters in Nairobi. [File, Standard]

The Teachers Service Commission (TSC) has picked Cheptumo Ayabei as its new Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, making him the first person with a disability to head the commission.

Ayabei emerged top in interviews conducted on Monday, beating four other candidates, including the commission’s acting chief executive, Dr Evaleen Jesang Mitei, to become the country’s top teachers’ employer.

His selection ends a prolonged search for a substantive head of the commission, which has operated under acting leadership since the departure of former CEO Nancy Macharia in June 2025.

Ayabei, who hails from Baringo County, is currently TSC’s Director of Finance, having served at the commission for more than two decades. He joined the institution in 1999 as a Finance Officer before rising through the ranks to become Director of Finance in 2009.

His elevation marks a significant milestone for the representation of persons with disabilities in the country’s public institutions.

Ayabei was the first candidate to face the selection panel at 9am at the commission’s headquarters in Upper Hill, Nairobi. He was followed by Mitei at 10am, Robert Odette at 11am, Lawrence Ngai Kaburu at noon and Farah Abdi Saman at 1pm.

The five candidates were shortlisted from 124 applicants who responded to a fresh  issued on September 29. Applications closed on October 30.

Ayabei holds a Bachelor of Education degree in Mathematics and Economics from Kenyatta University and a Master’s degree in Finance and Banking from the University of Stirling in the United Kingdom. He is also a Certified Public Accountant.

Before joining TSC, he worked at the Ministry of Education between 1990 and 1999.

He takes over at a critical time for the commission, which oversees the employment, deployment, promotion and discipline of teachers across the country. He will inherit mounting pressure over teacher shortages, recruitment, promotions, transfers and the management of the teaching workforce.

The recruitment process had faced legal challenges, with a petition filed at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Kisii seeking to halt the exercise.

The case, filed by Evans Morara Nyangongo under Cause E038 of 2026, challenged the fresh recruitment and raised questions about Mitei’s participation in the process while serving as acting CEO and seeking the substantive position.

Nyangongo sought to stop the commission from proceeding with the appointment until the issues raised in the petition were determined.

However, the court dismissed both the application and the suit, with no orders as to costs, clearing the way for the interviews.

In its defence, TSC maintained that the decision to advertise the position had been made collectively by the commission’s board and not by the acting CEO.

In a replying affidavit, TSC chairman Jamleck Muturi John maintained that Mitei had neither participated in the board’s deliberations on the recruitment nor influenced the process.

The fresh recruitment followed an earlier court decision that nullified the previous exercise over procedural irregularities, forcing the commission to restart the search for a substantive chief executive.

World.title: GTA 6 shatters entertainment industry records: The Washington Post
World.content:
In an unprecedented achievement for the global entertainment industry, The Washington Post reported that Grand Theft Auto 6 – the long-awaited installment of the GTA video game franchise – has reached a record-breaking sales of US$ 3.79 billion within just 24 hours of its release on Thursday.

According to the developer, Rockstar Games this marks the largest entertainment product launch in history—surpassing films, music, and other video games—amidst widespread global celebration and renewed concerns regarding the impact of its violent content.

The newspaper noted that Rockstar Games on Friday announced that 32.5 million copies had been sold prior to the official launch, shattering the record for pre-orders.

The game, which took 13 years to develop and involved tens of thousands of people, generated $1.5 billion in pre-order revenue.

It noted that pre-sales approached half the sales volume of Michael Jackson’s “Thriller”—the best-selling album in music history—while the game earned a score of 99 out of 100 on the platform Metacritic, making it the highest-rated video game ever.

The game surpassed the record set by its predecessor, GTA V, which reached one billion dollars in sales within three days in 2013.

For comparison, the film Avengers: Endgame (2019) took five days to reach the one billion dollar mark, while Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey took three weeks to hit that same figure.

The founder and president of Rockstar Games, Sam Houser, said that the company is deeply grateful for the extraordinary response from players around the world.

The Washington Post noted how the game has evolved into a cultural phenomenon that has swept through American society.

This includes promotional campaigns featuring brands like Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) and Heineken, as well as the Miami Heat basketball team wearing jerseys bearing the name Vice City—the fictional, Miami-inspired metropolis where the game is set.

The game features over 33,000 non-player characters and offers a wide array of unconventional activities—such as managing character weight, renovating homes, purchasing clothing, birdwatching, and interacting with pets—alongside a simulation of daily life infused with political and social satire.

The game has drawn criticism within the US Congress and raised security concerns regarding the impact of virtual violence, while police in San Juan, Texas, have issued warnings against imitating criminal behaviors outside the game world.

World.title: Egypt’s Health Ministry warns citizens against unauthorized ‘Hitler’ flu shot
World.content:
The Egyptian Health Ministry issued a warning on Saturday against common medical practices that could be harmful to health, RT reported, including a so-called “Hitler” shot being touted as treatment for the common cold.

The ministry emphasized the importance of receiving medical treatment only under professional supervision and reassured citizens regarding the availability of medications for chronic diseases.

The spokesperson for the Ministry, Hossam Abdel-Ghaffar, warned that what is popularly known as the “triple injection” or the “Hitler Shot” lacks a sound scientific basis and can lead to adverse health consequences.

He explained that this mixture typically contains an antibiotic and painkillers—and sometimes cortisone—even though antibiotics are ineffective against viruses.

Furthermore, Abdel-Ghaffar noted that unnecessary use of antibiotics contributes to the development of antimicrobial resistance.

Proper treatment is available

For proper influenza treatment, he emphasized that the vaccine is available year-round, though it is best to receive it before winter.

Abdel-Ghaffar said that the vaccine reduces the severity of symptoms and complications, particularly in children, the elderly, individuals with chronic illnesses, and those with weakened immune systems.

The ministry spokesperson also stressed that artificial intelligence and telephone consultations cannot replace in-person medical examinations, explaining that diagnosing illnesses often requires a clinical assessment and medical tests to reach an accurate conclusion.

Abdel-Ghaffar denied any shortage of treatments for chronic diseases, including medications for hypertension and diabetes.

He explained that while a shortage of certain brand-name drugs may occasionally occur due to supply chain disruptions, alternatives are available that contain the same active ingredient, in the same dosage, and with the same method of administration.

World.title: Ecuadorian fishermen sue US over mysterious boat strike
World.content:
Ecuadorian fishermen have filed a lawsuit against the US government over a mysterious attack against their boat involving small, explosive-laden rotor drones, their lawyer Jorge Chiriboga Dávalos announced Tuesday.

The crew of La Negra Francisca Duarte II claims the US is to blame for the strike that sank their vessel on March 17 off the Galápagos Islands, within Ecuador’s exclusive economic zone. They say they were wrongfully targeted in the US military’s campaign against alleged drug-trafficking vessels.

They are seeking compensation for their economic losses and physical injuries, as well as an injunction to end the United States’ deadly strikes against boats in the Pacific and Caribbean, according to American attorney Dan Kovalik, who filed the lawsuit along with Chiriboga on Monday in federal court in the western district of Pennsylvania.

The lawsuit, which named the United States of America as the defendant, is demanding $5 million in damages.

The US Defense Department has previously denied involvement in the attack. CNN has reached out to the US attorney general’s office for comment on the lawsuit.

The US Southern Command told CNN it “does not comment on pending or ongoing litigation” as a matter of policy.

Kovalik, who previously filed another lawsuit over a US strike that presumably killed a Colombian fisherman last year, told reporters Tuesday that they have proof the US was involved in the March 17 attack against La Negra Francisca’s fishermen, all of whom survived, some with serious injuries.

Footage appears to show Ecuadorian fishing boat “La Negra Francisca Duarte II” on fire on March 17, 2026, hours after it was allegedly attacked with explosive-laden drones off the Galápagos Islands. The footage was recorded by another fishing crew passing by the area. The US Department of Defense has denied knowledge of or involvement in the incident. Courtesy Darwin Pico Flores

He claimed the fishermen were subsequently detained on another ship by members of the US Navy and US Coast Guard and that at least one of the two drones involved in the attack was a US drone.

Hours after the alleged strike, another fishing crew arrived at the site and took videos of the empty boat in flames, Chiriboga said.

The lawsuit accuses the US of willfully attacking, kidnapping and torturing the fishermen.

The US has acknowledged conducting dozens of lethal attacks on alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Pacific and Caribbean, but La Negra Francisca Duarte II is not among the acknowledged incidents.

In early March, the US began unspecified operations to target “designated terrorist organizations” in the South American country, according to the Pentagon.

Kovalik said defense cooperation agreements between the US and Ecuador do not protect them from what he described as attempted murder.

He insists that La Negra Francisca’s crew were not involved in drug trafficking. He noted that hours before this attack, the Ecuadorian Navy had boarded and inspected the boat and cleared the crew of any wrongdoing.

“Even if that weren’t the case … the US has no right to be bombing boats in the Caribbean and the Pacific on the claim the people are narco-traffickers. If they believe someone is a narco-trafficker, they need to go get a warrant for their arrest,” Kovalik said.

One of several unexplained attacks

After La Negra Francisca’s fishermen were purportedly attacked and detained, they were transferred to a Salvadoran Coast Guard ship in the middle of the sea, the crew previously told CNN. From there, they were shipped away to El Salvador, where they stayed for several days before eventually being flown back to Manta, Ecuador, the coastal city from which their boat had departed.

The lawsuit claims all the plaintiffs have lost their livelihood and are in “dire economic straits.” It also says they all suffer severe psychological trauma and that some are still dealing with physical pain, scarring and disability as a result of their injuries.

The March 17 strike is one of three unexplained attacks against Ecuadorian fishing crews earlier this year.

The vessel Don Maca experienced an almost identical attack on March 26, its crew members previously told CNN.

Another Ecuadorian fishing boat called Fiorella disappeared during a fishing voyage on January 20, along with eight crew members, and is believed to have been attacked as well, according to Fernando Bastias, an attorney with Ecuador’s human rights committee.

Attorney Chiriboga said the lawsuit is only being filed on behalf of La Negra Francisca’s crew. He added that the court will be asked to investigate if the CIA was involved in the attack, as the Washington Post reported.

World.title: What a wealth tax looks in the age of AI billionaires
World.content:
Los Angeles, California — Anthropic’s initial public offering has created overnight multi-millionaires (and some billionaires), and the timing is complicated.

They are coming into incredible wealth just as some states are trying different forms of wealth taxes, fueled by a shrinking middle class and growing unease about the concentration of wealth and power.

New York City is about to charge an extra yearly tax on expensive homes that aren’t anyone’s primary residence. Washington, DC is considering a tax on investment income for wealthier households. Washington state will levy its first modern income tax on households making more than $1 million in 2028.

California’s Prop 40 “billionaire tax” failed on Election Day, but Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D- MD) told Politico that the failure of Prop 40 suggests one state can’t do it alone. A bill introduced in both the House and Senate already proposes a 5% tax on the net worth of America’s billionaires, which could become a flashpoint in the 2028 presidential election.

Prop 40’s defeat — and the sudden emergence of a new class of AI elite — has simply launched a more heated national debate about how exactly the rich should be taxed.

Not as much cashflow as you think

“If someone’s worth $1 billion, that doesn’t mean that they have $50 million of cash around to pay the tax,” said Anderson Lafontant, managing director of Blue Zone Wealth Advisors.

Lafontant, whose clients include employees of AI companies, said a lot of this net worth is mostly on paper. Companies in IPO scenarios have restrictions on when shareholders can sell stock after it goes public, so an employee may not hold much liquid cash until their shares are sold. (Lafontant does not currently work with any Anthropic employees or founders.)

Prop 40 would have levied a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires who lived in California on January 1, 2026, not counting real estate or most retirement accounts.

“That’s the point about a wealth tax, is it hits paper wealth,” said Tom Steyer, billionaire climate activist and former California gubernatorial candidate. He argues that a person could borrow against stock to pay taxes. He called Prop 40 “imperfect” but “better than nothing.”

Tensions with the rich

Megan Lisa Jones, a private wealth and tax attorney at Holland & Knight, said some of her clients have left or talked about leaving California to seek better tax rates and avoid a potential Prop 40. Lafontant also said some of her clients have moved for tax reasons, though not necessarily over a wealth tax.

Both said their high-net worth clients did not want to speak with CNN.

“Some of my clients would say, ‘Well, I can’t leave now, but I’ll leave in four years…and I’m not a billionaire yet, so I don’t need to worry about it yet.’ But if they tax the billionaires, it’s just a question of time before it starts trickling down and taxes everyone,” Jones said.

“Yes to 40” and “Save Lives” signs during a “Yes on 40 for Ballots Over Billionaires” rally in San Francisco, California, October 3, 2026. Jason Henry/Bloomberg/Getty Images

Steyer has said a national wealth tax would be better, so the wealthy don’t keep moving to find tax havens.

“I’m not mad at people for being rich. It’s just that people are really suffering on the other end,” he said.

California Governor-elect Xavier Becerra has called Prop 40 “sketchy policy” and said the state needs a long-term solution instead of a one-time affair.

His spokesperson told CNN in a statement that the success of Prop 3, a state measure that made extra taxes on high-income earners permanent, is proof that California voters support taxing the rich.

Beyond the Golden State

Washington state voters upheld a so-called “millionaires’ tax” on Election Day, where any income over $1 million will get taxed. This means two spouses each making more than $500,000 would be taxed like millionaires.

There is currently no income tax in Washington state. Pending a constitutional challenge, this tax of 9.9% goes into effect in 2028.

That has prompted Michelle Dellino, a family law attorney in Seattle, to advise her clients to think through big life decisions.

“Some of those choices — like marrying, signing a prenup or moving — can’t really easily be undone,” she said.

Some of her clients might also be subject to a “scary” tax bill when company stock vests and is taxed like salary, even if the employee doesn’t have cash from selling those shares.

What ‘rich’ really means

The soaring cost of living nationwide raises questions about whether being a millionaire still holds the financial significance it once did. For example, the median single-family home in Seattle sold for about $1.1 million in October, according to an analysis by JanusGroup Real Estate.

Lafontant said those who own assets in America are winners, “and if you’re not an asset owner, you are just getting gobbled up by inflation.”

If a “wealth tax” is implemented she said she’d prefer to see taxes levied when people sell assets, not when they’re holding them.

As AI changes society, Jones poses a broader question about the American tax policy relying heavily on ordinary income.

“If we don’t have people working the same way, if AI really does replace jobs, then we’re going to have another big challenge with our tax system and how we’re going to fund things,” she said.

World.title: Israeli settlers launch attacks across West Bank as Netanyahu rival decries “Jewish terrorism”
World.content:
Israeli settlers launched a series of attacks across the occupied West Bank, torching at least a dozen cars and vandalizing several homes overnight Sunday, in what Gadi Eisenkot, the main rival of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, decried as “Jewish terrorism.”

Video from the village of Kufr Malik, about 10 miles northeast of Ramallah the seat of the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank, showed several cars in flames with thick smoke pouring into the sky as a siren blares in the background. In the same village, a home was tagged with Hebrew graffiti, including the word “revenge.”

Similar scenes unfolded in the nearby villages of Deir as-Sudan and Deir Abu Masha’al, two Palestinian communities northwest of Ramallah that were also attacked by settlers.

Mustafa Barghouti, the president of the Palestinian National Initiative, said the brazen attacks were part of an escalating pattern of settler violence.

“Palestinian families are facing violence, destruction and the loss of their homes,” he said on X.

Eisenkot said the violence was the result of the policies of pro-settler, far-right politicians Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who he said “brought the area to the brink of anarchy.” Smotrich was the key architect of a massive expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts in the West Bank over the last four years, while Ben-Gvir has been accused of turning a blind eye to settler violence.

Eisenkot said the attacks were “acts of Jewish terrorism, and we must call them by their name.” Eisenkot, who has four more weeks to attempt to form a government and oust Netanyahu, said the Israeli government should use administrative detention and targeted operations against the assailants.

A Palestinian man inspects a damaged car, which Palestinians say were burned by Israeli settlers, in Kafr Malik, near Ramallah. Mohamad Torokman/Reuters

Netanyahu has not issued any public statement about the attacks. CNN has reached out to his office for comment. Netanyahu has repeatedly tried to downplay settler violence, previously saying it wasthe result of what he has called “juvenile delinquents.”

The West Bank has seen a surge in settler violence in recent months, particularly around the annual olive harvest, where Palestinians have repeatedly been harassed and attacked. , There have been 410 settler attacks related to the olive harvest since the beginning of September, according to the UN.

This weekend’s attacks occurred across several locations in the middle of the night. There were no reports of injuries.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it also received reports of an attack on the Palestinian village of At-Turwani in the southern West Bank near the city of Hebron. The IDF said in a statement it “condemns acts of violence of this nature, which harm public order.” Israeli police said on Sunday they would enter the Palestinian villages under IDF escort to collect evidence. Police have not announced any arrests after the attacks.

“Settler terrorism in the West Bank does not take place in a vacuum,” said Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Arab Joint List party, which saw a surge in support in recent elections. “It is the direct result of the deepening occupation and a government policy under which violence against Palestinians has become an everyday occurrence.”

The attacks on Palestinian villages and sites have not been limited to the West Bank.

On Thursday morning, a mosque in northern Israel was torched and vandalized with graffiti similar to the messages sprayed across Palestinian homes in the West Bank. Pictures shared by Arab lawmaker Ahmad Tibi showed the inside of the mosque burned and charred.

He blamed anti-Arab rhetoric and “people who were poisoned by Netanyahu’s incitement” for the arson.

“The police and the Shin Bet must get to the perpetrators. And immediately,” he said on X.

Zeena Saifi contributed reporting.

World.title: ‘Cancer does change you’: Princess of Wales talks candidly about her experience in new documentary
World.content:
London — is opening up about her experience with cancer in a deeply personal new documentary that offers a rare glimpse into the life of Britain’s future queen. Catherine, Princess of Wales is opening up about her experience with cancer in a deeply personal new documentary that offers a rare glimpse into the life of Britain’s future queen.

“Cancer does change you. It changes your body. It changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” the 44-year-old says in a trailer for the film, “Heal.”

The documentary, which premieres on the BBC on November 29, explores the emotional and physical toll of cancer and the challenges of recovery.

“Often it is through pain that we realize there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that,” Kate says in the trailer.

The film follows the princess as she takes on the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours.

Hiking alongside her brother, James Middleton, Kate reveals she never rang a bell traditionally used to mark the end of cancer treatment.

“I didn’t ring the bell,” she says.

“Maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James replies.

The princess hopes the documentary will help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer, while improving access to holistic cancer care that supports patients’ physical and emotional wellbeing, Kensington Palace said.

Catherine reflects on her cancer journey in the forthcoming documentary. Matt Porteous/Kensington Palace

Kate publicly revealed her cancer diagnosis in March 2024, two months after undergoing abdominal surgery. She announced that she had completed chemotherapy that September and confirmed in January 2025 that her cancer was in remission. She has not disclosed what type of cancer she had.

All funds received through the documentary’s distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, which supports the hospital where she was treated, to support people living with and beyond cancer, according to Kensington Palace.

The princess has been slowly been returning to her royal work, accompanying her husband Prince William to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony earlier this week. The visit marked the couple’s first official overseas trip in four years and represented a major milestone in Kate’s return to duties since her cancer diagnosis.

“Heal” will air in the United States on NBCUniversal on November 30, followed by Channel 9 in Australia on December 1 and CTV and Noovo in Canada on December 7.

World.title: Bahrain strongly condemns Iran’s continued attacks, calls for reparations
World.content:
The Kingdom of Bahrain on Sunday harshly condemned Iranian air attacks on its territories, including a strike on a civilian industrial facility that caused a fire and material damage.

The Bahraini Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the attacks as a direct threat to civilian lives and a flagrant violation of Bahrain’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the UN Charter, particularly Article #2(4), international law and UN Security Council Resolution 2817 (2026).

It noted that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had publicly claimed responsibility.

Bahrain categorically rejected the IRGC’s justifications for the aggression, stressing that the target was an exclusively civilian industrial facility.

It called on Iran to end its repeated violations of other states’ sovereignty and stop using disputes with third parties to justify its attacks.

The ministry reaffirmed Bahrain’s right to take all necessary measures to protect its sovereignty and the security of its citizens and residents, including individual and collective self-defence under Article #51 of the UN Charter and the GCC Joint Defense Agreement, in coordination with its allies and partners.

Bahrain also urged the UN Security Council to take decisive action to ensure Iran fully implements Resolution 2817 (2026), including by immediately ending attacks and threats against civilians, civilian infrastructure and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, and ceasing any support for proxy groups.

The Ministry further called for accountability and full reparation for the damage caused, in accordance with international law and Human Rights Council Resolution #61/1, to safeguard regional and international peace and security.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Transport Minister inspects railway safety upgrades, train services
World.content:
Transport Minister Kamel al-Wazir inspected railway stations in Cairo, Tanta and Alexandria to monitor train services and accelerate efforts to improve safety and maintenance across the national railway network.

During visits to Cairo’s Ramses station, Tanta, Sidi Gaber and Alexandria stations, al-Wazir reviewed train operations, passenger services, signaling systems and maintenance work.

He directed railway officials to enforce operating and speed regulations, keep automatic train control systems running throughout trips and strengthen maintenance procedures.

The Minister also ordered safety barriers along railway tracks in densely populated areas to protect residents, alongside improved station cleanliness, passenger assistance and electronic ticketing services.

He stressed the importance of practical, on-the-job training for railway staff operating modern signaling systems to enhance safety and operational efficiency.

World.title: As COP31 Debates Ocean Protection, Liberia Offers 15 Offshore Blocks
World.content:
An offshore oil platform at sea. Photo: Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority

Summary

Liberia is offering 15 offshore petroleum blocks to investors while pledging to expand marine conservation and protect coastal livelihoods.

Fishing communities face existing pressures from coastal erosion, declining catches and industrial fishing, while residents of West Point say they have not been directly consulted about the offshore oil and gas plans.

With plans for two marine protected areas and four co-managed fisheries areas, questions remain about their locations, potential overlap with petroleum blocks, environmental safeguards and how the government will protect coastal communities.

By Aria Deemie

As world leaders negotiate stronger commitments to protect the oceans at COP31 in Türkiye, Liberia is offering 15 offshore petroleum blocks to investors while pledging to expand marine conservation and protect coastal livelihoods.



The Liberia Petroleum Regulatory Authority launched its 2026 Offshore Direct Negotiation Licensing Round in October, offering 12 blocks in the Liberia Basin and three in the Harper Basin. Interested companies have until April 15, 2027, to submit letters of intent. The round is intended to attract exploration investment, with the government promoting the country’s offshore petroleum potential to international investors. The LPRA licensing invitation provides details of the blocks and application process.

“The oceans are central to their chances of survival,” Australia’s Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen said at a COP31 presser, referring to countries and communities whose existence is threatened by rising ocean temperatures and other climate impacts. “We’ve said this would be the implementation COP, the COP of implementation and acceleration.”

For Liberia, the negotiations carry implications beyond climate diplomacy. Its offshore licensing plans are unfolding alongside commitments in its 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution, or NDC 3.0, to establish two marine protected areas and four co-managed fisheries areas by 2035. The country also depends on marine ecosystems for food, employment and income, particularly in coastal communities where fishing and fish processing support household livelihoods.

The potential environmental risks of offshore exploration concern Bruna Campos, an oil and gas campaigner at the Center for International Environmental Law. She said activities associated with oil exploration and production can affect marine life through several pathways, including seismic surveys, drilling waste and accidental spills.

Seismic surveys use powerful sound waves to map geological structures beneath the seabed. Campos said the noise can disturb marine mammals such as whales and dolphins, while other impacts can affect smaller organisms that form the foundation of marine food chains.

One of those groups is zooplankton, tiny drifting animals and larvae that provide food for fish and other marine species. Campos said disruption to these organisms could affect the wider food web.

“So if you’re having a reduction in zooplankton, you’re basically having a reduction on all the fish,” she said.
