World.title: Agentes del ICE causan terror al detener a dos personas en el embarque de un vuelo en Seattle
World.content:
Un vídeo muestra la fuerza usada por los funcionarios federales en la dramática detención de dos mexicanos que se disponían a volar

La pasarela de embarque de un avión fue el escenario la mañana de este sábado de una nueva detención dramática en la que agentes migratorios usaron la fuerza para arrestar a alguien. Sucedió en el Aeropuerto Internacional de Seattle-Tacoma (Estado de Washington) mientras los pasajeros subían a un avión de Alaska Airlines. Un vídeo casero muestra a los agentes llevándose a rastras a un hombre, mientras una mujer grita que cuentan con un permiso de trabajo.

Los agentes enmascarados llegaron hasta la pasarela cuando se procedía al embarque, causando confusión entre los pasajeros, que asistían al forcejeo de los agentes, que empujaron y tiraron con fuerza a una mujer al suelo, mientras lanzaba gritos desesperados.

El ICE tenía como objetivo a Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, un migrante mexicano que “permaneció en el país más allá del tiempo permitido por su visado, infringiendo así las leyes de nuestra nación”.

Durante el altercado, otra pasajera “arrojó café caliente a los agentes”, señaló el comunicado del ICE. Según la agencia, se determinó que dicha mujer, identificada como Sofía Hernández Mejía, se encontraba en Estados Unidos de manera ilegal —siendo originaria de México— y que había permanecido en el país más allá del tiempo autorizado por su visado. También fue detenida y podría enfrentar cargos por agresión a un agente federal.

“Estábamos caminando por el túnel, como en un proceso de embarque normal”, contó el pasajero Aidan Mendoza, de 20 años, a la emisora KUOW, de la red pública NPR. “De repente, se oyeron gritos. Al instante pensé: ‘Vaya, alguien se está peleando’… Y, al igual que todos los que me rodeaban, nos quedamos en absoluto silencio, porque nos preguntábamos: ‘¿Qué está pasando?”.

El vuelo de la Alaska Airlines 1306, con destino Los Ángeles, fue retrasado por el incidente. La aerolínea informó que los agentes del Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE, por sus siglas en inglés) no avisaron sobre la operación, la cual tuvo lugar durante un fin de semana de gran actividad, previo a la festividad de día de Acción de Gracias.

“Nos preocupa la intervención de las autoridades ocurrida esta mañana durante el embarque del vuelo 1306 de Alaska Airlines”, señaló la aerolínea. “Somos conscientes de lo angustiante que ha sido este incidente tanto para los empleados como para los pasajeros afectados”. La empresa añadió que está comprometida a “tratar a cada pasajero con dignidad y respeto”.

También el Puerto de Seattle emitió un comunicado en el que afirmó que la detención resultó angustiante no solo para la familia afectada, sino también para otros pasajeros, y que las autoridades locales “se pondrán en contacto con funcionarios federales para comprender mejor lo sucedido” y para averiguar si se habían incumplido los protocolos.

El gobernador del Estado de Washington, Bob Ferguson, reaccionó al incidente diciendo que el ICE está descontrolado. “Al igual que muchos estadounidenses, me indigna que agentes enmascarados, que no se identifican, saquen a rastras a personas de las pasarelas de embarque mientras se disponen a subir a un avión, sembrando el caos en nuestras comunidades. Lo ocurrido hoy en el Aeropuerto Internacional de Seattle-Tacoma no es más que el ejemplo más reciente de las tácticas del ICE, que son profundamente contrarias a los valores estadounidenses”, dijo y anunció que iría informando según se conocieran los detalles.

Desde el verano, el ICE ha intensificado las detenciones en los aeropuertos, centrándose especialmente en personas que en el pasado permanecieron en el país más tiempo del permitido por sus visados. El Gobierno de Trump forzó una colaboración de la Administración de Seguridad del Transporte (TSA, por las siglas en inglés) con el ICE, por la que entrega a la agencia migratoria los datos de pasajeros. El Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) batió récord de detenciones, superando las 50.000, en los meses de verano y ha mantenido una cifra similar en octubre.

La senadora del Estado de Washington, la demócrata Patty Murray, criticó la actuación de los agentes: “Me indigna el perturbador video en el que agentes del ICE obligan a una mujer a tirarse al suelo en un pasillo de embarque en el aeropuerto SeaTac. Hoy mismo exijo respuestas al Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) y seguiré luchando para poner fin a esta enfermiza campaña de terror”, escribió en X. Murray advirtió que a partir del 3 de enero, cuando se abra el nuevo Congreso en el que los demócratas tendrán mayoría “Trump deberá rendir cuentas”.

World.title: “¿Por qué se queja tanto esa zorra?”: la terrible parodia de SNL que estremece a las hermanas que cuidan a ancianos de su familia
World.content:
De un tiempo a esta parte, los sketches de Saturday Night Live parecen hablarme directamente a mí. En Protective Mom, Marcello Hernández y Pedro Pascal me ayudaron a reconciliarme con mi identidad de madre latina (no se me estaba dando muy bien la crianza estrictamente respetuosa). Amy Poehler supo mostrarme en Emo Mum cómo, gracias a la bajada de estrógenos de la perimenopausia, ahora me parezco más que nunca a mi yo adolescente. Pero este sketch, titulado Sister, donde se presentan las funciones cuidadoras de “la hermana” –the sister difference– como si de la app más optimizada del mercado se tratara, me ha dolido con su puñetera lucidez más de lo que estoy dispuesta a asumir. Y, a la vista del número de visualizaciones que lleva en redes, debemos de ser muchas las hermanas escocidas. Y si no tienes hermanos, da igual, tu madre seguro que los tiene, o tal vez trabajes en una residencia de mayores o en un hospital. O tengas ojos en la cara, vaya. Todos reconocemos y hemos sentido cerca ese poder (propongo una traducción algo rancia pero reconocible para la app en español: “Tieta”). En pocos días Sister se ha vuelto viral e incendiario en todos esos chats familiares en los que quien más o quien menos habita. Si lo mandaste por allí y nadie contestó (típica reacción del grupo a las opiniones de una verdadera sister) quizá tu caso sea mucho más grave de lo que parece.

Y si no lo has visto aún, hazlo. Llorarás de risa, te lo aseguro. Y de algo más. ¿Te ha estremecido igual que a mí? ¿Te ves representada? ¿Y a tus hermanos? ¿Cómo han podido dar en el clavo de esta manera? Quizá lo escalofriante no sea lo increíblemente buenos que son sus guionistas y actores si no lo naturalizado que tenemos el hecho de que dentro de la familia, serán siempre las hermanas, frente a sus homólogos varones, sobre quienes recaerá, por defecto, la responsabilidad del trabajo más exigente dentro de la ya demandante tarea de afrontar la dependencia en familia. Y es que es así, ante la incomparecencia de los servicios públicos, como se sujeta este pastel, con un servicio de soporte al cliente llamado Hermana diseñado para engrasar esta desigual estructura. Una app de cuidados con años de programación interna, compleja y fina como la sonda Voyager. Y ya, ya, antes de que empecéis: #NotAllBrothers pero siempre una hermana. Porque no estamos hablando de llamar a una empresa para buscar a una cuidadora, queridos. Ni de pasarse a “chequear” y aprovechar para verse un partido juntos mientras la hermana se pierde en el montón de tareas invisibles, la carga mental de la planificación o el trabajo emocional que genera una situación de dependencia. Claro, chicos, ¿acaso no estamos interiormente adiestradas para organizar las horas de las tomas de medicamentos o saber distinguir el mejor algodón de las sábanas para que no produzcan escaras? A todos vosotros, os deseo que el sketch os haga sentir incomodisimos del mejor de los modos. Ese que os lleve a preguntar y a implicaros antes de caer en el más ácido punch line del sketch: “See u in the funeral (¡Ya nos vemos en el funeral!)”. Ouch. Y es que toda sátira eficaz, está llena de verdades incómodas, ¿verdad? Con la risa congelada, te deja pensando en cómo la externalización intrafamiliar (es decir, la activación de Sister) debe de ahorrarle millones al Ministerio de Derechos Sociales y de Sanidad. Para que luego digan que las mujeres contribuimos menos al PIB. Si ya lo dijo mi tocaya Federici hace décadas: Eso que llaman amor es trabajo no pagado.

De lo que más escuece no es tanto la representación de la desvelada hermana en sí, si no la naturalidad de los hermanos al asumir la eficacia de Sister, cualquier otra sister de recambio, véase, la sister-in-law o cuñada. También la comunión que se produce entre el hombre cuidado y los otros hombres, los que le han abandonado: “¿Por qué se queja tanto? Es una zorra".

Por cierto, a la funcionalidad “Marido de la hermana” y para la segunda parte de este tremendo pelotazo de sketch (que estoy segura de que la habrá), la app debería incluir las recompensas en forma de sentidas palmaditas en la espalda y chorros de autoestima social que se llevará el Hermano cuando mueva una falange de su meñique en el sentido acto de arrimar el hombro. Aunque el siguiente nivel del humor cáustico no está en la sala de guionistas de SNL. Está en el corazón de la generación sándwich, la que está atrapada entre el cuidado de los hijos y los padres, y es una bomba de relojería lista para estallar. Tic, tac. Antes de convertirte en esa bitch preocupona, preguntona, pesada, en fin, amargada al haber asumido la responsabilidad del cuidado, conviértete en una bitch de verdad, y plántate ante el mandato de género más acendrado que llevamos las Sisters: ese que reza que somos las mejores candidatas para limpiarle el culo a nuestros padres. Ejem. No. Que la dureza del cuidado caiga repartida entre hermanos. Y, por supuesto, recuerda que la oferta de Sister “no es válida si la hermana tiene un buen terapeuta”. Y añado: una buena terapueta feminista. Búscala si puedes pagarla. Antes de que sea demasiado tarde y entre en el chat familiar el mensaje fatal de “Papa se ha caído”.

World.title: De la España vaciada al futuro digital: las pymes aragonesas que crecen empujadas por los centros de datos
World.content:
La inversión de AWS en Aragón ha abierto oportunidades para empresas locales de sectores tan distintos como las telecomunicaciones, el hormigón prefabricado o la obra civil. Una colaboración que impulsa el empleo, la innovación y la especialización de un tejido empresarial rural que puede encontrar en la economía digital una vía de expansión

Hay pocas cosas que hoy no podamos hacer desde un móvil conectado a internet. Y, para que todos esos millones de operaciones sean posibles, detrás hay una infraestructura crucial: los centros de datos. Edificios que en sí mismos constituyen un prodigio de la técnica: kilómetros de fibra óptica, redes de comunicación interna, sistemas de seguridad de vanguardia para proteger instalaciones así deestratégicas, estructuras de ingeniería tan sofisticadas que son un reto para aquellos con el encargo de construirlos, equiparlos y mantenerlos. Edificios que, además, pueden convertirse en una oportunidad para el impulso del empleo y el crecimiento económico en zonas rurales, como está ocurriendo en Aragón, según las conclusiones del informe de la consultora GfKencargado por Amazon Web Services (AWS) y tal como atestiguan algunas pymes de la zona, como las constructoras Gilva o Giral o la empresa de comunicaciones Gotor.

Desde noviembre de 2022, España cuenta con infraestructuras de servidores y datos de AWS en tres áreas de la región de Aragón, unas instalaciones que, en palabras de Suzana Curic, directora para España y Portugal de AWS, “convierten al país en uno de los centros neurálgicos para la nubeen el sur de Europa”. 33.700 millones de euros. Esa es la cantidad que prevén invertir en España hasta 2035 para ampliar y dar soporte a estas infraestructuras aragonesas, afirma Curic, una inversión que estiman que contribuya al PIB con hasta 31.700 millones y que apoye al empleo con 29.900 puestos a tiempo completo en empresas locales, contando los directos, indirectos e inducidos.

Esa transformación que, dice Curic, “hará que España pueda competir globalmente en la era de la inteligencia artificial” ya está en marcha. José María Alzaga, directorgeneral de Gotor Comunicaciones, define lo que están viviendo como “histórico”. ¿Por qué? “Estas inversiones no solo generan actividad económica y empleo, sino el desarrollo de nuevas capacidades y el refuerzo de la competitividad. El mayor legado será contar con empresas aragonesas más preparadas, innovadoras y capaces de abordar proyectos exigentes dentro y fuera de nuestra región”, cuenta Alzaga.

Gotor Comunicaciones Ingeniería de telecomunicaciones 1989 Fundada en Zaragoza Desde que comenzó a colaborar con AWS en 2022, su plantilla ha crecido un 20% “El mayor legado de estas inversiones será contar con empresas aragonesas más innovadoras” José María Alzaga, director General de Gotor Comunicaciones

Esta empresa de ingeniería de telecomunicaciones zaragozana fundada en 1989 es la encargada de instalar y configurar las redes físicas que conectan los aparatos alojados en esos centros de datos, las que permiten ese tránsito de información. También serán ellos quienes velen por su buen funcionamiento futuro. Tareas nada sencillas para las que necesitaron un periodo de entre seis y ocho meses de homologación de procedimientos técnicos, corporativos y de prevención de riesgos y que les obligaron a tirar de ingenio y sacar lo mejor de sí mismos.

00:50 Así es un centro de datos de AWS por dentro Así luce por dentro uno de los centros de datos de AWS en EE UU. Vídeo: AWS

Más empleo y nuevos negocios

Los datos del informe de GfK son elocuentes: un 60% de los proveedores de AWS ha aumentado su plantilla; uno de cada cinco empleados, de media, dedica sus jornadas a tareas relacionadas con estos proyectos; un 85% afirma que el impacto de los negocios con AWS ha sido muy positivo y dos de cada diez explican incluso que, gracias a su experiencia con AWS, han logrado abrir nuevas vías de negocio o expandirse fuera.

Gilva Constructora especializada en prefabricados de hormigón 1973 Fundada en Calanda (Teruel) Desde que comenzó a colaborar con AWS en 2023, su facturación ha crecido un 23% y ha pasado de 101 a 115 empleados “Hay un efecto que va más allá: estas inversiones fijan población y generan empleo cualificado” Jaime Valimañas, CEO de Gilva

Dice Jaime Valimañas, CEO de la constructora especializada en estructuras de hormigón Gilva, que en lugares donde “cada puesto de trabajo cuenta”, pueblos como “Alcañiz, Calanda y el Bajo Aragón en general, generar empleos cualificados y fijar población” se recibe casi como una bendición.

La suya es una empresa familiar de Calanda con más de 50 años de historia que se enorgullece de contribuir a “la construcción de una de las infraestructuras tecnológicas más exigentes de Europa, con estándares de calidad, seguridad y plazos de entrega al nivel de los mejores del mundo”. Su plantilla —cuentan con ingenieros que diseñan y plantas que fabrican en la zona— también creció, un 15%, y tienen motivos, más allá de “dar empleo en una zona deprimida como la provincia de Teruel”, para presumir de su particular contribución. Fruto de las necesidades de AWS, han diseñado una solución de hormigón prefabricado muy innovadora para las canalizaciones del cableado, un producto que, en sus palabras, “aporta rapidez, porque las piezas llegan terminadas de fábrica; calidad homogénea, porque todo se produce en condiciones controladas; y durabilidad y protección del cableado”.

Trabajos que, además, te hacen mejores

Para Javier Giral, CEO de la empresa oscense dedicada a las excavaciones Giral, con más de medio siglo de historia, su dilatada experiencia no hace menor “el reto que supone una obra de estas dimensiones”. “Hemos aprendido mucho”, cuenta un Giral que explica cómo desde que se implicaron en 2021 en este proyecto han tenido que afrontar cambios importantes dentro de la empresa: “Hemos invertido en maquinaria nueva, hemos incorporado tecnologías con las que antes no trabajábamos y hemos tenido que adaptar nuestros equipos a lo que nos demandaba la obra. También hemos podido contratar a más trabajadores y dar formación a los que ya teníamos. Se trata de una inversión que nos sirve para seguir creciendo en este negocio”.

Giral Constructora especializada en excavaciones 1971 Fundada en Huesca Desde que comenzó a colaborar con AWS en 2021, su plantilla creció un 25% y su facturación un 22% “Creo que lo mejor de todo es lo mucho que hemos aprendido por el camino” Javier Giral, CEO de Giral

Es un valor que todos los testimonios comparten: el aprendizaje que ha supuesto y cómo este les ha preparado para ser mucho más competitivos y valientes a la hora de atreverse a abordar proyectos internacionales. El futuro, dicen, está ahí, en trenes como este “que no hay que dejar pasar”. Sobre todo en zonas como Aragón, donde de los 731 municipios contabilizados, 541 (el 74%) tienen 500 habitantes o menos, según el Instituto Aragonés de Estadística. Una de las regiones donde la incidencia de la despoblación es más grave.

“Nos gustaría que, con los años, estos proyectos ayudaran a crear empleo estable, a fortalecer las empresas que ya tenemos y a dar oportunidades a los jóvenes para que puedan desarrollar su futuro profesional aquí”, asegura Giral, que resume el deseo de todos: que la España vaciada vea por fin ante sí un horizonte próspero.

World.title: La hora de Hernández de Cos
World.content:
El candidato mejor situado para la sucesión de Christine Lagarde al frente del BCE es el español Pablo Hernández de Cos, antiguo gobernador del Banco de España y actual director general del Banco de Pagos Internacionales. Hernández de Cos cuenta con el aval de las principales capitales europeas y el decisivo consenso de PSOE y PP, que prueban así la utilidad del sentido de Estado en cuestiones europeas. Si no hay sorpresas de última hora, se prevé que el Consejo Europeo del 26 y el 27 certifique la designación, junto al alemán Markus Brunnermeier como economista jefe y la francesa Laurence Boone como jefa de operaciones de mercado. El candidato español, por su trayectoria y talante, posee las cualidades necesarias para guiar la moneda única en un mundo en acelerada transformación.

El momento es sensible, con persistentes presiones inflacionistas en la Eurozona. La subida de los tipos de interés para contener el aumento de precios ha agudizado las dificultades de gran parte de la población para llegar a fin de mes. La inflación nunca es inocua políticamente, como evidencia la ola de protestas en Europa o la fortaleza de los extremismos que se nutren de la insatisfacción. Al mismo tiempo, las renovadas tensiones en el mercado de deuda soberana, por efecto de las dudas de los inversores sobre las cuentas públicas de un país central como Francia, traen infaustos recuerdos de algunos de los momentos de la crisis del euro, y han puesto en alerta a las autoridades monetarias por el temor a un contagio.

La lista de deberes para el sucesor de Lagarde es enorme. Hernández de Cos tiene un perfil propio y difícil de encerrar en categorías simplistas, y una nutrida experiencia en crisis inesperadas y complejas. Fue un firme defensor de las medidas de Mario Draghi en su cruzada para salvar el euro en 2012, ante las que su rival en la carrera por el BCE, el neerlandés Klaas Knot, se mostró bastante crítico. Durante la pandemia, promovió las compras de deuda a gran escala y los tipos negativos. Knot, considerado un halcón, criticó en aquella ocasión las medidas no convencionales de la entidad. Pero eso no convierte automáticamente a Hernández de Cos en paloma: en 2022 apoyó la fuerte subida de tipos del BCE ante el empuje de la inflación, en línea con los partidarios de una política monetaria más estricta.

Esto es una ventaja en un cargo que exige equilibrios constantes entre distintas culturas y sensibilidades, al frente de la institución común y plenamente autónoma de las capitales. Su pragmatismo y flexibilidad han decantado el respaldo de Francia a su candidatura. La posibilidad de que Marine Le Pen gane las elecciones presidenciales de la próxima primavera puede complicar la crisis presupuestaria en la que está sumida la segunda economía del euro y exigir una actuación decidida e imaginativa por parte de la autoridad monetaria. Por otro lado, el economista madrileño ha dado suficientes pruebas a lo largo de su carrera de independencia respecto al poder político, principio sacrosanto de la política monetaria alemana, y esto convence al Gobierno de Friedrich Merz.

El sucesor de Lagarde tendrá que esforzarse por realzar la credibilidad de la política monetaria y comunicar con claridad unas decisiones que requieren pedagogía y debate. La misión del BCE es estabilizar los precios en torno al 2%, y es fundamental atenerse a ella, pero el ejercicio de la máxima autoridad del euro obliga en ocasiones a pensar fuera de los marcos convencionales y encontrar soluciones que no constan en ningún manual, como demostró Draghi al anunciar que haría “lo que sea necesario” para rescatar el euro. En Bruselas nada está pactado hasta que todo está pactado. Pero este es el momento de Hernández de Cos, como ha señalado el vicepresidente Carlos Cuerpo, porque es el candidato adecuado, el más preparado y el mejor adaptado a estos tiempos cruciales para Europa y su moneda común.

World.title: IDFA 2026 winners: Chinese family portrait takes top prize
World.content:
The Year of the Ghost, a Dutch-Chinese documentary about a filmmaker’s mother and sister after his father’s death, has won the top prize at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA).

Louis Hothothot’s film won three awards at Thursday’s ceremony at the Eye Filmmuseum. It took best film in the International Competition, which carries a €15,000 prize, as well as best editing and the €5,000 award for best Dutch film.

The festival’s 39th edition runs until Sunday, with 253 films from 80 countries. One of the five documentaries in our preview, You Can See Everything, came second in the audience vote.

These are the films that took the main prizes:



The Year of the Ghost

Hothothot was born in China in 1986 as a second child under the one-child policy and moved to Amsterdam in his twenties. His first film, Four Journeys, opened at IDFA in 2021. In this second film, Covid restrictions stop him from getting back to China in time to say goodbye to his father. He then follows his mother, who wants to stay in her husband’s home town to care for his spirit, and his sister, who is trying to get by as a single woman in a big city. The jury praised the film’s “bold honesty, a rare attention to detail, cinematic curiosity and love”.

Memories of Lightning

Riccardo Giacconi’s French-Italian film won best film in the Envision Competition for experimental work, also worth €15,000. Radio journalist Sibilla Scinti Roger (30) travels to an almost deserted village in Le Marche, central Italy, to make an audio documentary about a murder there in 1982 – and finds out the 14-year-old victim was her aunt. Scinti Roger also won the award for outstanding artistic contribution.

Hazara Town

Afghan-born director Khadim Dai won the award for best first feature and the international critics’ prize (Fipresci), as well as a special mention in the International Competition. The film follows his Hazara family, who fled Afghanistan 20 years ago and now face growing persecution in Pakistan. They have to decide whether to stay together or leave one by one, knowing they may never see each other again.

The Clearing

Dutch director Sabine Groenewegen won the award for best use of archive footage, sponsored by the media archive Beeld & Geluid. Her film is a feminist history of Dutch colonial rubber plantations in the Dutch East Indies, where local women were subjected to violence and sexual enslavement. On the festival’s opening night, Groenewegen also received the €50,000 Cultuurfonds documentary grant, which an anonymous donor gives every year to a Dutch documentary maker.

Women and War

The €5,000 audience award, announced on Friday, went to Elwira Niewiera’s German-Polish-Ukrainian documentary. Four women attend therapy sessions in a chalet in the Ukrainian mountains, each trying to recover from very different traumatic experiences of the war. Festivalgoers gave it an average score of 4.856 out of 5, just ahead of You Can See Everything on 4.842.

Other winners included Joël Akafou’s Lonan Tché for best directing and Tala Hadid’s Bardi, set among horse riders in central Morocco, for best cinematography. Raluca Lupaşcu’s A Modern Roma Fairytale got a special mention for best Dutch film, and Ant Hampton’s Dutch-Belgian All the Downtime won the DocLab award for digital storytelling.

The full list of winners is on the IDFA website.

World.title: Inburgering with DN: understanding education system acronyms
World.content:
International parents in the Netherlands often find the Dutch school system baffling: HBO, SBO, DUO, WO… the jargon is endless. So to help you pass this particular parenting test, our Inburgering course this month looks at educational acronyms and the like.

Lesson 65: educational jargon

Primary school in the Netherlands is relatively straightforward – although parents often face a bewildering number of school philosophies when deciding which school to entrust their offspring to. It is in groep 8, the final year of primary school, that the trouble really starts.

Doorstroomtoets

Previously known as the Citotoets and the Eindtoets Basisonderwijs, the doorstroomtoets is taken by children in their final year at primary school. The tests focus on language and arithmetic, and the results are used to help determine which type of secondary education children should go on to. In principle, the teacher’s recommendation takes precedence.

The Dutch love of tests and early streaming has been widely criticised, and more secondary schools now offer mixed-ability classes in the first and second years.

Secondary education itself is divided into three main streams. Schools may offer just one – typically in cities – or a combination.

VWO

VWO (voorbereidend wetenschappelijk onderwijs, or preparatory academic education) is the highest level of Dutch secondary education and is followed by some 20% of pupils. A VWO education takes six years, with pupils choosing a specialism (profiel) in the sciences or humanities after three. There are two variants: atheneum and gymnasium. Gymnasium pupils take Latin and Greek in addition to the dozen or so other VWO subjects.

HAVO

HAVO (hoger algemeen voortgezet onderwijs) literally means ‘higher general continued education’. It takes five years to get a HAVO diploma, which prepares school leavers for a hogeschool (see HBO below) rather than a university. Around 30% of pupils are in a HAVO stream. After three years, HAVO pupils also choose a specialism in the sciences or humanities.

VMBO

VMBO stands for voorbereidend middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (preparatory intermediate vocational education). Some 50% of pupils attend this type of secondary education, which is subdivided into four streams. It takes four years to complete a VMBO course.

The most academic VMBO stream is still widely known as MAVO (middelbaar algemeen voortgezet onderwijs, or intermediate general continued education), after the type of school it replaced in 1999.

Middle-class parents push hard to avoid a VMBO recommendation, hence the popularity of tutors and crammers – and exam stress – for 12-year-olds.

SBO, SO and VSO

Special needs pupils have their own category of jargon, depending on their age, the nature of their disability and how much care they need. The main types are speciaal basisonderwijs (SBO, special primary education), speciaal onderwijs (SO, special education) and voortgezet speciaal onderwijs (VSO, special secondary education).

Lighthouse Special Education in The Hague is the only international school for special needs pupils.

After secondary school, most young people move on to further education. Education is compulsory until 16, and until 18 for anyone who does not yet have at least a HAVO, VWO or MBO level 2 diploma.

MBO

MBO, or middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (vocational education and training), is the highest level of education reached by around 40% of the working population. There are four levels of MBO diploma, and students can either attend college full time or combine work and study.

HBO

There are two types of degree course in the Netherlands: the academic courses offered by universities and the more vocational courses (HBO, or hoger beroepsonderwijs) offered by hogescholen. Their umbrella body, the Vereniging Hogescholen, calls them ‘universities of applied sciences’ in English. The Netherlands has 36 hogescholen ranging from art academies to hotel schools and technical colleges.

WO

The Netherlands has 14 official universities offering wetenschappelijk onderwijs (research-oriented education), including the Open University. Delft, Eindhoven and Twente are universities of technology, while Wageningen focuses on agriculture and food. A bachelor’s degree takes three years, a master’s one or two.

DUO

If you have any connection to post-school education, you cannot avoid dealing with the education ministry’s Dienst Uitvoering Onderwijs (DUO), which runs student finance and related services. DUO holds the diploma records that colleges and universities use to check whether you can enrol, organises the lotteries for popular courses and works out how much student finance you are entitled to.

After you graduate, DUO will follow you for years to make sure you pay back your student loan. DUO should not be confused with DUWO, which specialises in student housing.

World.title: Prosecutors hacked and wiretapped Tata Steel, court hears
World.content:
The public prosecution service (OM) hacked into Tata Steel’s internal communication network, wiretapped phones, and made video recordings as part of its investigation into alleged criminal pollution, it was revealed on Friday in Amsterdam’s district court.

During the first hearing of the case, the OM revealed it had conducted a “covert intrusion into Tata Steel’s corporate network”, broadcaster NOS reported. Documents were also taken, witnesses questioned and deposition measurements examined.

The case, which has been years in the making, accuses the steelmaker of intentionally ignoring harmful pollution stemming from its coke and gas plants in IJmuiden.

Police and prosecutors are allowed to use hacking techniques in criminal cases under highly specific circumstances. This has been allowed since 2019, NOS reported, and only in a handful of cases, including child pornography and criminal communication investigations.

A defence lawyer for Tata Steel said that there was “unfounded distrust” against the company, that its employees go to work to do the right thing, and that “wire tapping and hacking” had been used as part of an “unbalanced” criminal file.

The investigation is ongoing and could lead to the prosecution of individual executives of the company. The process is not expected to be completed until the first quarter of next year, the OM said, at which point it will also become clear if the current CEO Hans van den Berg could be charged.

The public health institute RIVM records an above-average rate of lung cancer for residents living around the plant, and soot regularly collects in the surrounding neighbourhoods, including school playgrounds.

Many people have suffered serious health problems, which they attribute to the plant.

In 2021, lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of 1,200 residents and the following year prosecutors began investigating. In July, the OM summoned Tata Steel to court on criminal charges.

Shortly thereafter, the government said it could pull out of a planned €2 billion subsidy package for the company if the criminal case raises “serious concerns” for the Dutch state.

World.title: Bruna and Readshop avoid bankruptcy, for now
World.content:
Audax, the parent company of the popular Bruna and Readshop shops, was granted two months of protection against creditors by a Breda court Thursday.

The move follows a provisional cooling-off period granted to the company earlier this month and a hearing earlier this week attended by more than 10 creditors and auditors, many of whom signaled they were willing to grant Audax more time to get its financial affairs in order.

Audax, which was acquired by Lector Capital in January 2026, has been experiencing financial difficulties for years. It says at the time of the acquisition, Lector agreed to invest €8.6 million in Audax, money they say never came through.

Audax is said to owe its suppliers more than €9 million. Some have demanded payment before delivering new products, which could impact the upcoming Christmas shopping season.

World.title: Exiled Colombian climate activist wins children’s peace prize
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A 17-year-old Colombian climate activist, Francisco Javier Vera Manzanares, has won the 2026 International Children’s Peace Prize given out by the Amsterdam-based KidsRights Foundation for “putting children’s rights at the heart of climate justice”.

The young activist is currently living in exile in Spain after receiving death threats over his activism in Colombia.

“Although our 17-year-old winner Francisco is an example of peaceful activism for climate rights defenders around the world, he has been forced to flee due to violent death threats against him,” KidsRights chairman Marc Dullaert told broadcaster NOS.

“It is shocking that peaceful child activists are threatened and that governments are unable to protect these children and their right to be heard.”

But in the imposing Peace Palace in The Hague Thursday afternoon, it was all celebration as Francisco received the prize from 72-year-old Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian child rights activist and 2014 Nobel Peace Prize winner.

“All children around the world have the right to live on a healthy, clean, dignified, and peaceful planet,” Francisco said.

Child activist

Francisco got involved in climate action in 2019 after seeing devastating wildfires engulf the Amazon rainforest. At just nine-years-old, he and six friends founded Guardians for Life, which today has more than 1,400 young members from across Colombia and Latin America.

He became the first child ever in Colombia to speak before Congress that same year.

According to KidsRights, Francisco “believes children are citizens of today, not just tomorrow, and should have a meaningful voice in the decisions that shape their lives and futures.”

He’s served as a Child Advisor to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child, helping to craft implementation guidelines on children’s rights and climate change.

Francisco’s work has led to the planting of more than 5,000 trees across Latin America and Europe and the training of some 10,000 young people in climate leadership, human rights and citizen participation.

More young winners

Francisco was chosen from 280 nominations across 57 countries. Former winners include Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, who won the prestigious award in 2019.

Two finalists were also recognised at Thursday’s ceremony, Chilean justice activist Issaiah Guzman Arancibia (15) and 17-year-old Sufaira, a Rohingya refugee from Myanmar currently living in Bangladesh who works to prevent child marriages.

Some 700,000 Rohingya fled to Bangladesh refugee camps after a 2017 government crackdown that judges in the same Peace Palace ruled hours before the award ceremony was a genocide committed by Myanmar against its Rohingya population – the first time a country has been held responsible for committing genocide.

World.title: Students walk out against conscription and defence spending
World.content:
High school and university students nationwide will walk out of their classrooms at 1pm on Friday in a National Peace Protest against conscription and increasing defence spending, part of an international action day also taking place in 24 other countries including Germany, England and France.

“In our opinion, money is being taken away from care, education and housing to go to defence,” National Student Union (LSVb) chairwoman Evy Kras told RTL news. “At the same time, they want us to enlist. Young people feel betrayed and say: so far and no further. We want to be invested in us.”

She says these political spending choices are at the expense of young people, and that campaigns by the defence ministry paint an unrealistic picture of war. “They pretend it’s all very adventurous and flashy, but fighting in a war is not flashy.”

The LSVb, together with research and activist group Stop Wapenhandel, published a report earlier this week saying that defence spends €260 million annually on recruitment campaigns at schools and online. Meanwhile, they say, students have trouble making ends meet.

In at least 16 Dutch cities and dozens of schools, students will leave their classrooms at 1pm, fighting for an “affordable future”. In Amsterdam, students will gather at the Stopera, while in Utrecht, they’ll head to the Domplein and in Groningen to the Broerplein.

The Dutch group Stop the War Fever, which is organising the walkout, says on its website that the government refuses to work towards peace yet “pumps billions into weapons and war.”

Conscription

The group is asking to do away with conscription, move defence out of education and invest in the future of young people instead of weapons of war.

Currently, both men and women in the Netherlands aged between 17 and 45 must register for conscription, but since 1997, there has been no obligation to serve.

But the government is preparing legislation for a selective military conscription system that could be employed if it’s deemed necessary for security reasons.

Junior minister Derk Boswijk said in March that he couldn’t rule out the deployment of young people in the coming years.

“Many young people see it coming, now that the war is near at hand on the European continent,” student Camiel Breet told RTL News. “We want to fight against the cabinet’s plans.”

“This is the first post-Cold War generation that is both the generation of misfortune and grows up with the threat of war,” Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam professor of social change and conflict Jacquelien van Stekelenburg told RTL News. “A basic sense of peace is no longer self-evident for them.”

World.title: Tata Steel goes on trial accused of deliberate air pollution
World.content:
The criminal case against Tata Steel over alleged deliberate air pollution around its IJmuiden plant began at Amsterdam district court on Friday.

The public prosecution service (OM) accuses Tata Steel IJmuiden of intentionally and unlawfully releasing harmful substances into the air. The complainants say they suffer serious health problems and worry about local children, with soot accumulating in local playgrounds, broadcaster NOS reported. The public health institute RIVM has recorded above-average lung cancer rates in the area.

The case began in 2021, when lawyer Bénédicte Ficq filed a complaint on behalf of people living near the plant. Prosecutors opened an investigation the following year and announced in July that they would take the company to court. They are still considering whether individual managers can be held personally liable.

The case focuses on the plant’s coke-making ovens, where coal is heated at very high temperatures without oxygen to produce coke, a material used to make steel. If the coal is not heated for long enough, it remains partly unfinished (called raw coke) and can release harmful gases into the air and spread soot into the environment.

Tata says it is technically unavoidable that a batch is sometimes not heated for long enough. Prosecutors suspect the company accepts these incidents and deliberately does not report them. In July, Tata called the allegations “essentially unjust”.

Ficq told NOS it was “a tremendously important day” and said the emissions incidents were “foreseeable and avoidable”. She wants executives, including chairman Hans van den Berg, to be prosecuted as well.

€2bn subsidy at steak

The criminal case also affects a €2 billion state support package for Tata’s switch to greener steel. The cabinet said in July that it could pull out of the deal if the investigation raised “serious concerns”. According to NOS, talks have now been extended to March, and the trial is unlikely to be over by then.

We cannot do what we do without your support. A consortium led by FedEx has completed its €7.8 billion (34.5 billion zloty) takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost. The deal will see InPost remain headquartered in Poland, with founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska staying at the helm. Friday’s announcement brings to a close a process that was first announced in February and received European Commission approval in August. InPost’s shares have now been delisted from the stock exchange. The takeover follows years of rapid growth for InPost, which pioneered the use of parcel delivery lockers in Poland before spreading rapidly in major western European markets, including France, Spain and the UK. A consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF has completed its takeover of Poland's InPost, which is now private. InPost has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Founder Rafał Brzoska stays on as CEO, and the company remains headquartered in Poland. pic.twitter.com/HWigKVPC3w — IPO Newsroom (@IPONewsroom_) November 20, 2026 Under the deal, FedEx and Advent, an American private equity firm, each hold 37% of InPost. A&R Investments, Brzoska’s own investment vehicle, has 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. PPF, A&R and Advent were previously already stakeholders. The consortium acquired InPost at a price of €15.60 per share, valuing the company at approximately €7.8 billion. In a statement published on Friday, Advent confirmed that InPost would retain its name, branding, Polish headquarters and operational independence following the takeover. Brzoska, who founded his business in 1999, will continue as CEO alongside the existing management team. “InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network,” said Advent. They added that the new consortium would now “accelerate investment” in InPost’s operations, helping the firm “extend its reach further”. FedEx and InPost would also “explore opportunities” to cooperate with one another. “InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment,” said FedEx’s CEO and president, Raj Subramaniam. “Connecting our global network…with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth.” Brzoska, who is one of Poland’s wealthiest individuals, said that the new partnership would “deliver the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler”. President Macron has thanked Polish delivery giant InPost for its latest investment in France The firm, which already operates over 9,000 parcel lockers in France through its subsidiary Mondial Relay, will now spend a further €500m to expand its presence https://t.co/caOGNQemfm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 InPost is the largest operator of parcel lockers in Europe, with around 70,000 across the continent. That includes roughly 30,000 in Poland and 16,000 in the UK, including in branches of the British Post Office, with over 23,000 more in the seven Eurozone countries where InPost operates. In the second quarter of 2026, InPost had revenue of 4.18 billion zloty (€970 million), up 18.2% year on year, while its number of parcels handled rose 16% to 380.9 million. The strongest revenue growth came in the eurozone, where sales increased 37.9%, followed by Poland, with 12.7% growth. Revenue in the UK and Ireland rose 9.8%. Poland recently managed to prevent a planned Russian “false-flag operation” at the border that, if it had not been stopped, could have “ended tragically”, says a retired general who acts as an advisor to the defence minister. His statement follows a report earlier this week by a leading newspaper, based on statements by unnamed senior officials, that Poland had foiled an attempt by Russia to carry out a major “provocation” on the border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Polish government figures, including Prime Minister Donald Tusk, have confirmed that a Russian operation at the border was prevented, though they have not provided further details. Generał Mieczysław Bieniek o próbie rosyjskiej prowokacji przy granicy z Polską !!! Polskie władze potwierdzają udaremnioną próbę rosyjskiej prowokacji przy granicy z obwodem królewieckim. – Udało się udaremnić, być może tragiczny w skutkach, incydent – przyznał w "Faktach po… pic.twitter.com/raQMfJ4uUp — Andrzej Mitura #Mocnytakżeosobno (@AndrzejekMitura) November 19, 2026 “The public isn’t informed about everything,” retired general Mieczysław Bieniek, who acts as an advisor to defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, told broadcaster TVN on Thursday. Bieniek then revealed that, “based on information we received from both our allies and our own intelligence services, we managed to thwart an incident with potentially tragic consequences, because the planned false-flag operation could have ended tragically”. “For example, if a group of people crossed the border and later dressed in uniforms, whether Ukrainian or Polish, but were Russian citizens disguised as others, and carried out an attack on their target, the side whose uniforms were worn would naturally be blamed,” continued the general. “Fortunately, nothing of the sort happened,” he added. “Certainly this preventative action [by Poland] forced the other side to desist from these acts.” Bieniek’s comments followed a report published on Wednesday by the Rzeczpospolita daily, which said it had learned of a planned Russian sabotage operation on the border between Poland and the Kaliningrad exclave. The newspaper, citing unnamed high-ranking figures from the uniformed services, said that the planned incident could have involved Russia mounting an attack on one of its own facilities but blaming it on Ukraine. Such actions are known as false-flag operations. “It was supposed to be reminiscent of the Gleiwitz incident,” said one unnamed source, referring to a false-flag attack in 1939 staged by Nazi Germany, in which German operatives dressed in Polish uniforms. However, Kosiniak-Kamysz did not comment on or provide any specific details of what kind of incident Poland may have prevented on the Kaliningrad border. Later on Wednesday, Tusk himself reiterated to journalists that “we received signals that some unacceptable events could occur near the Polish-Russian border” and that “it seems that the mobilisation of the border guard and police in this place blocked any plans or ideas to carry out any provocation”. In June, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski even announced that he was “expecting an attack on Russian territory under a false flag, to which Putin will ‘respond'”. Sikorski pointed to the Gleiwitz incident as an example of such an operation. On Friday morning, two Russian missiles and what is believed to be a drone entered Polish airspace and hit the ground in three locations. Tusk condemned the incident as a further “Russian escalation” and said that it was likely to have been “an intentional provocation”. World.title: Two Ukrainians charged with vandalising Polish monuments on behalf of Russia
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Two Ukrainians have been charged in Poland with working on behalf of Russia to paint slogans praising the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), a nationalist formation responsible for massacring Poles during World War Two, on three monuments in the Polish city of Poznań. Polish prosecutors say that the operation was intended to fuel hostility between Poles and Ukrainians. The incidents in Poznań were part of a seemingly coordinated wave of similar graffiti on monuments in three other Polish cities. Ukraińcy malowali na pomnikach hasła „Sława UPA”. Działali na zlecenie wywiaduhttps://t.co/knLgZzo8ct — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 19, 2026 In early November, the words “Slava UPA” (“Glory to the UPA”) were painted in red on three monuments in Poznań commemorating World War Two soldiers. While the UPA is remembered by many in Ukraine for fighting for independence from Moscow-imposed Soviet rule, in Poland it is primarily associated with leading the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, were slaughtered as part of an ethnic cleansing operation. The history of those massacres, and the continued veneration of the UPA by some in Ukraine, has regularly stirred tension between Poland and Ukraine, who are otherwise close allies. On Thursday, the National Prosecutor’s Office confirmed to the Polish Press Agency (PAP) that two Ukrainians, who can be named only as Nikita S. and Dmytro Y. under Polish privacy law, had been detained and charged in relation to the vandalism. According to prosecutors, Nikita S., “acting on behalf of Russian intelligence and in order to obtain financial benefit of $500”, persuaded Dmytro Y. to “commit an act of sabotage by painting the slogans” with the aim of “publicly inciting hatred based on national differences between the Polish and Ukrainian peoples”. The suspects were identified by police and the Internal Security Agency (ABW), who had analysed surveillance footage of the perpetrator, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily. Both were detained in Poznań, according to PAP. In the wake of the Poznań vandalism, Poland-based Belarusian news outlet MOST reported that, a few days before the graffiti appeared, an advert offering $500 for someone to paint pro-UPA slogans on monuments in the city had appeared on messaging service Telegram. When an undercover journalist from the outlet contacted the person offering the job, they were told that similar work was available in other Polish cities. Around the same time, almost identical graffiti praising the UPA appeared on further monuments in the cities of Gdańsk, Gdynia and Warsaw, including one dedicated to the heroes of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising. Around a dozen monuments in Poland, including one dedicated to the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, have been defaced with graffiti glorifying the WWII Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Ukraine’s embassy in Warsaw has condemned the vandalism and blamed it on Russia https://t.co/iaZb2CyiPx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2026 Last week, local police in Gdańsk confirmed that they had detained a 17-year-old Ukrainian suspected of carrying out the graffiti there and in Gdynia. He has been charged with promoting fascist ideology, incitement to violence and hatred based on nationality, and desecration of monuments. The Ukrainian embassy in Poland has condemned the acts of vandalism, calling them a “disgraceful provocation” and “a manifestation of the hybrid war that Russia is attempting to wage by any means in European states”. Poland has been a primary target for Russia’s so-called hybrid actions in Europe, which have included acts of sabotage, espionage, disinformation and efforts to stir hostility towards Ukrainians. Such operations are rarely carried out by Russian operatives themselves. Instead, Russia often recruits people already on the ground, often members of Poland’s large Ukrainian and Belarusian migrant communities, as well as Poles themselves in some cases. In July this year, a Ukrainian teenager was indicted by Polish prosecutors on charges of painting dozens of pro-UPA slogans in public places, including on a monument to victims of the Volhynia massacres. World.title: Two Russian missiles and a drone hit Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Two Russian missiles and what is likely to have been a jet-powered drone struck Poland today amid large-scale attacks on Ukraine, the defence minister has confirmed. On Friday morning, an image published by Polish media outlet Wirtualna Polska showed a crater in the ground with a fire burning in the middle of it. The website reported that it had been caused by an object landing in a field in the village of Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland, around 60 kilometres from the Ukrainian border. 🔴Tu spadł niezidentyfikowany obiekt. Mamy zdjęcie Niezidentyfikowany obiekt spadł w piątek rano na pole w miejscowości Nowy Lipowiec w powiecie biłgorajskim. Stało się to kilkaset metrów od zabudowań. Nikomu nic się nie stało. Mamy zdjęcie z tego miejsca… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) November 20, 2026 At a press conference later on Friday morning, Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the object in Nowy Lipowiec was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile (the same type as one that entered Polish airspace and exploded in eastern Poland in July this year). The defence minister also revealed that another missile had fallen in the town of Rudnik nad Sanem and what is likely to be a jet-powered drone had struck in the village of Mołodycz. Both of those locations are also in southeastern Poland, not far from the Ukrainian border. He added that there were no reports of injuries or any damage to critical infrastructure as a result of the incidents in Poland, which he noted had taken place during “one of the largest Russian attacks on Ukraine since the beginning of the full-scale war”. Kosiniak-Kamysz also suggested that the fact that these incidents had taken place now was “no coincidence”, given that military exercises of the Coalition of the Willing – a group of countries supporting Ukraine – are taking place in Poland not far from where the missiles and drone struck. Addressing the media on Friday afternoon, Prime Minister Donald Tusk declared that Friday represented “another instalment in the Russian escalation”. He said that there was no doubt that the objects which had hit Poland were Russian. “I’m cautious in my wording, but it does seem that we’re dealing with an intentional provocation,” added the prime minister. NATO’s secretary general, Mark Rutte, announced that he had spoken with Tusk about “the grave violations of Polish airspace” and declared that the alliance “stands in solidarity with Poland and will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend”. Spoke with @donaldtusk about the grave violations of Polish airspace overnight. NATO jets were scrambled in response. We stand in solidarity with Poland and will continue to strengthen our ability to deter and defend. This incident is clearly dangerous – a consequence of… — Mark Rutte (@SecGenNATO) November 20, 2026 During the early hours of Friday, operational command of Poland’s armed forces reported that they had “activated the necessary forces in response to Russia’s strikes on targets in Ukraine”. Such communiques have become common in recent months, as Poland has had to scramble its forces in response to Russia’s increasing strikes on targets in western Ukraine, including a passenger train travelling between Kyiv and Warsaw that was hit by a jet-powered drone in September this year. In recent months, the Polish government has warned of intelligence suggesting the likelihood of “provocations” by Russia, including airspace and border violations. In September this year, a Russian helicopter briefly crossed the border from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Earlier this month, Poland claimed to have foiled a ground operation around the border with Kaliningrad. Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk claims that "individuals with flashlights" were observed at the Russian border last night. "We very quickly mobilised the appropriate forces and resources there, and managed to prevent a provocation," he added https://t.co/kD5OmpNagf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2026 In September 2025, around 20 Russian drones crossed Poland’s eastern borders in an unprecedented violation that prompted Poland to trigger NATO’s Article 4. Back in November 2022, during the early stages of Russia’s war in Ukraine, two people died in Poland after a missile crossed the Ukrainian border and struck the ground. It later transpired to have been a Ukrainian air-defence missile fired in response to Russian attacks. World.title: Poland hands e-commerce giant Allegro “greenwashing” fine for misleading tree-planting campaign
World.content: Why are you seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s consumer protection authority, UOKiK, has fined Allegro, one of Europe’s largest e-commerce platforms, 55 million zloty (€12.3 million) for misleading consumers over a campaign that promised to plant trees in exchange for collecting parcels through its delivery service. The case is one of a series of investigations into so-called “greenwashing” launched by the authority against companies operating in Poland. UOKiK found that two of the Polish e-commerce group’s practices relating to the tree-planting initiative had infringed consumers’ interests. The first involved promotional claims suggesting that collecting 10 parcels through Allegro’s delivery service would result in a tree being planted. In practice, however, Allegro calculated the number of trees to be planted using forecasts prepared the previous year, rather than linking plantings to individual consumers’ parcel collections. This meant that decisions on the number of trees had already been made before customers collected their parcels. 🌳 Greenwashing ma swoją cenę! Blisko 55 mln zł kary dla Allegro – ekologiczne obietnice miały zachęcać do odbioru paczek, ale rzeczywistość nie była tak zielona. Milionów deklarowanych drzew nigdy nie posadzono. ❌ Ekościema nie może się opłacać 🔎https://t.co/yPQznKz0H1 pic.twitter.com/UDcWXWq3LI — UOKiK (@UOKiKgovPL) November 18, 2026 The second breach concerned the conditions attached to the campaign, which Allegro failed to communicate clearly to consumers. According to UOKiK, Allegro’s promotional messages could have led customers to believe that collecting 10 parcels through their delivery was sufficient to trigger tree planting. In fact, customers had to do it within a single calendar year and, from January 2024, submit a dedication for the tree within a specified period. Without a dedication, collecting the required number of parcels did not result in a tree being planted or assigned to the customer. UOKiK also found that the option to submit a dedication was unavailable for extended periods. Between March and November 2024, the feature was disabled for a total of 264 days, the watchdog said. The prolonged interruptions could have led customers to forget about the requirement or abandon their attempts to submit a dedication, meaning they would not receive the promised tree. UOKiK imposed a fine of 29.9 million zloty for the first practice and 24.9 million zloty for the second. Its decision can still be appealed in court by Allegro, which has not yet commented on the decision. “Green claims must be truthful, specific and verifiable; otherwise, they may mislead consumers and constitute an example of greenwashing,” said UOKiK president Tomasz Chróstny. “If a consumer hears, ‘collect 10 parcels, and we will plant a tree,’ they have the right to interpret that literally,” Chróstny said, adding that “several million [trees] – more than half of the total number claimed by Allegro – were never planted at all”. When announcing its decision, UOKiK noted that, according to a 2025 consumer survey conducted by the European Union, 43% of Poles said that the environmental impact of a product or service influenced their choices. The Allegro case forms part of a broader crackdown on suspected greenwashing by companies operating in Poland. Alongside Allegro, UOKiK has brought charges against delivery companies DHL, DPD and InPost, mobility firm Bolt, retailers Tchibo and Zara, and cosmetics firm L’Oréal Polska. World.title: Poland deepens regional gas cooperation with Hungary, Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has signed memorandums with four of its neighbouring countries – Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania – pledging to strengthen regional cooperation on natural gas supplies and the security of infrastructure. The initiative comes amid Poland’s efforts to use its liquefied natural gas (LNG) capacity and transmission links to establish itself as a regional energy hub, helping its neighbours, especially landlocked countries to the south, diversify supplies and reduce their reliance on Russia. The two memorandums of understanding were signed in Warsaw during a ministerial meeting at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC), co-organised by the US Department of Energy, Poland’s energy ministry and the Global Energy Centre run by the Atlantic Council. Rozpoczęliśmy 7. edycję Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation (P-TEC) – jednego z kluczowych forów współpracy energetycznej Stanów Zjednoczonych oraz krajów Europy Środkowo-Wschodniej. ⚡️ W Warszawie spotkali się przedstawiciele rządu Stanów Zjednoczonych, państw… pic.twitter.com/7t8kLluubF — GAZ-SYSTEM (@GAZ_SYSTEM) November 18, 2026 One of them, signed by Poland, Slovakia, Hungary and the Czech Republic – who collectively form the Visegrad Group – establishes a framework for closer collaboration between their gas transmission system operators and more effective use of existing infrastructure. In late 2022, for example, a new gas interconnector opened between Poland and Slovakia. However, since then, the pipeline has seen very little use, as Bratislava has continued to rely on Russian gas supplies. Hungary has also remained reliant on Russian gas. By contrast, Poland quickly phased out its imports of Russian energy after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It now receives most of its gas via a pipeline that runs from Norway through Denmark and through LNG that arrives by sea, sourced mainly from the US and Qatar. From autumn 2027, the EU will ban its member states from importing Russian gas. In September, Hungary’s energy minister said that his country will be ready to meet that deadline. Slovakia, however, is challenging the import ban at the European Court of Justice. As part of the new memorandum signed this week, the four Visegrad countries will assess the impact of phasing out Russian supplies on regional energy security. The second memorandum, signed between Poland’s Gaz-System and Lithuania’s Amber Grid and KN Energies – which operate gas and LNG infrastructure in the two countries – focuses on strengthening the resilience and security of energy infrastructure around the Baltic Sea. It provides for closer coordination between the companies, including information-sharing on threats and incidents, joint risk assessments, exchanges of expertise on infrastructure protection and crisis response, and joint training sessions and exercises. “The LNG terminals in Poland and Lithuania serve as critical supply hubs for…Central and Eastern Europe, significantly enhancing energy security and bolstering regional resilience,” said Sławomir Hinc, CEO of Gaz-System. But that “security depends on the resilience of every link in the chain”, added his counterpart at Amber Grid, Nemunas Biknius. “This regional agreement will enable us to strengthen that chain in a structured and coordinated way.” Poland has declared its ambition to become a hub for supplying gas to the CEE region, including Ukraine, in particular by expanding imports of LNG from the United States. In addition to its existing LNG terminal in Świnoujście, which opened a decade ago, it is planning to build two further floating storage and regasification units that will be located in the Bay of Gdańsk. The first of those, under construction in South Korea, is due to open in 2028. Last year, a record amount of natural gas was traded in Poland, surpassing the levels seen before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the energy crisis that followed. We cannot do what we do without your support. Police and prosecutors have detained 123 people across Poland as part of a major operation targeting online child pornography. Among those arrested were some who had used AI to produce content depicting the abuse of minors. Around 170 searches took place, with prosecutors seizing a total of 1,096 electronic devices. Initial analysis indicates that almost 2.8 million files containing child sex abuse material were contained on them, said the National Prosecutor’s Office, which oversaw the operation. Those detained are all men, ranging in age from 18 to 73, and include a teacher and a doctor. All were Polish citizens apart from one Ukrainian and one Belarusian. Policjanci Centralnego Biura Zwalczania Cyberprzestępczości zatrzymali 123 osoby i zabezpieczyli ponad 2,8 mln plików z materiałami przedstawiającymi seksualne wykorzystanie małoletnich ‼️ Działania pod krypt. „INFERNO”, to już kolejna – 9 operacja CBZC przeciwko przestępczości o… pic.twitter.com/XBdNAmLjKz — Centralne Biuro Zwalczania Cyberprzestępczości (@PolicjaCBZC) November 19, 2026 The police’s Central Cybercrime Bureau (CBZC) reports that the detained teacher claimed “he was studying to obtain expert qualifications and was collecting and analysing the [abuse] material to check whether his psyche could withstand the associated strain”. The doctor, an anaesthesiologist, was found to be in possession of around 75,000 files containing child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors have already charged 94 of the suspects with producing, possessing and/or disseminating materials related to the sexual exploitation of minors. Those crimes carry a jail term of up to 15 years. Thirty-one of the suspects have been placed in pretrial detention. “Among those detained were people who used AI technology to produce materials depicting the sexual abuse of minors,” wrote the National Prosecutor’s Office. One suspect is also accused of taking photographs and videos of himself and children naked at a public swimming pool. In May this year, prosecutors announced the results of a similar operation against child pornography, which, by coincidence, also resulted in 123 people being detained. Among those detained at that time was a teacher accused of recording and photographing children, as well as another suspect accusing of grooming minors through a messaging app before encouraging them to perform sexual acts. World.title: Polish Supreme Court rejects government’s position on Constitutional Tribunal
World.content: Why are you seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s rule-of-law crisis has taken another twist, after the Supreme Court (SN) issued a resolution effectively opposing the government’s position towards another top court, the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), and endorsing that of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki. The SN found that TK rulings are only valid if issued by judges the president has sworn in and that they take effect even if the government refuses to publish them. Nawrocki has refused to swear in five TK judges, while the government has refused to publish 85 previous TK rulings. However, the government’s justice minister argues that the new SN resolution is itself invalid because it was issued by judges who were appointed unlawfully. Połączone izby Sądu Najwyższego o wyrokach Trybunału Konstytucyjnego jako podstawie wznowienia postępowaniahttps://t.co/DzgL6aDTGK pic.twitter.com/GpiGbWMvNn — Sąd Najwyższy (@SN_RP_) November 18, 2026 On Wednesday, the SN issued a resolution in response to questions over the validity of rulings issued by the TK. It found, among other things, that a valid TK ruling can only be issued by a panel of judges who, after being elected to the tribunal by parliament, have “taken an oath before the president, that is, in his presence”. Those latter words relate to a key dispute that has arisen around the TK. The government’s majority in parliament has this year chosen eight new TK judges, who would now form the majority on the 15-seat tribunal. However, Nawrocki has refused to receive the oath of five of those judges, citing concerns over the method of their appointment or their qualifications. Those five judges have instead arranged their own swearing-in ceremonies before a notary and then forwarded their oaths to the presidential chancellery. They and the government argue that this meets the requirement for them to take up their seats. However, Nawrocki and the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed under the former government, reject that position and say that the judges cannot take up their seats on the court until the president receives their oath in person. The Supreme Court has now effectively endorsed their stance. Meanwhile, the SN also addressed another contentious issue. Since March 2024, the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – has refused to publish any of the 85 TK rulings issued in that time. That is because, under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, three judges were unlawfully appointed to the TK. The current government argues that TK rulings only take force when published in the official Journal of Laws. Indeed, so did the former PiS government when, in 2016, it refused to publish TK rulings that contradicted its judicial policies. However, the SN has now deemed that valid TK rulings enter force even if not published. “In a situation where the body responsible for publishing TK rulings fails to fulfil this obligation…these abuses by the executive power cannot affect the universally binding force of TK rulings,” said SN judge Aleksander Stępkowski, quoted by the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna daily. However, the validity of the SN’s resolution is itself contested as it was issued by judges whose own status is questioned. That is because they were appointed to the court through the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS) after it was overhauled by PiS in a manner that brought it under political control and rendered it invalid, according to Polish and European court rulings. The current government has generally rejected decisions issued by such “neo-judges”, as it calls them. And that position was reiterated on Thursday by justice minister Waldemar Żurek, who wrote that “the neo-judges in the Supreme Court have adopted a so-called resolution”. “Any decision issued with the participation of even one person appointed through the politicised National Council of the Judiciary after 2017 is a non-existent judgement,” he added. Neosędziowie w Sądzie Najwyższym podjęli nibyuchwałę połączonych trzech izb (III CZP 41/26), uznając, że nieopublikowane rozstrzygnięcia Trybunału Konstytucyjnego mają moc powszechnie obowiązującą, a za wyrok TK można uznać tylko taki wydany przez osoby, które złożyły ślubowanie… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 18, 2026 The SN’s resolution comes as the TK itself is embroiled in a crisis. At the end of October, the eight new TK judges chosen by parliament this year took control of the tribunal and announced that its chief justice, Święczkowski, had been suspended for failing to fulfil his duties. Święczkowski, supported by Nawrocki and the SN’s chief justice, Zbigniew Kapiński (also a “neo-judge”), has rejected that move as an illegal “coup d’état” and claims he is still in charge of the tribunal. However, police have prevented him from entering the building. On Wednesday, just as the SN was issuing its resolution, the eight government-backed TK judges announced that they had lifted Święczkowski’s immunity from prosecution at the request of Żurek.
