World.title: EU, UK in ‘landmark deal’ on food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions
World.content:
The European Union – United Kingdom summit on November 20 produced a “landmark deal” on food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions, but negotiations on university student fees – with the EU wanting its students to pay the same as British students in the UK – are to continue.

The joint statement, announced at a joint news conference by European Commission President António Costa, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, is part of efforts to “reset” the relationship between the bloc and Britain, 10 years after Brexit.

Costa said: “A strong partnership between the European Union and the United Kingdom is a strategic investment in Europe’s security. But it is also an investment in our shared prosperity, in innovation, competitiveness and resilience. Because there can be no strong defence without a stronger economy”.

“There is much more we can achieve together. We are not competing against each other, we are building win-win solutions together,” Costa said.

The European Union is a union of sovereign nations which respects sovereign natures, he said: “We respected the sovereign decision taken by the British people in 2016”.

“And I recall the words of the European Council after the referendum. We regret but we respect. And we will equally respect whatever decision the United Kingdom takes about the future of its long-term relationship with the European Union,” he said.

“Of course, we follow with great interest the debate you have relaunched about our common future. And as you know, we remain open to have the closest possible relationship between the European Union and the United Kingdom.”

Von der Leyen said: “We know the world around us is changing fast, making a closer and stronger partnership between the European Union and the UK the more important. And indeed, the spirit of our cooperation is win-win. Our economies are deeply connected.”

“Last year, we agreed on an ambitious agenda, and today we are delivering. First, we are bringing our people closer together. From next year on, the United Kingdom will once again take part in Erasmus+,” Von der Leyen said.

She said that negotiations had been concluded on a youth experience scheme. “It will allow 100 000 young people from each side to spend up to three years in each other’s countries. To work, to study, to volunteer, to simply travel.”

Von der Leyen said that negotiations had been concluded on an agreement on food and other agricultural products: “This is a big success. It is a two-way street”.

“For our businesses on both sides of the channel, it means easier trade and lower costs. And for our consumers, it means more choice and more affordable food, so lowering the living costs. We have also concluded negotiations to link our carbon markets.”

“The agreement will cut emissions, and it will generate investments in cleaner industries. It will help us advance our shared climate goals. Work also continues towards the United Kingdom’s participation in our electricity market,” Von der Leyen said.

Burnham said: “We’re 10 years on from Brexit, but I think we can all confidently say this is a good day for Britain, and this is a good day for Europe”.

“The agreement that we’ve reached together is a win-win. And it is in tune with public opinion in the UK. People can see the status quo isn’t working,” Burnham said.

“It’s not good enough for Britain. Three quarters of people say that they favour closer ties with Europe, according to the most recent polls. And that is because we’ve had a decade of drift, too much division, low growth in the economy, and higher prices in the shops,” he said.

“They want a better deal than the hard Brexit we ended up with. And today, together, we have delivered that better deal. As I say, it will be good for people in Britain, and good for people in Europe,” Burnham said.

“It directly addresses the biggest challenges of our times, and the biggest worries that people have. The cost of food. The cost of energy. The lack of growth in the economy, and the cost of doing business. The levels of illegal immigration. And the challenges facing our young people.”

Ffor people who are worried about the cost of the weekly shop, this deal will help, he said.

“By cutting the costs of exporting, it will help relieve pressure. At the moment, it can cost up to £1400 to export a single shipment of salmon. And obviously, that’s too high, and it will bring costs for business down.”

The deal would bring the cost of food down “and nd it opens up the possibility of lower electricity costs”.

There are so many businesses out there who are worried about the cost of doing business, Burnham said.

Burnham said that Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey had “confirmed today that the UK Treasury has said that the deal struck here will add up to 0.5 per cent to UK GDP”.

“That is a £17 billion boost to the British economy. It is the single biggest growth measure that we could take in this Parliament,” Burnham said.

Brexit did take away opportunity from our young people, he said.

“And I can say to the young people of Britain, you will have, as a result of this deal, a new freedom. For anyone under 31, you will have much greater ease and ability to travel to any of the wonderful 27 member states of the European Union to live, to work, to study,” Burnham said.

“And that is such a positive note that we’ve been able to strike between ourselves so that the next generation can feel finally that people in our positions are directly doing something to recognise that they need more help and that they need more opportunity in their lives.”

Burnham said that a bill would be introduced in the British Parliament next week to implement this aspect of the deal.

(Photo: Council of the EU)

World.title: Two Russian missiles, Russian drone crash in Poland
World.content:
Two Russian missiles and a Russian drone have fallen in Poland, Minister of National Defence Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz told a news conference on November 20, as quoted by his ministry.

One missile exploded in Nowy Lipowiec, the other in Rudnik nad Sanem, and the drone in Mołodycz.

“This attack by the Russian Federation on Ukrainian territory, with its impact on the Republic of Poland, was one of the largest since the beginning of the full-scale war in Ukraine,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said.

He said that the missile that fell in Nowy Lipowiec, Biłgoraj County, was a Kh-101 missile.

“Throughout the night, our and allied pairs of on-duty jets operated – Polish F-16s and Swedish Gripens. Our pilots had a Dutch Air Force refueling aircraft at their disposal in the air. Our reconnaissance system, a Saab early reconnaissance aircraft, was also activated and operating in the Podkarpackie and Lublin Voivodeship,” he said.

Patriot systems located around Jasionka Airport in Rzeszów and near Świdnik in the Lublin region have been activated, as had the Poprad and Pilica+ ground systems.

Helicopters are also participating in the operation, as they continue to operate in the air, as are three brigades of the Territorial Defence Forces.

“We are dealing with another provocation by the Russian Federation,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said.

“In my opinion, the date is not accidental. Today, the Coalition of the Willing exercises are taking place, involving several countries on Nowa Dęba near these locations,” he said.

“The Coalition of the Willing exercises, the presence of the Defence Ministers of France, Great Britain, and the Baltic states, eight chiefs of staff led by our most important allies. It seems the coincidence of these events is no coincidence,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said.

“I will go to our allies, also with a request that they see what we have been facing here every day, every week, every month for four years. The threat to Nato and provocations from Russia are very serious. I will also request that the Alliance, the Secretary General, allocate additional forces and resources to support Operation Eastern Sentry. There are soldiers here from allied countries, for example, the Czech Republic, but more support is needed.”

We will not be intimidated, he said: “We will continue our actions, protecting above all our citizens, the Republic of Poland, and the strength of our Alliance”.

World.title: European prosecutors charge individual in 213.7M euro fraud probe into rail modernisation in Bulgaria
World.content:
The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) in Bulgaria has filed an indictment in the Sofia City Court against one suspect, following an investigation into a project for the modernisation of the Bulgarian railway infrastructure, EPPO said on November 19.

The project, which concerns parts of the railway section between Sofia and Plovdiv, is worth more than 213.7 million euro in EU financing.

The contract for the execution of the project was awarded to a consortium formed by three companies.

The accused is the legal representative of a company participating in the consortium.

According to the investigation, through the manager of the consortium, he submitted false information to the National Company Railway Infrastructure (NRIC) regarding the company he represented to illegally obtain EU funds.

His conduct enabled the consortium to be eligible to and to be awarded in 2019 the EU-funded grant agreement amounting to 213 714 235.14 euro.

Between 2019 and 2024, a total of 68 213 186.03 euro was paid out by the NRIC to the consortium, co-financed by the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the national budget.

In particular, the accused used the manager of the consortium, who had no knowledge of the relevant criminal circumstances, to declare that the company was not subject to insolvency proceedings. In reality, based on the evidence, it was declared insolvent already in 2012.

The investigation was supported by Bulgaria’s Interior Ministry National Police General Directorate and the State Agency for National Security.

Numerous searches and seizures were carried out throughout the investigation across various locations in Bulgaria, including company headquarters and private residences. Documents concerning the tender procedure and its implementation were also seized.

The initial crime report was submitted by OLAF, which also conducted a complementary investigation, EPPO said.

(Archive photo: NRIC)

World.title: Arrests in Bulgaria, the Netherlands and Poland in probe into multimillion euro VAT fraud
World.content:
At the request of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) in Munich, three suspects were arrested this week in an investigation into a multimillion VAT fraud, EPPO said on November 19.

The arrests took place in Bulgaria, the Netherlands, and Poland. Searches and seizures were also carried out in those countries.

The criminal organisation under investigation is suspected of operating a cross-border VAT carousel fraud – a complex criminal scheme that takes advantage of EU rules on cross-border transactions between its member states, as these are exempt from value-added tax.

It is understood that they sold AirPods via companies and missing traders based in Germany and Bulgaria.

The activities of these suspects alone may have caused an estimated tax loss of 23 million euro in Germany.

With the support of national authorities from Bulgaria, Germany, the Netherlands and Poland, searches were carried out at the premises of the suspects and companies under investigation.

These investigative measures are part of investigation Midas , targeting a transnational criminal organisation behind a 195 million euro VAT fraud scheme involving the sale of smartphones, small electronic devices and protective face masks.

(Archive photo: Interior Ministry)

World.title: Over 300 Italian Companies With Over 20,000 Employees Operate in Croatia
World.content:
November the 23rd, 2026 – Over 300 Italian companies with over 20,000 employees operate across Croatia, with economic ties between Croatia and Italy constantly strengthening.

In crucial sectors of the Croatian economy, more than 300 companies with Italian or mixed capital operate today, and according to estimates by the Italian-Croatian Chamber of Commerce (THGK), they employ more than 20,000 people. Marin Penavic reports for Poslovni that Croatian-Italian economic ties are strengthening further this year, given that over the first seven months of 2026, goods trade grew by as much as 13.4 percent.

Last year, good trade reached almost €8.5 billion, representative of 3.2 percent more than the year before, meaning that Italy remains Croatia’s second trading partner and one of the leading foreign investors. These figures were presented by representatives of the Chamber and Italian diplomacy at a ceremonial awards ceremony at the Sheraton Hotel in Zagreb, which brought together the Croatian-Italian business and diplomatic community. Prime Minister Andrej Plenković addressed the guests via video message.

Speakers also included THGK President Aldo Di Biagio, Italian Ambassador Paolo Trichilo and Director General of the Assocamerestero association Domenico Mauriello. The ceremony was also attended by State Secretaries Goran Romek and Zdenko Lucić, as well as Member of Parliament of the Italian national minority Marin Corva.

Di Biagio emphasised that behind the economic indicators stand concrete people. “Twenty thousand employees means twenty thousand families who look to the future with peace and security. For Italian companies, investing in Croatia means creating concrete opportunities, developing skills and returning value to the community,” the Chamber President said.

At the ninth ITA CRO Business Awards, Valamar Riviera, Carel Adriatic, WAM Adria and Bora Nera Specialty Coffee were awarded. A special recognition went to the Consul General of the Republic of Croatia in Milan, Stjepan Ribić, while Andrea Perkov received an Italian state decoration.

World.title: Claude Can Now Send SMS and Viber Messages via Croatia’s Infobip
World.content:
November the 23rd, 2026 – A Croatian company and the country’s first unicorn has taken things to new heights. Claude can now send SMS and Viber messages through Infobip.

In the shadow of largest public share offering in history announced recently, that of Anthropic, one important piece of information remained that positions Croatia even more strongly on the global AI map. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that Infobip is a partner of Anthropic, the company behind Claude, which has just completed the largest IPO in history. The collaboration with the Croatian technology company brings new capabilities to Claude: through Infobip’s platform, AI agents can send SMS and Viber messages and track their delivery.

This is a concrete example of Infobip’s role in the global AI ecosystem. The new integration enables sending messages via SMS, RCS, MMS and Viber through a single connector. It uses Infobip’s send and check_status tools, which allow AI agents to initiate message sending and check their delivery status. In this way, communication with users can be directly included in automated business processes.

For companies developing applications based on agent artificial intelligence (agent AI), the connector enables use in various business scenarios, from sending order confirmations and delivery notifications to reminders for scheduled appointments. Instead of developing and maintaining separate integrations for each communication channel, users can now simply include Infobip’s communication services in their Claude workflows.

Infobip was founded back in 2006 in the Istrian town of Vodnjan as a small startup. It has grown into Croatia’s first unicorn (a private startup valued at more than one billion US dollars) and one of the largest technology hubs in the region. Today it operates on six continents through over 70 offices and employs more than 3,500 experts. It develops globally recognised products and services for many world brands and technology platforms, including Nvidia, Anthropic, SpaceX, OpenAI, WhatsApp, Microsoft, Oracle, Adobe, Meta, Viber, Deutsche Telekom, Virgin Atlantic and Nissan.

World.title: Zadar and Munich to Remain Connected Throughout Winter
World.content:
November the 23rd, 2026 – Zadar and Munich will remain directly connected throughout the winter schedule thanks to Croatia Airlines.

Croatia Airlines will continue to connect Zadar and Munich during its winter timetable. Karlobag.eu reports that this popular route is being co-financed by the tourist boards of the City of Zadar and Zadar County, and enables passengers to travel directly to Bavaria as well as make connections via Munich Airport.

options for onward travel through munich as a global hub

Croatia Airlines is maintaining its direct air link between Zadar and Munich during the winter 2026/2027 timetable, thereby continuing the connection of Zadar Airport with one of the more important European traffic hubs. According to the official schedule of the national airline, flights are planned from the 26th of October 2026 to the 26th of March 2027, on Mondays and Fridays. The route is jointly co-financed by the Tourist Board of the City of Zadar and the Tourist Board of Zadar County. Maintaining it during the winter months is important for Zadar’s transport accessibility outside the main tourist season, as well as for passengers who use Munich as a starting point for onward international travel.

two weekly departures during the winter schedule

The winter schedule provides for two weekly flights, enabling passengers to plan travel between the two cities even during the period of reduced tourist traffic. It is particularly significant that the direct connection is maintained after the end of the summer season, when the air transport offer from some regional airports is usually different than during the busiest tourist months. As stated above, the Zadar route is listed in the winter timetable starting on the 16th of October 2026 and ending on the 26th of March 2027. In the display of the summer 2027 timetable, this route is not listed. The Tourist Board of the City of Zadar presented the service in its announcement as year-round connectivity, but the carrier’s official table currently confirms operations during the winter period. For travel planning it is therefore important to check the availability of flights for a specific date, especially for bookings that cover different seasonal periods.

an important winter link between a coastal croatian airport and a major travel hub

One of the most important advantages of this air link is the possibility of onward travel via Munich. Munich Airport is one of the significant European aviation hubs through which passengers can arrange connections to numerous international destinations. The Tourist Board of the City of Zadar highlights precisely this transport role of Munich as an important reason for maintaining the direct connection. This possibility is particularly useful for passengers whose final destination is not Germany but other European or world cities accessible by connecting air routes. Instead of organising a separate arrival at a larger airport, passengers can start their journey from Zadar and continue it via the Munich hub. Direct flights also enable arrival in Bavaria without an additional transfer at the beginning of the journey.

joint tourist board funding

Maintaining the route is part of activities aimed at improving the transport accessibility of the Zadar area throughout the year. The Tourist Board of the City of Zadar and the Tourist Board of Zadar County participate in its co-financing, thereby supporting air connectivity with an important European market.

According to the announcement of the Zadar Tourist Board, this air link is important for extending the tourist season and the accessibility of the destination outside the summer months. Maintaining international flights during the winter can be significant for different forms of travel, including business arrivals, shorter city breaks and travel related to international events. The availability of a direct route is one of the elements that influence the possibility of organising travel in a period when tourist traffic is traditionally weaker. The co-financing also shows the role of tourist boards in the development of the destination’s transport connectivity. Their cooperation with the airline is part of a broader effort to ensure that Zadar is not viewed exclusively as a summer air destination, but as a city accessible to visitors during other parts of the year as well.

zadar airport’s new passenger terminal

In addition to maintaining international air connectivity, an important part of the development of Zadar’s airport infrastructure is the modernisation of passenger capacity. According to information from the Tourist Board of the City of Zadar, the new departure terminal at Zadar Airport was put into operation in June 2026 as part of a larger investment cycle. The improvement of airport infrastructure and the maintenance of international routes are two connected elements of air traffic development. The new terminal represents an infrastructural change in the passenger part of the airport, while the winter connection with Munich expands travel possibilities outside the main part of the tourist year. For passengers planning a trip it is important to follow the current Croatia Airlines schedule because the times and availability of individual flights may change. The confirmed winter schedule currently provides for traffic on Mondays and Fridays, and the possibility of onward travel via Munich remains one of the main advantages of this international connection.

World.title: Forest the Size of 3,740 Football Pitches Has Disappeared in 3 Croatian Nature Parks
World.content:
November the 23rd, 2026 – Forest the size of 3,740 football pitches has completely disappeared across three Croatian nature parks.

Zagreb-based programmer and entrepreneur Lada Kovjanić, who attracted public attention in early October with an interactive map of the disappearance of forest cover on Medvednica, has expanded her research to several other large forest areas in Croatia. Slobodan Muftic reports for Index that according to her new analyses published on the portal šume.eco, in the nature parks Lonjsko polje, Papuk and Kopački rit alone over the past decade or so, a reduction in tree crowns has been recorded on almost 2,700 hectares – an area corresponding to approximately 3,740 football pitches.

a new portal tracks changes to forested areas across croatia

“As I announced, I’ve opened a special portal that will over time enable insight into all larger forest areas throughout Croatia, with a particular emphasis on protected areas such as nature parks,” Kovjanić explained, adding that the changes indicated by her research are not necessarily the result of illegal logging. “I didn’t deal with questions of legality and justification, but exclusively with the change, i.e. the disappearance of forest cover for any reason over the past decade or so. I analyse satellite photographs during spring, when vegetation is at its densest, and compare them with previous years.”

The largest changes were recorded in Lonjsko polje Nature Park, where analysis of satellite images from the period from 2016 to 2026 established the complete or partial removal of tree crowns on as much as 1,246.09 hectares, or an area corresponding to 1,745 football pitches. This is an area known for valuable floodplain forests of pedunculate oak, ash and alder, which are among the most important natural assets of Lonjsko polje. Worrying proportions are also shown by the map of Papuk Nature Park, where between 2017 and 2026 a reduction in tree crowns was recorded on 914.68 hectares. In Kopački rit the analysis records 509 hectares, or 713 football pitches, fewer high tree crowns than back in 2017.

According to the data published by Kovjanić, in the area of Lonjsko polje, Papuk and Kopački rit alone a reduction in tree crowns was recorded on a total of 2,669.85 hectares, which corresponds to an area of approximately 3,740 football pitches.

“lonjsko polje has suffered the most”

“The purpose of this tool is to show on which cadastral parcels the greatest changes have occurred and to determine who manages that forest. Lonjsko polje has suffered the most. There is quite a lot of clear-cutting, areas where there is no longer any forest, in Kopački rit and Papuk. A lot was damaged in storms and due to disease, but logging is not negligible either,” Kovjanić explains. Her analysis is based on images from the European Sentinel-2 satellites, and only zones larger than 0.3 hectares (one hectare has 10,000 square metres) are included in the published total areas. Smaller changes and selective felling of individual trees therefore remain outside the display.

croatian forests claims there are serious shortcomings in interpreting the data

In their response to an enquiry sent to them about the mapping of Medvednica, where according to Lada Kovjanić’s analysis around 150 hectares of forest – an area larger than 206 football pitches – disappeared over nine years, Hrvatske šume (Croatian Forests) stated that there are “serious shortcomings in the interpretation of the published data.”

“Areas that were already arable land, agricultural land, urban areas or infrastructure facilities before 2000 have also been marked as lost forest. Likewise, the areas marked in red include parts of the surface where young forest is located, which is poorly visible on satellite images,” Hrvatske šume emphasise, adding that individual displays of open areas cannot automatically be interpreted as permanent forest loss. “I believe that transparency is in everyone’s interest and that is why I invite Hrvatske šume and all interested parties to cooperate. I think this technology could help introduce order into forest management, both of state and private forests,” says Kovjanić.

“old forests disappearing is particularly concerning”

“The trend of disappearance of forest cover, especially old forest with trees higher than 20 metres that takes more than a hundred years to regenerate, is quite worrying. Since 2001 Croatia has lost 85,983 hectares of old forest, or almost six percent of its total area. These are forests that will not regenerate in our lifetimes and this affects the entire ecosystem.” Official data shows that forest areas across Croatia are increasing. According to the results of the Second National Forest Inventory, presented in June this year, the area of forest land increased from 2.378 to 2.431 million hectares compared with the previous inventory, while the total growing stock decreased slightly, from 552 to 548 million cubic metres.

However, an increase in the area under forest does not necessarily mean that the area of old and ecologically valuable forests is also growing. Abandoned agricultural areas can grow into young forest or scrub, while the restoration of old forest habitats can take decades, and sometimes significantly longer.

might a third of mature croatian forest vanish?

Old trees have hollows, thick cracked bark and dead wood on which woodpeckers, owls, bats and rare insects such as the stag beetle and the oak longhorn beetle depend. Old and mature forest also protects soil and water and holds the most carbon. Such habitats form only after a hundred or more years, according to the šume.eco website.

It is important to emphasise that the recorded reduction in tree crowns does not automatically mean that the forest has disappeared forever on all those areas. Changes can be the result of regular forest management, storms, drought, disease, natural processes or other interventions. The maps primarily show where the forests have changed and enable the competent institutions and citizens to check what actually happened in those areas. If the felling of old forest continues at the same pace as in the past five years, by the end of the century a third of such forest that existed back in the year 2000 will disappear. According to Kovjanić’s additional analysis, on around 40 percent of the areas where a loss of high forest cover was recorded between 2001 and 2005, the tree crowns had still not reached a height of ten metres by 2020. This shows how long the recovery of high forest cover can take.

World.title: Blows for Zagreb Airport as Five Airlines Reduce or Cut Flights
World.content:
November the 22nd, 2026 – There have been some serious blows dealt to Zagreb Airport recently, as five airlines reduce or completely cut flights. The tourism minister, however, assures that this isn’t the whole picture.

Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that a series of bad news in recent weeks has hit Zagreb Airport. First, about a month ago, Austrian Airlines announced that it would cancel the Vienna–Zagreb route after more than 40 years of operation.

no more zagreb-vienna after 40 years, reduced service from qatar airways and more

The last flight on this route is planned for the 10th of January 2027. The departure of the Austrian carrier represents a loss for Zagreb Airport because the route offered not only a direct connection with Vienna but also the possibility of onward travel to numerous European and overseas destinations via the hub in the Austrian capital. Of equal, if not greater, weight is the move by Qatar Airways, which has reduced the planned number of flights between Doha and Zagreb for the summer 2027 schedule. Instead of the originally planned daily flights, according to the latest changes the company will operate four times a week. Qatar Airways will thus retain the same number of flights it operates on this route during the current winter schedule, as well as in the recently completed summer season. This is a significant reduction in capacity on one of the key routes from Zagreb.

Via its hub in Doha, Qatar Airways enables passengers from Croatia to fly to numerous destinations in Asia, Australia, Africa and other parts of the world. The reduction in frequencies therefore affects not only the direct Zagreb–Doha link but also onward travel possibilities, writes the specialised portal Croatian Aviation. In the meantime, three more carriers have launched bad news for Zagreb. British Airways has decided to cancel the London–Zagreb route. British Airways, one of the largest European airlines, is discontinuing the route that connected London Heathrow Airport with Zagreb. For years this route was part of the British Airways network and served as a direct link between the two cities, as well as for onward travel to international destinations via the London hub.

The Spanish national airline will significantly reduce the number of flights on the Zagreb–Madrid route in the summer 2027 schedule. The new version of the schedule shows a noticeably smaller number of weekly frequencies, a later start and a considerably earlier end of seasonal operations compared with 2026.

Iberia had planned to resume operations to Zagreb at the end of March 2027, when the new summer schedule comes into force, with four weekly rotations in April and five weekly rotations in May. However, the company subsequently withdrew from sale all flights planned from the end of March to the beginning of June, thereby significantly delaying the start of operations compared with the original plans and this year’s schedule. Finally, in recent days Air France has also reduced the number of planned flights between Paris and Zagreb for the summer 2027 schedule. It has withdrawn a total of 43 return flights from sale. These are flights planned from the 28th of March to the 4th of July 2027. Air France has withdrawn three weekly afternoon departures (on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays) from sale, and passengers can no longer book tickets for those flights.

“the number of routes for next year is increasing at the national level”

Minister of Tourism and Sport Tonči Glavina believes that the changes at Zagreb Airport are not an indicator of the overall state of air traffic in Croatia. According to his announcements, the number of routes at national level should increase next year. “The number of routes for next year at the level of the entire Republic of Croatia is increasing; from most markets we will retain the same number of routes or we will have an increased number of routes,” Glavina stated.

Optimistic announcements are also coming from the Croatian National Tourist Board. HTZ Director Kristijan Staničić emphasises that the establishment of new air connections with the British market is expected, primarily to airports on the Adriatic. “I can only confirm the words of our partners, tour operators and airlines that there will be new routes from the British market to Dubrovnik, Split and Pula and that this will certainly affect the increase in tourist traffic from those markets,” Staničić said.

World.title: Lipovljani – The Croatian Town With 10 National Minorities
World.content:
November the 22nd, 2026 – Lipovljani is a continental Croatian town that rarely gets much of a mention, but it is home to as many as 10 national minorities. Known as “Little Europe”, Lipovljani is worth talking about.

For more than a century now, the descendants of Czech, Slovak and Ukrainian settlers who still nurture the cultural heritage of their ancestors have lived in a place not far from Novska. As Antonio Ivcevic writes for Putni kofer, if you asked someone where in Croatia you might find a place called “Little Europe,” they would likely not think of a small settlement near Novska. They might mention Zagreb, Rijeka or some Istrian town where different cultures have intertwined for centuries. Yet, this interesting nickname is proudly borne by Lipovljani, a small place in continental Croatia with fewer than 2,000 inhabitants, but a history that even much larger cities cannot boast of. For generations, Croats, Slovaks, Czechs, Ukrainians and members of many other peoples have lived here side by side.

different european cultures come together in a tiny pocket of continental croatia

Lipovljani is located near Novska and Kutina. According to the latest 2021 census, the settlement itself has 1,902 inhabitants, while the entire municipality has 2,807. Although it is a smaller place with typical family houses, a school, churches, shops and a park in the centre, the history of this area is truly impressive. Lipovljani is known for its large number of national minorities. Local tourist and historical accounts mention as many as 10 national minorities living in the municipality. The most numerous are Ukrainians, followed by Slovaks and Czechs, while among the residents there are also members of the Serbian, Albanian, Bosniak, Hungarian, German, Slovenian and Italian national minorities.

how lipovljani became little europe

To understand why Lipovljani received this nickname, we have to go back to the 19th century. At that time, economic conditions in this part of Croatia were changing, forestry was developing, and people in search of work and better living conditions came from different parts of the then Habsburg Monarchy. Among the settlers were Slovaks, Czechs, Ukrainians, Germans and Hungarians. They arrived with their families, knowledge, language and customs. Some engaged in agriculture, others in crafts and forestry. Over time they built their homes here, started families and began to create a new life. Their children went to school and grew up together, neighbours socialised, helped one another and gathered at celebrations. Although they came from different parts of Europe, everyday life connected them, and the customs and traditions they brought with them gradually became part of the life of the whole place.

from the ukrainian cultural centre to the slovak ethno house…

One of the places where this history can be particularly well discovered is the Slovak Ethno House. It is located in Željanska Street and is a traditional building housing an ethnographic collection dedicated to the life of the Slovak community. Old furniture, household utensils and various small items that were once part of everyday life are preserved there. These old objects can help us imagine how people once lived, prepared food, furnished their homes and carried out their work before modern kitchens, electrical appliances and shops became something we take for granted and use every day.

The Ukrainian community also plays a major role in the cultural life of Lipovljani. The Ukrainian Cultural and Educational Society “Karpati” was founded back in 1992, and its members nurture Ukrainian song, dance, language and gastronomic tradition. The same applies to the Czech community. Today’s Czech Beseda Lipovljani was founded in 2004 with the aim of continuing the tradition of the former Czechoslovak Beseda. Through its singing, music, folklore and other groups it gathers residents who want to preserve the cultural heritage of their families. Of course, all these stories are best experienced at the Lipovljani Gatherings, a wonderful event held every August and at the same time the largest event in Croatia dedicated to national minorities

World.title: Filipino Nationals Get Busy Learning Croatian Language
World.content:
November the 22nd, 2026 – Filipino nationals are getting busy learning the Croatian language as new rules loom next year. They are by far the most numerous foreign workers actively learning the language at the moment.

Just over six months separate Croatian employers and foreign workers from the 4th of June 2027, when the legal obligation to prove basic knowledge of the Croatian language and Latin script (level A1.1) comes into full force as a condition for extending residence and work permits. As Marija Brnic reports for Poslovni, as the deadline approaches, employers are increasingly focused on organising classes, which is most clearly confirmed by figures from the Croatian Employment Service (HZZ).

filipino workers are the most numerous language learners

Since the start of shorter informal Croatian language learning programmes for foreigners in April 2024, a total of 2,312 vouchers have been awarded. This year their number has grown many times over compared with previous years. While only 102 vouchers were awarded in 2024 and 259 in 2025, as many as 1,951 vouchers have been approved during 2026. According to the HZZ, interest has been more or less constant throughout this year, with around 200 vouchers awarded each month. The structure of the awarded vouchers shows in which sectors employers are most counting on the long-term retention of foreign labour. Since seasonal workers are legally exempt from the language exam requirement, the greatest interest unsurprisingly comes from activities with year-round operations. The processing industry leads with a share of 34.5 percent, followed by construction with 22.9 percent, hospitality with 21.8 percent and the food industry with 15.5 percent.

Viewed by country of origin of the participants, the vouchers are most often used by workers from the Philippines, who make up more than a third of all users (36.9 percent). They are followed by citizens of Nepal with a share of 29.5 percent and India with 15.7 percent, which together account for more than 82 percent of all approved vouchers for learning Croatian. The regional distribution of users brings another interesting piece of data that explains the dominance of the processing industry. The county with the largest number of voucher users is not the most populous and economically strongest City of Zagreb, but Međimurje County with 437 participants.

In general, the largest share of users is concentrated in the northwest of the country – in addition to Međimurje, Varaždin, Zagreb and Krapina-Zagorje counties stand out, i.e. the regions with the most developed manufacturing and processing base and a constant need for the long-term retention of workers. At the very bottom of the ranking is Vukovar-Srijem County, where only two users of vouchers for learning Croatian have been recorded so far.

the financial data speaks volumes

How much this year’s wave of applications has surpassed the previous two years is also visible from the financial data. Since the start of the voucher scheme for learning Croatian for foreigners, a total of €612,909 has been reserved, of which €342,792 has so far been paid out to educational institutions. The overwhelming majority of the funds were contracted precisely in 2026 – this year €527,784 has been reserved, while €260,527 has so far been paid out for completed classes. The difference between the reserved and paid amounts also shows that a significant part of this year’s participants are currently in the process of learning and that payment for the programmes is expected after the courses are completed.

Co-financing via vouchers, depending on the conditions and the size of the employer, can amount to between 30 and 70 percent of the education costs. The average value of a voucher awarded so far has been €283, with the cost varying depending on the activity and the specialisation of the vocabulary. The highest average amounts were recorded in the healthcare sector (€340) and construction (€321), while in the most used processing industry the average voucher amounted to €278. That employers are increasingly viewing the learning of Croatian not only as a pure administrative obligation but more and more as a strategic part of human resources management and worker retention is also confirmed by the Croatian Chamber of Economy (HGK). This trend is supported by the results of its EDUkarijera 2026 survey, conducted among 572 employers from various economic activities.

Among companies that already employ or plan to employ third-country nationals, as many as 81 percent highlight learning Croatian as an important measure for the easier integration of workers. At the same time, 62 percent list difficulties with their adaptation within the organisation itself as one of the main challenges of employing foreigners, which is why investment in language skills is becoming key both for productivity and for safety at work.

the language programmes are designed by sector

Anita Stipić, head of the Labour Market Department at the HGK, explains how the system works in practice, emphasising that the model is well organised, but that the right to a voucher is not automatic and depends on meeting the prescribed conditions. The submission of applications itself is fully digitalised through the Moj vaučer system, and the HZZ is obliged to assess a complete application within 10 working days.

As a particularly positive aspect, Stipić highlights the fact that Croatian language learning programmes are designed according to the specific needs of individual activities, including construction, tourism and hospitality, processing and food industry, healthcare and social care, transport, telecommunications and personal services. Such sectoral orientation is key because language needs are not the same for all occupations – a worker in hospitality needs different communication situations and professional terminology than a worker in production, construction or healthcare. Within the HGK, she notes, there is also a Community for Lifelong Learning, which brings together adult education institutions and actively works on connecting the education sector with the concrete needs of the economy.

World.title: Where Will the Snow Fall in Croatia Next Week? New Map Published
World.content:
November the 22nd, 2026 – Snow is set to fall in Croatia next week, but there are areas far more likely than others to turn into a winter wonderland.

In the middle of next week, a noticeable change in the weather is expected, bringing snow and lower temperatures. Index reports that according to the latest forecasts, on Thursday the 26th of November, snow should fall across a large part of the interior.

snow or rain?

The Croatian Meteorological and Hydrological Service (DHMZ) has published a forecast map showing the expected precipitation for Thursday. Areas marked in pink are those where more than one centimetre of snow is predicted, covering the interior and mountainous regions. On the coast and islands, marked in green, rain will fall.

colder temperatures

In addition to the type of precipitation, continental and coastal areas will also differ in temperatures. Although it will be colder everywhere than this week, the biggest drop is expected in the interior, where temperatures will fall below zero. The Meteorological Institute, in its forecasts up to the 28th of November, predicts that the lowest temperature in Zagreb, Osijek, Karlovac and Varaždin will be –4 °C. In Gospić –5 °C is expected, in Vukovar –3 °C, and in Rijeka –1 °C.

World.title: Bear spotted in Tartu's Ropka district, police urge caution
World.content:
A bear was seen on the banks of the Emajõgi River in Tartu's Ropka district on Sunday morning. Police said the animal may have returned to the forest.

The bear was first seen between Kaupmehe tänav and Ropka tee in the south of the city.

South and East Prefectures Operations Manager Jaanus Kokkonen said: "Today at 8:29 a.m., the Emergency Response Center received a report that a bear was roaming in the Ropka Park area of Tartu. Police officers responding to the scene located the animal on Aardla tänav. From there, the bear moved along the footpath through Ropka Park to Turu tänav, then on to Tehnika tänav and subsequently to a large wasteland that police could not access by patrol car. The animal then moved toward the Emajõgi River."

Police officers blocked the bear's possible path towards more densely populated parts of the city, and the animal continued toward Uus-Ihaste, he added.

"Later, an eyewitness reported that the bear may have been moving in the Iirise tänav area. Police and hunters checked possible routes both on foot and using a drone, but the bear has not been seen since," Kokkonen said.

Police patrols are currently monitoring the area to determine whether the animal has returned to the forest.

People must not approach the animal, attempt to photograph or film it, or block its path. Pets should also be kept away from the area, and pedestrians should choose an alternative route if possible.

If you spot the bear, call the emergency number 112.

World.title: Tallinn high school may restore historic name
World.content:
The most popular suggestion in the public competition to rename Tallinn Central Russian High School is to restore its historic name, Elfriede Lender High School.

School Principal Ingar Dubolazov told Vikerraadio's "Vikerhommik" program that, since 68 percent of children at the school are already studying in Estonian, its current name no longer properly reflects the school. The issue of changing the name was raised unanimously by the school's teachers' council.

The public naming competition received more than 60 submissions on its first day alone, from academics and professors as well as the school's own pupils. By far the most popular suggestion so far has been Lender High School, referring to the school's location in a building on Kreutzwaldi tänav, completed in 1935 and specifically designed for Estonian teacher Elfriede Lender's (1882–1974) private school.

Other suggestions have included Kreutzwaldi High School and Kesklinna High School.

The principal said he had met with alumni of the historic Lender High School and believes preserving its heritage is very appealing. However, he wants the community to make the decision together.

A state of Elfriede Lender in Tallinn. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"There are schools named after individuals, but there are relatively few schools named after women," Dubolazov noted. He added that several teachers working at other Tallinn schools have already written to him expressing their willingness to come and work at the school if its new name is linked to the building's distinguished history.

Transition to Estonian-language education

Behind the name change and the transition to Estonian-language education is also the practical need to halt the decline in pupil numbers. Over the past four years, the school has lost a quarter of its pupils, around 300 children, as families who speak other languages at home are increasingly enrolling their children in long-established Estonian-language schools. While the school previously admitted four first-grade classes, only two were opened this year.

"If we do nothing now, in a few years we will have another 200 to 300 fewer children, and then the school operator may start asking us why we need two buildings," Dubolazov said.

The principal hopes the name change will also help increase the number of pupils at the school.

"There are many people who do not work at this school today and are not descendants of any of its alumni, but who care about this history and have great respect for it. This building has value in its own right, and we very much want to preserve it. In a sense, that is also one of the reasons behind this change, because we want to keep this building for ourselves and our school," he said.

Ingar Dubolazov Source: Janek Luts/ERR

Dubolazov confirmed that the school's longer-term goal is to become a unified Estonian school, where children who speak Estonian at home will also be welcome to study.

"Definitely in the future. That is where we want the entire transition process to take us. The transition to Estonian-language education is the first step toward the much-discussed unified Estonian school, where children can receive a high-quality education in Estonian together, regardless of their mother tongue," the principal said.

As a first step, the school will open classes next autumn in which Estonian will be taught according to the native-language curriculum, as many current pupils already have a sufficiently good command of the language.

The school is accepting name suggestions, together with explanations, at nimi@tkvg.ee until the evening of November 30. On December 1, a committee comprising pupils, teachers, parents and alumni will meet to select a proposal to be submitted to the Tallinn City Government for approval.

World.title: Russian ship attack is a consequence of Russia's actions, says Estonia's FM, PM
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said that Saturday morning's drone attack on a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland is a side effect of Ukraine's self-defense in Russia's war of aggression. Officials once again denied that Estonian airspace is being used to carry out attacks.

A Russian cargo ship, the Sparta II, caught fire after being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish waters. The Finnish armed forces said it is "likely" that Ukraine is behind the attack.

Tsahkna said Estonia is closely monitoring the situation in the Gulf of Finland and is in close contact with the Finnish authorities.

"At Finland's request, Estonia has sent the Navy vessel Kindral Kurvits to assist with rescue operations, including firefighting and pollution response," Tsahkna said.

He also spoke with his Finnish counterpart Elina Valtonen on Saturday. "We are coordinating every step with our northern neighbors and acting decisively," the minister said.

The Russian ship Sparta II on fire in the Gulf of Finland. Source: Finnish Border Guard

"Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine is being felt increasingly close to Europe. Today's incident in the Gulf of Finland is another side effect of Russia's war of aggression and Ukraine's self-defense, and Ukraine has the right to defend itself," he stressed.

Tsahkna also confirmed that Estonia has not given any foreign country permission to use its airspace or maritime areas to conduct military operations, a common narrative spread by Russia.

"We take every violation of our maritime and air borders extremely seriously and are acting decisively together with our allies to ensure Estonia's security," Tsahkna said.

The foreign minister added that Estonia faces no immediate military threat and that the level of military threat to Estonia has not increased in light of this incident.

"The Estonian Defense Forces, together with our allies, take the situation seriously and are always ready to respond appropriately to any incidents to ensure the security of the Estonian state and people," Tsahkna said.

PM: Estonian airspace is not being used for attacks

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) also denied the accusations.

"It is also important in the current situation to clearly reiterate the facts. Estonia has not given permission for its airspace or maritime areas to be used for attacks against Russia," he wrote on social media.

Michal added that he had spoken with Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on Saturday about the situation in the Gulf of Finland.

The consequences of fighting Russia's aggression have reached the Baltic Sea. Another signal for the aggressor to stop. But nothing will stop us from supporting Ukraine. Estonian Navy vessel Kindral Kurvits has responded to Finland's request for assistance with the rescue operation involving a Russian vessel in the Gulf of Finland. Finland can always count on Estonia. That's what friends and neighbours are for. We stand ready to provide any further assistance needed, and I'm keeping in close touch with @PetteriOrpo as the situation develops. — Kristen Michal (@KristenMichalPM) November 21, 2026

"The consequences of fighting Russia's aggression have reached the Baltic Sea. Another signal for the aggressor to stop. But nothing will stop us from supporting Ukraine," he said.

"Finland can always count on Estonia. That's what friends and neighbours are for. We stand ready to provide any further assistance needed," the prime minister added.

On Saturday morning, the Estonian Police and Border Guard Board's (PPA) Aviation and Maritime Rescue Coordination Center received a signal that the dry cargo ship Sparta II, belonging to an agency of the Russian Ministry of Defense, had been hit and was on fire.

The ship then drifted out of Estonia's exclusive economic zone, entering Finland's exclusive economic zone and later Finnish territorial waters.

World.title: Tallinn's Kino Sõprus expands into former Club Hollywood smoking lounge
World.content:
Historic arthouse cinema Kino Sõprus is expanding into adjacent space formerly used as a smoking lounge by neighboring nightclub Club Hollywood, its manager said.

The renovation to the Tallinn landmark follows a roughly 30 percent jump in audiences this year, and aims to restore the 1955 building's bright original waiting halls for socializing and small events.

Speaking to "Ringvaade," Sõprus manager Gert Põrk said the cinema has been working hard to draw viewers back through curated special screenings which have been designed to make going to the movies more than just watching a film.

Kino Sõprus in Tallinn. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

The expansion comes as the future of the next door Club Hollywood remains unclear. The nightclub announced at the start of the year that it planned a conversion into an event center, and its social media shows its last parties had taken place in May. Representatives of the Sõprus building's owners did not respond to ERR inquiries.

"The cinema building's architect originally intended for this side of the house to have very bright waiting halls, and we are trying to restore that original space — albeit in a slightly more modern and distinctive key," Põrk said.

Crews have demolished the old smoking-room structures, painted the walls green, completed electrical work, and are halfway through the arduous process of restoring the original flooring before furnishing the lounge.

Põrk added that audiences increasingly treat cinema as a social venue to discuss films before and after screenings and host small gatherings — starting with a country party following a Dolly Parton tribute screening.

World.title: Estonian Navy: More attacks in the Gulf of Finland cannot be ruled out
World.content:
Navy Commander Commodore Ivo Värk on Saturday said further attacks in the Gulf of Finland cannot be ruled out and that conducting warfare in international waters is entirely legitimate for both Russia and Ukraine.

A Russian ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after a drone strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment. The crew was evacuated on Saturday night.

ERR: What operations are currently underway involving the Sparta II?

Ivo Värk: Salvage operations are continuing, led by the Finnish Maritime Rescue Coordination Center. Estonian, Russian Federation and Finnish vessels are at the scene. Efforts to extinguish the burning ship are still underway from a distance. The ship's crew has been evacuated onto a Russian Federation merchant vessel. Russia has one rescue vessel at the scene, and another is on its way.

Has it become clear what cargo the ship is carrying? The ship is still burning. Could the cargo also pose an explosion risk?

We do not know exactly what cargo the ship is carrying, but we do have information that there is a certain amount of flammable cargo on board.

The Russian ship Sparta II on fire in the Gulf of Finland. Source: Finnish Border Guard

Põlev Vene kaubalaev Sparta II Soome lahel. Autor/allikas: Soome piirivalve

How long is the fire expected to last? Can it be extinguished in a day or a week?

It is difficult to say or speculate about that. It depends on what is burning on the ship and how many firefighting resources are available at the scene. At the moment, all of this can only be done from a distance. There is nobody on board the ship fighting the fire.

How is cooperation between Finland, Russia and Estonia working? What does it look like at sea, and what role are the Russians playing? After all, they want to recover the ship?

The Finnish Maritime Rescue Coordination Center is coordinating operations with the Russian side. Cooperation between them is fully functioning and in place. Information is being exchanged and activities are being coordinated. We are simply participating in this operation with our rescue resources at the moment.

Is the [Estonian vessel] Kindral Kurvits at the scene, and what role is it playing in this incident?

The Kindral Kurvits is at the scene and carrying out rescue operations. At the moment, it is working alongside other rescue vessels to extinguish the burning ship from a distance.

Is this now the new reality, that further similar attacks can be expected in the Gulf of Finland?

That cannot be ruled out. Whether it is the Gulf of Finland, the Black Sea or even the Mediterranean Sea, everything outside the territorial waters of coastal states is an entirely legitimate place for both warring parties to conduct their military operations.

World.title: Police catch teenager gang stealing from restaurants across Estonia
World.content:
A group of teenagers who stole from pubs and restaurants across Estonia has been apprehended by police, but the City of Pärnu is still trying to tackle youth behavior.

In recent weeks, several restaurants in Pärnu, Tallinn and Viljandi have been broken into at night. Vandals broke into Aleksandri pub in Pärnu late on Tuesday evening.

"First they put a crowbar in and tried to force it open, damaging all the edges, but it's a very good, strong door and it held. But there's nothing you can do against a crowbar. They smashed a hole right through here, put a hand inside and opened the thumbturn, and that was that," said Aleksandri pub owner Andres Mathiesen.

A new security door costs around €6,000, plus installation. Although insurance covers the costs, the time and effort involved are many times greater than the value of what the intruders stole.

"Completely pointless. These days, there's no cash register, no money. What do you expect to get? They took half a bottle of Vana Tallinn," Mathiesen said.

In Pärnu, restaurants Rööm and Tuju, the R-kiosk at the bus station, and the Kastrul and Kohvila cafés have also been broken into in the same way. Police have caught the vandals, who are boys aged 14 to 17 from Tallinn and are already known to police.

"What has become typical recently is that they come from difficult family circumstances, and unfortunately that is a key factor in this case. Their aim was actually to get money. They then used the cash for things they liked, taking taxis from one city to another and enjoying themselves," said Hisko Vares, head of the proceedings division at the Lääne-Harju Police Station.

There are approximately 400 minors with behavioral problems in Estonia. Vares believes the state should take this situation seriously.

Throwing firecrackers

Another problem is also keeping police busy in Pärnu. Young people gather in groups in the city center and throw firecrackers at passersby. Most of them are 11 to 12 years old.

"According to them, they are protesting against the police confiscating scooters. They want them back. It seems they have nothing else to do with their free time," said Karin Uibo, head of the Pärnu regional group at the Western Prefecture.

Pärnu Mayor Siim Suursild himself became caught up in the events last Friday. On Tuesday, city officials met with police officers.

"Clearly, young people have this need for adventure and to test themselves. We've all been young and we know what it's like. We've discussed finding other ways for them to spend their time," Suursild said.

Families, schools, the police and the city must find a solution together. Police are urging parents to keep track of how their teenagers spend their free time. When hanging around in gangs of so-called "city kids," a child can be endangered by pyrotechnics even if they are simply watching.

World.title: Russian cargo ship on fire in Gulf of Finland after reported drone strike
World.content:
A fire broke out aboard the Russian dry cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday morning, with Russian officials claiming the vessel was struck by two drones.

Finland's prime minister has confirmed on X the Sparta II had been hit by drones, adding Ukraine has the "right to fight back" against the aggressor.

According to the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA), explosions which rocked the vessel took place when it was in Estonia's economic zone but within the area of ​​responsibility of the St. Petersburg Maritime Rescue Center and in shipping lanes open to international vessels, with the vessel later drifting north into Finnish waters.

Finland's Border Guard is leading rescue and spill preparation and said in a statement that the damaged vessel, which is on fire, drifted from international waters into Finnish territorial waters in the eastern Gulf of Finland, adding that the situation poses no danger to other shipping. The border guard is coordinating maritime rescue and potential oil-spill response with domestic and international authorities.

Finland's Ministry of Defense had earlier said the attack took place in international waters, left the ship damaged, and prompted Finland to notify its allies as border guard units headed to the scene.

On X, Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote: "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity. The Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor".

Russian arms transport ship Sparta II on fire on the Gulf of Finland. It was most likely struck by Ukrainian drones or missiles. https://t.co/WYkr6yJqd7 — Petri Mäkelä (@pmakela1) November 21, 2026

Estonia's Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) aeronautical and maritime rescue coordination center first received word of a fire and preliminary reports of explosions aboard the Russian-owned dry cargo ship Sparta II at 9:35 a.m. on Saturday. According to a PPA statement cited by Finnish public broadcaster Yle, the vessel had departed from St. Petersburg.

PPA duty officer Andres Tiik said Estonian authorities are monitoring the incident alongside Finnish counterparts and will respond if Russia requests international assistance. No marine pollution has been reported so far.

When the incident began, the Sparta II was operating in an international shipping lane 11 nautical miles north of Estonia's Vaindloo Island, inside the St. Petersburg maritime rescue coordination zone. Current data indicates the vessel drifted out of Estonia's exclusive economic zone at around 10 a.m.

Ukrainian military intelligence has classified the Sparta II as a vessel that has carried weapons and military equipment, and the ship is on the U.S. sanctions list.

The Sparta II, the Russian cargo vessel which caught fire on the Gulf of Finland Saturday. Source: SCANPIX/REUTERS

Earlier, Leningrad Oblast Governor Alexander Drozdenko claimed on Telegram that two drones struck the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship in neutral waters three nautical miles from Russia's border, and that crew evacuation was underway while damage was being assessed.

Meanwhile, the Finnish Defense Forces imposed temporary sea and air traffic restrictions in the Gulf of Finland twice on Saturday, Yle reported — first from early morning until 7:43 a.m., then again around 9:30 a.m. Finland's General Staff said the reimposed restrictions were not tied to a single acute threat, but were a precaution against Ukrainian drones straying into NATO airspace, a risk that also prompted an early-morning EE-ALARM warning in northeastern Estonia.

Russian media reported that more than 60 drones were shot down overnight in Leningrad Oblast.

PPA spokesperson: Ship's bridge was on fire before it drifted into Finnish waters

In an afternoon update, Estonian PPA duty officer Andres Tiik said explosions set the Sparta II's bridge on fire before the vessel drifted north into Finnish territorial waters, where Finnish authorities have likely evacuated the crew. Tiik added that the PPA raised the readiness level of its rescue helicopter, though Russia's St. Petersburg maritime rescue coordination center never requested assistance.

The Finnish Border Guard also said it has been in contact with Russian maritime rescue authorities as part of its response. Meanwhile, Russian media updated its overnight toll to report that 80 drones were shot down in Leningrad Oblast.

Editor's note: This piece has been updated to include confirmation from Finnish authorities that the vessel drifted into Finnish territorial waters, comments from Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, and background on the Sparta II and its sanctions status, and to include updates on the emergency response to the incident.

World.title: Gallery: Estonia's largest solar park opens in Risti with 340,000 panels
World.content:
Estonia's largest solar park has opened in Risti, Lääne County, with enough capacity to cover the annual electricity consumption of roughly 90,000 households.

Built by renewable energy firm Sunly at a cost of €125 million, the 244-megawatt site is set to expand into a hybrid energy hub with battery storage, wind and a data center.

Spanning 270 hectares with 340,000 panels, the facility is the second largest in the Baltic states. Sunly CEO Priit Lepasepp noted that 90,000 households equals the combined populations of Tartu, Narva and Pärnu.

A substation is already complete and battery park construction has begun with Rolls-Royce, while a wind farm and major data center are also in the pipeline. Lääne-Nigula Mayor Janno Randmaa welcomed the local community payments and future tech jobs tied to the project.

Rapid solar expansion in Estonia has pushed installed solar capacity past annual peak demand, driving summer midday power prices to zero. Lepasepp said standalone solar or wind farms are no longer viable, noting Sunly will earn revenue from frequency regulation and selling stored battery power when gas-fired electricity is expensive.

State-owned rival Enefit has paused standalone solar projects, with Baltic business development head Johann-Gustav Lend agreeing that future sites require hybrid setups paired with large on-site power consumers.
