World.title: King Faisal Specialist Hospital treats 288 patients with genetically modified t-cell therapy
World.content:
RIYADH: King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre (KFSHRC) has treated 288 patients with genetically modified T-cell therapy (CAR-T) as of the end of October 2026, reflecting its growing expertise in advanced immunotherapies for certain blood cancers.

The patients included 251 adults and 37 children, with pediatric cases accounting for about 13 percent of the total.

CAR-T therapy involves extracting immune cells from a patient's blood, genetically modifying them to recognize and attack cancer cells, and then reinfusing them into the body.

KFSHRC has also advanced its treatment delivery and manufacturing capabilities, shifting from reliance on international suppliers to local production. Two patients have received locally manufactured CAR-T therapy following the first dose administered in a Phase I clinical trial in 2025.

The move has reduced production and delivery times from 28 days to less than 14 days and lowered costs from about SR1.3 million to SR250,000, a reduction of nearly 80 percent.

The hospital said the improvements are expected to expand access to advanced treatment and reduce reliance on external manufacturing.

The development forms part of efforts to localize advanced therapies in line with the National Biotechnology Strategy, which aims to position Saudi Arabia as a global hub for life sciences innovation and advanced biotechnology industries.

World.title: More remains recovered in the search for 34 workers missing after an Indonesian candy factory fire
World.content:
JAKARTA, Indonesia: Rescue teams searching for 34 missing workers after a fire swept through a candy factory in Indonesia recovered human remains in 24 body bags, though authorities said Sunday it was too early to determine the death toll.

The National Search and Rescue Agency earlier said the fire killed at least three workers. However, in its latest statement, it said the recovered remains and body parts still required forensic examination and identification.

The blaze at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory in Banten province was largely contained Sunday, but some areas were still inaccessible.

The fire started around 5 p.m. Saturday and flames engulfed the three-story building in the Serang district of Banten province, which borders the capital, Jakarta.

Fifteen fire trucks, supported by water cannons, were deployed to battle the flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the fire began, said Rizky Dwianto, an operations official at the Banten Search and Rescue Agency. A joint rescue team, including police, the military, the Indonesian Red Cross and volunteers, was at the scene.

A drone view of emergency services personnel gathered near body bags outside a PT Fonusa Agung Mulia factory following a fire, in Cikande, Serang regency, Banten province, Indonesia, November 22, 2026. (REUTERS)

Debris littered the floor of the burned-out structure, including twisted metal and blackened, corrugated iron roofing.

The cause of the fire wasn’t immediately known. Survivors said the flames originated from a cooling unit on the third floor, local media reported.

Five workers were injured and 34 remain missing

The factory produces Milkita, an Indonesian brand of milk-based candies and snack products exported to more than 40 countries worldwide.

The company’s chief executive, Steven Wijaya, told a joint news conference with authorities in Serang on Sunday that about 300 workers were inside the factory compound, with 65 workers believed to have been in the affected area when the fire broke out.

He said as of Sunday afternoon, 24 workers had returned home.

“We are deeply concerned by this tragedy,” Wijaya said. “We have established a hotline for relatives seeking information on missing family members and are maintaining regular communication with affected families.”

Wijaya said that the factory regularly conducted emergency and evacuation drills in conjunction with local firefighters. He said that the facility had adequate evacuation routes and fire protection systems, including hydrants and water reserves, that complied with applicable safety standards and were functioning at the time of the fire.

In a statement released late Sunday, authorities said 63 people were believed to have been in the area at the time. Of those, 29 were confirmed alive, including five hospitalized with injuries, while 34 workers remained missing.

Authorities collect DNA samples for identification

The condition of the victims made visual identification impossible, prompting authorities to urge family members to provide DNA samples and other information that could be used to identify their loved ones, said Wahyu Hidayati Dwi Palupi, who heads the National Police’s victim identification division.

She said that body bags containing the remains of the victims were transferred to a hospital for identification.

Although the blaze had largely been contained Sunday, firefighters were carrying out intensive cooling operations before they could access all parts of the factory, said Tubagus Mahfud, operations chief of the Serang fire department.

“We are conducting sweeps in the areas that have already been brought under control,” Mahfud said. “Parts of the structure had collapsed, while poor lighting conditions required firefighters to proceed cautiously.”

He also said that the factory’s production materials could cause the fire to reignite, making it critical to complete cooling operations.

Anxious relatives waited for news outside the burned-out factory.

Indonesia has experienced a series of deadly industrial fires in recent years, raising concerns about workplace safety standards and emergency preparedness at manufacturing facilities in the country.

World.title: Canada’s PM Carney enlists fake Trump for laughs at annual press gallery dinner
World.content:
OTTAWA, Ontario: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shared the stage with a fake Donald Trump and another version of himself this weekend, enlisting comedians to help roast the US president and Canadian politicians at an annual dinner with journalists.

“I am pressing the emergency comedy button,” Carney said Saturday as comedian Mark McKinney appeared impersonating the prime minister, followed by Mark Critch playing Trump.

Critch recreated Trump’s trademark forceful handshake, exchanging grips with Carney and McKinney onstage.

Carney also poked fun at Trump’s lavish makeover of the Oval Office.

“This is a tough room. And I’ve been in the Oval Office. Alone. With its new interior decorator,” Carney said.

Since returning to the White House, Trump has filled the Oval Office with gold accents, gilded decorations and portraits.

The annual Parliamentary Press Gallery dinner is Canada’s version of a Washington political roast, where politicians and journalists trade jokes and insults.

Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre took aim at former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau’s relationship with American pop star Katy Perry, joking that Trudeau was doing to a “faded pop princess” what he had done to Canada during his decade in power.

The remark drew criticism online as sexist and demeaning toward Perry.

Gov. Gen. Louise Arbour, a former Supreme Court justice who represents Britain’s King Charles III as Canada’s head of state, mocked Carney’s extensive international travel.

“Do you know the difference between God and Mark Carney? God is everywhere, and Mark Carney is everywhere except in Ottawa where he’s supposed to be,” she said.

World.title: Flamingos flock to Al-Lith, highlighting Saudi Red Sea coast’s rich marine life
World.content:
JEDDAH: Flocks of greater flamingos have gathered along the shallow waters of Al-Lith on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast, adding a splash of pink to the shoreline and highlighting the governorate’s growing appeal as a destination for marine wildlife and nature tourism.

The migratory birds, locally known as fenteer, have been seen wading close to shore on their long pink legs, feeding in the shallows or taking flight in groups, creating a striking spectacle for visitors and photographers, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Sunday.

Their seasonal presence reflects the ecological richness of Al-Lith, where tidal flats, sheltered coastal waters, islands and coral reefs provide habitats for an array of marine life and migratory species.

Prof. Khalid Ali Asiry of King Abdulaziz University's Faculty of Environmental Sciences told SPA that greater flamingos visit the Red Sea coast, with their numbers typically increasing during autumn and winter, although some remain throughout the year.

The receding tides expose mudflats and shallow feeding grounds where the birds use their curved bills to filter small crustaceans, algae and microorganisms from the water and mud. Quiet coastal areas also provide resting places along their migratory routes.

Flamingos are social birds that gather in areas with abundant food, with changes in water levels sometimes prompting large numbers to congregate at a particular location, Asiry said.

He emphasized the importance of protecting their feeding and resting grounds, minimizing disturbances and monitoring their numbers to better understand how environmental changes influence their migration and distribution, SPA reported.

A coastline frequented by more than flamingos

Flamingos are far from the only wildlife visitors to Al-Lith. The governorate’s islands and coastal waters have also witnessed appearances by dolphins, sea turtles, tropical fish and a variety of migratory birds, underscoring the area's ecological importance.

In January, successive pods of dolphins appeared near Al-Lith's beaches and waterways, leaping and moving through the water in scenes that attracted visitors, marine enthusiasts and photographers, according to an earlier SPA report.

The sightings highlighted the appeal of the governorate's marine environment, with the dolphins' presence reflecting the richness of the surrounding ecosystem and offering opportunities for responsible wildlife excursions, nature photography and environmental exploration.

The islands also provide nesting habitats for sea turtles, particularly green turtles, while their surrounding waters host diverse tropical fish and extensive coral reef formations.

The Four Sisters and the Red Sea's natural wealth

Al-Lith's marine biodiversity is particularly evident around its Four Sisters islands — Marmar, Dohrab, Malatu and Jadir — which form part of an integrated coastal ecosystem along the southern shores of Makkah Region, SPA reported in July.

The islands feature clear waters, pristine beaches and extensive coral reefs that support marine life, maintain ecological balance and provide breeding grounds for numerous species.

Their importance extends beyond marine habitats, serving as nesting grounds for sea turtles and seasonal stopover sites for migratory birds moving across the region, according to SPA.

The largely unspoiled environment has also made the islands attractive to diving enthusiasts and visitors seeking opportunities to explore coral formations and observe wildlife in its natural surroundings.

Tourism potential rooted in conservation

Al-Lith's natural assets offer opportunities to expand marine tourism through diving, wildlife observation, boat excursions, nature photography and environmental exploration.

Potential investments include eco-lodges, diving centers and marine services designed to accommodate visitors while minimizing the impact on fragile habitats.

Such development could support local communities, generate employment and strengthen economic activities linked to the blue economy, while preserving the natural resources that underpin the governorate's tourism appeal.

The Saudi Red Sea Authority oversees the regulatory framework aimed at safeguarding marine resources and promoting sustainable development along the coast.

The development of Al-Lith's islands forms part of wider efforts to expand tourism along the Kingdom's Red Sea coastline, improve quality of life and establish Saudi Arabia as a destination for sustainable tourism, SPA reported.

For Al-Lith, the flamingos gathering along its shores, dolphins gliding through its waters and turtles nesting on its islands offer more than seasonal natural spectacles. Together, they showcase a coastal environment whose ecological value and tourism potential are closely intertwined — and whose long-term appeal depends on preserving its biodiversity.

World.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 11 in Kyiv region
World.content:
DYMER, Ukraine: Rescuers in Ukraine raced on Monday to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike, after overnight attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 11 people.

Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year.

An overnight strike on Dymer, around 45 kilometers (30 miles) north of the capital, hit a five-story building, killing at least eight people, according to Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko.

AFP images showed rescuers combing through the mound of smoldering rubble.

“Rescuers extricated the eighth body of a person killed by Russians in Dymer,” Tkachenko wrote on Telegram on Monday.

“Search and rescue operations continue.”

Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager and a woman in her forties.

Rescuers managed to pull out a child alive on Sunday evening, Tkachenko said on Telegram.

State Emergency Service said earlier they were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were “not responding or cannot be reached.”

Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets called the attack part of “Russia’s genocidal war against Ukraine.”

“The world must stop looking away. Condemn this terror, hold Russia accountable, and act now to stop the killing of innocent Ukrainians,” he said on X.

Two other people were killed and eight wounded in Vyshneve when a Russian strike hit a supermarket.

“People had simply gone to the store to buy groceries. An ordinary shopping trip turned into a tragedy due to a Russian attack,” Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine’s Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said on social media.

Moscow has ramped up strikes on Ukraine — particularly on its energy network — as temperatures begin to drop to around freezing.

Earlier this week, Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a “painful” response to Ukrainian strikes that damaged the Crimean bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule over the annexed region.

World.title: UN urges probe into Benghazi attacks, warns Libya against becoming battleground
World.content:
BENGHAZI, Libya: The United Nations mission in Libya on Monday called for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation into attacks at Benghazi Seaport and off the eastern Libyan city’s coast, warning against actions that could drag the country into wider regional conflicts.

The UN Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) expressed serious concern over Sunday’s incidents, stressing that Libya’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and the security of its citizens and assets must be respected.

It urged all parties to exercise restraint, refrain from circulating unverified information or politicizing the incidents while investigations are underway, and avoid escalatory rhetoric or actions that could fuel domestic tensions.

“Libya can not afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the mission said in a statement posted on X early Monday.

A combination of satellite images shows a Russian corvette and the northern port area before (above) and after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, with the latter image showing the vessel capsized, in Benghazi, Libya, November 21 and 22, 2026. (Vantor/Handout via REUTERS)

The incidents included an explosion aboard a Russian naval vessel docked at Benghazi’s naval base, which the eastern-based Libyan government said was suspected to have been caused by a drone attack.

Ten Russians and Libyans sustained minor injuries and were receiving treatment, medical sources said.

Satellite imagery provider Vantor identified the vessel as the Merkury, a Russian Navy corvette. Images taken Sunday showed most of the ship had capsized and sunk, leaving only its bow visible above the water, with smoke and debris around the pier.

The Russian ship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply on its way back to Russia, according to the eastern-based government, which condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety.

Later Sunday, a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel was struck by a drone boat off Benghazi’s coast, according to Libyan military sources. Naval forces rescued its crew, some of whom sustained minor injuries.

Libyan naval and air forces also intercepted more than 20 drone boats off the coast that evening, the sources said.

The eastern-based government has requested an international investigation, with Prime Minister Osama Hamad calling for scrutiny of suspicions that the drone boats originated from western Libya and for verification of the alleged presence of Ukrainian experts in the country.

The incidents come amid heightened maritime tensions linked to the Russia-Ukraine war. Ukraine has repeatedly used naval drones and missiles against Russian warships and naval facilities, primarily in the Black Sea.

Russia has previously accused Ukraine of targeting Russian-linked vessels in the Mediterranean, including an LNG tanker allegedly attacked by naval drones launched from the Libyan coast in March.

UNSMIL said it stood ready to assist Libyan authorities with the investigation, adding that the incidents underscored the need to reunify national institutions and strengthen their ability to safeguard sovereignty and security.

The mission called on all actors to act responsibly, preserve stability and build on progress in the political process toward a lasting settlement.

• With Reuters

World.title: 9 people shot at a central California concert; 1 in critical condition
World.content:
Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday.

The shooting broke out around 7:30 p.m. Saturday at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare County, a mountainous region in the center of the state, the county sheriff’s department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced.

One 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and required surgery. He remained in critical condition, the sheriff’s department said. Two other victims ages 19 and 22 also required surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries.

Authorities said that they believe the shooting “may be gang-related” but didn’t elaborate. The show in the town of roughly 3,000 people featured performers from neighboring states, the department said.

The department didn’t immediately respond to emailed questions seeking further details but said there was no longer any immediate threat to the public.

World.title: Automation system problem at Delta causes flight delays as Americans travel for Thanksgiving
World.content:
Well over half of Delta Air Lines flights were experiencing delays Sunday afternoon following a problem with an automation system during a busy time for travel ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

The airline said its teams were using manual workarounds to get flights off the ground while they continued to work to restore automation of a system that calculates weight to ensure an aircraft isn’t too heavy to fly. Hours later, Delta said that system was once again working, though flights were still not back to normal. About 1,000 of the airline’s flights were delayed as of Sunday afternoon.

Earlier Sunday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued about an hourlong ground stop to some flights into Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is Delta’s hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.

Complying with the weight and balance limits of an aircraft is critical to flight safety, according to an FAA document, and going above the limit can compromise the structural integrity of the aircraft.

The agency said on X that the delays weren’t related to FAA air traffic systems.

Earlier this month, a malfunction in the FAA’s network led to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. The stop lasted for more than four hours, and carriers canceled and delayed swaths of flights as they worked to recover. Just days after that, United Airlines saw its own system outage — forcing it to delay departing flights.

The Delta delays come as Americans have been encountering a growing number of problems with technology that are increasingly disrupting their lives.

As of mid-afternoon Sunday, the flight-tracking website FlightAware said 67 percent, or about 1,000, of Delta’s flights were delayed. FlightAware said that 54 percent of flights out of the Atlanta airport were delayed while about 50 percent of flights destined for the airport were delayed.

Delta said about 70 percent of the delays and cancelations noted by FlightAware were connected to the automation issue and the rest were because of inclement weather.

By mid-afternoon Delta was apologizing for the delays, and said it was rebooking customers and providing meals and hotel rooms where needed, and offering refunds if a flight was canceled. According to FlightAware, 2 percent of the airline’s flights were canceled.

World.title: Miami blow past Thunder, Hawks down Pistons in NBA action
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Miami Heat romped past the injury-hit Oklahoma City Thunder 123-113 to extend their winning streak to seven games in the NBA on Sunday.

Miami, who started without the injured Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin strain), took full advantage of a depleted Thunder line-up to record a wire-to-wire win.

Bam Adebayo led Miami with a triple-double, finishing with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists with two steals and three blocks.

Pelle Larsson added 21 points while Nikola Jovic scored 15 from the bench as seven Miami players finished in double figures.

“Coming into the game, obviously one of your best players is out of the game, so the next player has to step up – and that was me,” Adebayo said, referring to Antetokounmpo’s absence.

“We took care of business. I didn’t like how we finished the fourth quarter, but a W (win) is a W,” Adebayo added.

“We’re getting stops, we’re running in transition, we’re sharing the ball and guys are making plays for one another.”

Miami improved to 10-6 for the season after the victory while Oklahoma City, who were without reigning NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, fell to 10-7.

The Atlanta Hawks meanwhile improved to 11-6 with a 107-97 defeat of the Detroit Pistons.

Nickeil Alexander-Walker rattled in six three-pointers to finish with 27 points as Atlanta erupted in the fourth quarter to extend their winning streak to four games.

Detroit trailed by 10 points midway through the second quarter, but rallied to lead by as many as 13 in the third quarter before taking an 11-point advantage into the final frame.

But Atlanta flipped the script in the fourth quarter, embarking on an 18-0 run to take the lead before outscoring the Pistons 33-12 to surge to victory.

Isaiah Joe led Detroit’s scoring with 19 off the bench but Cade Cunningham was restricted to just five points while serving up 15 assists.

World.title: Pochettino demands response from ‘painful’ Man Utd debut
World.content:
Liverpool – Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card.

Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak.

United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick.

Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974.

“It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino.

“We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.”

Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro.

“I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino.

“At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.”

– ‘Changes the game completely’ –

A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes.

However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half.

“It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro.

“There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international.

“It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.”

Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory.

Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time.

“It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola.

“We have missed some clear chances today. In other games you will remember those chances, but today we’ve controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box.”

World.title: Iraq offers $33 per barrel discount for December oil sales
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi oil is once again being offered at significant discounts for shipments that will be loaded in December 2026, as challenges related to crude oil exports from the country’s southern ports persist.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has decided to offer Basra crude shipments with discounts reaching as much as $33 per barrel.

These offers cover both Basra Medium and Basra Heavy crude grades for loading in December, with buyers left to determine the specific quantities they wish to purchase.

These new discounts follow similar offers for October shipments—which reached as high as $37 per barrel—as Baghdad seeks to maintain its oil export flows amid rising shipping and insurance costs, as well as risks associated with navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

SOMO views the discounts on Iraqi oil as an opportunity to market shipments of Basra crude for this coming December, particularly with the ongoing crisis related to the restricted passage of tankers through the strategic waterway.

The offers include Basra Medium crude at a discount of $29.20 per barrel and Basra Heavy crude at a discount of $33 per barrel.

The discounts have narrowed by $5.30 per barrel for Basra Medium crude and by $4 per barrel for Basra Heavy crude compared to oil shipments in October.

World.title: Three Premier League talking points
World.content:
London – Mauricio Pochettino suffered a torrid return to the Premier League as Manchester United’s new manager watched his side thrashed 4-0 at Liverpool.

Xabi Alonso’s problems mounted as Chelsea were humbled by Leeds, while Manchester City spluttered again.

AFP Sport looks at the key talking points from this weekend’s action:

Pochettino’s baptism of fire

Mauricio Pochettino has waited a decade to be handed the Manchester United job, but he could not have made a worse start to his reign.

The Argentine’s decision to give Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start for nearly a year alongside Lenny Yoro in central defence spectacularly backfired in a brutal demolition at arch rivals Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes after a De Ligt error allowed Alexander Isak to race clear on goal.

Within five minutes the 10 men were 2-0 down as Dominik Szoboszlai fired home the resulting free-kick and Florian Wirtz turned home a cross from Rio Ngumoha.

Pochettino tried to limit the damage with the introduction of Harry Maguire after just 22 minutes, having dropping the England international in favour of De Ligt from the starting line-up.

Ngumoha and Victor Munoz added further goals but only wayward Liverpool finishing prevented a repeat of the 7-0 thrashing United suffered at Anfield three years ago.

Pochettino’s painful debut defeat keeps United second bottom of the Premier League table.

More tellingly, it gives Pochettino an early taste of the huge task he faces to turn around the fortunes of the fallen English giants.

‘Angry’ Chelsea won’t panic

Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia urged his team-mates to stick together after their humiliating 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday.

Leeds ended their 27-year wait for a Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in resounding style, sparking jeers from angry Chelsea fans at the final whistle.

It was a third defeat in four league matches for Xabi Alonso’s team who are marooned in mid-table and face a fight to climb back into the race to qualify for the Champions League.

“Everyone is very angry and disappointed. At home this is never the way you want to finish a game. We let them back in the game when we shouldn’t have,” Lavia said.

“This is something we will analyse and get better at. With these types of results, it feels like the end of the world, but we are not going to ring the bell now to say it’s a panic moment.”

Calling for a reaction in Friday’s trip to struggling Nottingham Forest, Lavia added: “This hurts. It needs to hurt so it provokes a reaction, and this is definitely going to help us for the next game.”

Man City must tighten up

Enzo Maresca challenged Manchester City to show more defensive resilience after their dismal run extended with a controversial 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday.

City needed a second-half equaliser from Elliot Anderson at the Etihad Stadium to avoid a fourth successive Premier League defeat after Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener.

City striker Erling Haaland also had a goal contentiously disallowed for kicking the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno.

Maresca is becoming increasingly concerned with third-placed City’s issues at the back, leading to 14 goals conceded in 11 league games.

“For sure we are conceding too many goals. We need to avoid that,” he said.

“Sometimes you need to win games 1-0, you need to keep clean-sheets and we are not able to do that.

“We concede almost 80 percent of our goals in the first 20 minutes, so there is something that we need to improve.”

World.title: Iran strike wounds two in Bahrain, Saudi condemns ‘criminal’ attacks
World.content:
Manama – Bahrain said Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on “a civilian industrial site” in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed on November 13 after a lull since early September.

“In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain… a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded,” Bahrain’s interior ministry said on X.

“His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition.”

Two residents told AFP they had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco.

In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked with missiles and drones US Patriot air defence systems at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic republic.

Tehran on Saturday said it had intercepted a US drone targeting Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategic maritime corridor at the heart of the war in the Middle East.

– Iran unveils missile launcher –

On Sunday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and the army both reported that two tankers had caught fire after hitting mines in the strait.

It was unclear whether they were referring to the same incident.

The US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.

British maritime agency UKMTO, meanwhile, said on Sunday it “received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman”, without providing further details.

The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the stalemated conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway and targeting vessels that cross without its authorisation.

The US military has been escorting ships through the strait, which carried one-fifth of the world’s oil before the war, and maintains its own counterblockade of Iranian ports.

On Saturday, Iran state television reported that Iran had unveiled a new missile launcher, and broadcast footage of senior military commanders touring an underground missile base.

“Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy,” said Majid Mousavi, head of the Guards’ aerospace forces.

He was shown with Guards chief Ahmad Vahidi riding through tunnels lined with military equipment.

– Houthi attacks –

Bahrain’s powerful neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday lambasted Tehran for its continued “brutal aggression” against Gulf countries.

The Saudi foreign ministry expressed on X “the strongest condemnation and denunciation… of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain”.

Saudi Arabia also announced early Sunday that it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis in the west of the kingdom.

The region is home to key energy infrastructure, including the oil terminal at the port of Yanbu, as well as the Jizan refinery, located in the far southwest of the country, near the border with Yemen.

Later on Sunday, the Houthis claimed responsibility for two attacks in Saudi Arabia. Their military spokesman Yahya Saree said on X that they targeted the Rabigh oil refinery on the Red Sea coast and a radar in Riyadh province.

Saudi Arabia has been battling a surge in attacks since fighting reignited in Yemen’s civil war in July, the latest front in the Middle East war.

Later on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen said it had intercepted and destroyed two drones launched by the Houthis towards the greater Riyadh and southern regions.

The Houthis have multiplied attacks against Saudi Arabia since October, targeting in particular its major oil installations and airports. They have also repeatedly struck the financial district of the capital Riyadh.

The coalition has also been striking Houthi positions in Yemen. Since July, hostilities have left more than 1,600 people dead and over 300,000 displaced in Yemen, the poorest country on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest UN toll.

World.title: Drone strikes hit homes, UN building in Sudan’s capital
World.content:
Khartoum – Drones struck Sudan’s capital Khartoum, damaging residential homes and a United Nations building on Sunday, witnesses and the world organisation said.

Explosions were heard in the area around Khartoum airport and other parts of the city from around 2:00 am until around 4:30 am.

A drone strike completely destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

“The drone attack at dawn today is a continuation of Ethiopian aggression against Sudanese territory, as the drones were launched from Ethiopia’s Bahir Dar airport,” the source told AFP.

Sudan has repeatedly accused Ethiopia of allowing attacks to be launched from its territory, a claim Addis Ababa has denied.

AFP footage showed a house reduced to rubble, with a security perimeter around the site. Pieces of furniture, household items and clothing were scattered among the debris.

Al-Nour Adam, who lives in the area, told AFP that upon entering the house after the strike, “we found a person lying on a bed, wounded in his left arm, chest and head”.

– ‘Where are we supposed to go?’ –

“The strikes are indiscriminate,” Adam said.

“A strike could hit while you are asleep. You might wake up to find your children gone… It is truly tragic. You cannot be certain of anything.”

Yasser Hassan, another resident, said that the occupants of the house “had only just moved in, after searching for shelter for a long time”.

“Then the drone struck them. Where are we supposed to go?”

Another witness reported that a drone hit the home of a mosque’s muezzin, the person who calls Muslims to prayer, in Jebel Aulia, around 45 kilometres (28 miles) south of Khartoum.

“People were trying to rescue family members trapped under the rubble,” the witness said.

The United Nations, meanwhile, said that “a UN premises with UN colleagues in the building was damaged”.

“This occurred in a civilian neighbourhood,” the UN’s humanitarian office (OCHA) said in a statement posted on X.

OCHA condemned the risk posed to humanitarian workers, saying it was “unacceptable” that UN personnel were being exposed to such danger.

– Drone warfare –

Authorities did not immediately report on casualties.

The conflict, which erupted in April 2023 between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese army, has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and triggered the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises.

The United Nations has repeatedly criticised both sides’ rampant use of drones, which killed more than 1,100 people in the first half of 2026.

Of the hundreds of child casualties this year, two-thirds were killed or injured by drone strikes, the UN said.

A Sudanese army drone strike killed 15 people, including four children, in a West Kordofan village days ago, as the army pushed through the state, recapturing territory from the RSF.

The rival forces have for the last year wrestled for control of the resource-rich southern Kordofan region, which connects the army-held centre and east to RSF-controlled Darfur.

In recent months, both the army and the RSF have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away without risking their fighters.

World.title: Four killed in power plant explosion in southern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – At least four people were killed and 35 others injured on Saturday following a massive gas pipeline explosion and fire at the al-Hartha thermal power station in southern Iraq.

The explosion took place around 6:00 a.m. local time at the Hartha power station, located north of the Basra province.

The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity mentioned that an explosion in a gas pipeline servicing the power plant was the cause of the fire.

According to reports, investigations are ongoing to determine the cause of the pipeline explosion.

Flames spread rapidly from the power plant to nearby trailers and informal homes.

Locals with burns and smoke inhalation make up the majority of the 35 injured, with officials warning that that the death toll may increase.

While Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Waheeb called for an emergency meeting to address facility repairs and power supply interruptions, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed the Health Ministry and the authorities in Basra to mobilize all available medical resources for the victims.

The power plant, which has a capacity of 800 megawatts and was producing about 400 megawatts before the incident, had to shut down entirely.

World.title: Iraq pushes to raise oil output to 10 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Sunday accelerated oilfield operations and extended working hours to advance Iraq’s push to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2032.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with Meg O’Neill, CEO of British Petroleum (BP), where he emphasized the importance of expanding the recovery of associated gas and ending gas flaring, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The development would bolster Iraq’s energy supplies and meet domestic consumption needs, according to al-Zaidi.

The meeting addressed the development of oil fields and the extension of exploration areas, particularly the Kirkuk field, the Eridu field in Dhi Qar, and the Rumaila field in Basra.

The discussion is part of the Iraqi government’s goal to increase production rates and produce 10 million barrels per day by 2032.

O’Neill affirmed BP’s readiness to expand its operations in Iraq, leveraging its advanced technical and technological expertise to increase production and develop oil fields in line with established plans.

Iraq produces 4.88 million barrels of crude oil per day, according to OPEC data for October 2026, which is based on official Iraqi figures.

BP is involved in projects to develop Iraq’s oil sector; in March 2025, the company signed a deal with the North Oil Company (NOC) and the North Gas Company (NGC) to develop and rehabilitate the Kirkuk fields.

Additionally, BP provides technical support for the development of the Rumaila field in Basra.

BP’s deal in Kirkuk is not limited to developing oil production; it also encompasses the development of gas resources and the establishment of projects to expand infrastructure and processing facilities.

Iraq continues to flare approximately 24 billion cubic meters of gas annually—according to World Bank estimates for 2025—despite its need for gas to provide fuel for power plants and reduce reliance on imports.

World.title: India-Iran bilateral talks: Cultural cooperation, manuscript preservation, joint SCO heritage network discussed on sidelines of forum
World.content:
India, Iran hold talks on cultural cooperation on sidelines of SCO forum

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India held bilateral talks with Iran on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum to explore avenues for cultural cooperation, with Tehran proposing the establishment of a joint network to preserve manuscripts and shared civilisational heritage.Union culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal confirmed the bilateral engagement on Sunday, saying the two countries remained in regular touch on areas of potential cultural exchange. He added that several ideas were discussed during the meeting, though no specific project had been finalised."There was a bilateral meeting with Iran. And India is in constant touch with Iran, and on areas in which there can be any cultural exchange, we are always in discussion. And discussions took place during the Summit too," Aggarwal told reporters at the historic Purana Quila, the venue of the three-day forum."Ideas have been thrown, though no such project has been concretised yet. But the discussions and engagements are on," he added.The Iranian Embassy in India, in a post on X on Sunday, said Tehran had proposed setting up an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilisational Memory" at the forum.Dr Faridoddin Faridasr, Cultural Counsellor of the Islamic Republic of Iran in India, addressed the First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, highlighting the importance of shared civilisational heritage as a foundation for cultural cooperation and mutual understanding among SCO member states, the embassy said.In his remarks, Faridasr emphasised the historical role of the Persian language as a language of science, literature, administration and cultural exchange across Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring regions, describing it as an important part of the shared cultural and historical heritage of the region.He also highlighted the work of the Noor International Microfilm Centre, affiliated with the Iranian Embassy in New Delhi, as an example of cultural cooperation between the two countries.Since 1990, the centre has collaborated with 72 academic and cultural institutions in India, resulting in the digitisation of "more than 150,000 Persian and Arabic manuscripts," the restoration and preservation of over three million pages of historical documents, and the preparation of nearly 300 catalogues, the embassy said.Faridasr also referred to ongoing joint projects with cultural institutions in Telangana and Hyderabad for the digitisation, restoration and preservation of historical Persian documents and manuscripts.Outlining the proposed SCO network as a practical initiative to strengthen regional cultural cooperation, the embassy said it would focus on preserving and digitising manuscripts and historical documents, exchanging technical expertise and providing training in manuscript restoration. It would also promote shared linguistic and literary heritage through joint research, publications and exhibitions.Faridasr reaffirmed Iran's "readiness to share its experience and technical expertise with other SCO member states", stressing that the preservation of shared civilisational heritage provided an opportunity to strengthen mutual trust, cultural understanding and cooperation across the region.Meanwhile, Aggarwal said no formal bilateral meeting took place between India and Pakistan on the sidelines of the forum, although members of the two sides interacted during banquets and conference sessions."There were no formal bilateral talks between the two sides," he said, responding to a question on whether any formal engagement had taken place between the two countries.He added that there were other "informal discussions" during the course of the event, including interactions with ministers and heads of delegations from participating countries."In general, there were also meetings between ministers and heads of delegations, as the aim of this (multilateral) forum is to exchange views, so there were many meetings, and a lot of things were discussed," the culture secretary said.Pakistan's Federal Minister Musadik Masood Malik, who attended the three-day forum, said he was in India to discuss regional issues and cultural ties in the context of the SCO, and not the Indus Waters Treaty."When you will call me for talk on Indus (Water Treaty), that time, we will surely talk on Indus (treaty). This time, you have not called me here for (talks on) the Indus treaty; this time you have called me to talk...," Malik told reporters."You have called me this time to talk about the issue in the context of the SCO forum, the regional issues, its relationship with culture, for which I am here," he said.The three-day forum, held from November 20 to 22, was organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs. It was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 20 and saw the participation of delegates from various SCO member countries, including Iran and Pakistan, as well as other countries.

World.title: Anti-immigration crackdown: US put 1,389 Indian children in custody in 4 years
World.content:
AHMEDABAD: The anti-immigration crackdown in US has swept 1,389 unaccompanied Indian children into custody since Americaâs FY23. These children have not been repatriated.

However, the unyielding drive against immigrants has reduced the number of unaccompanied Indian children found in US: 730 in FY23, 517 in FY24, 91 in FY25, 51 in FY26, and two in Oct 2026, the first month of US FY27.

The data is from US Customs and Border Protection (USCBP).

The decline mirrors the trend for unaccompanied children of all nationalities. US authorities recorded 1.1 lakh unaccompanied children in FY24, 29,584 in FY25, and 9,190 in FY26. In Oct 2026, 722 children were found unaccompanied.

People familiar with immigration networks in US said the decline could partly be linked to stricter enforcement and faster deportations.



Earlier, minors were allegedly used as âgreen card bringersâ to help parents or relatives strengthen their chances of obtaining legal status.

This practice is reportedly becoming less common as authorities swiftly deport those caught.

Changing trend

A businessman from Kadi, who was deported from US in 2012, said his 17-year-old son, who has been living in Texas since he was 12, is now afraid to attend his asylum hearings.

âHe thinks he will be caught and deported to India. He has been secretly working at a gas station and living with members of a religious sect,â the businessman said.





The trend comes even as Indians continue to feature among the top nationalities attempting illegal entry into US. In FY26, US authorities recorded 30,528 encounters with Indian nationals, placing India third among 21 countries, behind Mexico and Canada.

World.title: Food regulator FSSAI sanctions prosecution of Bisleri, 4 other firms
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) has sanctioned prosecution against five food businesses, including Bisleri International Pvt Ltd, over food products found unsafe or substandard, while suspending the licences of two other establishments over serious food safety and hygiene violations.

FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri over a sample of packaged drinking water that was found non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Referral Food Laboratory too declared it unsafe after detecting polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Bisleri International was contacted for its response but had not responded till the time this report was filed.

World.title: India, Nepal set to ink pacts on energy, infra, tech on Balen Shah's 1st visit
World.content:
Shah arrived in Delhi on Sunday afternoon at the invitation of PM Modi

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar called on Nepal PM Balendra Shah, who arrived in India on Sunday for what is his first bilateral visit abroad. PM Modi will host Shah for their first in-person meeting on Monday that will be followed by an exchange of "forward-looking" agreements spanning key areas of cooperation: infrastructure, technology, connectivity, development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, climate change and disaster resilience."India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal. Look forward to his engagements with PM @narendramodi tomorrow," said Jaishankar in a post on X after the meeting. Official sources said that the leaders will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives, apart from joining foundation stone-laying ceremonies for some new projects. Shah is also expected to reiterate Nepal's request for two-way low-altitude air entry corridors through Indian airspace near western border entry points.Securing direct air routes is essential for Nepal to attract international airlines and make its new Bhairahawa airport commercially viable. âThis visit comes at an opportune moment when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology and addressing issues like natural disasters and climate change,â said a source, adding that the leaders will look to provide political direction that will shape the roadmap for bilateral cooperation for many years to come.The two sides have finalised a joint vision for bilateral relations that is expected to be released after the meeting. Nepal is also seeking an economic package worth $2 billion from India. While Shah may raise the boundary issue, itâs unlikely to be a sticking point in the meeting.India sees its ties with Nepal as unique and comprehensive, characterised by mutual trust, open borders, shared traditions and close people-to-people ties. Govt sources highlighted how India is Nepalâs largest trade, transit and investment partner. Nepal enjoys duty-free access to the Indian market and India is also Nepalâs biggest export destination and receives about 80% of Nepalâs goods exports, they said.The visit is expected to build upon the goodwill generated in Nepal by Indiaâs assistance to the country after the devastating floods earlier this year. India provided about 140 tonnes of emergency supplies and extended technical assistance in tunnel rescue and forensic activities following the flash flood.India and Nepal are exploring the development of new pipelines and terminals to further enhance energy connectivity. Both sides are also discussing new possibilities, such as the RaxaulKathmandu railway link, which could open new avenues for cross-border passenger and freight connectivity

World.title: NHAI puts 50,000 km of highways under dashcam watch, to automate penalties for contractors
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Highway concessionaires, maintenance contractors and NHAI officials will no longer be able to dodge or delay action on defects, such as potholes, faded road markings, rutting and faulty lights, which remain major recurring problems on NH stretches.

NHAI has rolled out a system for weekly monitoring of 40 types of defects through dashcams installed in patrolling vehicles covering nearly 50,000 km of NH network.

NHAI officials said that not only will data and details be collected with exact location and visual evidence, but these will also be shared with respective contractors responsible for specific stretches.

âThe dashcams can detect potholes as small as two inches pothole.



Currently, failing to rectify defect within a set timeline attracts penalties, which are calculated as per contract conditions. In the next couple of months, the penalty calculation will become automatic. We have been sensitising contractors and officers for the past two months,â said a senior NHAI official.

Dashcams detecting highway defects

This covers all NH stretches under NHAI that are under operation and maintenance. This is significant considering that the highways authority has faced public ire over poor maintenance of several road stretches.





Data accessed by TOI showed that 92,088 defects were detected through dashcam recordings since the exercise was rolled out two months back. Nearly 23% of these related to faded road markings and around 15% to potholes. While nearly 72% of the defects were rectified, around 17% remain overdue for rectification.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

As per the set timelines, contractors get two days to fill potholes, one day to fix defunct lights and safety issues at work zones, and seven days to close unauthorised openings, to name a few.

âSince the details of defects are backed by evidence and every contractor and field officer can see them on our central server, there is no question of any dispute. Highway contractors also understand that timely maintenance reduces their burden. The defects are closed only when details of rectification with pictorial evidence are uploaded and verified,â said another NHAI official.

TOI has learnt that at a later stage, the public would also be able see the details and give their feedback.

World.title: Indian Navy allows marriage for Agniveers opting for 2-year service extension
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Easing rules to make naval jobs more attractive, the

has allowed Agniveers who opt for a two-year extension after the initial four-year service to get married. The policy relaxation comes just as the first batch of Naval Agniveers â recruited in late 2022 â completes its initial four-year stint this month.

The Union Cabinet recently approved a two-year extended service period for Agniveers, officially called âSecond Tour of Dutyâ.

âThose Agniveers who have completed their four-year initial service period and have opted for the two-year extension will be allowed to marry, though only after completion of their mandatory initial training on joining. The training will be professional and trade specific,â a defence source told TOI.



After completing their training, Agniveers can take the entitled leave for marriage purposes, the source said.

The marriage provision is currently not available for Naval Agniveers (ages 17.5 to 21) during the initial four-year service period under the Agnipath scheme. âNavy has made the decision on marriage provision and orders have been issued,â the source said. After the Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force could follow suit by allowing Agniveers to marry as per their own specifications.

Govt has also decided to create a pathway for âall Agniveers to be enrolled as regular soldiers (permanent job)â if they are willing to continue and meet selection criteria. To make the extension lucrative, extended-tenure Agniveers will receive Rs 43,500 per month in the first year of extension and Rs 47,500 per month in the second year (plus applicable allowances), while govtâs Seva Nidhi contribution will rise to 70% during those two years.

World.title: Ladakh chief secretary cites cites 70% panchayat poll turnout, sticks to December 4 hill council voting
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra on Sunday welcomed the high voter turnout in panchayat and municipal elections held the previous day, saying it reflected that people want democracy as he appealed for greater participation in hill council (LAHDC) polls scheduled for Dec 4.

The turnout was 70.03% in Saturdayâs panchayat elections and 52.4% in municipal polls. âWe must not forget that the last panchayat and municipal elections were held in 2018. This is the first time elections are being held since Ladakh became a Union Territory (in 2019),â Kundra said.

Kundra announced that talks between Ladakhi representatives and the Union home ministry (MHA) on autonomy would resume after the LAHDC elections.



Leh Apex Body (LAH) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk is at the forefront of protests by Ladakhi groups against holding the LAHDC polls in the harsh winter when they claim many people are away.

Kundra asked Wangchuk not to make âprovocative statementsâ during election season. Asked about LABâs demand to delay LAHDC polls, Kundra said: âOnly 10 to 12 days are left. Around 70% of the people voted in the panchayat election.

To claim that 40% of the people are not even here is not correct. It is not as if people are casting their votes without being present.â

World.title: Kaiga nuclear unit-1 attains criticality again, gets a second life
World.content:
A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a big milestone for the countryâs nuclear sector, Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 (KGS-1) in Karnataka successfully attained criticality early Sunday for the second time, giving a new lease of life to the nuclear power unit that had been taken offline for life-extension work after 25 years of operation. The disclosure was made on Sunday by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), the PSU that designs, builds, commissions and operates nuclear power plants across India.A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core.KGS-1 had reached first criticality on Sept 26, 2000, and had supplied 37,670 million units before it was shut down for refurbishment activities in April last year. The same unit had set a world record for 962 days of continuous operation on Dec 31, 2018, operating at a 99.3% plant load factor, surpassing the previous global record of 940 days held by Heysham II (Unit 8/Reactor 2) in the UK.âThe accomplishing this in just 600 days following its shutdown for major refurbishment activities of EMCCR (en-masse coolant channel replacement) and EMFR (en-masse feeder replacement) on April 1, 2025, KGS-1 has set a new fleet-wide benchmark as the first NPCIL reactor to reach criticality in such a short span,â NPCIL said on X on Sunday.It said, âThis remarkable success stands as a reflection of extraordinary dedication, technical excellence, and unified teamwork. âKaiga generating station has four operational nuclear units totalling 880 MW and two additional units (5 and 6) under construction, adding 1,400 MW and bringing the total planned capacity to 2,280 MW across six units.Kaiga Units-5 & 6 are state-of-the-art, indigenous 700 MW pressurized heavy-water reactors (PHWRs), which incorporate advanced safety features and are among the safest in the world. Three such PHWRs â KAPS-3&4 and RAPP-7 â are successfully operating in the states of Gujarat and Rajasthan respectively. The components and equipment for the project are supplied by domestic industry partners and works are being executed by Indian contractors, aligning with the Atmanirbhar initiatives of the Modi govt.Just days before, in another development, Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) granted permission for the first approach to criticality of Rajasthan atomic power project unit-8 (RAPP-8) at Rawatbhata, following satisfactory completion of safety reviews.
