World.title: In praise of Mymensingh’s Bangla folk ballads
World.content:
Folk-ballads are living archives that represent the imagination, values, ideas, and aesthetics of the people to whom they belong. Bangla literature has a rich repertoire of folk ballads. We are, however, quite oblivious of this treasure trove and, therefore, there is a dearth of research on these folk elements.

Czech Indologist Dusan Zbavitel's Bengali Folk-Ballads From Mymensingh And The Problem Of Their Authenticity can be called a wonderful exception in this regard. It is considered to be the first literary study of the beautiful folk-ballads from Mymensingh. The study was published by the University of Calcutta in 1963.

A brief background of the book may not be irrelevant here. In 1923, Rai Bahadur Dineshchandra Sen edited a volume of epic songs from the Mymensingh District of the then Eastern Bengal under the title Maimansimha-gitika. The ballads were mainly collected by Chandra Kumar De, a literary activist from the area. In the following years, Dineshchandra published three more volumes of balladic texts containing epic songs from different parts of Eastern Bengal. The beautiful ballads received enthusiastic response and admiration in India and abroad. However, for some scholars these ballads were too good, and they shared doubts about the ‍antiquity, authenticity and folk character of these lores. Dusan Zbavitel found this uncertainty "highly regrettable" and undertook a study to assign to the ballads their proper place—"one of the high points of Bengali literature". Dr Zbavitel tried to find out: "what is it that makes them so excellent?"

Zbavitel confined his analysis to the study of the ballads originating in Mymensingh—41 ballads containing more than 21,000 verses. He took an arduous effort of analysing each of these 41 ballads to prove their originality and, I must say, he achieved his goal with marked success.

One key argument put forward by Zbavitel in favour of the originality of the gitikas from Mymensingh is that these ballads are not collected by a single person and, still, there are similarities among the ballads: identical images, and similar artistic approach and common inventory of similes and metaphors. So these ballads couldn't be the creation of a modern poet as suggested by some detractors.

According to Zbavitel, the most significant aspect of these folk ballads is that they are devoid of any religious implications. They generally show harmonious co-existence of the Hindu and Muslim communities, without religious bias on either side. Zbavitel points out the fact that most of the Hindu ballads were collected from Muslim singers, which shows, according to him, that these folk poems were enjoyed and appreciated by both the communities with the same eagerness. The secular outlook of the folk ballads is diametrically opposite to the explicit religious connotation of the classical Bangla literary texts such as Mangal-kavyas and Vaisnava literature.

Zbavitel extensively discusses the ideological and artistic approach of the ballad writers, verse and rhyme technique, and use of similes and metaphors in chapter three and four of the book. The most dominant motif, according to Zbavitel, is love. Even the historical and heroic epics can be grouped into this category.

As to the literary techniques, the ballad writers, being true to the characteristics of folk epics, do not try to introduce innovations in their lyrical dictions. They are content with the poetic means offered by their predecessors. They want to tell an interesting and touching story in a simple garb, fresh with country scenes and feelings.

Zbavitel also discusses the manner of preservation of the folk ballads—preserved, in most cases, in torsos. Referring to two versions of the same ballad, Maishal Bandhu, he argues, "The 'original' ballads [were] sometimes rewritten by another folk poet, or other poets, quite freely, without any scruples; whole portions, as well as individual couplets and verses, were taken over, others were replaced by newly replaced passages, and the story itself was often changed." The reasons behind such changes, according to Zbavitel, might be an effort to offer listeners a 'better' story than the original one.

Due to this oral nature of preservation, it is always difficult to prove the originality of folk elements. If we undertake an effort to study the folklore of Bangladesh, Zbavitel's book will be an invaluable companion guide.

Rabindranath Tagore wrote to Dinesh Chandra Sen in appreciation of the book Maimansimha-gitika, "Classical Bengali literary texts such as Mangal-kavyas are ponds dug on by order and at the expense of the rich, but Maimansimha-gitika is a source of exuberance from the deepest level of the heart of rural Bengal, a clear stream of genuine pain. There has never been such a creation of self-forgetting rasa [aesthetic joy] in Bengali literature." [translation by the author]

While celebrating the Bengali new year this Pohela Boishakh, may we remember the melody and the essence of communal harmony embedded in Maimansimha-gitika.

Shamsuddoza Sajen is a journalist and researcher. He can be contacted at [email protected].

World.title: Fizz takes three in Mumbai rout
World.content:
Pace sensation Mustafizur Rahman recorded his best bowling figures of the Indian Premier League today when he finished with 3 for 16 in Sunrisers Hyderabad’s 85-run victory over Mumbai Indians at Vishakhapatnam.

The three-wicket haul took the left-armer to joint-second in the wicket-takers’ list with a total tally of 13 scalps from nine matches. He is one short of Mitchell McClenaghan, who has taken 14 wickets in 10 matches.

The 20-year-old currently has the best bowling average, 15.61, and best economy rate, 6.15, amongs bowlers who have played at least eight matches in the tournament.

The Sunrisers Hyderabad might have depended on Mustafizur a number of times in the ongoing Indian Premier League, but today was a collective effort. Ashish Nehra, Bhuvaneshwar Kumar and Barinder Sran had reduced the Mumbai Indians to 49 for 6 in nine overs before Mustafizur was given the ball.

The wily left-armer sent back Hardik Pandya with his first ball with a cutter which Pandya failed to adjust himself against. Pandya attempted a slice through point, but the ball curled away to the hands of the keeper, with the umpire judging that out even though the television replays were inconclusive.

Then in the very first ball of his second over again, Fizz bowled yet another slower delivery which moved away from the batsman, getting the edge of Tim Southee on the way to the keeper.

The man from Satkhira returned got the scalp of McClenaghan in the final delivery of his third over, getting the batsman to offer a loopy catch to midwicket.

Mustafizur did not get to bowl a fourth over as David Warner gave the other bowlers their chance to mop up the tail. And they did efficiently, bundling out the hosts for just 92 runs in 16.3 overs.

Earlier, brilliant performances from Hyderabad openers, Warner and Shikhar Dhawan helped the team post 177. Dhawan scored 82 off 57 while Warner smacked 48 off 33. Yuvraj Singh also had a good time with the bat, scoring 39 off 23.

World.content:
Months after flood devastated families, survivors live in trauma

Loss of loved ones, homes and livelihoods, coupled with uncertainty over the future, is taking a heavy toll on the people displaced by the Bhotekoshi disaster.

People reach a hospital in Kathmandu to search for their relatives missing in the flood. Nepal Photo Library

World.title: India likely to announce $1.5 billion package for Nepal, air-route deal under discussion
World.content: Anil Giri is a Chief Sub Editor covering diplomacy, international relations and national politics for The Kathmandu Post. Giri has been working as a journalist for more than two decades, contributing to numerous national and international media outlets.

World.title: Biratnagar’s three-year-old rail cargo infrastructure is crumbling
World.content:
Biratnagar’s three-year-old rail cargo infrastructure is crumbling

Despite the commissioning of the Bathnaha-Biratnagar railway line, cargo trains have failed to operate regularly as the yard, platforms, storage areas and internal roads have already suffered damage due to poor maintenance.

With the structures linked to the railway line not in a condition suitable for efficient operation, plans to expand freight transportation by rail have failed to gain the expected momentum. Parbat Portel/TKP

World.title: Chiefs and Bills set for showdown while Lions, Bears roll
World.content:
The Buffalo Bill’s Josh Allen and the Kansas City Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes shined on Sunday ahead of next week’s NFL Thanksgiving showdown, while the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears extended their win streaks with comprehensive victories.

Allen threw for 304 yards and a touchdown, and James Cook ran for 89 yards and a touchdown to spark host Buffalo to a win over the Miami Dolphins 26-9.

The Bills (9-1) stretched their win streak to six games by dumping the one-win Dolphins ahead of Thursday’s blockbuster home game against Kansas City (8-2).

World.title: Tarik Skubal agrees to record 9-year deal with Mets worth $450 million
World.content:
Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner, has agreed to terms on a record nine-year deal worth $450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports on Sunday.

The 30-year-old left-hander spent his first six seasons with the Detroit Tigers before joining the Los Angeles Dodgers in a trade last August, but he was unable to help the club lift a third consecutive World Series trophy.

The $50 million average annual value would make the deal a record for pitchers, surpassing the $43.3 million annual value of contracts for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander.

Skubal’s deal also would be the richest contract for any pitcher in MLB history, surpassing the mark of $325 million set when the Dodgers signed Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year deal in 2024.

Skubal became only the 12th pitcher in MLB history to win back-to-back Cy Youngs when he captured the award in the American League in 2024 and 2025.

He completed the AL triple crown in 2024, leading the league in wins with 18 and in ERA at 2.39 while also topping MLB in strikeouts with 228.

Skubal, a unanimous Cy Young choice in 2024, also had the AL’s lowest ERA in 2025 at 2.21 and struck out 241 batters over 195⅓ innings to repeat.

In 2026, he won an arbitration hearing and was awarded $32 million for the 2026 season, but the campaign was interrupted in May when he had to undergo surgery for loose bodies in his elbow.

He returned in July and went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 62 innings, then went 1-1 in the playoffs, where the Dodgers were eliminated by the eventual champion Milwaukee Brewers.

Skubal, considered the top free agent available, made the agreement as MLB owners and the MLB Players Association stand deadlocked over how to divide profits with the Dec. 1 deadline for a new deal fast approaching.

If the sides cannot agree on terms for a new collective bargaining agreement, a lockout is expected next month.

Owners demand a salary cap system while the union has been against such a format for decades.

World.title: Hiroshima joins forces with bus operators to redraw local routes
World.content:
The city of Hiroshima and eight bus operators are stepping up efforts to restructure the local bus network through a public-private partnership, Japan’s first such initiative to jointly operate fixed-route bus services.

Now in its second year, the partnership has begun trial operations of new routes and increased services on existing routes in three areas of the city under a three-month pilot program launched in October.

They plan to use what they are learning from the program to help shape a broader restructuring of the network.

World.title: Max Verstappen mocks George Russell as ‘so far below my level’ after Las Vegas GP
World.content:
Max Verstappen lobbed a verbal shot at George Russell, labeling the latter as “so far below my level” following his victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night.

Verstappen also laughed at the Mercedes driver’s late-race mistake on Saturday and characterized the driver’s 2026 season as a “complete joke.”

“Ha ha, well done! My God,” Verstappen said on a radio broadcast moments after Russell careened into the wall on the 48th of 50 laps in Las Vegas.

Verstappen, a four-time Formula 1 world champion, didn’t stop there.

“This actually had nothing to do with Formula 1,” he told Dutch broadcaster ViaPlay. “But I did enjoy some of the action. Especially because one person in particular didn’t stand a chance. He deserves that too.”

Russell, 28, took issue following an incident with Verstappen during practice on Friday, saying that latter shouldn’t be able to “walk around like they are bigger and better than everyone else.”

Verstappen, who drives for Red Bull Racing, said he was unfazed by Russell’s comments.

“His comments don’t motivate me, because he’s nowhere near me,” Verstappen, 29, said. “All talk off the track and a complete joke on it this season. Perfect karma.”

Verstappen held off multiple challengers in the Nevada desert on Saturday night to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the second straight year and third time in four editions since the circuit was added to the schedule.

The win — the 75th in his F1 career — was important beyond one race for multiple reasons.

The 29-year-old saw Great Britain’s Russell take the Vegas race in 2024, a year after Verstappen won the inaugural event. After winning it again in 2025, Verstappen on Saturday was able to get the back-to-back wins.

Russell, who was a significant challenger during Saturday’s race as he exchanged positions 12 times while dueling with Verstappen for the lead, finished ninth.

The win also continues Verstappen’s resurgence after a rough start to the season, one that saw him go winless until October. Verstappen had openly questioned his future in F1 after this season and criticized both the series and the media. Vegas marked his fourth win in six races and firmly planted him in second place in the standings with two races left.

Russell is three points out of a tie for third with Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton.

World.title: Carlos Alcaraz rolls past No. 1 Alexander Zverev to win first ATP Finals title
World.content:
Seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz powered past world No. 1 Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (9-7) on Sunday to win his maiden ATP Finals title.

The Spaniard, who came back at the U.S. Open after a four-month break due to a wrist injury, saved three set points in the tiebreak before completing his 14th consecutive victory and ending the year with a third straight title, having also triumphed in Vienna and Paris.

The 23-year-old, who is the youngest man to have completed the career Grand Slam, secured the biggest tour title that had eluded him after finishing runner-up at the ATP Finals last year.

World.title: Defense, AI, high tech: A delicate balance between armies and industry
World.content:
The rapid integration of high tech and artificial intelligence into the armed forces presents a tricky dilemma: entrusting part of their future to private companies while risking their sovereignty.

On one side are digital and mission-critical technology specialists driven by market forces and controlled by private capital demanding profits, independent from any political control.

On the other are military leaders who answer only to political authority and are obsessed with strategy, hierarchy and the sacrosanct nature of defence secrecy.

World.title: Studio Ghibli composer Joe Hisaishi given honorary doctorate by U.K. college
World.content:
The Royal College of Music on Friday awarded an honorary doctorate to Japanese composer Joe Hisaishi, known for his music for Studio Ghibli animated films, recognizing his “outstanding contribution” to a wide range of musical fields.

Hisaishi became the first Japanese to receive an honorary doctorate from the college.

At the award ceremony, Royal College of Music Director James Williams introduced the 75-year-old Hisaishi’s orchestral works and music he composed for animated films directed by Hayao Miyazaki.

“He has forged a distinctive artistic voice that unites structural clarity, melodic immediacy and profound emotional resonance,” Williams said.

Addressing about 200 composition students at the ceremony, Hisaishi said, “Challenging what already exists and creating something new will pave the way for the future of music.”

“All you have to do is start with a small idea and develop it,” he added.

The Royal College of Music is a prestigious institution in London that has produced notable British composers, including Gustav Holst and Ralph Vaughan Williams.

World.title: Tower Records becomes latest Japan retailer hit by data breach
World.content:
Music retailer Tower Records Japan said customer information was leaked following unauthorized access, making it the nation’s latest retailer to disclose a data breach.

The intrusion exposed login information for about 10.2 million accounts, including email addresses and user IDs, the company said in a statement updated Sunday. The unauthorized access was detected on Thursday, it said.

Tower Records’ disclosure follows a data leak involving online apparel retailer Zozo, which said on Friday that information belonging to about 15.2 million customers had been compromised. Zozo said it was affected by the breach of a Plaid Inc. marketing platform that the retailer uses to manage customer information; Marui Group, which uses the same platform, has also reported a similar incident.

Japanese companies’ longstanding reliance on traditional IT systems has frequently been cited as a vulnerability in the face of increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. The impact of recent weaknesses found in PHP, a widely used programming language, has been particularly evident in Japan.

World.title: Beijing hails Election Committee poll for affirming ‘patriots-only’ system in Hong Kong
World.content:
Beijing has lauded Hong Kong’s Election Committee poll for demonstrating what it called the broad representation, political inclusiveness and fair competition of the “patriots-only” system, saying the latest race proved the effectiveness of the model.

In a statement issued on Monday, the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office (HKMAO) also said the poll – which drew a record turnout of nearly 99 per cent, or 5,640 registered voters – reflected that the revamped electoral system was now operating with “increasing maturity” and strengthening people’s confidence in building “high-quality democracy” in the city.

The overall turnout of the Sunday poll jumped by about 9 percentage points from 2021, as 856 candidates competed for 723 seats in the 1,500-strong powerful electoral college tasked to choose the city’s next leader.

World.title: Reform of Hong Kong’s sexual offence laws better late than never
World.content:
Reform of Hong Kong’s sexual offence laws better late than never

Long-needed updates to sexual offence laws are here after 20 years of waiting; now all of Hong Kong must work together to make them stick

World.title: Tai Po fire: will the right lessons be learned?
World.content:
Based on interviews and an independent committee’s scathing report, Connor Mycroft details the key turning points behind the avoidable Wang Fuk Court fire, as part of a series marking one year since the tragedy.

As Hong Kong marks the one-year anniversary of the deadly Tai Po fire, survivors and the city’s residents alike are still questioning how a tragedy of such a scale could have happened in a first-world city.

The report by the independent committee tasked with investigating the fire was scathing. “Deliberate misconduct”, “decades of failure” and “a lack of sense of crisis” are just some of the terms that are now embedded in the city’s collective consciousness.

World.title: Hong Kong Election Committee race: ‘healthy’ contest with some upsets
World.content:
Hong Kong’s Election Committee poll on Sunday drew a record turnout of nearly 99 per cent and delivered surprise upsets, with prominent business and professional leaders losing out in tighter races for seats on the body that will choose the city’s next leader.

With Beijing urging that turnout be “the higher the better”, 5,640 registered voters cast ballots on Sunday as 856 candidates competed for 723 seats on the powerful electoral college. Just 69 electors failed to vote. Overall turnout jumped by about 9 percentage points, from 89.77 per cent in 2021 to 98.79 per cent.

With no “blessing list” in most subsectors and candidates competing in a free contest, some results dealt a blow to industry heavyweights.

World.title: Man arrested in Hong Kong over dog found hanging from tree on Tai Po trail
World.content:
A man has been arrested in Hong Kong in connection with a mongrel found hanging from a tree on the Wilson Trail in Tai Po, the South China Morning Post has learned.

A source said police arrested a 54-year-old man on Sunday evening on suspicion of cruelty to animals, hours after his elder sister alerted them.

At around 12.24pm, the 57-year-old woman called police after finding the stray dog – which her brother had fed for about a year – hanging lifeless from a tree outside a stone hut on section eight of the trail.

World.title: When ambition takes a different path
World.content:
To pursue that aspiration, he set up two companies, a creative styling agency and a vintage store that opens up a market for celebrities' pre-loved clothing, the second of which reflects his long-held wish to use fashion to promote environmental protection by giving garments a second life.Getting the ventures started proved difficult. "In the early stages of my start-up, because I lacked a track record and financial history, my application to open a business account was rejected by other banks, leaving me feeling very lost and uncertain," he recalls.

Known professionally as SoMad, So Pak Kit Matthew describes himself as a multimedia creator, a costume and art director, and a brand consultant. He won Best Costume and Make-up Design at the 44th Hong Kong Film Awards for Sons of the Neon Night. His aspiration, he says, is to use his madness, creativity and vision to help others achieve their dreams while staying true to himself.

Some of the happiest moments in SoMad's career come when an artiste he has dressed for the red carpet wins a best-dressed award that night. That, he says, feels happier and more real than winning an award himself. Building businesses of his own, however, called for more than creative flair.

[The content of this article has been produced by our advertising partner.]

In his account for OCBC Hong Kong's latest brand campaign, he says the bank sat down with him to discuss what he needed, saw his potential and set up the accounts his businesses required. It has since provided wealth management guidance as his ventures have grown.

"This human touch and trust have given me the peace of mind to entrust my wealth management to them ever since, making them the most solid backing for my career," he says.

SoMad is among 24 people featured in the bank's social media series, launched in October under the theme "Together, Lifting Everyone We Serve". Participants from entertainment, business, sport and social services share how they have pursued their goals, and how financial planning has played a part.

From the bank's perspective, the stories connect financial planning with the decisions people face throughout different life stages, from starting a business and funding a child's education to providing for a family and preparing for succession.

A different kind of responsibility

And for Edmond Lau, chief executive of SAHK, the connection between finance and personal purpose has developed over a career spanning monetary policy and social welfare.

Lau spent much of his earlier career at the Hong Kong Monetary Authority before leaving to study for a master’s degree in social work and work in the non-profit sector. In April 2025 he took over at SAHK, which provides rehabilitation, education and community services for people with disabilities and their families.

Participants in SAHK’s Little Seeds, Joyful Learning Heart programme, supported by OCBC Hong Kong. (Photo: SAHK) The work is different, but Lau sees familiar demands for sound planning, responsible management and partners who can be relied on. For an NGO, he says, every resource comes with a duty to the public and the people who depend on its services.That responsibility is evident in SAHK's partnership with OCBC. They launched the two-year Little Seeds, Joyful Learning Heart Nurturing Scheme, supported by an exclusive HK$1 million contribution from the bank.

Through Community Fun Day, parent-child colouring competition, parent-child activities and community educational activities, it helps young children, including those with special educational needs, develop curiosity, patience, concentration and other learning skills.

In September 2026, SAHK reported findings from a survey of 923 parents and early-childhood educators. The research found that while young children are often eager to explore, self-control, patience and the ability to follow plans tend to develop more gradually. The programme is expected to benefit more than 20,000 children and parents over two years.

Edmond Lau of SAHK, featured in OCBC Hong Kong’s “24 Real Stories of Aspiration” series. (Photo: OCBC) Stories of Aspirations Lau describes the bank as a long-standing partner that understands the organisation's needs and helps it plan ahead.

In October, OCBC Bank (Hong Kong) Limited launched its annual brand campaign under the theme “Together, Lifting Everyone We Serve”. The campaign reinforces the bank’s purpose of helping people realise their aspirations and its role as a trusted wealth management and financial services partner.

A centrepiece is the social-media series “24 Real Stories of Aspiration”. It features 24 people from diverse sectors sharing their journeys and how professional financial services can support Hong Kong people at different stages of life. Behind every aspiration, the bank says, lies a purpose worth protecting and a dream worth pursuing.

The participants are at different points in their lives: young professionals building wealth, successful individuals seeking a more strategic approach to their assets, parents planning for children’s education and family protection, and entrepreneurs preparing for succession.

Through the series, they share the challenges they have faced, the financial decisions they have made, and the role that professional financial advice and solutions can play in supporting their aspirations.

World.title: Hong Kong films shine as Angela Yuen, Anson Kong win at Golden Horse Awards
World.content:
Hong Kong actress Angela Yuen Lai-lam has won the best actress prize at the prestigious Golden Horse Awards in Taiwan, while Anson Kong Ip-sang of boy band Mirror has snagged the best supporting actor trophy.

The 33-year-old Yuen beat fellow contenders for the top acting prize for her performance in Hong Kong film Afterpiece, in which she plays an amateur actress who auditions for a leading role in a stage play and later becomes embroiled in a complex dynamic with its director.

Yuen drew widespread support in October after calling out deep-rooted misogyny in the entertainment industry in a personal essay posted on her social media account.

World.title: One Stanley developer reports alleged extortion bid involving ‘tens of millions’
World.content:
The developer of the luxury One Stanley housing estate, where suspected substandard construction work was recently uncovered, has reported an alleged extortion attempt to police, with the South China Morning Post learning that the firm was asked to pay tens of millions of Hong Kong dollars.

A spokesman for K&K Property said on Sunday that the company had reported the alleged extortion attempt to police on November 4.

“The case has already been handed to police, and we will not comment on the matter,” the spokesman said.

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019307/Lost Ground: China’s Coffee Brands Break Starbucks and Nestlé’s Grip on Yunnan
World.title: Lost Ground: China’s Coffee Brands Break Starbucks and Nestlé’s Grip on Yunnan
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019307/Lost Ground: China’s Coffee Brands Break Starbucks and Nestlé’s Grip on Yunnan
World.content:
For coffee growers in China’s southwestern Yunnan province, Starbucks and Nestlé used to be the only buyers in town. Every harvest season, their purchasing stations would have lines of loaded trucks stretching for days.

Plantation owner Zou Qingquan recalls once waiting a whole week to sell her beans to Nestlé. Back then, she says, the company revised its purchase price twice a week based on changes in the international commodity market, “so your beans were making or losing money as they sat there in the truck.”

Over the past five years, however, these two global giants have been losing their grip on the Yunnan coffee market. Rapid growth among domestic brands such as Seesaw, Manner, Luckin, and the Mixue Group, along with a shift toward specialty coffee, has opened new sales channels for farmers and pushed up prices.

According to the agricultural industry analysis platform Beedata, Nestlé and Starbucks paid an average of 48.09 yuan ($7.20) and 48.18 yuan per kilogram, respectively, for commercial-grade Yunnan green beans in the first quarter of 2026. For Luckin, it was 50.37 yuan.

But while growers’ incomes have risen, some warn that an increasingly indiscriminate buying frenzy, which in some cases is leading to the sale of unripe beans, risks disrupting established trade relationships and negatively affecting the quality and image of Yunnan coffee.

Light roast

Ma Xiaojin, who manages two coffee-growing cooperatives in Yunnan’s Menglian Dai, Lahu and Va Autonomous County, used to regularly drive the 10 hours from his farm to the Starbucks Farmer Support Center, a training and purchasing facility in central Pu’er, a city arguably best known for its eponymous tea. There, he’d join the line of trucks and wait four or five days to have his beans graded, costing him at least 2,000 yuan in truck rental costs.

Starbucks has exacting quality standards and purchases beans only from growers certified under its Coffee and Farmer Equity (CAFE) Practices program, which in January included 3,400 farms in Yunnan. The American company is also known for paying more for high-quality beans than its Swiss competitor, Nestlé.

“You can’t just show up and expect Starbucks to take your beans,” says Hao Yi, who used to work for Starbucks in coffee production. “They don’t just check each batch; they monitor your quality over several consecutive years. That’s why, in the early days, getting your beans into Starbucks was a source of pride. It also brought your subsequent harvests to the attention of specialty coffee roasters.”

In 2017, Starbucks began selling selected Yunnan beans as part of its high-end Reserve line. For growers, making the cut was no easy feat. If their products passed a preliminary check, they had to provide three large samples from each sack for testing and agree to follow-up screenings.

Specialty beans from Zou’s estate were selected in 2021, with Starbucks offering 48 yuan per kilogram. At the time, her farm was selling to the open market for more than 60 yuan per kilogram. “We earned less, but working with a big brand was good publicity for us, so it was still a net gain,” she says. The following year, many new buyers approached Zou to purchase the same beans.

Nestlé and Starbucks’ strong bargaining power stemmed not only from their steady and large purchasing orders but also from their role in establishing industry rules and standards in the region. In 1989, Nestlé introduced the province to catimor, an arabica coffee cultivar popular for its high yields and resistance to coffee leaf rust, while Starbucks has helped standardize commercial production here since the late 2000s.

Both companies also set up local agricultural support centers, dispatching agronomists to train farmers and promote good practices. Ma, whose beans were selected for the Starbucks Reserve line in 2025, remembers training sessions taking place every month or two in the early days.

“The older generation of coffee growers is very grateful to Nestlé,” says Zhang Yong, founder of Pushan Coffee, a local bean trading company. He notes that while visiting Yunnan’s coffee-growing regions last year, he found multiple farmers who were still willing to sell to the Swiss company even though its prices were lower than other brands.

However, not everyone has remained loyal to the two biggest players. On a recent trip to Pu’er, Hao talked with coffee growers and traders who said they had sold very little to Starbucks in 2025. One farmer whose beans had previously been selected for the Reserve line revealed he was now targeting other specialty coffee brands that pay more.

Ma’s two cooperatives produce 120 to 130 tons of beans a year. More than half of this output used to go to Starbucks, but over the past two years this has fallen to just over 10 tons of Reserve-grade coffee.

“It’s hard enough to buy beans in Pu’er, but it’s even more competitive in Baoshan,” Hao says. Baoshan, Yunnan’s other main coffee-growing area, is almost 10 hours by road from the Starbucks Farmer Support Center in Pu’er. With the demand for beans soaring, few are now willing to make the trip.

Working with Starbucks and Nestlé once brought huge pride and prestige, but Ma believes that the global titans’ stringent standards are increasingly seen as “too demanding,” particularly by younger farmers. It’s just easier to sell directly to smaller companies, he adds.

Taste test

Seesaw and Manner, both founded in the eastern metropolis of Shanghai, were among the first domestic coffee brands to establish a presence in Yunnan.

After launching a 10-year plan in 2014, Seesaw sent buyers to teach growers in Pu’er and Baoshan refined harvesting and processing techniques, and introduce them to specialty coffee.

Hua Runmei, a third-generation coffee grower from Pu’er, took over the family farm in 2015 after graduating from university. That year, international coffee futures — the global benchmark for pricing — were depressed, and Yunnan beans were typically sold cheap.

She agreed to transition toward growing specialty coffee in collaboration with Seesaw, which assigned a technician to guide her and assist with processing. “They tell us what they’re looking for, coffee with a clean taste and certain flavor notes, and we need to figure out how to achieve that,” Hua explains.

Her farm delivered its first 3 tons of specialty coffee beans to Seesaw in 2016. The following year, the company placed an order for 40 more.

Manner, which operates about 2,000 outlets nationwide, entered the Yunnan market in 2018, opening purchasing stations in Menglian and Baoshan. “It’s not just about a commitment to buying local. Yunnan beans are genuinely high-quality,” Wang Xu, an executive assistant to Manner CEO Jin Binbin, told the domestic media outlet Kankan News in March 2025.

The shift toward specialty coffee brought greater financial returns for growers. Hua recalls that many brands offered favorable prices and advance payments. “I think the brands that came to Yunnan in the early days were genuinely driven by a passion for locally grown coffee,” she says.

Brands generally set prices for premium beans based on production costs, allowing farms a profit margin of about 20%. They would pay up to 40% above the international futures price, sometimes more depending on the beans’ flavor profile. This not only secured beans that met their specific requirements but also encouraged growers to continue investing in cultivation and processing.

However, as domestic brands expanded, specialty coffee prices began to align with those for bulk-bought commodity coffee. “Starting around 2019 or 2020, companies changed the way they purchased beans,” Hua says. “Everyone started to want coffee that was both good and cheap.”

What emerged was a new category of bean between commodity-grade and specialty: premium commercial beans. These beans don’t have distinct flavor notes, but they do have cleaner flavor profiles and lower defect rates than standard commercial-grade beans, and typically sell for 1 to 3 yuan per kilogram more than the international futures price.

Specialty coffee brands bought relatively limited quantities of these beans. The real force reshaping supply and demand in Yunnan was companies with larger needs, such as Mixue Group and Luckin.

Mixue, a food and beverage giant based in Zhengzhou, capital of the central Henan province, acquired the budget coffee chain Lucky Cup in 2020 and expanded it as a franchise, requiring vast quantities of beans. After visiting dozens of farms, the company decided to offer freshly brewed Yunnan coffee in all of its 20,000 outlets nationwide and signed agreements with several growers for their green beans.

Chen Junxian, whose trading company Senyu Coffee was among Mixue’s first suppliers in Yunnan, recalls that local farmers and processing plants were initially lukewarm toward the Zhengzhou company, best known at the time for its ice cream and tea products.

“People didn’t really know the brand,” he explains. “They thought it was purely a milk tea company and didn’t believe it actually wanted to buy coffee beans. Now the processing plants are far more friendly.” Chen says that orders from Mixue to his business alone have nearly doubled since 2020. “We’re delivering a lot.”

The largest buyer of Yunnan beans in 2026 has been Luckin, headquartered in Xiamen, in the eastern Fujian province. Unlike other brands, which sent teams to purchasers in the region, Luckin relied for years on trading companies to handle procurement. It wasn’t until 2024 that it built its own coffee processing plant in Baoshan.

During Luckin’s Q1 2026 earnings conference call in April, co-founder and CEO Guo Jinyi announced the company had purchased more than 30,000 tons of Yunnan coffee during the 2025–26 harvest season. According to government-run news outlet Yunnan.cn, Luckin’s target is 80,000 tons a year by 2030.

For growers, the expanding market has led to enormous orders, more flexible requirements compared with Starbucks and Nestlé, and higher prices. For domestic brands, Yunnan beans mean lower transportation costs and provide an opportunity to tell the story of China-grown coffee.

Fresh take

The challenge now is keeping up with the huge demand. Industry insiders point out that even if coffee plants were grown in every suitable place in China, there would still be a supply shortage.

Chen, who started his business in 2018, says most Yunnan growers were struggling to make a profit before the market boom. Now their beans are a hot commodity, they no longer seek his help to find buyers — he needs to beg them to sell to him.

“Many aren’t comfortable with digital communication; you have to meet them in person,” says Chen, explaining that his team had to visit countless plantations, processing plants, and even farmers’ homes to secure enough beans to fill orders. This involved traipsing across sparsely populated countryside and driving 13 hours between various counties across Pu’er and Baoshan.

The thriving local economy has also attracted many Yunnan natives to return home to open coffee farms, while Pu’er tea growers have even cut down trees to make space for more coffee plants.

Some farms are also taking a chance on rare and prestigious varieties, such as Geisha, which can command a price of up to 1,500 yuan per kilogram. However, Zhang is concerned for those rookie growers who expect to sell the beans from their newly planted trees for less than 500 yuan per kilogram.

“They are investing heavily, perhaps recklessly,” he says. Geisha plants take at least three years to bear fruit and typically reach peak production around six to eight years old. No one knows what the market will look like by then, Zhang adds.

Trouble brewing?

As the buying frenzy continues, concerns about quality also grow.

Last year, Ma had to reject a whole batch of beans delivered by one of the farms he manages. “They were so bad that I couldn’t stand looking at them,” he recalls.

Coffee cherries ripen at different times, so pickers typically make three or four passes over the three- to four-month harvest season, selecting only fully ripened cherries to ensure quality and consistency. Now, in the haste to satisfy demand, some growers are cutting corners, making only two passes and picking unripe green cherries together with ripe red ones.

“Some people are willing to buy beans like these. I just don’t understand it,” Ma says. “If people keep harvesting so carelessly, in another two or three years, Yunnan coffee will be worthless.”

Chen sees the same problem. Once the outer fruit has been removed, it’s extremely difficult to distinguish between ripe and unripe beans during sorting, increasing the risk of defects. When his company tried to enforce quality standards at the source, growers simply told him that if he didn’t buy their cherries, someone else would. “There’s nothing we can do; we have to buy them,” Chen says.

When prices were 20 to 30 yuan per kilogram, his company would take green beans classified as Grade 1 — the highest level, applying to plump, unbroken beans measuring at least 6.5 millimeters — and sort through them again to try to reduce the defect rate.

But when ripe and unripe cherries are harvested together, quality control becomes impossible. “At prices above 60 yuan per kilogram, even a 4% loss is a huge amount of money. We can’t afford to do it anymore. We have no choice but to bow to market pressure,” Chen adds.

Even with a 5% defect rate, the market average, Chen’s company had sold its entire inventory by the end of April 2025.

Nestlé originally chose Yunnan because it provided a stable, low-cost source of beans for its instant coffee factory in the southern Guangdong province. Later, domestic coffee brands came to capitalize on both the market appeal of the homegrown coffee story and the logistical advantages.

However, as prices continue to rise, Pushan’s Zhang has observed that the market is starting to look overseas for alternative suppliers.

From January to May this year, China’s coffee bean imports from Vietnam increased 76.9% year on year by volume and 87.1% by value. Unlike Yunnan, which primarily grows arabica beans, Vietnam is a major producer of robusta, a cheaper variety with higher caffeine.

With this in mind, Zhang highlights a recent shift he’s noticed in how Chinese brands market their coffee. “Previously, many would advertise that they used 100% arabica, but as costs have risen, they’re no longer making that claim. They may well be blending in robusta,” he says.

Ultimately, the effects of the influx of domestic brands and rising prices will be felt in the consumers’ coffee cups.

(Due to privacy concerns, Hao Yi is a pseudonym.)

Reported by Li Dan.

A version of this article originally appeared in The Mirror. It has been translated and edited for brevity and clarity, and is republished here with permission.

Translator: Carrie Davies; editors: Wang Juyi and Hao Qibao.
